or Twi, is the language prevalent in the Gold Coast countries between the rivers Asini and Tanno on the W. and the Volta on the E., and extends even beyond this river; its southern boundary is the sea-coast, while the upper course of the Volta, and the Kong mountains are its northern limits.

rarely Etwi or Otwi, is the form used in the vernacular. It is pronounced like 'Chwee', ch and w being uttered simultaneously. The vowel i has a rising and falling tone, thus: î or ii. Twi probably denotes 'polished, refined'; from twi, to rub, polish.

or Akan, probably meaning 'foremost; genuine'; from kaŋ, first; e.g. ɔyɛ Ɔkanni, he is a born or genuine Tshi man. 'Akan' is used in a wider sense (a) for the dialects of Akem, Asante, Adanse &c. (s. § 2), and (b) in a narrower for those of Akem and Asante only.

The name 'Twi' being used not only by the natives themselves, but also by the Accras and tribes to the east of the Volta, (in the form 'Otshui'), it has been retained as the generic appellation of the language.

The dialect is considered to be spoken purest (a) in Akem; but by its "dainty and affected mode of expression" (e. g. the frequent ɛ & ɔ, where most other dialects have simply e & o, as, ades, ases, kɔree, ɔbɔɔ, sɔɔ, = ade, ase, kɔe, ɔbo, so), it appears less suited to become the common dialect of all-Tshi tribes.

The dialect of Asante agrees in all essentials with that of Akem, only the pronunciation is "broad and hard (tɛtɛrɛ denneenɛŋ)", e. g. people say "kērɛ" instead of "kyerɛ", - whilst in Akem it is "soft and delicate (bɔkɔɔ freŋkyemm)".

The dialect of Akuapem, derived from Akem and Akwam (an Akan dialect of old standing) and having points of contact with Brɔŋ and Fante, became about 1842 the literary form intelligible to all the other.

The name applied by the Asantes to a group of dialects (also known as Kāmănă) spoken in the districts N. & N. E. of the Akan districts, including Okwawu, Dkorănsă, and others, which are considered genuine Tshi but may contain foreign elements.
A dialect spoken in the districts N. & N. E. of the Akan districts, also known as Brɔŋ, which does not differ much from genuine Tshi.

A branch of the Akan language spoken by several maritime tribes in the South, which differs from other dialects by changing initial sounds (kw, gw, hw) before palatal vowels and by curtailing final vowels.
A language belonging to the Kwa group, spoken in the area between Senegal and Eastern Nigeria, specifically within the Ewe-Tshi subgroup, encompassing the Akan-Fante dialects.

pl. a-, witch, hag; wizard, sorcerer. pr. 59-62. 139. 2154; cf. bayi, ayɛŋ, baninyɛŋ, baayɛŋ, ɔbonsam, kabere. The natives describe a wizard or witch as a man or woman who stands in some agreement with the devil. At night, when all are asleep, he (or she) rises or rather leaves his (her) body, as a snake casts its slough, and goes out emitting flames from his eyes, nose, mouth, ears, armpits; he may walk with his head on the ground and his feet up; he catches and eats animals, or kills men either by drinking their blood or by catching their soul,-which he boils and eats, where-upon the person dies; or he bites them that they become full of sores. Some change themselves into leopards, snakes, antelopes; some apply their witchcraft also to trade when selling things.

a sweet-scented gum or resin (s. ohũam); the tree yielding it. The name (lit. will eat, i. e. misuse a sister) conveys an obscene notion, meaning that the use of the perfume by a girl will allure even her brother to lasciviousness; but s. pr. 2503.

[red. bobɔ] to strike; to be in, or cause, vigorous motion. This apparent primary idea of the v. has many ramifications. We shall arrange the different significations and combinations with nouns

To be in, or cause, vigorous or excessive motion: 1. to throb, palpitate: ne kōma[m'] bɔɔ no pãa, his heart smote him. 1 Sam. 24,6. — 2. to heave, to rise and fall (the river has overflowed its banks). — 3. to break out, burst forth impetuously: asu abɔ, the river has overflowed its banks. — 4. to become loose: ne yam' abo, his bowels are loose; ɛbɛbɔ ne yam', it will cause him diarrhoea. — 5. to emit excessive heat: ɔ̃wia bo, the sun shines vehemently, burns. — 6. to blow vehemently: mframa bɔ, the wind blows; cf. 15. — tr. to whirl up: mframa bɔ tutuw, the wind raises, whirls up the dust; intr. otutuw bɔ, the dust rises. — 7. to start (up), startle: bɔ birim, pirim, piriw; (from fear) bɔ mpunimpu, toyam, hũboa. — 8. to rise or cause to rise in tumultuous disorder: bɔ bum, to rise at once; tr. to make havoc; cf. 54; bɔ ẅi, twi, nyinnyan, to alarm, to be alarmed or confused. — 9. to fall back: bɔ pemmɔ (into a sitting posture), dɔmpemmɔ (of an army.) — 10. to hasten: bɔ hwii, paŋkraŋ, aperenteŋ. — 11. to move forward with impetuosity & tumultuous rapidity: bɔ kirididi, to run to and fro; bɔ (kirr) kɔ or hyeŋ. ., to rush into; bɔ hyeŋ, hyia, toa or tua. ., to rush against; bɔ tow or gu. . so, to rush, fall, or come upon. — 12. to rage: bɔ dam, bɔ gye, to run, go or be mad; to drive mad; s. dagye.

To emit a sound that 'strikes' through the air (and makes it strike the organs of hearing): 13. to strike, ring (to sound by percussion): ɔdɔŋ bɔ(pãŋ!), the clock strikes (bang!), the bell rings. — 14. to strike, beat, play on, to cause to sound by beating (of musical, resounding instruments): bɔ dɔŋ, dawuru(m'), donno, mmaa-mu (s.abaa), saŋkũ, adakabeŋ. — 15. to roar: mframa bɔ hũu, the wind roars; cf. 6. — 16. bɔ mu, bom', to cry (syn. paɛ mu, tɛstɛɛ mu, kekaw mu); bom' na ennyigyɛ! cry aloud! - to roar, thunder: gyata bobom', a lion roars; Onyankɔpɔn, ɔprannaa, osu bom', it thunders.

To increase by an inward vigorous movement or process (to full size or maturity): 17. to grow big, large, ripe, esp. of edible roots: ne nueɛma (ode, bankye, kooko, ntommɔ, ŋkate) abɔ, his (planted) things have grown large; brɔde no abɔ, those plantains are well grown; n'abũrow abɔ (= anyinnyin na asow aba, aye akɛse-akɛse, ahoa, abere), his corn is fully grown; ɔde abɔ, the yam is ripe, emmɔe ɛ, it is not yet ripe. pr.826 f.; -tr. n'asase bɔ (= ba) aduan, his land yields (produces) much food. Ps. 67,7. - wabɔ nufu, she has got full-sized breasts, her breasts are grown to full size. Cant. 8,8. — 18. to grow big, heavy, old, esp. of persons; abofra yi abɔ se ɔde: the child has become as stout as a yam; wabɔ duru, a) he has become heavy with eating, has a loaded stomach; b) she is big with child, pregnant; wabɔ apã, he or she has grown old; bɔ aberewa, to become an old woman.

To grow or turn into: 19. to grow or divide into: dua no abɔ nta, the stem divides into two branches; abɔ ŋkorata anaŋ, it has got four branches. — 20. to grow or swell into: bɔ kukuduudú, to bud; abɔ horónóa, it has become a blister, a blister or pimple has arisen; abɔ dodɔŋkú, it is puffed up. — 21. to turn into: àbɔ abirá, it has turned the reverse; bɔ no abirá, now take the reverse.

To enter into close contact, to join closely (= strike together): 22. to agree, be in unison or concord: ɔnè no bɔ, he is intimate, on friendly terms with him; ɔde ne hɔ bɔ mo hɔ, he sets his love upon you. Deut. 7,7; wɔbɔ = wokã, wɔafa wɔŋ hɔ ayoŋkɔ. — 23. bɔ mu, bom' (to strike together in the same place, Gr. § 214. Rem. 2), to join, unite; to discharge itself into, become reconciled; caus. kã . . bom', they have become reconciled; caus. kã . . bom', to reconcile, make one; kã or de (fa) . . bom', to join, unite, connect, compact, compose, consolidate; de . . bɔ . . mu, to admix, to join with: ɔde ne hɔ bɔ Kristofo mu, he enters into.

I pointed it out to him (in his face), charged him with it, upbraided him with it.
To remove, resort to a place or person: to change abode, remove to: mede makobɔ Date, I have removed (with my things) to Late, have taken my residence, have established, settled myself at L.

to gather into a ball; bɔ pɔw, to tie a knot; bɔ tirim (pɔw), to make a plan, to plan, project, design, contrive, devise; to make a resolution, resolve, make up one's mind. — 97. to invent, fabricate, forge (a falsehood, lie): wabɔ amä me, wabɔ ato me so, he has imputed to me, falsely charged me with; cf. ɔbɔmäfo. — 98. to procure by digging, scooping, filling in: bɔ fa, dɔte, hyirew, ntwoma, to dig out earth, clay, white clay, red ochre, cf. tu; bɔ akótó, to dig for crabs. pr. 329. 505. 857; bɔ nsu, to scoop or draw water, cf. saw; bɔ ŋkyene, to buy salt, which is filled into sacks (= kotó ŋkyene; ebia wɔbɔ no boaa nti na wofre no sa, s. bɔ 96); also to dig salt. — 99. to procure by cutting and peeling off: bɔ apam, to cut sticks for supporting the yam-plant; — bɔ aduru, to peel or loosen bark from trees for medicine. — 100. to procure for one's self: bɔ (nnosoa-soafo, adumayefo) paa, to hire or engage (carriers, labourers); bɔ .. were, to secure one's (own) confidence, i.e. welfare or success; bɔ (obi bɔ) bosea, to borrow money (from another). — 101. to procure for another: bɔ (obi) bɔsea, to lend money (to another); bɔ..akoŋhama, to maintain or support (with food). — 102. to apply: bɔ .. bentoa, to apply a clyster; bɔ .. hyirew, to make strokes with clay on a person's body; bɔ ntonto, to draw lots; bɔ aka, bɔ odɔm(-nsu), to try by ordeal. — 103. to cause, call forth: bɔ mmusu, to cause, conjure, or do, mischief. pr. 555. — 104. to cause, to bring upon, strike or affect with: bɔ no mmusu = kā mmusu gu no so, kā ɔhene ntam gu no so; bɔ .. hūammo, to disappoint; bɔ .. dwɔŋŋo, to confound; F. to astonish, surprise; bɔ .. yare, to cause a sickness to; bɔ .. ahohora, adapaa, anyampa, to expose to disgrace, dishonour, infamy; bɔ'.. trä ase, to cause to sit down. — 105. to exert; bɔ mmɔdeŋ, to make strenuous efforts; bɔ mmɔforo, to make new efforts. — 106. to perform, commit, practise: bɔ .. bra, to lead one's life, form one's conduct, conduct one's self: bɔ krɔŋ (krɔno), to commit a theft or robbery, to rob; bɔ ŋkyekwaakyëma, to behave proudly. pr. 1921. — 107. to exercise or practise.. against, to treat with: ɔbɔ no so dwae, he treats him with insolence, haughty contempt; ɔbɔ no kāŋ (kàne) or ayamɔŋwene, he is illiberal or stingy towards him: ɔbɔ no atirimɔdeŋ, he treats him cruelly, is harsh or cruel towards him.

K. § 180. - 5. to deceive = twa ŋkontompo. pr. 1225; wabra me wasisi me, wadaadaa me. - 6. bra .., mu, to withhold or keep back, to hide or conceal something in speaking, to dissemble, dissimulate: obráá me asɛm no mu, he wokă asɛm no ara pe a, bra mu, when you relate the case, do not say all; okyerɛe me kwaŋ no, wab'ra me mú, when he showed me the way, he misled me; cf. mmabram'.

kwaŋ no mu abieŋ dedaw, we have already gone half of the way, we are already half-way; - wobuu yɛŋ mu abieŋ, we were formed into two companies; s. 29 d. - 8. to break down, demolish (ɔdaŋ, cf. buruw, dwiriw); intr. to break down, tumble down, fall to ruin: ɔdaŋ no abu.

9. to break off (abŭrow, the ears of Indian corn), to reap. - 10. to cut off: obubu n'awɛrɛw, he pares his nails; - to cut the hair: obu n'anim = oyi yi ne ŋhwi ano, he shaves his forehead; obu n'atiko = oyi n'atiko ŋhwi ano, he shaves the back of his hair; cf. anim B. - 11. to cut or hew down, to fell (trees): bu kwae = dow, to cut the bush. pr. 652; mekɔ kwaem' makobu nnua, I will go into the wood to fell trees. - 12. bu..mu, to break or cut in the middle, to cut off: bu.. mmerem', a) obu ne mmerem' = wasi so [ɔrenyiŋ na onuŋa ŋwiee nyiŋ] na wapatuw awu, he dies a premature, untimely death, is cut off in the prime of life; - b) wábù nɛ mmére (à óde báwo) mú = ne mmere atwam', she is past age. (Heb. 11,11). - c) bu nna mu, s. abunnàm'; - d) to divide. Ezek. 5,1; cf. abupeŋ.

13. to break off the end or point, to blunt (opp. seŋ ano). pr. 994. - 14. bu..so, to break, transgress, disobey (a law, command, order, injunction); obu n'asɛm so = onnyina n'asɛm so, he breaks his (own) word, does not keep his promise; obu ne nã asɛm so, he disobeys (acts against) his mother's word; daa obu m'asɛm so ba ha, inspite of my prohibition he always comes back (lit. here). - 15. bu..so, to go beyond, surpass: ebu n'abasa so, it surpasses his power or ability; adwuma yi abu me nsa so, this work is too much for my strength; ebu ne nsa so, his means are not sufficient to pay this. St. III § 17; ɛdom no bu yɛŋ so, the enemy is stronger than we are; syn. kyɛŋ, buŋkam; cf. bram so. - 16. bu so, to run over, overflow: wahwie nsu agu mu mã abu so, he has poured water into it so that it has run or flown over. Ps. 23,5; syn. boro so, fe hō. - 17. bu so, to be abundant, plentiful, frequent, often met with, common. pr. 649; mamã ŋhoma no abu so, I have made that book common, caused it to be in the hands of many; cf. ka. - 18. bu so, to be common, unclean: nni nea abu so, do not eat unclean things. Acts 10,14.

19. To break out or forth: obu faa wɔŋ so, he broke out upon them. - 20. to end or turn out badly: n'asɛm abu, his undertaking did not come to a good end, has turned out badly. - 21. to befall: abú abù no, lit. an eruption has broken out upon him, i. e. a great calamity has befallen him. - 22. to fail, fall short, fall off in respect to vigour, activity &c.; bó bù, to get out of breath; ne bo abu, he is out of breath (s. ebo) = ne home atew no; n'ani bu, lit. his eye breaks, i. e. he is weary of waiting longer; wohwe obi kwaŋ na ɔmma a, na wo ani bu = ɛye wo ahometew.

23. To count (orig. by bending the fingers, cf. 5c: bu nsa), to reckon, compute, calculate. - bu akontaa, to cast up an account; to cipher; ɔnè no bu ak., he reckons with him. Mt. 18,23. 24; bu hō ak., to account for. - bu ano, to cast up (a sum), to sum up (in a total); bu.. fra (mu), gu..so, hye..mu, kã..hō, si..so, tia, to reckon among, to add to (cf. kaŋ.. fra): bu yi fra (hye) akontaa no mu, gu ak, no so, kã ak. no hō, tia ak. no, add this to the account; bu sika no si so na yeghwɛ, add the money to the former sum and let us see (what the amount will be); obu n'aka-foforo si dedaw so, he calculates his new debts and adds them to the old ones; - bu..mã, to impute; - bu bɛrɛ me, charge it to me! Philem. 18. - 24. bu akapɛrs, to balance an account, counterbalance a debt: obu me ak., he adjusts his account due to me by a contra-account (cf. bu 25) or by shifting off payment to another person indebted to him. - 25. bu tew, to neutralize or cancel a debt by balancing against it an equal amount owed by the creditor: mede wo ka, wo nso wode me bi, na mã yemmu ntew! wode me dare 10, me nso mede wo d. 4, enti mebu dare 4 yi matew, na yi dare 6 a aka no mã me! - 26. To account (one) for, consider.
think, deem, judge (one able, capable, apt, fit), acknowledge as; to estimate, esteem, respect, honour.
to despise, s. abomf.
to despise, disregard, hold in contempt; cf. tiatia, anim.
to behave, conduct, bear or carry oneself; bu bra = bɔ bra.

to observe the social or civil duties; ˈòbù maŋ pá, he comports (himself) well with his fellow-citizens, behaves, demeans, or carries himself well in this town, is sociable; he rules (or manages the affairs of) the town well; he labours for the welfare of the townspeople; ˈòbù (a)mam-mònè (bra-bone) se biribi, he behaves very ill; he is extremely unsociable; yɛnè mmu maŋ yi = ntrã maŋ yi mu, we can no longer live with him; yɛnè nipa yi bu maŋ yi, we live peaceably together, are on friendly terms; cf. amammu, amammui. - bu maŋ kwaŋmu a wompam', f. to administer judgment impartially.
to observe certain days; cf. Gal. 4, 10.
to pronounce sentence in favour of a person in a lawsuit, to acquit of an accusation; atemmufo (asennifo) abu no bem, the judges have acquitted him.
to give (bring in) a verdict, pass sentence against a person, to pronounce guilty, condemn; woábù no kúm fɔ, they have sentenced him to be killed.
to judge, to decide a case, to give, pass or pronounce sentence or judgment on (upon) or against: wəabu no nea ɔyɛe no so nteŋ, they have passed sentence on him for what he did.
to bring to a decision, do away with (a case); wəde asem no ahye duam' abu mu = wəde abɛre mpanyimfo na wəawie asem no di, wəabu fɔ nè bem (etə-dabi-a wəde dua hye dua ntam' bu mu).
to judge unrighteously, to pass an unjust sentence, to pervert judgment.
to pronounce an unfair, partial judgment, to judge partially.
to pronounce judgment in the manner of the Asantes.
to speak, utter, use a proverb; to make a proverb; de..bu bɛ, to turn into a proverb.

inf. bending, breaking &c.; breach, wound.

fall, ruin, overwhelming calamity, disaster, great misfortune (cf. asiane); destruction. Prov. 10, 15; mischief. the sound of calling, crying, shouting, shooting; wəde wən nsa hwee wən afonom' bùbububu, they shouted, beating their cheeks; atuo no towe bbbb.
pii, plenty, abundantly; əse-sáw' (nsu, nsā, ŋkyene, ŋŋo) no buu buu; cf. pèe 2.

v. [red. buábùa] 1. to cover, to shut, close, esp. with so; b. daŋ (so), to put a roof or thatch a house; bua adaka no so, close that box! bua aduan no so, cover that food! cf. kata so, mŭa, hini; mmuatama; opp. bue, hie. - 2. buá dà, lit. to cover (scil. the food) and sleep, i.e. to fast, to go to bed without having eaten; obuá dà, he is fasting. - 3. to come down upon: ne mmusu abua n'atifi, his mischief has fallen on his own head. - 4. to grow thick, bushy, luxuriantly.

rankly (esp. of climbers); to flourish; ɔdɛ no abúa kùsuu = ayɛ ahaban pii; ɔdɔtɔ, hama-kóro mmuá, one climber alone does not make a thicket. pr. 981; cf. bum. — 5. to answer, reply; mamma no, I gave him no answer; wɔkobuabuaa wɔŋ hɔ, they gave each other (rough) answers, scolded each other; cf. gye so. pr. 752. 2817. — 6. to congratulate: kobua wo nua a ore-saw no, congratulate your dancing brother! — 7. bua..sɔ, to charge or upbraid with, to reproach, to scold or abuse by reminding one of some reproachful deed or matter, to cast something in the teeth of; esiane se mebɔɔ ne kuruwa nti, obuàà-me sɔ, he scolded me for having broken his jug; s. asɔ-bua. — 8. bua ntsɛŋ, F. = bu nteŋ. Mt. 7,1. — 9. buabua tun, F. to conclude.
pl. m., tobacco-pipe; cf. abūrobua,

red. v., s. bu (2), to break or bend repeatedly, to double, fold: bubu ŋhoma, to fold a letter. — (7) to break many things simultaneously; to break in many pieces; to pluck: bubu asɔ̃-merewá ahaban nɔa nom, pluck some leaves, together with the stalks of the herb called asɔ̃m., boil them and drink the decoction; - to break completely. pl. a., a man lamed by sickness, palsy; F. also late in learning to walk (of children). — ɔkásá búbuafo, a lame, i.e. awkward language or manner of expressing oneself. — Cf. mmubui.
goods in exchange for provisions; shɔfo nnim sika nti, ab. na wode kɔ hɔ tɔŋ didi, money not being known to the people there, they (the travellers) carry goods with them to buy provisions.

the plucking of the ears of maize; corn-harvest.

a wicked, mischievous thing or deed; ill luck, disaster. pr. 118. (opp.: akrade); F. abomination, Mt. 24,15; a cursed thing, Deut. 7,26; curse, Zech. 14, 11; iniquity, Ezek. 18,24-26. Hab. 1,3.

(Ak. butu), v. to overturn, turn upside down, upset; obutúw n'agua, he turns his chair (as the natives, from a superstitious notion, do when they rise); b. korow, to overthrow, capsize a canoe. pr. 1297; - intr. to be overthrown. Jon. 3,4; to lie or stand upside down, to lie on the belly. pr. 2023. — kɔŋ'kɔ (tómère) bùtuw poŋ so, a tumbler stands upside down on the table; abofra ne d'ani butuw' ne nã hɔ, the child laid its face against its mother; obùtuw n'agya so, he leans against his father. — bùtuw aba so, to brood. pr. 235; batá bútúw' wo, you fail in your trade, (your trade fails); cf. ɔbata. - misuro se ɔwĩfo bɛba abebutuw me, I am afraid a thief will steal my things. — [red. butubutuw].

couching-place. Ezek. 25,5.
resting-place (for beasts). Zeph. 2,15.

v. 1. to sit on and cover eggs or young, as a fowl, to brood; ɔsáŋsá kɔ abúw = ɔkɔtɔ ŋkesua na wada so na wasow = ɔkobutuw aba so. pr. 2776. — 2. to heap together, to keep together under a covering (abe, palm nuts, till they begin to rot, -abúrow, maize, in a vessel or under the ground,

to malt it for making ahaŋ, beer, - kookóo, to ferment cocoa). - 3. to spare, save, lay up: óbùw ne sika de akɔware yere, he saves his money to procure a wife by means of it. - 4. to watch, keep sentry, guard: asrãfó buw abaŋ, soldiers guard the fort. - 5. to watch, lie in wait or ambush: óbùw no ɔkwaŋ so, he waylays him, s. tew; b. mogya, to lie in wait for blood. - 6. to watch or overtake one in the way in order to call him to account; cf. tware 2.
inf., s. buw, v. 1. - o-búw, inf. s. buw 5.

nest, coop, cage, cot, cottage, hut, lodging. pr. 2483; cf. berebúw, akókobuw; ɔdaŋ bi a wofre abosom nè asam aŋfo wɔ mu = ɔbósómbúw, abosonnáŋ, asamaŋfrédáŋ. - F. = ntama daŋ, tent, tabernacle. [G. buu].
pl. a, = okomfó; onipa a otumi frɛ nsamaŋfo nè abosom nè mmonsam mã wobɛkã wɔn anom' asem.
F. = bue, buabua.

v. [inf. nna, red. deda] 1. to lie (of a single person or thing; deda, of many persons; gu, gugu, of many things; cf. bew, bea, boa, sam, buw, butuw, teŋ, tew); ɔda fám' he lies on the ground; ɔda ayan-nyá, he lies on his back. - 2. to be in a certain place, be situated: ne küro da bepɔw so, me de da boŋ mu, his town is situated on a mountain, mine in a valley; Akwam da Firaw hɔ, Akwam is on the river Volta; kyékye da ɔsram ŋkyeŋ, the evening-star is near the moon; - to float, swim, be buoyed up: hase a éda nsu ani, a floating cask. - 3. to live in a place: ɔdeŋkyem da ŋsum', omampam nso da wuram', the crocodile lives in the water, the guana in the bush; onni daŋ na ɔda wuram'. pr. 647. 859. - 4. to sleep (esp. in the perf.): ɔkɔdá, he goes to sleep; wádá, he is sleeping. pr. 704; mèsɛŋ wo nná, I surpass you in sleeping. pr. 2892; mérekasa no, ɔfáá mu daè, whilst I spoke, he fell asleep; - obiara kã wo sa a, dá, if any one tells you so, sleep, i.e. take no notice of it! ne ti ada, s. eti. - to die: ohene dae na wansɔre. - 5. to be quiet: ne nsa nná, his hand never rests, he is industrious = oyɛ nsì, oyɛ osìfo, ɔdeyɔfo; n'ánò nná he grumbles always in my ear, I do not forget it. - 7. to weigh down: nsenea, wotom' tom' a, édá, when you continue to put things into the scale, it sinks. pr. 2986. - 8. to curdle, coagulate, congeal, thicken; to crystallize: nufu' no ada, the milk has curdled; ŋgo no ada, the palm-oil has thickened. - 9. da, Ak. = da so, s. 25 c.

Phr. 10. da abá sò, to sit on eggs to hatch them; to brood, hatch; syn. buw, butuw. - 11. da adagyaw, pr. 699, da kwaterɛkwa, to be manifest, evident, open or clear; cf. da gua, da hɔ, yi adi. - 13. da dweŋ, to lie and think, to meditate. - da hwe, to consider; s. 28, da tirim. - 14. da afã, to sleep in a separate place. pr. 384. 705. - 15. da fam', a) to be level; ɛhɔ da fam', it is a level place. Ps. 26, 12. - b) to laugh at, ridicule; syn. serew; ɔda-me fám', he laughs or laughed at me; wògu-me f., they laugh &c. - mèda-wo fám', I beg your pardon; yeda wo (mo) f. - 16. da ogya (hɔ), da gyentia, to sleep by the fire. pr. 559. 2128. - 17. da hɔ: a) shɔ da hɔ (pefee), it is manifest, evident, obvious; it is open, accessible: asɛm yi hɔ da hɔ, the matter is (now) plain or clear = asɛm yim' yɛ pefee; ne hɔ da hɔ, he lies or lay uncovered, is or was naked; - emu da hɔ, it is clear, plain, intelligible, open; opp. emu asiw me; - ɔpóŋ anò da hɔ, the door is open. - b) n'ani da hɔ, he is modest, sober, careful, attentive, mindful, heedful; syn. n'ani kã ase. - c) ɛso da hɔ, it is uncovered. 1 Cor. 11, 5. - d) ɛda hɔ mã me sɛ mewu, I am (destined) to die. - 17a. n'ani so da hɔ haŋŋ, s. haŋŋ. - 18. da hɔ = da so, s. 25 c. - 19. da hyia, to border upon, to confine with; syn. bɔ hye
to be or lie in or between; da akuru mu to be full of sores. pr. 700. - tokuru da dua no mu, there is a hole in the tree, the tree is hollow. pr. 426; - ɔkwaŋ no dam, the road is passable.
to be heard among other voices and noises: nnawutá dà mú; n'ano da mu, s. ano 12.
to be guilty, in fault; to be bound, to be under obligation (to perform a duty). Mat. 23, 16.

23. da mpǎn, Akp. F. = to be or lie empty, cf. 27.

24. da ase, a) to lie under: òda wo ase, he lies under that tree (Gr. § 118,3). - b) to thank (lit. to lie down); òdá no taá sò ase, he thanks him for the tobacco; yeda ase nè afotu, we thank for the advice; mèda wo ase, ('I lie down at your feet') I thank you; miyi me yam' meda wo ase, I thank you heartily; meda-ase aberaw, id. (s. aběraw); me ti da ase, thank you! efunu ada-ase, the corpse has passed (a person or house) without pushing, settled down, s. afunsoa. pr. 135. 643. 2129.

25. da só, a) to lie or sleep upon; òda né kèté sò, he is lying on his mat. - b) to sleep after having heard a message &c.; waŋkodá sò, it did not let him sleep; óteé no, wànná so, he obeyed it forthwith; wanna so na òbae, he came on that very day. - c) to go on, continue doing something. When put before another verb, to denote continuation of the action expressed by 'da so', that other verb may be rendered in Eng. by the adv. on, still: òda só kàn, he goes on reading, he reads on; òda só yàré, he is still sick; in Aky. 'so' may be omitted: wòda (so) di akɔ, they are still at war, cf. kɔ so, toa so & Gr. § 107,16. - F. da-hɔ, da-do, da-ro, Mt. 19,6. Mk. 5,35, 9,17. - d) òdà ne hɔ so, he is wary, cautious, circumspect, heedful, careful. - e) n'ani da me so, s.ani.

26. da nsow: òda nsòw, ne ti da nsow, he bears a mark, has a characteristic, is marked out or distinguished by some sign or character: onipa yi, ne duabaŋ da nsow, the figure of this man is of a particular shape or make; cf. dansow.
27. da nsram, Ky. Gy. = da yafumpǎŋ mu, to sleep with an empty stomach.
28. da tirim hwe, to consider, deliberate: asem a wokǎ kyere me yi, meda mahwe, or me(re)da me tirim mahwe, I will consider the matter you have told me about.

pl. nná, a day (of 24 hours; ŋkwǎ-da: a nnoŋherew 24 wom'; emu 12 ye adekyee, na emu 12 ye adesĕe; a time definite or indefinite; dá nyinaa all dáy; every day, always; nna nyinaa, all days, always; s. daa; - ébà nna-nná, it comes at times, now and then, occasionally, seldom = étò-dábi-á ébà, it happens sometimes; dà se nné, a day or time (occasion) like this. pr. 696-8; this day week; Gr. § 248,6. - bu nná, s. bu 28; - wonnim nna, or obi nnim nna, one does not know what time will bring = perhaps, peradventure. at the end of negative sentences = da bi, any day, ever, or, together with the negation, never. pr. 596. 1479. 1587; miŋhúú no dà, I never saw him or it; dèa émmaè dá sŭa, what has never yet come to pass is not much. pr. 2116; ade a ete saa yi, miŋhúú dà, I never saw such a thing; wobeba ana? will you come? - dà! no, never! a festival day, returning every forty-third day; one feast, called àdae késé, akwasidae (adwedae), is celebrated on Sunday; another, 24 days later, called awukudae, falls on Wednesday. An offering of mashed yams or plantains, a sheep, and rum is made to the spirits of the king's ancestors (in the stool-house), and their favours are solicited. The king then receives all his elders and honoured guests in public and gives them drink and presents. — di adae, to celebrate or keep Adae; gye ad. (prop. to receive the Adae-presents), to attend the Ad. festival; adae to a, ɔmaŋ ko-gye ɔhene adae, at the Ad. festival the subjects receive drink and presents from their king. pr. 2452. Ak., dée, emph. part. & conj., by which a person or thing, or an action (or sentence), is made prominent or opposed to another or others. [It is derived from the n. ade (s. bel.) which again is derived fr. the v. de]. It means taken apart, concerning, as for, as to (Gr. § 75,3); mé dé, méŋ'kó, my thing or part, i.e. as for me, I do not go. When the sent. or part of a sent., which is made prominent by de, precedes a corresponding co-ord. sent., the latter begins with na or nanso, but, and de is usually not translated (if we will not express it by indeed, it is true, take it for granted, Gr. § 140. 251 c.); but when it follows the corresponding sent., de is translated by but, however: mafré nò dé, nà ɔmmá, I have called him, but he does not come; ɔbékɔ, na mé dé, métrá ha, he will go, but I shall stay here; me de, mete daŋ mu, I am sitting in the house, but my brother is working outside; Abŭrokyiri (de), oba di n'agya ade; sha-yi de, ente sa, in Europe a child inherits his father's goods; here, however, it is not so. — The particle may be used twice: asém yi dé dé, miŋhú asé, as to (the concerns of) this matter, I do not understand it.

[red. didi], F. dzi [dzidzi]. This verb of manifold meanings seems to be related with the v. de; but whilst de chiefly means to have in the hands or to hold, and describes a state: di means to take (in the hands) and to handle, or to use, make use of, employ, and describes actions. It is, however, not confined to actions, nor to objects taken with the hand (for which we have the vv. fa, gye, yi, som'...), but is most frequently employed with abstract nouns, and the activity expressed by it is more of an abstract and compound than of a concrete and simple nature. - We arrange the various significations, which di has in connection with its common or specific objects or other complements, in groups marked by A-Z (to which we superscribe some general meaning), and subdivided by the continued numbers 1-110. A. To take and use; to receive, obtain, suffer: 1. to eat, to take & taste (food): ódi aduaŋ, dɔkono, dè, baŋkye, fufuu, mɔ, kwadu, kokosi, nãm, cf. we. pr. 226. 862-65. 870. 875. 882 f. 905. f. 914. 1644. 2690. 3111; to devour, destroy; odi adifude, he is greedy. - The red. didi is used, when no object is mentioned and the act of eating is denoted in a general way: me-kodidi, I am going to eat; odidi, he is at his meal, sits at table. - 2. to eat, feed, live upon: onni afuw, na odi ntodii, he has no plantation, but lives on bought things, has to buy his victuals; di .. ade, s. ade 8 a. - 3. to spend, use up, waste: wádi ne sika nyinaa, he has used up all his money; watɔŋ no adi, he has sold him and eaten, i.e. used up the money received. - 4. to use in traffic: Akyémfó di sika, Akuapemfo di ntrama, the Akems use gold-dust, the A-kuapems cowries for their currency. pr. 917. - 5. to take or keep and use for one's self: pr. 1070; sε m'akoa di da a, migye no mmaŋ du, if my slave takes a day for himself (staying away on one of three days [Sunday, Tuesday, or Saturday] which even hard masters did not deny their slaves), I take from him ten strings. - di bere, to be a loiterer, sluggard, time-killer. - 6. to use freely, to enjoy; di bere, to enjoy one's time, to live a luxurious life; pl. wodi mmere. - fa ne hõ di, to obtain the free use of one's own self, to become free, be emancipated; to live independently, to enjoy one's liberty or freedom. pr. 1075. 1439. - 7. to use naturally, to have sexual intercourse with; cf. fa (ɔbea, oyere, sigyafo), euph. kɔ..hõ, hũ, hyia; di ne hõ, pr. 881, to practise onanism, masturbation; of beasts, pr. 3411. - 8. to receive, get, accept of and use up; to partake of, have the benefit of: di ade, s. ade 8 a; di abaguade, to receive or draw fees for attending palavers; di mmoaa, adaŋmude, to receive presents or bribes; - cf. odi smanterenu-ade, he is a double-dealer, insinuates himself with both parties &c. - 9. to inherit: odi n'ade, he inherits his goods, is his heir, he succeeds him in his office or on the throne. pr. 845; s. ade 8 b; odi ghyira, ŋkwà, he receives, inherits a blessing, life. - 10. to obtain: di nĩm, ŋkɔnĩm, to gain or get the victory, be
victorious, to triumph. 11. to suffer: opatafo di abaa, the peace-maker receives blows. pr. 2637. - obedi mmusu, mischief will come upon or befall him; wadi kōmusu, ŋkōgu, he has suffered a defeat.
B. To be meet or fit to receive, to be worth, becoming, right: 12. to require, demand: di ntomū, ntewsō. pr. 2934.

[red. dodɔ], 1. to increase in quantity or number, to multiply, to become numerous; ne sika dɔ, his money increases; ne sika yi de, ɛdɔ, id.; ɛwo no adɔ, the honey has increased, has filled the comb. pr. 721. 813. 1348. Gen. 1,22. 7,17; wóádɔ = woaye bebree, wɔafew; cf. dōsõ [dɔ & sõ], few. — 2. to bring forth abundantly: asu no dɔ mmoa mànyã-manyã, the water swarms with animals. Gen. 1,20. — 3. to produce, attract, gather: dɔ srade, awonŋua, “to gather fat”, to fatten, grow fat (only of beasts). pr. 499; dɔ ŋkănare, to gather rust, to rust, grow rusty; dɔ mmoawa, to breed worms. Ex. 16,20. — 4. to fill, become full: wádɔ wúuw, (wadidi pii, n'afuru ahye), he is crammed, stuffed, cloyed (full); wadɔ ntwom, he is full of itch. — 5. to become hot: nsú no adɔ, the water is hot; dade no adɔ, the iron is red-hot; me hō adɔ, I am

hot = mayɛ hyew, hyerehyere. — 6. emu dɔ, to become deep, to deepen: asu no mu dɔ, the river is (or was) deep; emú dɔ dɔ-pá, it is very deep; ɛhɔ de, emu nnó, there it is shallow. — twú(w) kɔ nea ɛdɔ, push off into deep water! Lk. 5,4. — 7. do asuko, to dive. — 8. F. to sink under the water, sink down = mem, Mt. 14,30; be choked. Mk. 5,13. — 9. to sink, infiltrate, penetrate: dɔ mpumpunase: asu no adɔ mp., the rivulet has lost itself in the ground, flowing or oozing below the surface. — 10. to enter, lose one's self in: ode ne hɔ or ne ti adɔ wuram', he has absconded, concealed himself in the bush; s. 11. — 11. dɔ mu, dom', to go abroad, into foreign countries: aŋkyɛ na ɔdoom' kɔe, not long afterwards he set out on a journey; wádóm', he is away on a journey, abroad; śdóóm' kɔɔ Hũam', ɛmmáè ɛ, he went on a journey to Krepe and is not yet back; woŋ nyinaa dɔdóóm' kɔɔ ŋkúrów sɔ, they all went abroad into foreign countries; ɔdɔɔ wurám', he concealed himself in the bush, s. 10. — 12. to enter (the nose, said of the smoke or smell of something burned &c.): aduru no (mako no) adɔ me, the smell of that medicine (pepper) has entered my nose (causing me to sneeze, making me sick &c.) — 13. to enter deeply into, to grieve: asɛm no adɔ me (= yɛ me yaw), the matter grieves me. — 14. to take refuge with, have recourse to, resort to: wabéda mè, he has taken refuge with me; madɔ panyin no, I have applied to that gentleman; opanyin na, ade hĩa wo a, wuguaŋ kɔdɔ, you have recourse to a man of consequence when you are in distress. — 15. to swear by: mèdɔ (= meká) Onyankɔpɔŋ sɛ asɛm a meká yi wom', I swear by God that what I say is true. — 16. to love: ɔdɔ no, he loves him (always, continually); śdɔ no, he loved him (formerly); dɔ wo yoŋkɔ sɛ wo hɔ, love thy neighbour as thyself; wòdɔdɔ woŋ hɔ, they love each other. Gr. § 57. 102,6. pr. 123 ff. 2378. 3081. - to like, prefer; wódɔ n'ásém = wope n'asem, you like him. pr. 2164; cf. pɛ, pɛ asem. — 17. dɔ ..hɔ, a) to love, to like. Gen. 27,4.9. b) to spare, save, take care of: ɔdɔ ne náŋ hɔ, he does not like to exert (tire) his feet by walking. pr. 283. — 18. .. hɔ dɔ, to be of importance to, excite an intense interest or sympathy in: Iesu hɔ dɔ (= hĩa) yeŋ a, aŋkã yenyã ne hɔ asɛm bi kã. — Phr. 19. ne koŋ dɔ (ade), (his throat deepens for, i.e.) he has an appetite, a longing, desire for, eagerly desires, lusts after (something). — 20. dɔ ŋkrãŋ, to become wild, fierce, frightening; n'ani dɔ ŋkraŋ, he rages, chafes. — 21. dɔ..nã, to dislike, s. nã. — 22. dɔ aniwu, to be bashful. — 23. dɔ so: to take preventive measures: ɔdɔ so ntém slésie hɔ nã ammá sà, he quickly takes precautions that this may not come to pass. — 24. dɔ = dow. pr. 333. — 25. dɔ, dɔ..sɔ, to suffice, be sufficient; eyiara dɔ mè sɔ, that will just do for me; ádɔ me sɔ, it suffices me; annɔ me sɔ, it is not enough for me. - ne dɔ a ennɔsɔ, its insufficiency. — 26. ne tirim dɔ = oye atirimodeŋ or otirimodeŋfo, he is cruel, hard-hearted.

[red.] to feel or search for with a long instrument, to poke; to probe (a wound); to sound, fathom; fa dua yi duedue nsu no mu, search in the water with this stick. 6. [red.] to search or inquire after, investigate: mereko duedue ɔmaŋ mu = mekohwehwe ɔmaŋ mu asɛm mahwɛ, I will try to gather information as to the sentiments of the people or to obtain a favourable attitude among the people. 7. [red.] to stroll about, wander, rove, ramble; cf. (ɔba)dueduefo. 8. The significations given under 2 & 3 have given rise to a peculiar use of the v. in the imp. to express a) pity on any misfortune that befell the addressed person, b) a threat or prediction on account of some misdeed: a) dúé! hush! soothe or appease thyself, set your heart at rest, compose your mind, alleviate your pain, i.e. may your pain be alleviated! (Ade twa obi a, wose: dué, dúél obi nǐ wu a, n'abusuafo se: due, due!) — dué, gener. repeated 2 or 3 times, has become an appeasing and consoling interjection, pronounced towards a person who has hurt himself or met with an accident; the thing afflicting or incommodating is added with nè: dué nè amanehúnu = due, na woahũ amane, may you bear your affliction easily! may you recover from your affliction! múnnué nè kó! I pity you for the trouble and ill result of the fighting! due nè adwumaye na adwumaye bekũ mo! you are to be pitied for such hard or grievous work, it will kill you! It is also used in several common forms of salutation: dùe-nè-awó-óo, said in the morning, when it is cold; due-nè-wí'óo, said in the middle of the day, when it is hot; due-nè-ŋwín'óo, said in the evening, when it is cool; due-nè-sú-óo, said after a shower of rain, - meaning, as it were, may you easily bear the inconvenience caused by the cold (awow), the sun (awíá), the coolness (oŋwini), may you recover from the effect of the rain (osu). — b) dué! woe unto thee! mún-

v. to think (of); to meditate; to consider. pr. 309. — ódwèŋ ne kōmam' bone, he meditates or devises evil in his heart; dweŋ tirim, to devise. Ex. 31,4; to meditate. Ps. 27,4. — dweŋ so or hɔ: to think about, to meditate on, to consider; to mind, regard, care about; midweŋ asem (so), I think about a matter; odwɛŋ ne nua so or hɔ, he is thinking about his brother; ade a wokɔye yi, dweŋ hɔ yiye, consider the thing well which you are going to do; n'asem nynaa yɛ ntwiri, miŋŋweŋ so, all his talk is slander, I do not mind it; F. wandwen do antse (= antie), he neglects to hear. Mt. 18,17. — ne nsem a ɔkãe nyinaa, madweŋ akyiri mahũ, I have turned over in my mind all he said, and found it true. — Cf. susuw. — wudweŋ no dwemfã or dweŋfã, you form an incorrect opinion. — dweŋ adwempa, to be discreet, sober-minded. Ps. 39,4. — inf. adweŋŋwéŋ, adweŋŋwéne.
Mf. egwen, gwɔŋ, grey hair; edweŋ aba ne tirim, ne ti afuw dweŋ, he has grey hair. pr. 737. 2333.

Mk. 5, 15. - tew adwenem', to teach, train. Tit. 2, 4. - n'adwenem' abue or ada hɔ, he has good (common) sense, is intelligent; n'á-dwénem' asáŋ, he is a clear-sighted, highly-gifted man, a man of great ability. - n'adwenem' ye (no) hare, he is light-minded, frivolous.

inf. 1. clearness of thought, intelligence, shrewdness, alertness. 2. sound mind, sobermindedness, sobriety, female modesty. 1 Tim. 2, 9. 14. 2 Tim. 1, 7. - adwéne-ntá-ntá, double-mindedness; adwéne-ntántáfó, the double-minded.

v. [red. dwirádwira] 1. to dash or strike against, to spatter, sprinkle. Osu bɔ dwira me daŋ hō nti, shō hyirew nyinaa ahohoro, because the rain strikes vehemently against my house, the white earth (with which the wall had been whitewashed) has been entirely washed off; ɔde prae dwira me, he struck me with a broom; ɔde nsu dwiraa m'ani so, he dashed water in my face; n'ano a ose ɔrebue na nusu adwiram' (Akp. aguare no), when he wanted to open his mouth to speak, tears stifled his voice. - 2. to cleanse from guilt or moral and religious uncleanness; to sanctify; to consecrate. Obi kūm fi (e. s. ofim' aba fi bi) a, wodwiram', if one makes a dwelling (ceremonially) unclean (if a dwelling has become defiled), it is purified; wode ŋguaŋ mogya n, dwira ofie, the habitation is rendered clean again with the blood of sheep &c. - Sɛ ebia mefom meko-di biribi a mikyi a, wotew adweŋŋwere nɛ ɔwekom' ntwōma na wode adwira-dwira me nsa nɛ m'ano. [red. dwudwo, q. v.] 1. to cool; nsu no adwo, the water is no longer hot; ma ŋkway no ŋŋwo ansa, let the soup cool first. — 2. to be calmed, appeased; to abate, subside; to become or be soft; to relax from a state of excitement; to be calm, quiet, gentle, mild, meek, tame, peaceable, humble, espec. in the perf. and with bo (pr. 492), ho, ani. — 3. tr. to make quiet, soft, tame, cf. dwudwo. pr. 1064-66. — Aboa yi dwo, this animal is sitting quietly, not moving; oguanteŋ dwo (ne ho dwo, n'ani .dwo), na aberekyi ani ye deŋ, the sheep is gentle, but the goat is bold; epo adwò, the sea is calm; onipa no dwo, he is a quiet man; ódwò, he is humble (not proud = onye mpanyinsem); ne bo or n'abufuw adwo, his anger is appeased; n'ani dwo, ne kōma hō dwo, he is mild; gentle; ne hō dwo, he is meek. — 4. to come to rest, feel comfortable. pr. 748; kaŋ no oye hiani, nnansāyi de, ne hō adwo, formerly he was poor, but now he is better off; me hō adwo me kakra, I feel a little better. — Omaŋ mu adwo, the town or country is quiet, in peace; afei yeŋ bere so adwo, now peace is restored again. — N'asōm' adwo (no), he has become free from disturbance, has come to peace; aboa biara didi nea n'asōm' dwo no, a beast eats at a place where it is not molested. pr. 527. — Ne kete mu dwo, his bed is soft. — Ne kotokum' adwo (= aye duru, opp. aow), his purse is well-filled. — Dwo wo ani, lit. cool thy eye, i. e. moderate your haste, moderate your demand; restrain your passion or desire! dwò wo ani didi, eat slowly; dwo wo ani be-rezoo! act or proceed softly, gently, slowly! pr. 622. 1063. — N'asem dwo, he is mild or gentle; n'asem ano reŋŋwo, his affair will not come to a peaceful end; Isa. 42,4: he shall not fail. — Cf. abodwo, ahōdwo, asōm-dw(o)ee. — o-dwó, inf. meekness, gentleness, mildness. v. [red. fefa, fofa] to take; cf. gye, kukuru, tase, mã so, som', yi, & de, fua, kita, kura. — 1. to take to make use of: pr. 1081; to lay hold on for use. In these senses it takes the place of the aux. v. de in all negative and imperative sentences; s. Gr. § 108, 26-29. 205, 5. 206, 2. 208, 3. 4. 237. 240 a. c. 241. Cf. 26 (below). pr. 47. 136--66. 168 f. — 2. to take away: hena na wafa me tuo? who has taken my gun? — 3. to carry off (said also of inanimate objects): nsu afa no, the water has taken him, i. e. he is drowned. pr. 389. 3073. 3085; mframa afa me kyew kɔ, the wind has carried off my hat. — 4. to lay hold on, to seize: wáfà wo gyáw, he has embraced his legs, i. e. implored him, begged his pardon. — 5. to pick up and keep, to appropriate what is found: paane yi, mahũ wo fam'; mémfa ana? I have found this needle on the floor; may I keep it? fá! you may have it! fa abɔfɔ, to find a dead animal (or game) in the bush. pr. 497; fa or tase ŋwaw, to pick up or gather snails. pr. 1080; F. to gather (fishes in a net). Mt. 13, 47. — 6. to take, i. e. keep for one's own: wubu kyew yi mã hena? mibú mafá, for whom do you make this cap? I make it (so as to keep it, i. e.) for myself. Ps. 22, 19; cf. Gr. § 109, 32. 243 b. Rem. 2. — 7. to take possession of what is left or prepared by others: asase a Germanefo no gyawe no, Wendefo befae. — F. fa ahemman tsena mu, to inherit the kingdom. Mt. 25, 34. — 8. to obtain possession of by force, to seize, capture, conquer: fa dweŋ, to seize for a slave, to make booty of; woafa no dommum, he has been made captive; wofaa nnommum pii, they made many captives (in war); wafa kũrow no, he has conquered the town. — 9. to take and use or misuse: fa ɔbea, osigyafo. pr. 167. 430; cf. nũ 6; fa ɔyere (fa kun, F.), to take another's wife (husband) illegally, i. e. to commit adultery. — 10. to take, get, win, acquire: fa abarimá, to engage as a servant. pr. (1077). 3676; fa adàmfo, to enter (into) someone's service; or = fa ɔyɔŋkõ, to make friendship with. pr. 1078. — 11. to obtain, get: wafa afuru, she has got a belly, i. e. she is (big) with child. — 12. to bear in mind: mafa me tirim, I have got (it) in my head, i. e. I have grasped the sense or the warning, I understand = máhũ asé; I remember = makáe. — F. fa adwen, to take thought, concern oneself = dwendweŋ. Mt. 6, 25-34; ofaa hɔ adwene se ɔde asɛmpa no bekɔ T., he thought of carrying (made up his mind to carry) the gospel to T.; F. fa apăm, to take counsel. Mt. 27, 1. 7. — 13. to take inwardly, to conceive: ɔfà (me) a-bufúw daa, he often grows angry (with me). pr. 1079; wafa me adɔnã, he has taken a dislike to me; to choose 15. to take in a net or catch: obère, yare, sickness: ɔfà me, gets tired; wafa no, he has been taken in a calamity; to suffer a mischievous deed. — 16. to take away, to take one's way: wafa me wura kwan, wofa beŋkum a, wamfa abɔnteŋ so, went behind the street. Cf. 26. — 17. to respect. K. § 133; a ɛfa no, whithersoever 17, 8. — ode fa no, it is indecisive. — 18. to be right, lawful: 22, 17. 27, 6. — 19. to go through, take one's way: mfensereu mu fa, the winde — b, this was — g on, faa no mu hatee, — c) memfá mu, I do not care (about it); to take a part o, 17; cf. 24; F. ye fa, we gain by it? — d) kwan (to take a way), okwaŋ foforo so, they returned to their own, another way. Mt. 2, 12; of nam so in im (to do) by means of — e) to pass over, an affront. — to fall into, forgotten or neglected, m'aní sɔ = m'ani sɔ, m'ani afi sɔ = me overcome: — fa r, to overcome n. enen, so koraa, at this come. — e) to make, fa mfaso; watɔŋ ŋl, he has sold the eggs f) se woyaw ɔpan, biribi befa w'ani sɔ.

twi: 14. to take, admit; to choose, elect.

15. to take in a passive sense, to get or catch: ɔbɛre, fatigue, weariness, ɔyare, sickness: ɔfa ɔbɛre ntem, he soon gets tired; wafa ɔyare, he grew sick, has been taken ill; fa mmusu, to incur a calamity; to suffer the results of a mischievous deed. pr. 398. 555 f. 1738.
eng: 15. to take in a passive sense, to get or catch: ɔbɛre, fatigue, weariness, ɔyare, sickness: ɔfa ɔbɛre ntem, he soon gets tired; wafa ɔyare, he grew sick, has been taken ill; fa mmusu, to incur a calamity; to suffer the results of a mischievous deed. pr. 398. 555 f. 1738.

twi: 16. to take a road, a course, to take one's way over...
eng: pr. 1071. 1076; me wura kwaŋ ni, obi mmfa hɔ! wofa beŋkum a, mɛfa nifã, Gen. 13,9; wamfa abɔnteŋ so, na ɔfaa mfikyiri, he went behind the houses, not along the street. Cf. 26. — ɛfa hɛ ara a, in every respect. K. § 21 b. — baabiara a ɛfa no, whithersoever it turns. Prov. 17,8. — ɔde fa ha ɔde kɔ hɔ, he is indecisive.

twi: 17. F. fa kwaŋ mu, to be right, lawful, permitted.

18. fa mu, a) to walk through, take one's way through; ɔfaa mfenserem' guaŋe, he escaped through the window. — b) ɔfaa mu dae, whilst this was going on, he fell asleep; nna faa no mu hatee, he fell fast asleep. — c) mɛmfã mu = mɛmfã hɔ hwee, I do not care (about). — d) fa..mu (bi), to take a part of something.
eng: Lev. 9, 17; cf. 24; F. yefa mu bɛy, what may we gain by it?

twi: 19. fa so, a) with kwaŋ (to take a way or road): wofaa ɔkwaŋ foforo so kɔɔ wɔŋ kurom', they returned to their (own) country by another way.
b) instead of nam so in imp. & neg. sentences: (to do) by means of, s. Gr. § 108,27.
eng: b) instead of nam so in imp. & neg. sentences: (to do) by means of, s. Gr. § 108,27.

twi: c) to pass over something, e.g. an affront. - to fall into oblivion, to be forgotten or neglected: afa me so, áfã m'ani sò = m'ani afã so, m'ani apa so, m'ani afi so, me wɛre afi.
eng: c) to pass over something, e.g. an affront. - to fall into oblivion, to be forgotten or neglected: afa me so, áfã m'ani sò = m'ani afã so, m'ani apa so, m'ani afi so, me wɛre afi.

twi: d) to overcome: wafa n'atamfo so, he has overcome his enemies; eyi na ɛfaa no so koraa, at this he was quite overcome.
eng: d) to overcome: wafa n'atamfo so, he has overcome his enemies; eyi na ɛfaa no so koraa, at this he was quite overcome.

twi: e) to make profit, to gain = mfaso; watɔŋ ŋkesua no afa so, she has sold the eggs advantageously.
eng: e) to make profit, to gain = mfaso; watɔŋ ŋkesua no afa so, she has sold the eggs advantageously.

twi: f) sɛ woyaw ɔpanyiŋ bi na mete a, biribi bɛfa w'ani so, if you insult an adult & I hear of it, you will suffer for it.
eng: f) sɛ woyaw ɔpanyiŋ bi na mete a, biribi bɛfa w'ani so, if you insult an adult & I hear of it, you will suffer for it.

twi: g) bu..fa so, (wóbù no fã so), s. due 4.
eng: g) bu..fa so, (wóbù no fã so), s. due 4.

twi: 20. fa ase: a) fa ase ye, to do secretly.
eng: 1 Sam. 18,22; cf. nam ase.

twi: b) fa ase, to act as an aperient, to evacuate the bowels; aduru no befa n'asé, that medicine will purge him.
eng: b) fa ase, to act as an aperient, to evacuate the bowels; aduru no befa n'asé, that medicine will purge him.

twi: 21. fa hɔ, a) to move along, to pass by; cf. siane hɔ, twa hɔ, twam'; mmã mframa mmfa wo hɔ bɛrebe, do not let the wind play about you too much, i.e. keep yourself warm.
eng: 21. fa hɔ, a) to move along, to pass by; cf. siane hɔ, twa hɔ, twam'; mmã mframa mmfa wo hɔ bɛrebe, do not let the wind play about you too much, i.e. keep yourself warm.

twi: b) to touch on, to concern, affect, import; to have to do with: eyi fa hɔ biribi, this has some relation to it; ɛfa hɔ dɛŋ? what has that to do with it? wofa hɔ dɛŋ? what is it to you? asɛm no mfá me hɔ hwee, or, memfá asɛm no hɔ hwee, that business is no affair of mine, does not concern me; ɔfa mo hɔ biribi, he has something to do with you = onè mo wɔ asɛm bi; (śfá mo hɔ biribi, he takes s. th. from you); ɔmfá (= ɛmfá) no hɔ, F. he shall be free, it is nothing to him, no business or concern of his.
éde refà ... hɔ, as to, relating, concerning.
eng: éde refà ... hɔ, as to, relating, concerning.

eng: c) to dwom fa ɔsaŋkū hɔ, to sing to a musical instrument; e. g. to dwom fa ɔsaŋkū hɔ, to sing to the guitar; cf. saŋkū.

ɔmfá ne hɔ nni, he is not his own master; Kwasida mo nyinaa moafa mo hɔ adi, on Sunday all of you are free, have your time for yourselves. Cf. ɔfadi, fa-wohɔ-kodi.
eng: ɔmfá ne hɔ nni, he is not his own master; Kwasida mo nyinaa moafa mo hɔ adi, on Sunday all of you are free, have your time for yourselves. Cf. ɔfadi, fa-wohɔ-kodi.

twi: 23. fa di, to take and use up, to consume, spend, waste; cf. afaadi.
eng: 23. fa di, to take and use up, to consume, spend, waste; cf. afaadi.
24. fa (mu) to partake of.

twi: 25. Very often fa in its imp. and neg. forms and in the inf. is used, in connection with another verb, as an aux. v. introducing or referring to a passive object of the principal verb, and at the same time imparting to the princ. verb a causative meaning.

eng: lit. take come, i. e. bring; kofa bɛra, go take come, i. e. fetch; fa ko take go, i. e. firi me, for-give me! Cf. 1 (above). — 26. In other cases fa is used as an aux. v. referring the action of the principal verb to a place, as taking its way through, or to a means employed; cf. 16. 19 b. a-bove; it serves then to express the Eng. prepositions through, by &c. 6. to come out, become public, be revealed: asɛm no afi, this thing or affair is known. Ex. 2,14; cf. fi adi 14 b.
7. to become clean: m'atade afi, my dress is clean; kuruwa no hɔ afi, na emu mfii ɛ, the outside of the jug is clean, but not yet the inside. pr. 1236.
8. to be justified, be declared guiltless: ne hɔ afi, he has been or is acquitted.

9. to come or go from, forth from, out of (a place, person or thing). pr. 170 ff.; to proceed or begin from. In these meanings it is followed by a locative complement (Gr. 207. 208,5), and serves most frequently as an aux. v. showing the direction (from some starting-point) of a movement expressed by another verb and supplying the Eng. prepp. from (with the complement mu, out of) and since; cf. Gr. § 109, 30. 31, 208, 5, 223,4. 224. 229,1. 230,3. 239,1. 240. a. b. 265,1. Ohuruw fii hyɛn mu tɔɔ pom', he sprang out of the ship into the sea; wotow no fii hyɛn no mu kyenee po mu, they cast him out of the ship into the sea; ofii dua no so durui (= sii fam'), he came down from the tree; wanyãŋ afi nna mu, he has awoke from sleep; nám no abɛŋ, yi fi kùtu mù, the meat is done, take it out of the pot; éfii sê nê bá wui no, ònseréwé dà, she has never laughed since her child died. Cf. efise. - éfi ha kɔ ne fi ŋware koraa, it is not far from here to his house; his house is not far from here; éfi ha kɔ bɛye sε eha nè hẽ? how far is it thither? Enni obiara a ŋware no gye aberaŋ, it is too far for any but a strong man [lit. there is not any one for whom it is not long except strong men]; efi nea woda hε de kɔ me daŋ no hɔ ŋware, the place where they slept is not far from my house. -(caus.): de..fi..so kɔ..mu or so, to lead from (one place, condition, subject) to (another), to form the transition from... to. K. § 76.

better; a-fômpɔw.

tuber (e. g. of yam, coco, turnips), bulb. -Phr. miŋhú nɛ ti, miŋhú ne fɔre, I cannot see the end of it (e. g. of a lawsuit).

a cutaneous eruption; mfówabéré, mfówa-pá, with pimples not containing a fluid; mfówa-aníni, mfówanini, with pustules containing pus; cf. dwe 2.

wind-house; cf. mfare.

a ceremony performed among the Akwamus and the Aburi people on account of a woman in the fourth to the sixth month of her first pregnancy. - di mf., to perform this ceremony. [Ak. fu, related with fi, v. = fiw] 1. to shoot up, come forth abundantly, grow luxuriantly or rankly; ŋwura refuw asase no so, weeds are shooting up on that land. — 2. to overgrow: ɔkwáŋ yi afũw, this path is overgrown. — 3. tr. to cause to grow, to get by growth, produce plentifully (hair, feathers): me tiri fuw dweŋ, I am getting grey hair; ne ti afuw, his head is covered with hair. pr. 669; onnyä mfuw bogyésɛ ɛ, he has no beard yet; anɔmaa no afuw ntakára, the bird has (got) feathers; nnɔmaa no, wɔŋ hũ fuwi ansã-na me-koyii woŋ, the birds were fledged when I took them. — Onyame mpɛ sɛ ne mma anom befuw wura, God does not want his children to starve. — 4. ne bo fuw, he is angry (with me); syn. ɔfa abufuw, wafa (me) ab. — tr. ófũw mé bò, he causes my breast to swell, i.e. he provokes me to anger, makes me angry, syn. oyi me abufuw. — 5. [prob. related with fua] to unite in holding: wófũw nó ahwè no, they together hold him in order to flog him; hwe may be omitted and still be understood: ɔnè ne nua afuw me, he and his brother have flogged me; s. dɛŋ & di..mfuaŋ-hwe; mɔŋkofuw adwuma no hɔ ŋkɔwie = mo nyinaa mɔŋkosusò adw. no mu ná monyɛ, you all shall unite in, conjointly put your hands to, the work to finish it. — 6. F. to become spoiled (of fish).

[Pret. górii; red. gugoru], Ak. go, gorɔ, 1. to play, sport, frolic, divert or amuse one's self (mmofra g. abɔnteŋ so; agyinamoa, mpataa g.; g. asafo, pr. 1478). — 2. to be of a friendly, communicative disposition, be sociable; ɔnè biara goru, he is friendly with everybody; ɔnè bi ni ŋ'ŋóru, he is unsociable; - to have intercourse, be intimate with each other. pr. 1367. — 3. to play for money, to gamble; cf. tow ŋhoma, tow ntrama, si ntɛw. — 4. to perpetrate some wickedness; g. aguamaŋ-ŋoru, to commit fornication; ɔnè bea g., he commits adultery, whoredom; - g. abayigoru, to practise witchcraft. — 5. g. hɔ, a) to mock at, deride, scoff. - b) to neglect, slight. pr. 1219.

inf. Ak, agó, agórɔ, 1. playing; play, sport, amusement, espec. singing and dancing. pr. 481. 1211-18. 1499; game; gu ag., to give up a play or game; cf. gu 21. pr. 1139; tutu ag., to arrange a play or game; tu ag., s. tu 25. — 2. sociableness, friendliness; onnim ag., he understands no joke, is sourminded; s. ago. — 3. agóru-ba, pl. -mma, a child born out of wedlock. — Different kinds of play or game, consisting of singing and dancing (s. asaw), are: adewá (a common name); of women: adɛŋkum, nnyaané, peewa; of men: dasummaŋ, dwae, agyemannare, aheŋkwaá, onníbia-måne, nnontwuwa, paw, ɔpɛrenteŋkoro, asafo, osekye, asibɛletɛ, sobom, timbo or timmo, antɔrepira. Other plays or games are: ɔware-tow, dam-di or - to, ntɛw-si, atwɛ-di or -sisi or -tow &c. Children's plays or games: aba, abaa, ba-bɔ, odotow, amũamũani, ɛsono-nè-ne-mma &c.

inf. the giving up of a play or game. - góru-kyere, inf. play, drama, performance of a play. K. § 104. - o-go(ru)kyerɛfó, pl. a-, actor, stage-player, performer. - agoru-pá = ago-merɛw. - agó-sɛm, joke, jest.
a small earthen pot in which palm-oil is kept. pr. 2135.
pl. ŋ- [ŋŋo, soa, fo] palm-oil carrier. pr. 1220.
[agoru a ɛtra so] a play carried to excess; wugoru ag. a, kaansèsè eyé a, wo ani wu akyiri, if you play overmuch, though it be nothing bad, you will afterwards feel ashamed.
v. [red. gugow; Ak. gono, red. goŋgono] 1. to slack, slacken, relax, loosen: a) to become slack, be made lax, i. e. less tense, firm or rigid, to become loose: hama yi mu agow, ɛ.s. emu yeree,

na afei asaŋ aye merew. - b) to render slack, make less tight, make loose: gow wo amirikatu mu, slack thy riding; s. 5. - 2. to weaken: a) to become weak: ne nsam' agow, his arms are weak; - b) to make weak, infirm, feeble: onipa foforo no gow nipa dedaw no mu. - 3. to soften: a) to become soft, tender, mellow: duaba no abere na ɛŋ-nowe ɛ. pr. 1022; aduan a woanɔa no agow = aye mersw; - b) to make soft; s. 7. - 4. hɔ gow, nsam' gow, to become soft, comfortable: ne hɔ agow no, prop. every thing around him is soft, i.e. he has an easy, comfortable life = ne hɔ adwo no (asɛm bi nni ne so, nanso biribiara a ohɛwbe, ne nsa kà); ne nsam' agow = wape ade anya bi; cf. 2 a. - ne nsam' gow, also he is open-handed, liberal. - 5. to moderate, restrain: ogow (= odwoo) n'ani kãe, she said in an under-tone or modestly. - gow wo ani si fam', step lightly. - tutu wo anaŋ gow mu di kaŋ, go ahead slowly; ŋŋow wo amirikatu mu, slack thy riding. 2 Kg. 4,24; s. 1b. - 6. mu gow, to be spacious: ɔdaŋ yi mu gow, this room is spacious; opp. emu kyere, it is narrow. - 7. gow..mu, to mitigate, alleviate, soften, allay, assuage, soothe; to lessen, diminish, temper.

pl. agow-agów, I. n. fragment, piece, damaged part, rag, remnant; remains, ruins; cf. ɔfã, fere, siŋ; opp. emu, pl. amũamũ; ne mũ ni, this is the thing in its perfect state or as a whole; né gów ni = né fã ni, this is a fragment of it; n'ágów-agów ni = n'afãafã ni, these are the fragments or pieces of it; kũrow' no ayɛ gów, the town is in a ruinous state; wamã kũrow no ayɛ àgow-agów, he let the town fall to ruins. - II. adj. 1. damaged, spoiled, broken; the attrib. adj. in the sing. is compounded with its noun: adaka-gów, ɔpoŋ-ŋów, ahina-gów (pl. ŋhiná agòw-agów), ahwehwegów; koragów, a leaking calabash. - 2. ragged, tattered: kentegów, ntamagów; m'asepatere ayɛ gów, (pl. me nsep. ayɛ àgow-agów), my shoe is torn. - 3. ruinous, decaying, dilapidated: abaŋ-ŋów, ɔdaŋ-ŋów; ɔdaŋ no ayɛ g., yerebebu; kũro no ayɛ gow; woamã ɔdaŋ no ayɛ agow-agow; s. I.
a nickname of gin, rum, brandy.
[It.granata, Sp.grenade] grenade.
pomegranate, the fruit being in shape somewhat like an orange (akutu) or a burokũruwa; cf. ntoropo.

v. [red. gugu] I. intr., sometimes causatively used, generally with a locative complement: 1. to fall, pour down (of a collective multitude, whereas hwe and tɔ are used of single things or persons): dua no ŋhwiren regu fam', the blossoms of the tree are pouring down; aba no bi kugu abo so, some of the seed fell on stony ground. Mt. 13,5 f.; cf. 11 & porow 4. - 2. (contin.) to lie (of a collective multitude, whereas of individual things or persons da is used): mede abũrow' migũ nsúm', I am pouring corn into the water; mframa te-tew ahabay gu fam', the wind severs the leaves and blows them down; yerebebu daŋ yi agu fam', we are going to demolish this house and to knock it down; - ɔde ne nsa guu me so, he lay or put (both) his hands upon me; ɔde ne nsa guu n'akyi, he put his hands behind his back. - ɔkã ŋŋuaŋ no gu daŋ mu, he drives the sheep into the stable. - 4. of fluids: to flow out (into, upon), be spilled, shed. pr. 87. 459; (contin.) to be scattered, sprinkled (somewhere): ɔde ŋŋo no bae no, ebi gui (= guu fam'); ebi gùgùù dáp mú hɔ, when he brought the palm-oil, part of it had been spilled; some has been scattered on the floor there in the room; cf. 13. - 5. caus. to pour (into, upon): fa nsú gù tumpáŋ yim', pour water
to fall or hang down, hang loose and waving, flow: ne ŋhwĩ gu ne kɔŋ mu, ne mati, his hair hangs down onto the nape of his neck, on his shoulder.
caus. to throw over, put on: ɔde ŋguguso guu ne kɔŋmu, he threw a loose garment over his shoulders, wrapped himself up in a mantle.
to accrue, be added, increase, augment; ne Twi no, biribi regugu mu, his knowledge of the Tshi language is increasing; cf. mmagum'. pr. 2514.
to intervene; nda gum' kakra no, F. after some days (Mk. 2, 1).
so, a) gu kwaŋ so, to be on the way: ògu kwáŋ sò rébà; cf. hwe 1.

b) to lean upon, i.e. to rely for support, depend on, be committed to one's care: nnipa pii gu me so nti, minyã sika a, entew, because I have to care for so many people, the money I earn does not stay with me; cf. boa, v.

c) to be bent upon, diligently occupied with: ogu n'adwuma so, he is at his work; n'asɔ̃ gù só, he listens; ogu reye ara na mekyeree no, I caught him in the very act; wogu aduaŋ no so redi, they are still in the act of eating; to continue (persevere) in: wogu so de kã ara mã odasu saree, they went on talking far into the night.
d) to come down upon, numerously and violently, to attack: wòkoguù no so (cf. wokotow hyɛe no so, Acts 7, 57).
e) caus. òbù n'aní gú so, ɔkã n'aní gu so, s. ani; kã ntam gu.. so, to conjure, s. ntam (Gr. § 243 b); ye ..gu.. so, to do against. Gr. § 109, 32.
gu ase, lit. his face falls down, i.e. he is ashamed, abashed, put out of countenance. — ɔnè yeŋ gu ase, he lives in peace with us.
gu asu, to make or suffer shipwreck. 1 Tim. 1, 19.
intr. without a locative complement: 11. to fall, come down: obosu gu, dew falls.
12. to be shed, spilled, s. 4 ebi gui.
13. caus. hwie..gu, kã..gu, to spill, shed; wakã mɔgya agu, he has shed blood. Gen. 9, 6. Lev. 17, 4.
14. to succumb, be defeated; to run away, flee: dɔm agu, the (hostile) army has been beaten, routed, put to flight, defeated, dispersed; woagù, they have given way, are fleeing.

15. caus. kã .. gu, to rout, put to flight: yeakã dɔm no agu, we have fought and defeated the enemy; bɔ..gu, pam..gu, to scatter, disperse; cf. 3 the last ex. & yepam dɔm no guu (a)habaŋmu, we routed the army and drove them into the forest.
16. to become desolate, to fall into ruin: kũrow no agu.
17. to be abandoned, finished: agoru no agu, the play has been given up. pr. 1910; cf. 21.
18. to be finished, be over; ɔkɔm agu, the dearth (famine) has ceased.

19. ase gu, to be decreasing; to cease, die out, be exterminated, become extinct: n'asé agù, his posterity is utterly destroyed; ɔde, mmoa, nnipa no ase regu = wɔresã; Abótakyifo ase agù, the inhabitants of Abótakyi have been (as it were, i.e. nearly) extirpated.

III. tr. without a locative complement: 20. gu ase, to extirpate, exterminate: magu wura no ase, I have exterminated those weeds; magu m'abrode ase, I have entirely taken out my plantains; - wogu akũnini a wototoe no nusu ase, they perform the last funeral ceremonies for the fallen chiefs; s. 23.

21. to end, to abolish, prohibit: gu aguadi, to stop the trade; gu agoru, a) to cease from playing for a time, to put a stop to it for this time; cf. 17; - b) to give it up or abolish it altogether, to prohibit it.
gu adwuma, to finish the work (altogether, = wie yɔ koraa).
22. gu né ŋkyèrɛw', gu n'ápàre or né mpàre, to finish, complete, conclude, consummate: woagu ne ŋky. = wɔawie adwuma biara ye; s. ŋky.
23. gu nsã, to perform the concluding part of a funeral custom.

24. gu.. so nsu, to sprinkle an adversary (in court) with water; a ceremony performed by the king (or chief) when contending parties cannot agree on account of the obstinacy of the one. By this ceremony both parties are bound over never again to mention the

matter in question. (If the recusant party consists of several persons, all of them are sprinkled). The king (or chief) may also have one of his councillors sprinkled instead. Woágù nó sò nsú n,s. woaẅie asem bi di, na nnyafiŋkae nti ohene mã wogu ne dehye bi so nsu, na obiara antumi ankae asem no bio.
to sow: gu mõ, to sow rice (cf. dua, v.).
to pour out, i. e. put forth blossoms, to blossom.
to emit a sigh, groan; gu homtsen, F. to emit a long breath, sigh deeply.
(iron, brass, copper, type, bells), cast (lead, tin, zinc, silver, gold), cf. gude; to coin, stamp (dare, dollars).
to cast or throw (out) the net. wori gugu wɔ pom', F. they were casting a net into the sea. Mk. 1,16.
a) to make water, urinate, euph. (= dwensɔ); b) to unite by oath.

aux. v., when it shows the direction of the movement or action expressed by a preceding princ. v. as kã, hwie, bɔ, pam, tow; in connection with a following mu or so it answers to the Eng. prepp. into, upon (s. 3.5); when no complement follows, it answers to the adv. away (hwie gu, tow gu!), or the notion of loss or waste is contained in the Eng. v. (as in to spill, to rout). Cf. Gr. § 109,32. 223,4.
to cast away.
lit. to do & cast away, i.e. to do in vain, work for nothing; nea oyɛe no nyi-naa, oyé gui, all he did, he did in vain.
inf. falling; casting; sowing; abolition &c.
Ak. = guaw.

1. public place, market-place; market pr. 139.310.1222; open place, cf. abanŋua, court; - okãe wɔ gua so, he said it publicly; ɔko gua so, he went to the market; woafi gua ase, market-ing has begun; hye (pl. hyehye) gua, to open a 'market', a bazaar; fi gua, Ps. 68,25, s. fi 15; ádà guá (= ada adi), it is manifest, evident, public, notorious. - 2. a public assembly, council pr. 1221; bɔ gua, to hold a council &c., used espec. of the elders of a town who assemble for deliberations on public affairs; s. bɔ 88; bɔ (obi) gua, to receive somebody in a public meeting, to convene an assembly for him or on his account; okɔ guam', he went to the place of assembly; gua atu = wɔaträ ase asore, woahwete gua, the assembly is dispersed, the session is broken up; cf. bagua, guabɔ, guam'fo, agua ase.

3. trade; di gua, to trade, traffic, deal (in); cf. di bata, mpɛswa, nsesã, nse-sãgua, nnukurogua; odi no gua (or bata) = odi gua mã no, he trades for him; onè me di gua, I am engaged in trade with him (mutually); onè me di bata, he and I go and buy things &c. - odi süm mu gua, he is a hypocrite. - né guá abò no, he has fallen short, has come off a loser, has suffered a loss, in his trading. pr. 927.
pl. ŋ-, seat, chair, stool; throne, s. ahenŋua; naŋ ase agua, foot-stool; cf. akoŋŋua, akenteŋŋua; apoŋŋua; mãŋoó. pr. 3602. Phr. agua atɔ fam', the king (or chief) is dead.
v. 1. to separate; - guaa ne hɔ, to retire, retreat, withdraw; guaa wo hɔ fi wɔŋ hɔ = twẽ wo hɔ fi wɔŋ hɔ, separate or withdraw thyself from them!
2. to level: wɔaguáa bɛpɔw bi ani ase, the lower slope of a hill has been levelled. - cf. guae.
(retreat, flight): bɔ ne hɔ aguáá, to retire, retreat, get away, make off, run away (secretly), take to one's heels, flee = guaŋ.
oguáwá, pl. a-, F. oguaba, the guava fruit and tree.
F. gwa, Ak. dwa or even guà, v. [red. gugua] to cut in pieces, cut up (an animal), carve. pr. 126. 3025.
- to flay, skin, strip off the skin of an animal; gua nantwi-ŋhoma, to skin a bullock; wágùa abóa ŋhóma atɔŋ. pr. 1223. 2849 f.
- to gut, eviscerate, take out the bowels. - ɔprannaa ŋ'gua m'apampam (me mp...)! s. dwa.
[Sp.guayaba; Psidium pyriferum, white guava; Psidium poniferum, red guava]. O-guaá, E-, Cape Coast (Port. Cabo Corso), with Cape Coast Castle, Fort Victoria, Fort William, & Fort Macarthy.
-ŋ a thorny creeper; ŋuáre bi à wóde yè əsáw; wówè.
Ak. adwabírèm, q. v., a large place for assemblies (nea wodi aseŋ-kese a. s. wòbə gua kese bi). pr. 1978; broadway. Prov. 1,21.

inf. [bə gua] the act of assembling, the state of being assembled; assembly; wəŋ g. no aŋwie fe yə, e.s. wəammə gua no sənea wòbə gua; wəŋ g. no akyi ansi yiye. (Wəbə gua di asem, di adae, yi wəŋ hō adi, trā ayi ase, nom nsā, goru, bə səməde, di ŋkəmmə). - a failure in trade; s. egua 3.
[nea ogua boŋ] one who flays a beast. pr. 1223.
disturbance, uproar of an assembly, in a market. pr. 3254; bə ag., to cause dist. &c. - aguabúm-bəfó, pl. id. disturber in a market.
[egua ade] goods, wares, merchandise; - aguadé-dáŋ, shop, magazine. - aguadé-si-beá, mart, emporium, staple.
inf. [di gua] trading, trade; cf. gye 35. pr. 270. - aguadí-dáŋ, factory. pr. 565. 1224.
-fó, pl. a- -fo, trader, merchant; cf. əbatani, opeəwadifo.
oguá-dùà, guava-tree.

v.: g...mu, to disjoin, part, separate, sever, sunder, break, rend; to tear asunder; g. ne ŋhwim', g. ŋwuram', to part one's hair, the weeds, the bush (in order to go through); syn. bae mu, dae mu, hāŋ' mu, pae mu, pāŋ mu, tāŋ mu, terəw mu. - oguaé tām no, he draws the cloth (curtain) aside.
adv. very much: ne sē bə so g., his teeth chatter from feverish cold; ōwia pae g. = kétékétékete, the sun burns, shines very bright.

guahá [egua, ha] 1. a bit of straw, or a stalk of grass, with some cowries strung on or added to, it, used to conclude the sale of a person or a thing. It was broken in two, the parts being put into the hands of witnesses, whilst the buyer also gave them a small sum of money (say 25 strings) besides the actual price; - tew ne ti g., to conclude (complete) the sale of, lit. to break a straw concerning one's head or price, in testimony of the sale, which seems to indicate, that the previous connection between the seller and the person or thing now sold is broken off. pr. 3332. Watew ne yere ti g., he has (completely) sold his wife. The witnesses were bound to keep the ends of the straw and the cowries handed over to them, and, if necessary, to produce them in testimony of the bargain; the giving of this testimony was then called wəkotoa guaha, lit. they join together the ends of the straw. Me ti guaha da n'akoŋŋua ase, the straw of my purchase price lies under his chair, i.e. I have been bought by him (as a slave). - 2. fig. earnest, pledge. 2 Cor. 1,22. [kuru so.

a kind of weed; wóde ta guàm, v. [red. guŋŋuam] 1. to grow together, be double; duába no aguàm ntá, águàm abieŋ' = aba no ye abieŋ, nso ebəm', the two fruits have grown together; pl. eguŋŋuám nta-nta or abieŋ-abieŋ; - apoŋkə a wəreguam, two horses put to a carriage, a team of horses. - to be closely united. Rom. 6,5. - woguam no atuo abieŋ, or, wəde atuo ab. na eguam no, two guns were fired at him at once, he was killed by two guns fired at him at once. - 2. to run or flow down copiously; fifiri reguam no = f. repram no, he perspires copiously. - 3. to run, gallop, of horses; əpoŋkə guam reba. Hab. 1,8; to prance about. - 5. F. to take at one time.

a-, pl. ŋ- [dim.] a little lamb, lambkin, kid.
[oguaŋ, pl. ŋ-, & baŋ] sheepfold, sheep-cot, pen.

v. [inf. a-, red. guaŋ'guaŋ] to flee, run off or away; to avoid (asɛm, kaw); to escape. - pr. 839. 1784. 2250; guaŋ dɔ, g. kɔ, g. toa, to flee to .. for succour, seek a refuge or hiding-place with a person or at a place.
pr. n. of the language of Date, Kyerepɔŋ, Anum, also .of Kărakye, Ntwummuru, (Nta); cf.. Gr. introd. § 5 A 1. § 1 D II, 5. 6. § 2,3.

a. fine, nice; onipa no aye g., the dress, face, whole appearance of that person look fine; wasra ne daŋ mu nti, emu aye g., because he has whitewashed his room, it has become nice; syn. fefe, kámà, osó.

pl. ŋ- [F. egwan, Ak. odwane, odžuane] the sheep; the term includes the goat also, but as there is a particular word for the latter (s. aberekyi), it is commonly used for sheep; if the sheep is to be expressly distinguished from the goat, it is called oguanteŋ. pr. 1612.

inf. the act of fleeing or running away; flight, escape, pr. 1929. — hasty, hurried steps: fa ag. = tu mmirika; fa ag. kɔ na bɛra! = tu aguaŋ, Ab., dze or tutu ŋgwaŋ, F. = de or tutu mmirika, to run. Mk. 5,6. 9,25.

[agya ade] paternal inheritance. Akuapemfo a wokasa Guaŋ, wodi agyadé, among the Akuapems speaking Guaŋ (and in the townships of Mamfe, Mampong, Tutu, Ɔbosomase), the father's property is inherited by the eldest son; the latter being dead, by the next son in age and so on. If the male heirs are extinct or if there are no sons at all, the property goes to the eldest daughter and so on. "People are in the habit of saying that the father's property is inherited by the father's brother in age; this is, however, not the case, but the brother has only the duty of a guardian and adviser." Cf. wofade. gya-dɛwɛé, a blazing fire.

here, this place; hither; hence; bɛrà há, come here. It may take the adj. pron. yi after it: bɛrà há-yi, come just here, or an attribute in the possessive case before it: bɛrà me há, come hither to me; me há yè me yàw', this place (of my body) here aches, it pains me here, this is the place which hurts me, this is the seat of (my) pain. It may stand as an attribute in the poss. case before a noun: ɛha ŋŋuan, the sheep of this place or country, or in apposition after a noun of place, when it must be rendered in Eng. by this: waba kùrom' ha ane, he came to this town to-day. - ɛha nna-hẽ, as long as. - éfi ha kɔ ho te sɛ ɛha nẽ hẽ? how far is it from this place to that? - ɛhánom (a kind of plural form), hereabout(s). - The emph. part. ara may be added.

pl. a-, ahemfɔ, ahèmfo; (Ak. ɔhen) 1. king, prince, chieftain, chief. pr. 279. 1301 ff. 2852. In Akp. this title is given to the chief of every town as well as to the chief of the whole country; in As. its use is more restricted; cf. ədekŭro, ɔmaŋhene, ɔsafohene, (ɔsee). In public assemblies frequently other words and names are used to designate the king, e.g. katakyie, opanyin, (Agyakwa) &c. - 2. the office of a king, kingship, royalty: odi hene, he exercises the office of, or he rules as, a king; ódi né héne yiyè, he rules well; wodi amaŋ so hene, they rule over the nations; wogye ne nsam' hene, the kingdom has been taken from him, he has been dethroned &c. - 3. di ahene, to make a pompous exhibition or display of royalty: ɔredi ahene nns = ohene rebeŋ gua de no hɔ ahe-kyere (a.s. abekyia), he is about publicly to display his royalty (or, to give a reception); ahene a ɛbehyiaa mu nnano no redi ah, nne, the kings who came together the other day will turn out in parade or appear in state to-day.

[ohene ade] the insignia of the king or chief, consisting in the chair (ahepgua), the sword (afɔa), and the ornaments (trinkets of gold and corals). ahéne-aseŋ, beads worn round the hips. ɔ-héne-ba, pl. ahene-mma, son or child of a king, royal prince. pr. 1159. 1321. ahene-basá, beads strung & tied round the wrist. ahéne-dí, inf. the pompous exhibition or display of royalty, s. ohene 3.
1. s. oheneba. - ahénemma-sem: di ah., s. di 53. - 2. the best sort of sandals; s. mpaboa.
a tree with edible fruits.
ahene-pányiŋ, s. ahené.
pl. a-, a small, petty king, prince, chief.
a small bead.
a name given to the members of certain families in different Tshi tribes, in answer to a salutation. Gr. § 147, 9.
red. v. háŋ.
ahweŋhema, s. osŭã.
(ahénni, the act of reigning), inf. [ohene-di] 1. kingdom = kingship, exercise of kingly dominion. - 2. ahenni, kingdom, meaning a land and people under kingly rule; cf. ahemmaŋ.
[ohene adiakyiri] 1. the successor to the throne, hereditary prince. - 2. ring-finger, the fourth finger from the thumb, coming after the nsateaahéne; it is also called nsatea safohene.

1. = ohene anim, the king's face; the place in front of the king; nea ohene aŋkasa te hɔ, the king's presence; ɔkɔ ah, akɔkã asem, he went before the king to report. - 2. = ohene day anim, the place before the king's dwelling; the court.
(tet. ayoŋkorawa), a certain tree; mmofra de n'aba si ntew.
ohene kese, - ɔhèŋ-kúmaa = ohene akumaa.
(Ak.-kŭró), pl. ŋ- [ohene kurow] the town in which the king resides, residence, capital; chief town.
pl. ŋ- [ohene akoa] 1. the servant of a king (or of a fetish = abosopkwas). pr. 1322 ff. 2269; courtier. John 4,46. — 2. a kind of play; s. agoru.
pl. n-, crown; ahemmotiri.
a climber, the fibres of which are made into a kind of sponge (hama bi a ewɔ wuram' a woboro ye sapɔw); the sponge itself; mèpɛ ah. bi matɔ máguáré; cf. osaw, sapɔw.
manners, doings, matters, tales of a king; history of kings; majesty. Ps. 45,4; ye ah., to play the king; di ah., s. di 5.
(a)hensiá, awénsáá, pl. ŋ- (As. ayénsáá), a kind of mouse or rat; ne hɔ ye tumm, pr. 1326.
royal apparel. Esth. 8,15. Acts 12, 21.
= ohene ntam, the "king's oath"; cf. ntam, pr. 1327.

(héntúa), pl. ŋ-, noose, running knot; loop; mesh, stitch; - bɔ .. h., to make (into) a noose &c.; wabɔ (hama no) h.; wodé sà mmóa, 'wode kyekyéré adé; cf. bɔ 91.96; nterewsó; - mabo no h. du na mereye wo nnuaa so, I have ten stitches on the needle and am knitting. - to h., to ensnare.
any beautiful or costly vessel; esp. the better kinds of decanters.
ahentówa, pl. ŋ- [ohene tɔw] a small lump of "fufuu", as becoming kings, who ought only to eat little; cf. s-tɔw, ŋkwaseatow.

pl. ŋ- [ohene agua] the stool or chair of a king or chief, throne. pr. 1325. — 2. its carriers (in connection with a pr. n.); e. g. Owusu ah., the stool-carrier Owusu. — aheŋŋwá, Ak. id. — ahen-nuan' = ohene aduan, the king's food, royal food. Dan. 1,5.
= ohene-adwuma, kingly office. K. § 235.
[ohene aware] the marriage of a king; mmusu di wo akyi a, ede wo nè ah., when misfortune dogs you, it dogs you till you become a king's wife. pr. 2054.3132.
[ohene yere] pl. - nom, ahenyere, a wife of a king; cf. ɔhemmaa. pr. 3558. Eccl. 2,8.
v. F. = hara. — heram, v. F. = häram.
F. roof. Mt. 8,8 (Mk. 2,4).
hi..., s. hye, hye, hyi...

v. [red. bihi] to come or draw to an end or close; to close; to be fulfilled or completed; [cf. hini, ehiŋ, ghiŋa]. - m'adagyew rehĩ, my leisure is passing away; me bere ahĩ = aka ketewaa sè na asà, my time is nearly spent; me nna a mede merebɛko no rehĩ or reye ahĩ, my departure is at hand; ohiá ahĩ atò no, poverty has (now finally or fully) overtaken him; - to be spent, wasted or worn out by frequent use: osèkàŋ no rehĩ or ahĩ akà kétewaa bi, e. s. woasew dade bi asew na esè; otuo no ano ahĩ; - to cease burning; ogya no de, éhĩ; ogya no ahĩ = awie dew mã aka nnyansramma ŋkɔ. Syn. sã, hwere.

perh. an inf. of hĩ: an ending, stopping, reluctance to proceed, used of what is irksome, tedious, which causes dislike or displeasure (ade a sye taŋ or dennónnenney). pr. 1328; - indignation. Phrases: ye ahĩ, to provoke, to excite disgust, indignation, resentment: asém yi yè me ahĩ = taŋ, this matter is vexatious, irksome, afflicting, provoking, teasing, loathsome, disgusting, repulsive, odious to me, I am tired or weary of it, I have had enough of it; ne hɔ ye me ahĩ = mfonee, I am weary or tired of him, I loathe him; n'anom kasa ye ahĩ, his talking is intolerable. pr. 1492.2803. - tew ahĩ, to be refractory, to resist, to set at naught, to despise, utterly disregard; watew me ahĩ = wásèŋ mé sò, wammú mè, n'ani ansɔ m'asɛm, m'asɛm ansɔ n'ani, he disregards me, disdains, slights or scorns to obey me; watew m'asɛm ahĩ = meka mekyereɛ no sɛ: nyé sɛɛ! na obuu so koyee; woatew ohene asɛm ahĩ, e. s. ebia wonè ohene abɔfo a ɔsomaa wɔŋ kɔɔ hɔ kodii asɛm no anni asɛm no yiye na wayaw sε wohwee wɔŋ; - wátèw wɔŋ ahĩ = omps wɔŋ nneyse, wɔŋ nneyse nyé fe, nsó n'api, he has become averse to them, he disapproves, disowns disavows them; ɔpɔŋko no atew wúrà (só) ahĩ, that horse is refractory against his master.
1. fright, affright, dread, terror; oyi no ahií, he frightens him = oyi hũ; cf. bo birim ɔr piriw. - 2. mocker, derision, insult; oyi no ahií, he mocks at him (= odi ne hɔ fɛw).
adv.: osũ hĩi hĩi, he is sobbing.
v. = hiŋ; dompe, kasae, nsɔé ahĩ mè = ahĩŋ me, a bone is sticking my throat. pr. 444.
