N'ani afura nti ɛhía no sε obi kye no kwaŋ, or, ɛhía no kwaŋkyerɛfɔ because he is blind, he wants or needs to be conducted by somebody, he is in want of, in need of a guide. - 3. kã hia mu, to besiege, invest (a town). Dan. 1,1. - Red, híahía, q. v.
inf. poverty, indigence, want, necessity, straitened circumstances, strait.
wife of a king; cf. ɔhemmaa, 58. Eccl. 2,8.
heram, v. F. = F. roof. Mt. 8,8 (Mk. 2,4).
s. hye, hye, hyi...

to come or draw to an close; to close; to be fulfilled or ted; [cf. hini, ehiŋ, ŋhiŋ, ŋhinaa]. agyew rehi, my leisure is pass- ay; me bere ahí = aka ketewaa asã, my time is nearly spent; a me de merebekɔ no rehí or reye y departure is at hand; ohia o no, poverty has (now finally y) overtaken him; - to be spent, or worn out by frequent use: no rehí or ahí aká kētewaa bi, voasew dade bi asew asew na otuo no ano ahi; - to cease g; ogya no de, èhí; ogya no ahí ie dew mã aka nnyansramma ŋkɔ. ä, hwere.

I need or am in want of money; ehíá se..., it is required or necessary that..., cf. etwa se, Gr. 157,2. 255,1 b. - eŋhíá, it is no matter, of no importance, I don't care for it; me nè fàm' de, eŋhíá, s. fàm'. N'ani afura nti ehía no sø obi kyere no kwaŋ, or, ehia no kwaŋkyerefo, because he is blind, he wants or needs to be conducted by somebody, he is in want of, in need of a guide. - 3. kä.. hía mu, to besiege, invest (a town). Dan. 1,1. - Red. hìàhìa, q. v.

inf. poverty, indigence, want, necessity, straitened circumstances, straits. pr. 116. 146 f. 332. 740-45. 1336-56. - ohía de no, hía no, akã no, poverty has overtaken him, he has become poor, has been impoverished; odi hia, he is needy, destitute, hard up, poverty- stricken. pr. 880; ne hía a odi, his neediness: ohía rehí ato no, poverty stares him in the face, awaits him (s. hí).
some membraneous part on the liver of an animal.
a kind of bead; s. ahene.
hiawa, harem.

day or time of necessity, trouble, danger, distress, need. pr. 1357; time of need; h. bi, if need be, in case of need. híáhia, red. v. hía; 1. me hø híáhia me, I am pained or straitened. Lk. 12,50. - 2. tr. ohíáhia me hø = óguàŋ me hø, he troubles me, is troublesome or loathsome to me, presses me hard or close, is hard upon me &c. pr. 1358.
a, F. = hìhìaa. Mt. 7,14.
inf.: wodi h., they look after each other, help each other, in time of need = wodi mmoa or nnoboa, s. di 84.
imitation damask.
velveteen, Damask silk.
(dim.) = ohíani 2, ayemfo.
a matter of necessity, urgent matter; syn. øseŋhia.
poverty.
baptism of an infant whose premature death is expected.
an urgent need, anxiety: eye (aye) me ah, nè ŋkømmo, it is (has become) to me an object of earnest concern, anxious care and solicitude.
(inf.) sale enforced by necessity, forced sale.
white lie, K. § 122.
As. = hìaa, nsaŋkyiri, awiriwa, mmaam', adafae.
ade a eye ahi, something exciting disgust, indignation &c., s. ahi.
v. [red. híhlé], Ak. hini, to open, to let out; hie poŋ no = bue daŋ no ano, open the door! hie yeŋ, open to us! Mt. 25,11; hie no, let him out! kohie ŋguaŋ no, let the sheep out! cf. hini, bue.
red. v. hie.

red. v. hi; ɔde nne a ehíhí bi käe se.., he said with a trembling voice... - ahihí, inf. speaking with a hoarse (& trembling) voice; vexation, annoyance; ah. reserew ahähä, one fool laughs at the other's foolishness.
[Gr.] hieroglyph, a character in the picture-writing of the ancient Egyptian priests; nseŋkyerene-kyerew. Hist.
a. narrow, strait, straitened, close; cf. tëatëa, mũamũaa.

hyim, v. [red. hínhím] to move or cause to move one way and the other: intr. to shake, tremble, shiver; to totter, stagger, reel; to roll; to swing; dua ahabaŋ hím, the leaves of the tree shake; ebyeŋ hím, the ship rolls; ebü mã ne hō hím, fear makes him tremble; awow nti ne hō hím, he shivers from cold; F. ne hō hím, he hurries. - tr. to shake, agitate, to make one tremble or totter, to swing; to wag, wave, flourish, brandish; mframa hím nnua, the wind shakes the trees; mframa hínhím po msu, the wind agitates the water of the sea; ɔpoŋko hím ne dua, the horse wags his tail; óbim ne hō, he swings. - hím dwom = to dwom, to sing. - hím aprɛm gu kürow bi so, to bombard a town. Syn. popo, posow, wosow; fère, fefere.
ahyim, inf.: di ahim, to shake: ɔde ne ti di ahim = ohíŋhím ne ti; - to wave, soar, hover: akrōma redi ahim wō ahuŋmu. - twa ahím, F. to be a lunatic, to be epileptic. Mt. 4,24.

v. [red. hímáhímã] 1. to shake, - 2. to turn, change; ɔmãã ne ti himae = daŋe, he shook him in his resolutions, he caused him to change his opinion or intention. - 3. to remove, withdraw (Neh. 9,29): bima wo nsa, wo ti, wo hō, turn aside! - to turn off, cast out, drive away: wahima wō tãmfo, Zeph. 3,15. - 4. b. ɔkwaŋ, to alter the direction of a path or road, to transplace a path or road. - 5. to turn aside, diverge, deviate gradually from a given direction: asubɔnteŋ no nē ɔkwaŋ no himae, asu no hima fi kwaŋ no hō, the river and the path parted. - 6. to reach the age of maturity; ɔbea no ah. (= adaŋ ne hō, abōe bra) nti wōye no popomporúwá; to menstruate (in general); cf. kyimã, v. - 7. to punish, chastise (obs). pr. 131. - Ahímã, ('punishment') pr. n. given to a slave by his master, pr. 131.

ŋhimahō-dàntabáŋ, tropic, the place, or circle, or zone at or over which the sun in its vertical position gradually shifts its apparent course from the northern side of the equator to the southern, and vice versa, Geog.
F. earthquake. Mk. 13,8.

hyiŋ, v. to stick fast; nsoe ahíŋ me (ahíŋ me menewam'), a fishbone is sticking in my throat; mihíŋ..ntam', I am in a strait betwixt. Phil. 1,23; twerebo, mahiŋ dade ntam', the flintstone (says), I am hemmed in, wedged in or sticking between iron, i. e. I am in difficulty. - Red. híŋhíŋ; wōbegyee asem no híŋhíŋ' mu, they interceded, interfered or interposed in the matter (stopping the proceedings). - A'híŋ mé ahàŋ me, prop. I stick fast am loosed, i. e. I am in a dilemma, critical situation, strait, perplexity, I am doubtful which to choose, undetermined what course to pursue.

ehyiŋ, pl. a-, edge, corner [perh. end, extremity, cf. hì]; As. = twea; septum, diaphragm, e.g. the white of an egg intervening between two yolks of the same egg (ŋkesua no mu da hiŋ); cf. ŋhiŋ, duhìŋ, naŋgyehìŋ. - híŋ a emu nnaa(e) [cf. daa, v. 1] an acute angle; h. a emu daa(e), an obtuse angle; hiŋ-pá, a right angle.
ŋhyiŋ [con. nē ŋhiŋ] the root tree, espec. the buttress-like part at ground of some large trees, as, on owowa; cf. duhiŋ, dupuŋ, ntini.
pl. ŋ-, a pot, an earthen vessel with a big belly and comparativel narrow opening, for water, palm-wine, palm-oil; cf. kuku. pr. 148. 184. 19 83. 2188. - ahínaá, ahínaá, pl. ŋ- dim. of ahína.

nyináa, ŋhínáŋã, ŋhínára, ŋhínara, n. (supplying also the place of the Eng. adj.) 1. all, every, prop. the whole (number or sum, of individual objects), pr. 2428. - 2. whole (in contradistinction to fragment), prop. whole, total, totality, completeness, entireness; the whole quantity or amount. - Wadi ne ŋhinaa, wannyaw me, he has eaten all and left nothing for me. pr. 604. 802-4. 2327; né ŋhíná no or neŋ, that is all; ne sika ŋhíná asã, all his money is gone; Onyame wō mmaa ŋh., God is everywhere; ŋh. de woŋ hō, they are all free; da or nna ŋh., every day, always 2378; nnipa ŋh., all men, i. e. every body; yeŋ baanu ŋh., both of us; nē no ŋh., we two together. - Ne asem ahye asase no ŋh. so, the ruin of him has spread over the whole country; yerebebu daŋ no ŋh. - fam, we are going to break the whole house down. - Observ. The pronunciation of this word being very unstable, a great variety of forms is with in the earlier attempts to write it, as: ning-yinára, ninyinra (= ŋhíná), yina, ninwa, adingna (= ŋhíná), niyina, nenana (Nig. Exp. - under all, each, every, whatever, wh. iniara, inyiana, inyinã (R.), in (Diet.), nnyínã (Chr.), nyinarra (Mf.), nyinara (Prk.) - When the Ed. (C) had learnt that in Elmina it is pronounced hínã, he changed the writing into ŋhíná, and thinks it probable that it is made of ŋhí no ara, at the end, utmost, last remainder; cf. hí, v., ehíŋ, ŋhíŋ. This is confirmed by the way in which it is rendered.
the root of a tree, espec. the buttress-like part above ground of some large trees, as, onyãã, owowa; cf. duhiy, dupuŋ, ntini.

Gr. § 118-120, the exterior: 1. a) of things: the outer or outward part, outside, surface, appearance; colour (cf. ani). Nu. 11,7; — b) of persons: the human frame; — c) the whole body; — d) the whole person. — 2. of place: the outward parts, the space without or outside (excepting cases in which akyi or akyiri stands); near-ness, proximity. — 3. a) of local relations: on, at, by, near, to, sidewards, about, around, against; — b) of causal relations: of, at, about, touching, concerning, relating to. Gr. § 121,2. 240 a. 243 Rem. 1. A. Examples in which hō is the grammatical subject of a sentence. 1. Ne hō yɛ hū, — ŋwoŋwā, — anigye, his appearance excites fear, — wonder, — laughter, — causes joy; mmaa hō ye haw, women cause trouble. — nea ne hō di ne.., he is addicted to.., it is his habit to.., what is his heart's desire is..; ɛnyɛ ne ne hō di, a) he is not addicted to this; b) he is not afraid (of it). — 2. When denoting the outer part of a thing of which the predicate expresses an action, condition, or quality that may be perceived by the senses of vision, smell, or touch: it is, in Eng., generally left untranslated, its attribute being the subject of the Eng. sentence: Mpataa hō wə aboŋ, fishes have (lit. the surface of fishes has) scales; adaka no hō yɛ hãnã-hãnã, this furniture is very bright; ahina hō yɛ hyeshyɛɛ. pr. 1383. — nantwi bi ni, ne hō kɔkɔɔ nɛ̀ fufu, there is a bullock of a red and white colour; akoa (afãnaa) no hō yɛ fe, this fellow (woman) is nice-looking. pr. 19.30; wō hō (a)ye fi, you are dirty; ne hō yɛ ŋwini, ye taŋ, he is nasty, ugly; ahohow hō bɔŋ, the red ant stinks. pr. 215.2427; wəŋ hō ye hūãm, they are or become sweet-scented, have a sweet smell; ɔpoŋ no hō yɛ torotoro, this table is smooth; ɔye onipa a ne hō ŋhwi-ŋhwi, he (is) a hairy man. 2 Kg. 1,8; okura poma, shō apow-apow, he has a knotty stick in his hands; mahū dua bi, ɛhō nsɔe-nsɔe, I have seen a tree with the bark full of thorns. — 3. In the sense of body (in contradistinction to mind) hō occurs in a number of expressions which denote conditions and qualities of the bodily constitution of man: Wō hō tɛ̀ dɛŋ? how are you? me hō tɛ̀ pɛsɛe or piŋtiŋ, I am perfectly well; me hō ye kakra, I am tolerably well; me hō ŋ'yé koraa, I am not at all well; me hō nye me dɛŋ, I do not feel well; ne hō ayɛ no dɛŋ bio, (ne hō agyae), he has become better again, he has recovered; ne hō yɛ dɛŋ, ne hō pirim, he is strong, healthy, stout; he has a strong constitution; ne hō hūm, popo, saw, he shakes, trembles, quakes, shivers; ne hō yɛ hyew, he is hot; ne hō huru no, yɛ no hyew or hyerehyere, he feels hot; ne hō keka

no, ye no hẽne or henehéne, his skin itches, is irritable; ne hõ apa, his body is bare, espec. of beasts: asẽ amã oguaŋ no hõ apa, the mange (scab, or itch) has caused the sheep's hair to fall off; ne hõ abubu no koraa, he is entirely shattered, broken down, exhausted, weak, laid low; ne hõ aba ne hõ bio, ne hõ asaŋ, he has recovered from his sickness, is well again; ne hõ tua ne hõ, he is fat, well fed, corpulent; ne hõ twa, ne hõ ye hare, kamkam, wẽwe, he is nimble, quick, active, brisk, alert; ne hõ da hõ, he is uncovered, exposed, denuded; ne hõ aĩ, he is pure, clean; fig. he has been cleared from guilt, acquitted, justified; ne hõ tew, he is bright, pure, blameless, holy; ne hõ ye no yaw, he feels pain in his body; oyare; ne hõ worow, his skin peels off. — no hõ awu, s. wu. — 4. Other combinations of hõ, body, self; with a verb, have, by a transfer from the bodily to the mental province, become expressions for mental conditions and affections. In some such phrases hõ signifies the things round about or the circumstances of a person or object. ne hõ abow no, he is disheartened; ne hõ bo no, F. he is amazed. Mk. 2,12; ne hõ dwiriw no, he is amazed, terrified; ne hõ adwo, agow (no), akã, kã ne hõ, asãŋ no, pesew no or sepɛw no, atɔ (no), atu no, he is at ease, calm, composed, comfortable, happy, joyful, rejoiced, contented &c.; ne hõ afɔm no, he is in a strait; anxious, terrified, cast down, dejected, dismayed; he hõ hia no, kyere no, yeraw no, he is in distress, trouble, perplexity; me hõ akã, s. kã 17; ne hõ haw no; hwãnyãŋ no, pere no, usɛŋ no, titi no, he is impatient, restless, uneasy &c.; ne hõ hyia ne hõ, his means meet his wants, he has all he wants, he has a competence; ne hõ awow, his means are dried up, i. e. exhausted; ne hõ twa, ne hõ wo, lit. his about is smooth or dry, i.e. he is not disorderly (sakasaka), he is clever, adroit, smart, well-mannered; shõ twa, it is clean, tidy, neat; ne hõ ye sakasaka, he is disorderly, ill-mannered. — 5. In some phrases hõ means the space about, the way to get at, or a source, a place to receive something, or the concerns of a thing: Afũw no hõ dã hõ, the access to the plantation lies there, i.e. is open, not impeded, the plantation is not fenced in; ŋhoma yi hõ ye me nã or hĩa me, I am anxious to get this book; ŋhoma yi hõ ys nã, this book is not easy to be got at; asɛm no hõ hĩa, that word (or matter) of importance. Ne hõ ye fow, good wages may be had from him, he gives good wages. Me hõ wo ade, - akyede, I am fortunate in getting things, - presents. Ne hõ du ne hõ, s. du, v.

B. Examples in which hõ is an attribute in the possessive case: Wo hõ ade ye dep, 'things belonging to your nature are very hard', i. e. you are an unlucky fellow = wo hõ ade nyé; - ne hõ ade a eye nti.., fortunately, happily, luckily; s. okra 2; - wo hõ ade ye nã, things from you are difficult, i.e. there is little to be expected from you, you are not very helpful. - In most cases hõ in the poss. case must, in Eng., be rendered by prepositions: Okõ no hõ asɛm ni, this is the history of that war; ne hõ hũ nti woguaŋe, out of fear of him they fled; wakyerew me n'akwantu hõ ŋhoma, he has written me a letter about his journey.

C. Examples in which hõ is the object of the predicate: 1. hõ, (.. hõ-hõ) in the reflexive pronoun forms the object of refl. verbs; onipa biara dɔ ne hõ, every one loves himself, or, his own life; wodo woŋhõ-woŋhõ, wodo woŋhõ-hõ or wodo-dɔ woŋ hõ, they love each other; wonè woŋhõ-woŋhõ kɔe, they fought with each other; cf. Gr. § 57.59.218, 1 a. — 2. hõ = the outside, outer part: dufua ne dua = the woafũfũaw hõ kakra.

onipa hɔ aboa; cf. tiboa, nsaboa; - ne hɔ mmóa kekã no, he is flushed with excitement, joy, passion; n'ahóboa tui = n'ani fii ne hɔ so, he lost consciousness.
ahóboabóá, inf. preparation; sym. ahòsiesié.
adv. loudly, aloud, noisily, clamorously, tumultuously; sù, kasa, bom', tẽɛm', ye h. = hòo, hùu.
inf. (F.) [hɔ, bow v.] wonder, astonishment, amazement; surprise; 12*
(= ahōdwiriw, ŋoŋwā), I marvel, wonder, am astonished. Mt. 13, 54. 22, 33. 27, 14.
wonder, miracle. Mt. 24, 24.
s. ahō-b(ē)re...
[daadaa ne hō] self-deceit, self-deception.
[daŋ ne hō] turning, conversion. Acts 15, 3. K. § 271. Cf. adwensakra.
pregnancy; cf. oyem.
[dannaŋ ne hō] repeated change or transformation; nimbleness, agility, versatility. pr. 2547; di ah., s. di 36.
[da ne hō so] readiness, preparation. precaution, circumspection. Ah. nye hū, pr. 1393. — ahōdasó-de, confidence. Prov. 3, 26.
ahōdze [ehō ade] personal property, effects, things, possessions; substance, goods. Lk. 8, 3. 15, 12 f. pr. 3502. 3646; gener. property.
[de ne hō] independence, liberty. 1 Pet. 2, 16.

twi: ahō-dɛ́ŋ, ahō-dɛ́ŋ [hō ye or wo ɔdeŋ]
eng: (bodily) health and strength; strength in general, power, might; valour; cf. tumi, pr. 1394. 2498; hye .. ah., to strengthen, invigorate. — ahōdɛ́nhyé, inf. invigoration.
a strong, healthy, stout man or person, a man of valour; cf. oberaŋ, otwentemfo, otumfo. pr. 1395f.
valiant, powerful or mighty deeds. — ahōdénne-yé, inf. the performance of mighty deeds.
mighty works; any work that requires strength; manual labour &c.
great strength. Ps. 33, 17.

twi: ahō-dɔ [dɔ ne hō] self-love; love; n'áhōdɔ nti okum ɔwɔ no, he killed the snake in order to preserve himself; wo ah. nti ɔyes adwuma denneenneŋ, out of love for you, he worked very hard.

eng: [dōm ne hō] effeminacy, delicacy, softness, weakness; ɔyɛ abdodo, he is too delicate (in feeling), too tender or weak.
a weakling; a tender, delicate, effeminate person; one given to pleasure. Isa. 47, 8. 1 Cor. 6, 9.
= horow, ahorow. ahō-dwane, Ak. = ahōguaŋ.
[dwira ne hō] purification. Lk. 2, 22.
[hō dwiriw] terror, horror, amazement; ŋwoŋwā, ahōyeraw. — ahōdwiri(w)de, wonder(s). Ps. 105, 5. 2 Thess. 2, 9; astonishment, horror. Jer. 42, 18.
[hō dwo] rest (from trouble); quiet, peaceful, happy state and circumstances.
slack, lax, relaxed, loose; weak, feeble, strengthless; syn. bɛtee, berew, boro-gɔɔ &c.; ɔye adwumaye mu hh., he is slack in his work, not diligent in his work.

[red. hodwóhòdwow] 1. to be or become slack, relaxed, loose, weak, feeble; ohodwów; - n'adesoa ah., his load is no longer tight; wabɔ akwakoraa nti or ne yare nti wah., he has become weak through old age or sickness; ne nsam' ahodwow = agow; - to melt away. Ex. 15, 15. Ps. 112, 10. — 2. tr. to slacken (adesoa mu, to make a bundle less tense or tight); to loosen (hama or ɛpɔw mu, a string when tied, or a knot), opp. mia, yere mu; to untie = sãŋ, opp. kyekye; to weaken, enfeeble, debilitate, relax; woahodwow' no hodwohodwo, he has been entirely disabled, sprained or exhausted (so that all his limbs are, as it were, out of joint).
[fa ne hō di] emancipation, manumission, liberty. 2 Cor. 3, 17. — ahōfadi-ŋhóma, bill of emancipation.
an emancipated slave. ahōfadi-prɛ́fó, the liberal party. Hist.
outward, -ly; eh. abaŋŋua, the outer court. Ezek. 10, 5; cf. akyiri-fám'.
[fa ne hō mā] voluntary offering of one's self for some purpose, voluntariness, volunteering; deed of dedication. K. § 33. 295b. — ah. a volunteer company, corps of teers, free corps.
volunteer.
(fairness), fineness, handsomeness, grace, elegance, prettiness. pr. 1397. — ahō-ɔfé-de, a thing of beauty or glory. 1 Chron. 22, 5.
a fine, handsome, pretty person = nea ne hō ye; cf. oso.
[hō fi] holiness, purity; innocence; acquittal, deliverance (by the verdict of a judge).

twi: ɛhō-fó, the people or inhabitants of a place, town or country; s. shon.

eng: [hō fɔm] dejection, abasement of spirit or mind; astonished, numbed or motionless state. Ezra 9, 3.
confession of adultery on the part of the husband; cf. Ẅia.
= ahō-ɔhūām, pr. 1396.
[hwe ne hō so] check, heedfulness, carefulness.

twi: ahohwí, debauchery, dissoluteness, intemperance, lasciviousness, wantonness (Rom. 13, 13), lewdness, licentiousness, extravagance, lavishness, prodigality, rioting. — cf. uŋyennenytwi; b. to luxuriate &c.; ah. abrabɔ, lewd behaviour; ah. asetrā, luxurious life. 2 Pet. 2, 7. 13.

eng: leading a luxurious or bad, immoral life.
debauchery, intemperance.
debauchee, sensual or dissipated person; prodigal, squanderer; cf. ogyennyentwi. pr. 1398.
profligacy, vicious and pernicious or destructive dealing.
gono or gow] 1. ease, easiness; freedom from pain, disturbance, trouble, toil, distress, exertion, annoyance, poverty or difficulty; rest, quiet; aid of any thing that ruffles, discom.
[fa ne hɔ mã] voluntary offering of one's self for some purpose, voluntariness, volunteering; devotion, dedication. K. § 33.295 b. - ah. dɔm, a volunteer company, corps of volunteers, free corps.
pl. a-, volunteer.

oféw [hɔ ye or wo ɔfew] beauty, (fairness), fineness, handsomeness, grace, elegance, prettiness. pr. 543. 1397. - ahó-efé-de, a thing of beauty or glory. 1 Chron. 22, 5. - ɔ-hóoféfo, pl. a-, a fine, handsome, pretty person = ne ne hɔ ye fe; cf. oso.
F, Aky. ahófiiri, inf. [hɔ fi] cleanness, purity; innocence; acquittal; deliverance (by the verdict of a jury).
the people or inhabitants of that place, town or country; s. ehoni.
inf. [hɔ fɔm] dejection, depression of spirit or mind; astonishment; numbed or motionless state. Ezra 9, 3f.
inf. confession of adultery on the part of the husband; cf. wiakyere.
Ak. = ahó-ohũam. pr. 2762.
inf. [hwe ne hɔ so] chastity; heedfulness, carefulness.

debauchery, dissoluteness, intemperance, lasciviousness, wantonness (Rom. 13, 13), lewdness, licentiousness; extravagance, lavishness, prodigality; rioting. - cf. nnyennyentwi; bɔ ah., to luxuriate &c.; ah, abrahɔ, licentious behaviour; ah, asetrã, luxurious living. 2 Pet. 2, 7. 13.
inf. leading a luxurious and bad, immoral life.
yś, inf. debauchery, intemperance.
pl. a-fo, debauchee, sensual or dissipated person; prodigal, squanderer; cf. ogyennyentwi. pr. 1398.
profligacy, vicious and pernicious or destructive dealing.

Ak., ahógow, Akp. inf. [hɔ gono or gow] 1. ease, easiness; freedom from pain, disturbance, trouble, toil, distress, exertion, annoyance, poverty or difficulty; rest, quiet; absence of any thing that ruffles, discomposes or frets, tranquillity, peace. - 2. carelessness, indifference.
inf. [guaŋ hɔ] vexation, harassing, troubling, oppression, (act. cf. ahóyeraw, pass.). Job 3, 26. - ɔ-hó-guaŋfó, pl. a-, a vexatious, troublesome person, vexer, troubler, disturber.
inf. [gye ne hɔ] self-defence, self-deliverance.
war of independence, liberation-war.
inf. [óyè ah. = ode ne hɔ gyigye mu] interference, meddling (in); forwardness, cf. téretereyé.
pl. a-, busy-body, saucy or inquisitive person, meddler.
Ak. = ahóyeraw.
inf. [hɔ hãrãn] splendour, magnificence; cf. anuonyam.
oháre, Ak, ahó-obére [hɔ ye hare] swiftness, quickness, lightness, nimbleness. pr. 506. 3447. - ah.-ye, inf. activity. - ɔ-hóohárefó, pl. a-, a fast person; the swift. Am. 2, 14.
inf. [hɔ, hène] itching, pruritus.
inf. [hɔ hĩa] distress, embarrassment, perplexity, pressure (passively), trouble. - ahóhĩa-dú, day of adversity.
pl. a-, distresser, adversary, enemy; syn. ohóguaŋfo.
inf. pressure (act.), vexation, tribulation, trouble. pr. 1399. - ahó-hiahía-bére, troublous times. Dan. 9, 25.
inf. [hɔ him] trembling; terror. Isa. 28, 19.
red. v., s. horo.
s. ehó C.

pl. a-, 1. stranger, foreigner, cf. ɔnanani, ɔmamfrani. - 2. guest; méyè ho h. = migye no wɔ me fi, mekɔkye no aduan, I show him hospitality; méye ne h. = mesɔe ne ŋkyeŋ, I put up, stay at his house, am his guest; wakɔsoe h., he has gone to take up his lodgings; ɔsom me h., s. sɔm. - pr. 285. 659. 1400 ff.
very deep &c., s. hóo.
(sighing, groaning): ye h., to sigh, groan.
inf. [hoahoa ne hɔ] boast,
a foreign place; oko h., he went abroad. h.-asetrɛ, pilgrimage. Gen. 47,9. — hɔhobɛá-t’rɛ, sojourning, temporary residence in a foreign land. 1 Pet. 1,17.
a house (or room) for strangers or guests; guest-chamber, reception-room; inn, hotel; s. ahoho-fi.
food of a guest, obtained by the hospitality of others. pr. 1413.
-asoe, a house where travellers are lodged and entertained; syn. ahɔhodaŋ; cf. asoe.
ahɔhɔm, ahohoŋ, a species of ant living on trees; cf. ahohow; phr. osow ah., he gapes.

ahorohɔrá, Ak. ahorohórowá, disgrace, dishonour, reproach, ignominy, infamy, shame, scandal. pr. 1414. 3603; wáyɛ ah., n’anim aye ah., he has been disgraced (perh. disgraced himself), has become infamous, abject; bo or ye..ah., to defame, disgrace, dishonour; to insult, abuse, revile; syn. yaw, kɛ anim, tɛstɛe, mã ani wu; cf. didi atɛm, gu anim ase.
ahɔhɔrá-yɛ, inf. defaming, defamation &c. — ahɔhɔrá-de lewdness. Ezek 23,44..

a-fo, an infamous, despised, despicable, abject, vile person (exposed to contumelious treatment); onipa a ɔye bone na obi mmu no; opp. onuonyamfo. 1 Cor. 4, 10 pr. 1414. — ahɔhɔrá-sɛm, reproach. Ps. 74, 10.
inf. [horaŋ ne hɔ] arrogance, assumption. Ah. na ede kɔ ba, pr.
red. v. hore, to heave, swell, rise (said of dough); to grow fast, thrive: abofra no ahóhorè koküroo, onipa no ah., aye kese. - tr. h. aduaŋ bi, to prepare a dainty dish.

mucus, spittle, phlegm; ɔbɔ waw na ɔfe h., he coughs and spits out phlegm; cf. ntasu; - odi ne yam’ (ne ba hɔ) h., she is grieved (on account of her child), she is in anxiety (about her child) = ne were how ne ba hɔ, ne yam’ hyehye no ne ba hɔ.
red. v. horo.
lodging. Philem. 22.
red. v. how; hɔhow..ani, to rest on the surface (of..).
ahóhòw, pl. ŋ., a species of ant, emitting an offensive smell, of a reddish colour, living on trees, espec. lime - and orange-trees. pr. 28. 2427.
ahóhòw, = ahúbúw, huruhúrow a efi nipa anom, breath; n’anom ah. bɔy, ye húãm, ye hyew.
s. hohow, v.] superficiality, negligence, carelessness; cf. aniani; wɔmmɔ ŋh, mpae, they pray with all their hearts; oye ŋh. adwuma, he works carelessly.
a-, inf. reception and entertainment of strangers or guests, hospitality.
sweet scent or smell, pleasant odour, fragrance.
inf. defiling oneself (by contact with a dead person). Ezek. 44,25.
inf. [hɔ huru] heat, warmth. pr. 1416. - ahɔh.-ŋkárii, ahɔh.-súsùw-adé, thermometer.
summer. Ps. 74, 17. Mt. 24, 32.
inf. s. hwányáŋ.
inf. [hyehye ne hɔ] = ahɔ-hoahoa.
inf. [hye ne hɔ so] self-command, self-discipline, chastity; modesty. K. § 349.
ɔhyéw, heat of the skin or body in fever &e., cf. ahɔhuru.
-iɔ, a single man; nea onni bi kã ne hɔ, onni yere, nni mma; cf. ɔhókwafo.
ɔhókãfó, pl. a-, companion, neighbour. Ex. 32,27. Jer. 6,21; Iudafo h., proselyte. Acts 6,5. [23,24.
long shield, buckler. Ezek.
inf. [hɔ keka] itching, pricking, tingling; prickly-heat, a cutaneous eruption of red pimples, s. fifisɛ.

inf. [kekã ne hɔ] adornment, decoration; attire, dress. - moveme ahɔkekáde, ahɔkekádé, ornament, adornment; set-off, finery; trimmings; jew ahɔ-kokó, inf. [kokɔ ne hɔ] delicacy, delicateness. Deut. 28,56.
inf. 1. uncleanness. Zech. 13 cf. efi, buru, — 2. suicide.

-fó, pl. a-, 1. a single, unmarried person, bachelor, spinster obaniŋ-hɔkw., ɔbaa-hɔkw.; also a widower or widow; nea ɔte hɔ kwa; ɔbɔkafo, osigyafo, okunafo. — 2. sound, healthful, hale, hardy, rob person.
inf. [hɔ kyere] = ahɔhia.
inf. [kyere ne hɔ] ostentation, vanity, (self-)conceit, vain-glory; ahantaŋ, ahɔhoahoa, ahɔhyehye, ahɔ ahupoo.
pride. Jer. 12,5.
pl. a-, an ostentatious, vain, proud, insolent, (self-)conceited person. Jer. 43,2.
Ak. F. pron., s. mo & Gr. § Rem. 1. 2. pr. 1817.

v. [red. hɔŋhɔm] F. to outrage; treat with violence, roughly, rude ɔhɔm nó sò, Ak. ohye no so, odi no mmerantesem &c. - hɔm do, F. to r over (Mk. 10,42); to press down or hɔm so, to oppress. Ezek. 18,7.
a-, F. = hɔme, strength. 1510. Mk. 12,30; breath.
v. F. = hɔme, to rest, repose.
inf. F. 1. = ɔhɔme. — 2. : ah. = oye ahɔkyere, ahantaŋ, ŋhye he is haughty, proud, despotic. — n’ahɔm kã nohɔ, he is happy. 5,12. Ps. 128,2.
Aky. = hãmã.

tet. hɔma; F. ahɔma, wɔt ŋwɔma, 1. the skin or hide taken fr an animal body (diff. were). pr. 5 1070; cf. oguaŋhoma, nantwiŋho asoŋhɔma. — 2. leather. pr. 149. 3. paper; cf. borɔ-ŋhoma, krãtaá. 4. playing-card(s); tow ŋh., to pi (at) cards. — 5. letter, epistle;

inf. [kekä ne hö] adornment, decoration; attire, dress. - movement. ahökekäde, ahökekäde, ornament, adornment; set-off, finery; trimmings; jewels. ahö-kokö, inf. [kokö ne hö] delicacy, delicateness. Deut. 28,56.
inf. 1. uncleanness. Zech. 13,1; cf. efi, buru. - 2. suicide.

-fö, pl. a-, 1. a single, unmarried person, bachelor, spinster; əbanin-hökw., əbaa-hökw.; also a widower or widow; nea öte hö kwa; cf. ohökafo, osigyafo, okunafo. - 2. a sound, healthful, hate, hardy, robust person.
inf. [hö kyere] = ahöhia.
inf. [kyere ne hö] ostentation, vanity, (self-)conceit, vain-glory; cf. ahantan, ahöhoahoa, ahöhyebye, ahöm, ahupoo.
pride. Jer. 12,5.
pl. a-, an ostentatious, vain, proud, insolent, (self-)conceited person. Jer. 43,2.
Ak. F. pron., s. mo & Gr. § 58, Rem. 1. 2. pr. 1817.

v. [red. höhöm] F. to outrage; to treat with violence, roughly, rudely; öhöm nö sö, Akr. ohye no so, odi no so mmerantesem &c. - höm do, F. to rule over (Mk. 10,42); to press down or on; hom so, to oppress. Ezek. 18,7.
a-, F. = höme, strength. pr. 1510. Mk. 12,30; breath.
v. F. = höme, to rest, repose.
inf. F. I. = öhöme: - 2. öyè ah. = öye ahökyere, ahantan, ŋhysso, he is haughty, proud, despotic. - 3. n'ahöm kä nöhö, he is happy. Mt. 5,12. Ps. 128,2.
Aky. = hämä.

tet. höma; F. ahöma, wöma, ŋwöma, I. the skin or hide taken from an animal body (diff. were). pr. 523. 1070; cf. oguaŋhoma, nantwiŋhoma, asoŋhöma. - 2. leather. pr. 149. - 3. paper; cf. boro-ŋhoma, krätaá. - 4. playing-card(s); tow ŋh.. to play (at) cards. - 5. letter, epistle; cf. mänä-ŋhoma; bubu ŋhoma, to fold up a letter. - 6. book; syn. brükuü. - 7. ŋh. or ŋhomam', book-learning; literary knowledge; osüa ŋh., he learns (is learning) to read; he studies; cf. bo 108; onim ŋhomam', he is an educated, learned or literary man, a scholar. (ŋhömäá), ŋhömawá, pl. ŋhoma-ŋhöma, tract, treatise, pamphlet, little book.
a bad book. K. § 104.
library, archives. Ezra 6,1.
inf. learning. Acts 26,24.
[ŋhoma a ágüaŋ] a dried skin; owu ye aŋh. yaw, pr. 3490 ff.
red. v. hömaŋ.
inf. tanning (leather). - ŋhöma-hyéfo, ŋh.-hyéfó, tanner.
inf. ŋhöma káŋ, reading books; cf. Gr. § 203,1. - ŋhomakáŋbéa, reading-room.

inf. writing on paper, writing of letters or books; cf. bo 108. - di ŋh., to correspond, have epistolary intercourse. - ŋh. hö kwaŋnyä, liberty of the press. - ŋhömakyeréwdí, inf. correspondence. - ŋhöma-nyáunsá, science. [scholar.
pl. id. a learned man, a ŋhöma-pám, inf. bookbinding. ŋhöma-pámfó, bookbinder.
a roll of leather or paper, scroll (Ezra 6,2).
ŋhoma a wöapo no aye krätaá, parchment. 2 Tim. 4,13.
inf. exaltation of one's self, pride. Eccl. 7,8.
inf. = ŋhöma süa, learning from books.
inf. printing; ŋh.-tíntím-afri, printing-press; ŋhomatíntím-béa, printing-office.
stationer's shop, bookseller's shop.
inf. card-playing; wöyeɛ ŋh. mäá obodamfo, card-playing was invented for a madman.
v. [red. hömáhömaŋ] to swell (of a bud, a carcass), to bloat, distend; to be puffed up or bloated, inflated or flushed (with pride); to be proud. Isa. 16,6; to puff oneself up; wahomaŋ
wɔŋ so, he flew upon them, railed at them, spokoroughly and angrily to them, used insolent and reproachful language, 1 Sam. 25,14. Cf. horaŋ.

v. 1. to breathe. pr. 2771; wawu, ɔnhome bio, he is dead, has ceased to breathe; ontumi ŋhome nsi so, he cannot breathe well, breathes with difficulty; se woforo bepɔw yi wie a, wòbehóme. 2. to rest, repose; mabɛre, mekohómé kakra; òwigyinae mehomee wɔ Aburi; se woforo bepɔw yi wie a, wòbehóme. 3. to vibrate, pulsate, beat or throb, as the arteries and the heart; ntini home, s. ntini.

ɛ- (inf.) 1. breathing, breath; ne home si so, s. si 43. 2. strength: 3. Phr. mé hómé téw, lit. my breath rends (my breathing is difficult), i.e. my strength fails me, I can bear it (my strength fails me, I can bear it in despair, consternation, despondency; it is used in the present tense; in the pret. and perf. tense the phr. "me hō yeraw me" is used for it. 4. rest, repose, quietness (Eccl. 4,6): eyi ansã-na manyã ɔh., now at length I have found rest; also: ... I have got well; ɔh. bi nni asase so, there is no rest on earth. 5. Phr. me home kã me hō, my rest is undisturbed, I have peace; cf. ahōmekã.

(inf.) 1. breath, blast, cf. ahohow, abuhuw, ahum; sigh; gu ah., to sigh. pr. 291. 2. F. rest, repose: kògye wo ahómé, go take your rest; mã min-nye m'ah., let me have my repose. hómé-béa, pl. h.-mmea, place of rest. Isa. 66,1. hómé-bére, pl. h.-mmere, time of rest. Lev. 26,34f. hómé-dá, pl. h.-nna, day of rest, sabbath; di h., to keep the sabb. hòmédá-dí, inf. the observance of the sabbath. ahomèe, resting-place. Ruth 3,1. ahome-gú, inf. a sigh; sighing. ahome-gyé, inf. recreation, refreshment, recovery of strength and spirit after toil; F. rest. Mt. 11,28 f. ahomegyédá, F. (Akp.) sabbath. ahomegyéhòmè, a sabbath of rest. Lev. 25,4.
inf. [me home akã me hō] satisfaction, gladness, joy, happiness. ah.-tūro, paradise. K. § 208.

inf. [home tew or tew home] breathlessness, the being out of breath; distress, excessive trouble, vexation, anguish of spirit (Ex. 6,9) &c.; biribi a stew wo home (something that takes away your breath or rest), ɛ.s. emmã wunnyã ahomeyé, shaw wo; syn. abotu, ahōyeraw. Òwɔ de ahometéw (a.s. ahōyeraw) na ɛka, the snake bites when annoyed. pr. 3446; èyè àhometew, it is annoying; hye ah., to disquiet. Jer. 50,34.
= ahometew a ɛtra so, excessive trouble, despair, desperation. K. § 272.
-ɔméréw, weakness, infirmity, debility.
-kã, F. = ahomegye, ahomekã.
F. gladly. Mk. 12,37.
the criers in hunting game. shouting while hunting game; also: shouting in general; bɔ h., to make a noise in welcoming; cf. bɔ twi. Wɔbɔ homo gyee no awo.
[ahome tenten] F.: gu h., to sigh deeply. Mk. 8,12.
an unfortunate person; syn. ɔkrabiri(fo).

v. [red. hoŋhoŋ] to pull out that which stuck fast (the blade of a knife, the iron of a hoe from the handle, a nail from the wall), pr. 2616; to (extirpate or) eradicate, pull up by the roots (a horn from a goat's head: hɔŋ oguaŋ abɛŋ no, hophɔŋ abɛŋ no); to screw out, unscrew; hòphɔŋ akyene no mfewá, take out the screws of that drum! - intr. akūma no hɔŋ tɔɔ nsum', the axe came loose (off) from its handle and fell into the water.
denotes the noise heard when something sticking fast is pulled out.
F. = wɔŋ, they, them, their.
v. to seize by the nape and push away; óhɔŋ no = ɔwɔ no ŋkonsĩaw, ɔpo no taw, osum no atiko.

v. [red. hòŋhɔŋ] to swell; me nsa rehoŋ, my hand is swelling; n'afɔno ahɔŋ, his cheek is swollen; ne ti ahɔŋ, he is puffed up, he has become haughty = wahòmaŋ, wahoraŋ. - tr. to cause to swell: mã hɔŋ me naŋ, the Guinea-worm causes my leg to swell.
marrow in the bones; brain; Ak. amemene; - tirim h. the brain(s); ohɔŋntini, the nerves.
a. & adv. deep, very deep, said of a wound, a well, the eyes in their cavity; cf. hɔo. - F. very wide and well kept (of a path).
the humming or buzzing of flies; wotu a, wote woŋ ntabaŋ mu h. - cf. bɔnyɔhɔŋyɔ.

n. or adv. imit. of blowing or of a confused noise: mframa bɔ huu, the wind blows strongly; aŋkɔnam mmɔ huu. pr. 1708; nnipa no kasa huu = hòbobo; ye huu, to roar. Jer. 51, 55; kùrow nom' aye huu = hòo.
2. completely: wadow kwae no nyinaa huu, he has cleared (away) the wood altogether; syn. koraa. pr. 983.
interj. an exclamation to call one from a distance; ho, hoy! Isa. 55, 1. Zech. 2, 11f.
attention! - húu, ennim' oh, that is not true!

Ak. hunu, v. to see; diff. hwe, gyeŋ, kari; 1. to perceive by the eye, to behold, discern, descry; mihũù no (= m'ani tuaa no) wɔ hẽ mprempeŋ (Ak. mihunuu no hɔ̃ sesee ara), I saw him there just now; ohũi se wawu, he perceived (saw) that he was dead; - to have in sight; to take notice of; hũ ade, to see. Gr. § 202, 1. pr. 187-93. 760. 1428-53. 2023; oŋhũ akyiri adé, he cannot see things far off, he is short-sighted. 2 Pet. 1, 9; oŋhũ akyiri, he does not know how it will end.
2. to discover, find, find out, invent; mehwehwe me paane na miŋhũ, I am looking for my needle and cannot find it. pr. 2670.
3. to recognize: mihũù no ne yarepa so na maŋhũ no bio, I saw him on his sick-bed and did not recognize him.

n. fear, fright, terror. pr. 1393; ehù akà no, fear has seized, overcome him, he is frightened. - ye hù, yi hù, 1. to excite fear. pr. 3. 2847: éyè (or éyi) hù, it is frightful, awful, dreadful; óyi.. hù, he frightens; ne hō ye hù, his appearance excites fear, he is frightful, formidable, terrible. - 2. to be fearful, afraid, timid: óyè hù sē akóko, he is as timid as a fowl = àye ohùfó. - bɔ hù, F. to be amazed (Mt. 12,23).

1. a treasure found in the earth or ground; sika a wotu wɔ fam' a, s. nnupúŋ mù; syn. odweg, asasedé; - tu ahú, to find or dig out a treasure hidden in the ground; wátú ahú (afà), he has found some hidden treasure, wafa odweŋ. - 2. = ahūnu, a thing seen. pr. 1455.

v. [red. hūhūá, (hūahūa)] to smell, scent; mema no aduaŋ a, ohūá hwè ansá-na odi, when I give him food, he smells (or snuffles) at it before he eats (it); okramaŋ de ne hwene ahū(a)-hūa ara akohù abòkà no, the dog has traced out with his nose, i.e. has scented the carcass. Cf. ehūá, hūām; hūá tie, s. tie. pr. 1565.
F. hwã, Ak. hwã = fwã.

v. 1. to scrape, scratch; hūã ode, to scrape, or scratch, or pare, off the burned parts of the roasted yam; to graze, to rub or brush lightly in passing (cf. hūãsu); syn. twere, twerew; cf. hūāŋ, hūane, & red. hūhūã. - 2. (hūa, cf. red. būāhūã) to lay a fresh leaf in front of the fire to make it soft and flexible; tew ahabaŋ no hūã (kã, tōtō) gya posa sɔ kuru no mu. - 3. [inf. abūã] to beg, to crave (for food only); óhūã aduaŋ', ɔkohuá nò aduaŋ', he craves for food, begs food from him; obehūã ha daa. pr. 213; cf. sēre.
inf. begging (for food). pr.207. 1560.

pr. n. the country to the east of the Volta beyond Akwam and Anum called by the inhabitants Ewe, by the Akras Ayigbé, by the Europeans Krepee (Krepē). - Hūã is also the name of the language spoken there. Ɔkɔ Hūãm', he has gone to Krepe. Ohūãni, pl. Hūãfó, q. v.

smell, odour, scent (good or bad) - te h., to perceive the smell, smell; mete atuduru h., I am smelling the powder; (tie h., pr. 1565). - gye hūá, to scent, smell: akramaŋ g. hūá na wotoa wɔŋ aboa; migye no hūá. - yi h., to give (yield, produce) a good odour. Cant. 1,12; to have bad smell, to stink = bɔŋ.

a kind of plant; all sorts plants.

a treasure found in the earth around; sika a wotu wo fam' a, s. ũŋ mù; syn. odweŋ, asasedɛ; - hũ, to find or dig out a treasure in the ground; wátù ahũ (afà), was found some hidden treasure, odweŋ. - 2. = ahũnu, a thing pr. 1455.

[red. hũahũa]] to smell, memã no aduaŋ a, ohũa hwè na odi, when I give him food, onells (or snuffles) at it before he (it); okramaŋ de ne hwene ahũ(a)- ara akohũ abokã no, the dog has d out with his nose, i.e. has ed the carcass. Cf. ehũa, hũãm; tie, s. tie. pr. 1565.

Hũãfó, q. v.

hũa, smell, odour, scent (good or bad). - te h., to perceive the smell, to smell; mete atuduru h., I am smelling the powder; (tie h., pr. 1565). - gye hũa, to scent, smell: akramaŋ gye hũa na wotoa wɔŋ aboa; migye no hō hũa. - yi h., to give (yield, produce) a good odour. hũa, brodɛ hũa, the viscid juice oozing from a newly cut bunch of plantains; (sɛ ɛkã wo ntama ana wo nsam' a, ɛka ho, it stains the clothes or hands).
hũãã, a. & adv. viscous, viscid, sticky, glutinous; tenacious, tough; syn. hũàuũ, twãã, sãã, mãã, fãã, prãprã &c. Me fufuu sɔ hũãã.

hũãm, v. 1. to pluck, pull off, out, or from, with a jerk; to take by force; to rescue. Acts 23, 10. 27; syn. paŋ, pɔŋ, tew, tu; obi reŋhũãm wɔŋ me nsam', no one shall snatch them out of my hand. John 10, 28f. - 2. to decrease, abate, to flow off. Ps. 58, 8; syn. hũaŋ, twẽ; nsú no ahũãm. - 3. to smell, i.e. to investigate by smelling; combined with tie & te or hwe & hũ: mihũãm taa matie se eye ana, óhũãm taa hwɛ (Ak. ohwam tawa no hwɛ) sɛ ebɛye de ana? I smell, he smells the tobacco to know if it is good.

o-hũãm, Ak. 'hwãm, 1. the scent or odour emitted from sweet-smelling substances, perfume, fragrance, aroma. - 2. sweet-smelling substances, perfumes; aduru bi a eye hũãm, sɛ krobɔw, be-weonua (two kinds of gum), mmōwa (a bark), abeefo (roots & bark of a creeper), hwentáa (a fruit), péprè (aloë), osikó, fofoowa, ŋhwãane, sōŋ-weré. - ye or sra h., to perfume or anoint the face, neck, arm-pits, upper arms.

hũãm, hũãmhũãm, Ak. hwãm, hwãm-hwãm, a. odoriferous, fragrant, sweet-smelling; - ye h., to be fragrant, smell sweetly; ne hō ye hũãm. pr. 2427. 3556; éyè hũãm; ŋhwiréŋ yi yè hũãm, this flower smells sweetly: ŋhw. a éyè hũãm yi, a sweet-smelling flower; ŋŋó hũãmhũãm; əte sɛ biribi gyigye ne hwenem' hũãmhũãmhũãm, he perceives a very sweet odour, which produces a tickling sensation in his nose.
o-hũãm-fufu, frankincense. Ex. 30, 34.
hũãm-afɔré-múkà, altar of incense.
hũãmhũãã, (Okw.?) a flat lizard.

o-hũãmmɔ, ohũammɔ, inf. [hũaŋ, bɔ] or hũammo [ɔbo a ehũaŋ] disappointment; bɔ or di h., to disappoint; to fail. Isa. 58, 11; to be deceitful. Jer. 15, 18; to be disappointed; wadi me h., he has disappointed me; ete sɛ wáhũãŋ biribi a ekura ade bi mu na ade no abo fam' (ahwe ase). pr. 1458.
o-hũãmmɔ-adé, deceit. Isa. 30, 10.
ahũãmmɔ-dwùmá, work of mockery. Jer. 10, 15.

hũaŋ, v. [red. hughũaŋ], Ak. hwane, 1. to pull, drag or draw away, off or forth, to withdraw forcibly, espec. a thing from under some other object; wasoma me soro áhũãŋ m'ase antweri, pr. 3002; wáhũaŋ ne náŋ, he has forcibly withdrawn his foot. - 2. to disjoin, dislocate, put out of joint; to sprain with mu; wáhũaŋ ne naŋ mu, he has sprained his foot; - to be dislocated, out of joint:

3. to snap, to spring or fly up or back, rebound; afīri no ah., the spring has snapped off. pr. 3031. 3392. 4. to recede, flow back, lower, ebb; eso ahüaŋ, the sea ebbs. 5. so hüaŋ, to decrease, decline, diminish, lessen (of fluids or anything accumulated, of strenght, pain &c); to abate. Gen. 8,3; eso ah., it has become less or lower; ne tumi so re-hüaŋ, his power is on the decline; ne kaw no so ah., his debt has decreased; caus. huan .. so, to diminish; wahüaŋ me kaw so amā me, he has lessened my debt for me; to keep back. Jer. 26,2; opp. dore, hyia so, to mu. K. § 324. 6. öhüáŋ apakyé = ötö ap., okā ('he touches') ne naŋ mu, ne sisi mu, ne gyaa mu, he limps, walks lamely, in consequence of a dislocation or fracture in a joint or leg; oh. dwonku, he halts upon his thigh. Gen. 32,32.

a yearly festival, annual custom of the Guang people (Date, Kyerepoŋ, Mamfẽ, Mampoŋ, Tutu, Asantemma) and part of the Akems, celebrated with feasting, playing and dancing. Amaŋ a wokasa Guang nyinaa na edi hũm, te se Akropoŋfɔ nè Aburifo twa odwira; cf. odwira, aberekwasi, akoŋ- huro. - odé-hũm', a festival for the fetish at the time of planting yam; s. ahumkaŋ, ahuŋkyiri. - abeté-hũm', a festival for the fetish at the time of reaping maize (in some towns in June or July, in others in Nov. or Dec.).
pl. a-, a brazen gun, blunder- buss; tuo tiaa bi a wóde di àhemfó anim'; ŋwóbwá na wotaa de ye nade a eda ne bōnâ mu no.
1. a strong wind, gale, storm; mframa kese or bebree, cf. mfare, ɔprannaa; ah. retu, a storm is rising; ah. tui na ebuu dua too kwaŋ mu; ah. abesi maŋ mu. - 2. s. ahuŋ 3.
introduction of a song; bɔ ahum(a), to introduce a new song(?)

the day on which the Guang people celebrate the ohum festival; s. ohūm. - ahūm-dí, inf. the celebration of the ohum festival.
the bearers of the king's guns; woŋ a wokura ahum di bene anim; s. ohum & gyaasefo.
the time of the first ohum custom; s. ahuŋkyiri.

1. mistletoe, a parasitic plant on trees. - 2. a creeper of a finger's thickness, with large thick leaves, winding round trees. ahūm nè ahám, 'anything in the world'; e.g. stones, trees, gold, birds, sheep &c.; nneema a ɛwɔ wiase nyinaa, cf. nnanŋó.
inf. [hū.. mmɔbɔ] pity, sympathy, compassion, commiseration, mercy; cf. timobɔ, ayamhyechye. - n'ahūmóbɔ dōsɔ dodo, F. he is most gracious.
F. mercifully.
inf. the blowing of a strong wind; gale, storm. Mt. 21,14.
inf. understanding. Ex. 31,3; discernment. 1 Kg. 3,11f.; nim ŋh., to be endued with understanding. 2 Chron. 2,12; ye ŋh., to act wisely or prudently. 2 Chron. 11,23.
pl. id. a wise, understanding, skilful, expert person. 1 Chron. 25,8.

Ak., ahuno, ahunu. 1. ahúŋmù, ahúnum', the air, atmosphere, the apparently empty space above the earth. pr. 2549; cf. ŵim; [fr. hunu, a.] - 2. ahúŋmù ásì or átò nó sò, something (invisible, from the air) has come down on him, has affected him, i.e. he has fallen into a swoon, is in a fainting fit, has had an epileptic fit;

twi: ahuŋ ye ade a wuŋhū, ete sɛ ɔhome ara; cf. ahum = mframa, ahoŋhom, & ahunum, piti, beraw, abiribiriw.

eng: 3. ahúŋmù, ahúm, ahúntwam' (kàkrà), a little while; mã ahuŋ ntwam' kakra, ansā-na mentoa m'asem so, wait or let me wait a little and then I shall proceed with my narrative, or, with my story; wokɔ yi, ahuŋmu twam' kakra a, bĕra, if you are going now, come again in a little while; ahuŋ(mu) fa mu kakra a (or, ahuŋ [ahum] kakra fam' [twam'] a), na agyae, in a little while it will be over; ahuŋmu faa so no, ɔsoree, after a little while he arose.
air-ship, air-balloon; cf. mframatoa.

[red. hunahúna] 1. to importune, tease, defy, provoke, challenge; wopɛ sɛ wo yoŋkɔ hye wo ase na wohye no so a, na wuhuna no neŋ. - 2. de ne hɔ hh... mu, to obtrude upon, to burdensome to; to intrude among; ɔde ne hɔ hunahuna adumayɛfo no mu te sɛ nea oye adwuma no bi, nanso ɔnye bi. - 3. to threaten, frighten, terrify, bully; ode abaa, sekaŋ, tuo, huna no = yi no hū. red. v. hunu.

[ehū kye]: Wose: huŋkyerɛ, na wonse sɛ nnaŋkyeree, the coward comes back from the war, but not the courageous man. pr. 2809, = wose: woye hū a na wokye, na wonse sɛ: woye nnaŋ a, na wunyīŋ kye. inf. [hūnu] Ak. = ŋhūi; wany ŋh., he has often seen. Gr. § 104, ĕ.
the time of the last ohum custom: cf. ahum-kaŋ.

can be taken to pieces and put together again.

red. v. hunu.

Ak. hug, huno, a. empty, void, hollow. - 2. unsubstantial; vain, worthless, unsatisfying. - 3. idle, inactive, unemployed, unoccupied. - 4. unfruitful, fruitless, ineffectual. - 5. mere, simple; bare, naked; without any thing else; nsu hūnu, plain water. pr. 3087; - wokɔo okɔ-hūnu = wokɔe no, wonnim aseŋ-kɔ ase, 'they went in their simplicity' (lit. a mere going), i.e. without knowledge of the matter in question. - 6. having no proper right: ŋkūrɔfo hūnu ne nuipa bi a wɔmfrā wo abūsūam' na ɛdɔ so ana ayoŋkɔgoru so na wonè wo trā. - 7. groundless, false (ntam). - Cf. huhuw, kwa; cpds. adehūnu, aseghūnu, ntaphuŋnu. - (ne) hunu a eye, nothingness.

Ak. hug, huno, adv. merely, only, for nothing, to no purpose, in vain, for no reason, without reason. pr. 363. 1799. 2375; ̀tāŋ mé ara hūnu, or, ̀tāŋ me hūnu ara kwā, he hates me without cause. Syn. kwa, teta, gyan.
v. Ak. = hū, to see &c. pr. 1453.
one who has seen. pr. 1454.

something that causes suffering; ade emā wuhū amanne; h. bra = amanne-hunu-bra, a life of suffering. pr. 1456.
one who is always on the same spot, one who makes no progress, is always the same.
s. ahug; ahunum' = ade-to-wo-so; ete se abiribiriw, nanso etetew wo ani so a, ensaŋ mma bio se abiribiriw.
inf. vanity. Eph. 4, 17.

1. imperiousness, arrogance, presumption, insolence; boastings. Ja. 4, 16; violent behaviour. pr. 746. - 2. exaction of unlawful profit: imposition, extortion (ɔ́yè ah., ɔnam bɔ ŋkūrɔfo ah. = odi tumi hye ŋkūrɔfo so gye wɔŋ hɔ nneema); cf. amimdi. - 3. exaction of undue reverence: pride, haughtiness, ambition; ɔ́yè ah., ɔbɔ ah. = ɔ́ye huu huu, ne nneyse mu ɔye se ɔwɔ biribi, nso onni ahuro; vainglory; ɔ́ye n'ade hūn hūu, he does
things in a light-minded way, acts frivolously. Cf. ahantaŋ, ahōkyere-hunu, ahōhoaboa.
pl. a- fo, an arrogant, overbearing &c. person; ǝye oh., e.g. he goes to settle matters as if in the king's name, without his authority.
doings or dealings implying ahupoo, q. v.; great swelling words. Jude 16.

v. 1. to be covered or overgrown with; to overgrow, to shoot up on; ne ti ahura dweŋ or dweŋ ah, n'atifi or ne tirim, his head is covered with hoary hair; esíw no sō ah. mmẽre, or mmẽre ah. siw no so, mushrooms have shot up on that ant-hill. — 2. de.,h., to convey, throw or cast to; ne dig ye me se ohũãm a mframa bo de hura me, his name is to me as a fragrance which the wind blows or wafts to me (Cant. 1,3). - pãmpãŋ bone bi bɔ huraa no kum no, he was killed by poisonous damps, which arose and enveloped him. — 3. h, hō or mu: to soil, make dirty, bemire, bespatter, besmear, bedaub, stain, defile, pollute; h. hō, to profane. Ezek. 23,38 f.; - intr. to be soiled, dirty, polluted, defiled &c.; o-hura daŋ no mu; ɔdaŋ no hō ah., n'a-daka hō ah. = aye ŋtuw; ne nnade hō ah. = agye ŋkãnare; - oh, ne som hō = ɔnsóm no yiye na osom no sakasaka, he is disloyal or dishonest in his service. — 4, h...anim, to abuse (with words), to revile, vilify; to disgrace, dishonour; to-insult, affront; cf. hys aniwu, bɔ ahobora.
a. a disease causing violent pain in the limbs; emã wo nnompem tutuw wo; ne nua ne atutuw; - fever; h. abɔ no, he has fever, he is in a fever.

v. Ak, — huruw. pr. 2014.

v. 1. to boil, bubble, effervesce; to foam, froth; to be violently agitated, to rage; nsú rehùru, the water is boiling; nsu a ahuru, boiling water; aduaŋ no huru gu, the food boils (is boiling) over; epo h., the sea is raging terribly. - also = hohore, to heave &c., like leavened dough. — 2. to excite, agitate:

a thing or affair seen and told; sɛ eye mo atoro oo, sɛ eye mo h. oo, mo ara na mokofaa asɛm no bae, whether it be a lie on your part, or whether you have seen and told it, it is you who have brought (out or forward) the matter.

hūntūma, F. = mfutumā, dust. Mt. 10,14. Mk. 61,1.

Prov. 6,19; h. dàgo [obs.] to tell lies; - òde amanne yi hùw' me, he 'poured' his news into my ears. - òhùw fàm' dà, he sleeps on the bare ground; he is very poor. - huw mfonini, to photograph. - h. (a)sòtore, to give a box on the ear.
v. to cut down. Isa. 10,34; h..gu, to cut off. Ps. 76,13; ohuw ne ti so, he is cutting his hair.
inf. breath. Isa. 30,33. - o-hùwfó, pl. huwfo, fanner, winnower. Jer. 51,2. - ŋhuwsó-apàwá, winnowing fan. Mt. 3,12.

inf. sound, noise. Lev. 26,36; roar. Ps. 65,8; rumbling of carriage-wheels, Jer. 47,3; bustle, tumult, stir. Isa. 22,2.

v. 1. tr. to raise up. Jer. 51,1; to stir, rouse, disquiet. 1 Sam. 28,15; to urge on. 1 Kg. 21,25; - refl. to stir or rouse oneself up to lively action or vigorous exertion, to stimulate oneself, to exert oneself; asafo bi hw. woŋ hɔ wo ofie na woŋhw. woŋ hɔ wo dom ano a, wofrɛ woŋ hũfo; wohw. woŋ hɔ kyere nnipa nti, woŋ hɔ ye hũ; ohene wo hɔ na waŋhw. ne hɔ a, woŋsuró no; ohw. ne hɔ = ɔkãnyáŋ ne hɔ, aye ne hɔ kese, okã ne hɔ mã obi wo hɔ a ohũ sɛ ne nsam' ye duru (a,s. aye onipa). - 2. ne hɔ hwãnyáŋ no = onseŋ ne werem', he is agitated, perturbed; cf. ne hɔ sɛpsw no. - 3. hw... mu, to agitate, disturb, derange, disorder, throw into confusion; ohw. ntramam', sikam', ntadem', nnipam' = opetẽ ntrama &c., ɔmã woye sakasaka; ohw. ne ŋhwĩ mu, she dishevels her hair, puts it into disorder; cf. pesew.

v. As. = hũa, fwã, to scrape, scratch.

sand-glass. - ŋhwẽa-ŋhwẽábó, sandstone.
(in) the sandy desert; sandbank. - aŋhwẽa-táŋ, aphwẽa-tám, loose sand, sands; a large sandbank, shoal. Acts 27,17.

Nu. 1,53. 3,7. 6. hwe.. yiye, to look well (to), to mind, take heed, take care, be careful; hwe yiye na ammo kuruwa no, take care not to break the jug; hwe wo hɔ yiye na woanhwe ase, be careful lest you fall; mehwe se moba hɔ bi, I want you to come there too. 7. to expect, desire, want; look out for, expect, wait for (expectantly). 8. hwe.. akyi, a) = hwe.. atiko, to look after, s. 1. b) to look for things during one's absence, prepare (something to eat) for one's return. 10. hwe.. mu, to look, pry or peep into; inspect, examine, revise. 11. hwe.. anim, a) to look into one's face. b) to have a regard for; hwe m'anim ye mã no, do it for him to please me, to favour me with it, for my sake. c) to visit; mebehwé wo anim, I (am) come to visit you. d) to expect (= hwe okwan): ɔhwɛ m'anim wɔ Osu nne, he expects to see my face to-day at Osu. 12. hwe.. a) to look upon (cf. 2); hwe so kyerew, look on (it) write, i.e. copy it! hwe so ye, imitate it! b) to examine, review, revise: hwe nea makyerew yi so, look at what I have written and correct it; - to overlook, survey. c) to inspect, control, superintend, govern, rule. Gr. § 213. d) to look after, tend (cf. 5): obwe ŋguaŋ so; ɔbea gyigyefo hwe abofra so. e) to do carefully: hwe so kaŋ, read (it) carefully! f) hwe ne hɔ so, to be chaste. Tit. 2,5; to guard oneself. 1 John 5,18. g) mo adwuma so na wobehwe atua mo ka, your reward will be according to your work. 13. hwe.. atiko, to look after (one). 14. to try, in hũa.. or hũam.. hwe, kã.. hwe, sɔ.. hwe, twa.. hwe, ye.. hwe &c.; kaŋ ŋhoma yi hwe, try to read this book!

to order, bespeak, give orders for, to commission (also with ase): mekohye kete (ase) wo hɔ, I am going to order a mat there; hye dwumayefo, to engage labourers for (any) work (without subsequent payment); cf. (hye) dotewa(w)fo or awɔ(w)fo, abetow, abeswo(w), adow. pr. 1112. 3485.

to burn: 1. hye, to burn = to hurt with heat or fire: awia hye or hyehye me ti, the sun burns my head. pr. 3307; ɔkanea hyee me nsa, the light burnt my hand.

powder. — 6. to dry up (tr. & intr. of plants, from an excess of heat); to wither. 1 Pet. 1,24; abŭro no ahyew koraa, all the maize-plants are withered. — 7. to be killed in battle, carried off by famine or sickness; to die in numbers : aguag no mu nnipa-mma hyew se sare, on that flight people perished like flies (lit. grass); — ɔde mo bhyew, he will cause you to perish in war. — 8. to be lost (said of money, espec. in weighing out gold-dust for separated items): mede agyiratwe (me)toto ŋkoko mfua-mfua, na emu ŋkokoa 2 hyee. — 9. to spend or expend (money) uselessly or to excess; mahyew sika bebree (wɔ) me yare yi hɔ. — 10. Phr. “Wo gya aphye me!” your fire has not burned me! i.e. your saying or threat has not made any impression, has not had any effect upon me. — ɔhyé(w), inf. burning, being burned. pr. 621.

v. [inf. ŋ-, red. hyiahyia] 1. to meet, fall in with, come together, assemble, join, converge; mihyiaa no okwaŋ mu, I met him on the way. pr. 1071. - kehyia.. kwaŋ, F. to go to meet. Mt. 25,1. - me nè no hyiae (wɔ) wuram', I came together with him in the bush; afe ano reye ahyia, the end of the year goes to meet (the beginning of another year), i.e. new-year's day is at hand. - Phr. wabyía Kyéiwá nè ne mmá, he has met a hero indeed. - 2. intr. to be close together, so as to touch reciprocally (said of the teeth). pr. 2831. - 3. to agree, accord, be ac- cordant; ŋkohyia, it does not fit properly; fa baabi hyia baabi, to agree, his desire(s) will not agree. - 4. to meet or encounter in hostility, to come upon; ohyiá no à, otumí nò, when he attacks him, he is a match for him, he is able to withstand him success- fully. pr. 3223; to be contrary to: mframa hyia yeŋ, the winds are con- trary, are against us. Mt. 14,24. Acts 27,4; hyeŋ no tumi hyia mframa, the ship is able to face the wind. Acts 27,15. - 5. to call, send for; to cite, summon; cf. fre; to call together, con- vene, convoke; to invite; Onyamé ahyía nò, God has called him (away, or to him, by death); ɔhene hyiahya ne mamfo, the king calls his people to- gether; wuhyiaa no adidi, wuhyiaa no

pon hō or pon ase, you invited (asked) him to dinner. - 6. hyia oyere, to marry, take a wife; cf. ware; hyia ayeforo, to marry, celebrate a wedding. - 7. hyia mu, hyiam', to meet or assemble in the same place; to have an interview; mpanyimfo hyiám' (wo) abonteŋ so, the elders assemble in the street. - 8. hyia so, to fill up by pouring in, to pour into. pr. 2545; opp. huàŋ so; nsu yi abehya nsu yi so; wahyia so = wamä aye mäto. - 9. Phr. me nsa hyia m'adwuma, my hands suffice for my work = metumi m'adw. yo, m'ade a mewo ye nyinaa, mitumi yo; - me nsa hyia me hō, I provide with my hands for all my wants. - ne hō hyia ne hō, he has all he wants. - 10. da hyia, bo hye hyia, s. ohye, hyebag. - 11. in connection with a preceding verb: to surround, encompass, pass around, go round; adv. & prep. round about. 1 Chron. 22, 18; hwe wo hō hyia, look round about! Isa. 60, 4. Jer. 50, 14f.; twa hyia, s. twa. - 12. óhyiaá no òtóó no [báabuŋ], he married her (& found her) a virgin [St. § 94]. ahyia, inf. F.: dzi ahyia, to assemble = kohyia fäkō. Mt. 22, 34.

Deut. 33. pr. 197. 2759. - 2. to invoke; by. wo Nyaŋkōpoŋ se obedí wo akyi ana, call on your God that He may assist you. - 3. to bless, praise, glorify for benefits, to extol for excellencies, Ps. 103. - 4. to deem or account happy. Jer. 4, 2. - 5. euph. to curse, blaspheme. 1 Kg. 21, 10. Job 2, 9; wahyira ohéne = watew gyedua ahabaŋ, he has cursed the king's life; s. gyedua. - 6. hy. so, a) to decide on, to give validity or authority to, to ratify, agree, assent to, to sanction: ohene ahy. so se wóŋkum no, the king has decided that he shall be killed; mahyira oguaŋ yi so se wóŋkum no, I have (destined) allotted this sheep to be killed. - b) to dispose of, to renounce, resign, give over: waby. so to a friend or for destruction) long ago. Mat. 14, 19. Lk. 9, 16. - d) to (ac)curse, condemn to destruction; to destroy utterly. Deut. 20, 17. Josh. 6, 21. - 7. Phr. hyire, white clay, a kind of white earth, used like lime to white-wash houses (sra ɔdaŋ). pr. 150. — bɔ hy., to dig white clay and form it into balls; - bɔ, mã (or sra) obi hy., to make strokes with white clay on some one's body to show that he or she has been acquitted of an accusation, or (gu or mã obi hy.:) that a woman has been set free by her former husband to marry again; - obɔ n'anim hyire, Ak. he rubs his face with white clay, i.e. entirely gives away his slave as a present to another person (- in Akp. only a blow on the slave's back was required for this purpose). — woabɔ me hyirehúnu, they have declar-ed me innocent without giving me any compensation. - gu hyire(w), to divorce. - gye hyirew = di bem. — ɔdɔm hyiréw, 'white clay of grace', i.e. the pardoning of a convict; justification by grace.
[Guaŋ, hiribi, oba a ɔpe agoru, n'ani ye hyew] a light-minded fellow = aperewa; oye ohy. = n'adwenem' ye no hare.
a bicycle; eye mmèraŋ bi.

[red. keka] 1. to bite, to seize or wound with the mouth; okraman aka me naŋ, a dog has bitten my leg; owo ka onipa, the snake bites (man); cf. kaw & sow. pr. 500. 2056. 3448. — 2. to sting: ntontom aka me nsa, a mosquito has stung my hand; cf. bo. pr. 1480.
v. Ak. s. kaw.

v. 1. to remain, be left (where or as it is); Benyamin kaa n'agya ŋkyeŋ wo fie, Benjamin remained at home with his father; mã eŋka! let it remain as it is, let it alone, forbear, leave off, leave it undone! nnyé me ŋka pii, do not keep me too long! eno de, ékà wo aŋkasa nsam' or wo fäm', as for that, it is left to you, that is your own business. pr. 372, 438, 3516. — impers. áká me, I am left; ákà me ŋkó, I only am left; ebeka wo ŋkó, you will be left alone. pr. 1097, 3477 f; ká (= eká) me ŋkó a, aŋkã wobenya nea wope, for aught I have to say, you might obtain what you desire; cf. Gr. § 276,5. pr. 1476-79; cf. to. pr. 3283-86. — 2. ka ho, to remain or continue in a fixed place, in an unchanged form or condition. pr. 4. — 3. ka so, to remain on or in, to abide with: mmere, wonni ŋka so, luxurious life is not indulged in, does not last, for ever. pr. 2036. — 4. ka akyiri, to remain or stay behind (one's companions in walking &c.); to be left unperformed or undone: woaka akyiri, mã wo naŋ so! you lag behind, make haste! yeaka obra akyi, we are quite backward in civilization; - ka nná-akyiri, to go to sleep very late or last. pr. 1481; cf. aka-nna-akyiri. — 5. to die: waka baabi, he is dead; okaa awoee, it died at birth, or, it was still-born. — 6. not to be where it ought to be, to be wanting or missing; generally impers. aka dokono, kofa bẽra! there is no bread here, go and fetch some, - go and fetch it; aka me biribi, I want something; eŋká hō ne hwee, he wants for nothing; eŋka hō bi, nothing is wanting, it is perfect, complete. K. § 267; aka mmofra no bi; wokɔ hẽ? some of the boys are missing; where have they gone? obaakɔ pe na aka, only one is missing; obiara ŋkae ɛ, woŋ nyinaa wo ha, nobody is missing, they are all here; hena na aka? or aka hena? who is missing? aka Kwaku, mighũ no, Kw. is missing, I do not see him; eŋkaa me s, mewo ha! I am not missing, I am here. pr. 1482. Gen. 18,28. - A'kà kúmaa or kàkràa or kète-waa (sè), (very) little is wanting, often corresponds with the adv. almost, nearly, soon: aka kúmaa (sè) na wato nsum', he had almost fallen into the water; aka kúmaa (sè) na dua yi bɛpo, this tree will soon lose its leaves; ekaa kúmaa (F. dé = sè) na woŋ nsa kãã ohene, they nearly caught the king; ekaa nsatea nè werew, aŋkã wokum no, he had a narrow escape from being killed. — 7. ka..mu, to be besieged, blocked up; s. kam'. - wogyee woŋ kaa okwaŋ mu, they were delayed on their journey; amã makam', it has kept me back; - to be missing. pr. 167; to be killed (on the battle-field), to fall; nsráfo pii na ekaam' ho, there (on the field of b.) were many soldiers killed. — 8. ka ano, ('to stick or be accustomed to one's lips'), to be ready, easy, fluent, to have at one's tongue's end: ékà n'ano, he has it at his tongue's end; dwom a misũae no aka m'ano, the hymn I learned is always ready on my lips, or, on my tongue's end; cf. ano B. — 9. ka ase, to remain (over), be left: ekaa ase mproprowa ŋkyereŋkyɛ dumiey, there were left 12 baskets of fragments. — 10. Phr. woaye ŋká obi nnyá obi, they treat all alike.

v. to be common, often met with, usual, frequent; ade a ska (= ewɔ hɔ daa) ni, this is a common thing; saa ŋhoma yi taa ka, such books are often met with; ntama yi ntaa ŋka (= enni maŋ mu daa or pii, wonnyã saa ntama no), such cloth is seldom be had; saa nnomaa yi ŋká dodo, su birds are not very common; woyee y nidɔ a eŋka, they showed us no lit kindness. Esth. 5,2. - aduru no kã̃ n'ano, the medicine touched his mouth. pr. 3315; hwee ŋkã̃ m'ano ɛ, nothing has passed my lips yet; wode kã̃ n'ano, they put it to his mouth. Gen. 27,22; kã̃ nsã yi hwε! try this wine! (Ps. 34,9). - 4. to touch, hit, strike against; to fall upon. 1 Sam 22,18. 1 Kg. 2,29; kã̃ gu, to spill; wakã̃ nsã no agu, he has spilled the wine; kã̃ mogya (gu), to shed blood. - 5. to touch, come to, reach; wo ŋhoma no kã̃ me nsa, your letter came to hand, reached me. - 6. nsa kã̃, to attain to, obtain, receive, get, gain: me nsa akã̃ ŋhoma no, I have received the letter; mesεre wo, wo nsa kã̃ a, mã mente (hõ bi), please, acknowledge receipt! ne nsa kã̃ nea ɔde too ne tirim, he obtained his purpose. Acts 27,13; cf. nsa, Phr. - 7. to touch, to meddle, interfere or have to do with: (mamfã me nsa) maŋkã̃ ŋhoma no, I have not touched the books; de ne hõ kã̃kã̃ ɔbea, to touch a woman. 1 Cor. 7,1; cf. 17a. - me hõ reŋkã̃, I shall have nothing to do with it. - 7a. ne hõ kã̃ mmeã abien yi, he has this twofold position. (pr. 1340). - awere-how bi akã̃ no, some grief has befallen him; nna akã̃ wɔŋ, they were heavy with sleep. Lk. 9,32; asõmdw(o)ee ŋkã̃ mo! peace be unto you! - 8a. to touch, i.e. affect one's feeling, make an impression on: ɔmã m'amanne kã̃ no, he sympathizes with me. Heb. 10,34. - 9. to beat (a drum, akyene, bommaa, atum-paŋ, ɔtents, mpintin). - 10. to strike or flog with (mmaa, mpire, twom); wokã̃ no mpire, they scourged him (Acts 16,23); wokã̃ no dade, Ak. = woakum no. - 11. to make a painful impression on: wadi asm(mone) na akã̃ n'ani = amã n'ani aye no yaw, or wahũ so akatua, he has done something (wrong) and it has affected his eyes (e. g. pepper rubbed into the eyes for punishment), i. e. he has had to suffer for it, has felt the bad consequences in a manner not easily forgotten; memã akã̃ wo ani! I shall let you suffer for it, serve you out for it! - 12. to touch, hurt (pr. 3389 f.), injure, harm, afflict, distress: yeaŋkã̃ wo. Gen. 26,29; to transgress against: yeakã̃ (= yeafom) yeŋ Nyankɔpɔŋ. - 13. kã̃ gya, to hold to the fire for a moment, to wither (green leaves) by fire; fa aba-baŋ yi kã̃ ogya posa sɔ kuru nom', put these leaves to the fire a little and then squeeze them out upon the wound. - kã̃ abe gya, to warm a palm-tree (felled to obtain palm-wine) with fire for the first time; cf. fita, v. - 14. kã̃..hyew,
to warm (up), cook up: kā nsú no byɛw, warm this water! fa ŋkwaŋ no kɔkā no hyew, take that soup and warm it (put it on the fire again!)
to stick together, be closely united in friendship, be on good terms, in union or concord; to agree together; to suit, accord, harmonize; ɔnē no kā or wōkā, they are good friends.
me hō akā (some part of me that was, as it were, attached to the departed, has gone from me, i.e.), I am in trouble about the loss of a relative.

ne hō kā ne hō, lit. his self, or, what is about him, sticks or fits to his self (?), i.e. he is well content, contented, satisfied, pleased, happy, feels comfortable; me hō kā me hō wɔ m'akuraa ha, I live quietly, peaceably here on my plantation; - me hō akā me hō = me hō ato me, cf. ahōmekā.

n'ani kā, his eye is pleased (prop. is attached to or captivated by any pleasing object), i.e. he rejoices, is pleased, rejoiced, delighted, glad, happy; m'ani kā ha (or akā ha, my eye has been caught or attached to, cleaves to this place), I like this place; m'ani akā, I am (or have been for some time in the state of) rejoicing.

n'ani kā ase or fam', lit. his eyes are fixed on the ground, i.e. a) he is bashful, modest, decent, chaste, sober, discreet, considerate, deliberate, careful (= oye n'ade yiye; opp. onipa a n'ani ye sorosoro, oye n'ade sakasaka).
to be in contact with, to adhere to, cleave to, stick to: ewo akā me nsa hō, the honey sticks to my fingers.
to be added, joined to, conjoined, connected with; to be given over or in; to belong to: akyede yi kā wo asranne no hō, this present has been added to your wages.
to accompany (in doing something), to go with, be with: ɔkā me hō na ye-kɔ Osu, he accompanied me to Osu; Onyaŋkɔpɔŋ kā yeŋ hō (= di yeŋ akyi) daa, God is always with us.
kā hō, when connected (as an auxiliary verb) with another principal verb, is often rendered by the adverbs also, moreover, too, besides: odi hĩa na oyare kā hō, he is very poor and sick besides.

de..kā hō, caus. to add, join, annex, unite to: fa kakra kā hō, add a little; in Eng. we may often use the adv. more: mā me kakra mēŋkā hō, give me a little more; ɔmāā me bi mekāā hō, he gave me some more; manyā ŋkesua du, na mepe du makā hō, I have ten eggs and wish for ten more.
kā..hō (aduru), to daub, paint: makā poŋ no hō aduru, I have painted the door (with colour); wakā adaka no hō kokoɔ, he has painted the box red.
kā ne hō, to adorn or dress oneself: wakā ne hō fɛtɛɛfe = wakekā ne hō, she has dressed herself very nicely.
kā..do, F. = kā..hō, di akyi(ri), to join, to follow; wobakā' no do = wobekāā no hō; wōŋkā mo do = mōŋkā me hō, mūnni m'akyi.
be in commotion: ne tirim kā, his head is a little touched, affected with insanity (in a slight degree); he is touched in the head, crackbrained, crazy.
kā ne hō, to move, stir; ɔŋkā ne hō bio, wawu, he moves no more, he is dead; - to bestir oneself, be active, lively, quick; wōŋ'kā wō hō ara'?! will you be quick?
kā..nsa, to be quick, active, agile, alert, diligent; kā wo nsa = kā wo hō, be quick! make haste!
kā ne nsa, he is diligent; (diff. akā ne nsa, it comes to his hands, i.e. he receives).
kā..máti, to rattle or draw up the shoulders, to shrug, give a shrug.
kā aduaŋ, a) to turn food in the mortar with the hand: me kā aduaŋ mamā me (nā.
kā aduaŋ, b) to stir food in cooking on the fire; ode ta abetɛ, ŋkokonte; cf. nū mu.
kā ŋkwaŋ, to ladle out soup and pour back repeatedly while it is boiling the fire.
kā ŋkwaŋ hwe, try the soup by tasting it while it is still on fire in order to see whether it is ready for use.
kā afa, to blow the bellows.
kā atuo, to take arms (prop. guns) in order to fight against some one.

to move, put or set in motion, impel; to drive, compel to move, urge or push forward, urge on a direct the motions of; mframa kā hyen no kɔ anim, the wind moves the vessel onward; kā ŋpuaŋ no kɔ daŋ mu, dī the sheep into the pen! kā ŋkoko no adi, drive the fowls out!
kā teaseɛna, to drive a chariot.
kā (arum) no kɔ ara, drive (the ass) and go forward!
kā..ko, to lead.
to excite, distract, agitate, trouble: ne bone akā no, his sin drives him about restlessly.
to stir (cause, bring about, tokwaw, a quarrel, brawl, scuffle, amanne, mischief (cf. to speak); kā aniwu, to cause shame.
to move, actuate, incite, induce, instigate: deŋ na ekāā no sɛ a-mɛra? what induced him to come?
to attack; kā..akyiri, F. to attack; wokɔkāā wōŋ ŋkāakyiri, they attacked them from behind, gave them the blow, destroyed, ruined them.
kā ŋkwaŋ mu, to commit highway-robbery.
to try to move or stir: ē no baabi èmmá (or, me-, wo-, ɔ-, wo-) no baabi [scil. a,] emma, wherever it is touched, or, try as you will, it does not.

then, in that case; (formerly,) under other circumstances. pr. 189. This word is put at the head of a sentence to indicate that the idea expressed in the sentence is no present reality, but either a) a thing of the past, or b) merely imaginary, its reality being made impossible by another fact or being made to depend on the reality of another idea expressed in a conditional accessory sentence preceding the principal: (a) kaŋ no aŋkǎ Onyaŋkǒpoŋ bɛŋ fam', formerly (it was so, that) God (or Heaven) was near the ground; (b) aŋkǎ mɛba, na meyare nti mintumí memmǎ, I should come, but I cannot, because I am sick; or, sɛ menyare a, aŋkǎ mɛba, if I were not sick, I should come; aŋkǎ mɛba, na biribi asiw me kwaŋ, I should have come, but ('something hindered me') was prevented by something; minní adagyew, aŋkǎ mekyerew wo, I have no time, else I should write to you. Gr. § 141,8. 276,5. - na aŋkǎ! (= na sɛ ente saa de a, na aŋkǎ ědéŋ?) what else? 'of course!'

v. [Ak. also koro, pret. kore; red. koko] to go; more particularly: 1. to go along, to walk (cf. nam, nantew); yékɔ ntém, we are walking fast, obayi-fo a ɔrekɔ ee! there goes a witch! pr. 600. 2. to go off, away; to pass away, leave, depart (opp. ba, to come, trã, to stay); 5kɔ, he is gone (cf. wakɔ under 3); mekɔ mabá, I go away but shall come again, cf. Gr. § 112. 147,4, pr. 1590; F.: kɔ bëra oo = ŋkyé bá! do not stay away long! - woko-bae no wòbekãe se: ewom' sa, when they had gone and returned, they reported, that it was so (that the matter was true); - wobeko, na me de, metrã ha, you will depart, but I shall stay here. - ekɔ-báe sa, or ekɔ-baé sa, it happened or came to pass thus. - to escape. pr. 601. 3. to go to a place: wokɔ hẽ? where are you going? mekɔ ofie, I am going home; okɔ n'akuraa, he has gone to his plantation; perf. wakɔ, he has gone and returned: wákɔ Osú prèkɔ, he has been at Osu once; yere-kɔ wuram', we are going into the bush; ɔkɔo bepow so, he went up a mountain; yebekɔ ɔhene ŋkyen, we shall go to the king. - se waŋkɔ aŋkɔ a, afe mu prekɔ okɔ ho, he goes there at least once a year; éfi ha kɔ B. beye se nɔŋhwerew abieŋ kwaŋ, from here to B. is about two hours'walk; éfi B. kɔ ho beye se dɔŋhwerew biakɔ kwaŋ, from B. to that place is about an hour's walk. - 4. to be going to do something, to set about doing,- with the ingressive prefix kɔ-, ko-, s. Gr. § 93. 96. 107,11. 280,1, b. c. (pr. 300. 1218. 2081 &c.) - 5. to go for some object, with some purpose or intention, used with an infinitive (v. n.) or other other noun: okɔ aduan-to, he has gone to buy food; cf. Gr. § 126. 280,2.* - ɔkɔo anyaŋ, she went for wood (fuel); wòrekɔ asika, they are going to wash gold; kɔ ahayɔ, to go hunting; s. 13-15. - 6. de..kɔ, fa..kɔ; in connection with de, fa or similar verbs the meaning of kɔ (esp. 2. 3) becomes causative: to take away, to take to a place, to lead, conduct: wode no kɔe, they led him away; mã wamfá no pkɔ, let them take him (away or with them). pr. 1332. - 7. In connection with other verbs, kɔ frequently supplies the place of an Eng. adv. or prep.: a) the place of the adv. away, denoting removal: Onyk. ayi m'amanne kɔ, God has taken away my affliction; b) together with a noun of place it supplies the place of a prep., denoting a direction towards a place: oguaŋ kɔɔ habaŋ mu or wuram', he fled into the bush; kã oguaŋ no kɔ daŋ mu, drive the sheep into the pen! wóŋkyekyère ne nsá ŋkɔ n'akyl, they shall tie his hands behind his back; c) woádì mfẽ dú de rekɔ, they are ten years old and upward. pl. ŋkópéŋ, battles; okó wo yené A-kwamfo ntam', there is war between us and the Akwam-people; wakó ŋkópéŋ du, he has fought ten battles; okó hórów, (different) battles; okó abieŋ yi, these two battles. Gr. § 44,2. pr. 1600 ff. 3098.
inf. fighting, war; di akó, to war, be engaged in war, be at war (with); wódi akó = wokó; Akyem nè Asante taa di akó, Akem and Asante are (or were) often at war with each other; cf. akódi.

adv. red, yellow; added to bere, to be or become red, ripe: aŋkaa bere kòɔ, the lemon ripens (or is) yellow. pr. 1504; the low tone of kòɔ may be changed into the high and low tone, whereby the idea of redness is made emphatic: akutu yi abere kòɔ, this orange has become quite red or ripe; ówia rekò kòɔ, the sun is setting. — onipa biara a wónè ne behyia na óda kòɔ, everybody whom they meet is done for. — kòɔ may be used as a predicative adj. when the verb is omitted (Gr. § 248,3 a): hwe no, n'ani koɔ! look at him, how red his eyes are! in other cases the form of the adj. is kokòɔ, q.v. — kòɔ, kokòɔ, are applied to different shades of red, brown and yellow, and likewise the v. bere and the adj. -bɛŋ (in cpds.), F. meŋ memmeŋ, memmene; whereas fiery red seems to be denoted by deŋ'ŋ, yɛŋŋ, yɛmmeŋŋ, scarlet or vermilion by -dam (in cpds.) and damɛrámá, crimson by -dam (cf. adam) and the v. bere-dum; cf. a-kutuhono, orange-coloured, aŋkaahono, yellow (as lemons), bofua (odubɛŋ), yellow; dodowee, brown.
kòkòɔ, kòkòkòɔ, adv. used with kyi or taŋ, to hate; òtaŋ no kòɔ, he hates him ardently, fervently, passionately, extremely, he abhors him.
the unicorn, oryx, an antelope, in size nearly equal to a horse or cow, furnished with one horn on the forehead; spoken of, as really existing, from Fante to Krepe. [G. ŋmãŋma].

pl. ŋ- [akowá, orig. akobá] 1. A male, man; fellow; akoa no hó yɛ fɛ, that is a handsome fellow; akoa no dii hene pi, that man showed himself a king indeed (a saying elicited from a native by the description of Solomon's throne. 1 Kg. 10,20). 2. A male slave; bondman, serf. pr. 110. 131f. 352. 1611 ff. 2946. 3. a servant, subject; Kokófu hene yɛ Asante hene akoa; Akyem hene ŋkoa dósó seŋ A-kwam hene de. — In cpd. words akoa is changed into kwa or kwaa and ko; cf. akokoa, akwakora (= a-kwakwaraa), akwaŋkwaa, abɛŋkwaa, awurakwaa; Kwadwo, Kwaaku (Gr. § 41,4), Kofi, Kofori &c.
