[bo kɔŋ] 1. talk, chat, familiar discourse, conversation. pr. 117. — bɔ ŋk., di ŋk., (F. twɛtwɛ ŋk.), to converse; me nè no bɔ (n'a-kwantu hɔ) ŋk., I converse with him (about his journey); deŋ ŋk. or ŋk. beŋ na mobɔ yi? what are you conversing about? what is your conversation? — 2. concern, care, sorrow, solicitude; eye me ŋkommo-mú, it is my heartfelt desire; mã yeŋkɔpe yeŋ ŋk. pá bi nni, we have better things to do (lit. care about) [than to sit here]. — 3. complaint, lamentation. — di ŋk., to complain, lament, moan; odi ne nua hɔ ŋk., odi ŋk. mã ne nua, he moans about his brother. — 4. beads worn round the neck; me ŋk. ni, mede merebo me kɔŋ. — ŋkəmmə-bó, ŋkəmmədi, inf. discourse, conversation. — ŋkəmmə-dí, inf. lamentation. — ŋkəmmədifó, pl. id. lamenter, moaner.

di .. ŋk., to simulate sympathy with a suffering person. pr. 662. — ŋkəmmədómfó, pl. id. = ŋkəmmodifo a ogoru nnipa hɔ, one who simulated sympathy and behind the mourner's back ridicules or censures him.
talkativeness, loquacity, by which others are prevented from taking their due part in the conversation. pr. 3569.
inf. [to ŋk., to meet conver-sation]: ɔsram ye ŋk., the moon comes up at the time of evening conversation, in the days following the full moon, about 7 or 8 o'clock.
inf. F. conversation.
a short discourse.
[nea obua ɔkəm] a provider against hunger. pr. 3106.
a pair of compasses. Isa. 44, 13.
a bird between the eagle and vulture.
reluctance. — ŋk.-do, grudgingly.
= Afútufó, a tribe in Fante, speaking their own language (Guan?) besides the F. — The Tshi people consider them as uncivil, or, counting them among the "potofo", as less civilized than themselves.
an uncivilized fellow, 'bushman' [lit. (he) has never been to the coast].

inf. [pono kɔŋ, or koŋmu pono] unwillingness; indignation, vexation, annoyance, trouble. — ŋkəmpón-adé, vexatious things, annoyances; daa batafo ye me ŋk. = hyɛ me anibere. — ŋk(r)əmpóno-sò, unwillingly, reluctantly.
[con. ne kó...] struma, goiter; s. donnorohu, duhuru.
bu ŋk. or k., to turn the head (prop. neck) in order to look round about or back: obu ŋk. hwe woŋ nyinaa, obu ŋk. hwe u'akyi; wammú nè kómpəw, he did not look behind him.
necklace, string of beads. Cant. 1, 10; ahene k. da ne kɔŋ mu (ahyia ne kɔŋ pɛ), atwa ne kɔŋ ahyia pú = esi ano pɛ); s. kɔ̃nã.
ŋkotɔ, inf. slumber.
inf. quietness, tranquillity, silence. Ps. 115, 17.
inf. [bu koŋ] breaking one's neck. pr. 1761. 2990.
defeat; di k., to suffer a defeat; s. ŋkōgu.
(full o), the gurgling noise of liquor pouring from a bottle; prattle. pr. 2742; also the noise of a bottle or pot full of liquor put or set up somewhere.
v. s. red. koŋkoŋ.

Ak. kono, the neck of a man's or animal's body; the slender part of the arm, s. bakoŋ; neck of a vessel. pr. 1380; bank of a river, s. nsukoŋ; throat, cf. menewa; - duá koŋ, the top of a tree; the part near its top. - ne kóŋ dò (aduaŋ, owu), lit. his throat deepens for, i.e. he longs for, lusts after, desires, covets, (food, pr. 3215, death); owu dò no (or ne) koŋ, he listeth to die; nnipa a ade dò woŋ koŋ, covetous, greedy, lustful people (Nu. 11,34). - de.. bo.. koŋ hō, to put something on the shoulder. Josh. 4,5. - óbò ne kóŋ, he speaks out in conversation, pours out his heart. - nusu abu ne koŋ, he is weeping bitterly; tears stifled his voice; cf. nusu. - obiara soa ne koŋ, every one is arrogant, proud. - ototo ne koŋ, he turns his neck about in show, display, in contempt, or disobedience; he looks, about in a haughty, contemptuous, impudent manner; ototo ne k. kyɛa, onam na ototo ne k., or, onam ne k. so, he walks in an affected manner, behaves proudly; cf. kyɛa. - ne koŋ hardens his neck. Prov. 29,1. - kóŋ-akyì, the back part of the neck, nape; wokura yeŋ k. kā yeŋ ko, by our necks we are driven. Lam. 5,5; afei yekura adwuma yi k., now we have this work fully in our grasp or power, have got the better of it, are able to manage it at pleasure. - kóŋ-mù, kóŋ-mù, the inner parts of the neck; the throat, in the throat; in or round about the neck: sika ntweabaŋ gu ne koŋ mu, he wears a gold chain round his neck (cf. Gen. 41,42). pr. 2844; ode sika bi (i.e. akrakoŋmu) ato ne koŋ mu=wabɛye ok'rá, he has become a body-slave; s. ok'rá 3. - ne kópmú yè deŋ, his neck is strong, enabling him to carry heavy loads on his head; osafohɛne no koŋ mu ye deŋ, that chief bears (as it were) or commands a large, powerful army; - yede tow no yii yeŋ koŋ mu afɔa, by that tribute we warded off the war or destruction impending over our heads; - yeayi yeŋ koŋmu ahuruhuro = yeayi adwuma a eye deŋ afi yeŋ koŋ mu. - Cf. ŋkoŋ-mu.
solitary, lonely; e.g. kwae mu ye kóŋŋ.
the sound of the dawuru; metee se dawuru bi da so k. k. k., I heard the d. sound.
necklace, string of beads. Cant. 1,10; gbene a wɛasina no hama 1 so a ahyia koŋmu pe; s. kompu.
osekantia k., a knife without a handle. pr. 2851.

[nea ne ŋkõ nam] 1. a lone traveller, a person walking or travelling alone, without a companion. pr. 1706-9; ye aŋk., to be desolate. Ps 25,16; waye aŋk., he has become a lone traveller; he is in despair, looks about him in desperation; cf. atobisa. - 2. a species of beetle. - 3. aŋk. (afiri), bicycle, velocipede.
a certain plant; s. otokotaka.
[akɔm daŋ] a house in which soothsayers have their business; syn. akomfodaŋ. [G. gbaṭšu].
Ak, a nickname of the Apagyafó.
[akɔm, ɔdawuru] pl. id. fetish-bell.
F. = akɔnnɔ.
inf. going and coming. pr. 1595 f. 2483. - di ak., to go to and fro; de..di ak., to drive and toss. Ja. 1,6. - ak.-dí, inf. intercourse, communication; commerce.
F. s. ŋkonnyã, miracle &c.
[akwaŋhãmá] subsistence, sustenance, livelihood, means of support.

to provide for; onipa yi, me na mebo no ak., this man is supported or fed by me. pr. 3635. - akɔŋhama-bɔ, inf. the act of maintaining, maintenance, subsistence. - akɔŋhamabɔ-de, akɔŋhamá-de, means of support, subsistence, provisions; allowance. - akɔŋhama-(bɔ) sukuu, -sũabea, boarding school.
inf. [skoŋ] distortion or spraining of the neck.
inf. [huro kɔm] lit. derision of hunger, the annual feast of the Akra people at the harvest of corn and yam; cf. odwira. [G. hɔmowɔ].
[akɔm ŋhyease] the prediction given in soothsaying. pr. 1703.

a. & adv. silent, absolutely still, speechless, perfectly quiet; waye k.; me nè no kasa a, ogyina ho k., ommua me bi; syn. kòmm, démm, díŋŋ. koniabɔ, better: kwaniabɔ, = akoa a n'ani abo no = anitore.

[ɔkõ, nĩm] victory, triumph. pr. 624; ŋk. abirá ne ŋkõgu, the contrary of victory is defeat. - di ŋk., to be victorious, to triumph. Col. 2,18. - ŋkõním-bɔ, reward or prize of victory. Col. 2,18. - ŋkõním-dí, inf. victory. - ŋkõnimdí-fó, pl. id. victor.
Akp. Aky. 1. a tree similar to tweneboa. - 2. a shrub whose (red) seeds contain red colouring-matter.
Okw. a tree = okoniŋ 1.
collar-bone; s. kãntãŋ.
si k., to retail; to broke.
pl. ŋ-, tumpler, large drinking glass. [Gä: kɔ, mikɔ = wofa a, mefa, e.s. wonom biakɔ, me nso menom biakɔ].

twi: koŋkóm ne hō, kɔŋkɔm ne hō
eng: v. red. & refl., to be puffed up, flushed, proud; to strut, flaunt, look big; syn. kyerɛ ne hō; wak. ne hō he = watrã hō se ɔhene bi na ompé se ɔye hwee.
ohye no ŋk. = ɔkɔkɔ no, he spoils him &c.
a game like hopscotch; s. akukomfi.
ascaris, pl. ascarides.
wabu ak., he stoops;
subsistence, sustenance, livelihood, means of support.
to provide for; onipa yi, me na mebɔ no ak., this man is supported or fed by me. pr. 3635.
inf. the act of maintaining, maintenance, subsistence.
means of support, subsistence, provisions; allowance.
sũabea, boarding school.
inf. [skɔŋ] distortion or spraining of the neck.
inf. [huro kɔm] lit. derision of hunger, the annual feast of the Akra people at the harvest of corn and yam; cf. odwira. [G. hɔmɔwɔ].
[akɔm hyease] the prediction given in soothsaying, pr. 1703.
a. & adv. silent, absolutely still, speechless, perfectly quiet; waye k., me ne no kasa a, ogyina hɔ k., ommua me bi; syn. kòmm, démm, diŋŋ.
better: kwaniabɔ, = akoa a n'ani abɔ no = anitore.
[ɔkɔ, nim] victory, triumph. pr. 624; yk. abirá ne ŋkɔgu, the contrary of victory is defeat. — di. ŋk., to be victorious, to triumph. — ŋkɔním-bɔ, reward or prize of victory. Col. 2, 18.
inf. victory.

eng: v. red. & refl., to be puffed up, flushed, proud; to strut, flaunt, look big; syn. kyerɛ ne hɔ; wak. ne hɔ te hɔ = watrã hɔ se ɔhene bi na ɔmpé se oye hwee.
a game like hopscotch; s. akukomfi.
ascaris, pl. ascarides.
wabu ak., he stoops; he is crook-backed; adesoaso bebree nti ne mu akurum na pɔw kakra bi aba n'akyi.

v. red. to be pending; to hang (down); to wave, soar, hover; demmere a abukaw na ekɔŋkɔŋ hɔ no, ommú no koraa (Isa. 42, 3); ɔdaŋ, akenteŋgua no k., hɔ, the house, the chair, is crazy, rickety, does not stand firm; ɔk. ne naŋkroma nè ne nsa so, he couches or cowers on his knees and hands. Dan. 10, 10; anõma bi k. daŋ no so, a bird soars over that house.
F. to be bruised: ndzembir a wakɔŋkɔŋ. Mt. 12, 20.
meagre, lean, thin; waye kɔŋ kɔŋkɔŋ, he has become very thin or lean; cf. kɔŋkũrɔŋ, fɔŋ.
a bird; s. asu-kɔŋkɔŋ.
a. dark, pitch-dark, deep, full, added to anadwo, night, ɔdasu, midnight; wofi ǎnadwo kɔŋkɔŋ or kkk. agoru agoru, they began in the dead of night and have played until now.
bo wo kɔŋ hɔ, put it (the pole of the hammock) on your shoulder.
a children's cough; (w)hooping-cough; dry cough.

a discolouring of the skin of natives, ascribed to too much sitting by the fire. Wotaa trã ogya hɔ a, na sye wo naŋ hɔ ŋkɔkɔ-ŋkɔkɔ, na woda hɔ a, sye wo akyi nso saa; mmerewa bi woda ogya pii no na etaa ye woŋ; nea aye pii na aye kɔɔ, na nea anye pii no na aye atuntum-atuntum a. s. ŋwraŋwraŋ.
adv. not firmly; opp. kuaw; so biribi mu k., to take hold lightly of something.
flattering, enticing words.
a certain green locust.
a kind of yam; ŋkani kɔkɔɔ; s. ɔde.
falsehood, duplicity, double-dealing, dissimulation, hypocrisy; ɔyè ŋk. — syn. ŋkóntompo, nnabrabá. — ɔ-kɔŋkɔnsáni, pl. ŋ-fo, a false, insincere, treacherous, hypocritical, double-

ode besii kwaŋmu. — 3. to make expressions, to use circumlocution: m a mede mibisaa no nyinaa, ɔde ɔkwaŋe ansã-na ode besii kwaŋ mu; asem no hɔ, ɔmfã nto kwaŋmu; de, wudi asem a, wope sse wode k. io! — akɔŋkwáŋ, inf. digression(s), cumlocution.
[akɔm, akyene] a fetish-drum, ten when a fetish-man performs.
kã ŋk., to put an end to.
s. akɔŋ. pr. 1768.
the axil or lla formed by a branch, shoot, or ny shoots, with the stem of a plant; young shoots rising from an axilla sheathing leaf, the new blades of ms, plantains &c. pr. 1608. 2720.
strength in the neck. pr. ).

twi: ., v. k. doté, to work or prepare earth clay, for building purposes by mixing with water and working it with a ; cf. wow; wòkòno dote de tare ) hɔ, s. tãre.

eng: [okɔ ano] the front of the battle. 312; F. field of battle.
[kɔŋ dɔ] lust, appetite, longing, ire, cupidity, concupiscence. pr. 23; wiase ak., worldly lusts; hɔnam nè aniwa ak. 1 John 2, 16. — éyè ak., it excites a desire in him. Cf. bere.

a thing eagerly desired, ect of lust; desire. Ps. 78, 29; pleasure. 133. — akónnɔ-ŋhyɛsé, passion, tfulness. Col. 3, 5. — akónnɔ-dúaŋ, toury meat, favourite dish. Gen. 4; dainty food. Job 33, 20. — akɔnnɔ-i-bra, chastity. — akónnɔ-sò, for asure. pr. 641; F. with delight, cheerly. 2 Cor. 9, 7.
Ak. s. kɔŋ-mu, ŋkɔŋmu.
s. akrɔŋ, 5rɔŋ, kroŋkroy.
kōma, heart.
a species of spider, sping strong yellow threads; s. ananse-1. — kónnore-búw, cocoon.
akrɔŋ, nine (Mf. Gr.).
ŋkɔnsĩaw.
explanation of soothsaying practices.
stiffneckedness, stubbornness, obstinacy. Judg. 2, 19.
kónsòmiri [Eng.] constable.
ówò no ŋk. = ɔpo no taw, óhòŋ no, ósùm n' atiko, he seizes or pushes him by the nape; s. wo 10.
As. to hobble, halt; Akp. si sii.
[ekɔŋ] headless body, trunk; torso; cf. akúntuŋsi.
kontromfi, chimpanzee. pr. 1871; baboon?
chain; fetters; cf. ntweabaŋ; wógù no ŋk., they bind him with chains.
a climbing leguminous plant; its fruit, the Calabar-bean, Ordeal-bean. The large brown reniform seed is highly poisonous.
= koranta, a drum-stick?
the wife's brother, brother-in-law; s. akóntagye. pr. 2814.

[Port. conta] account, reckoning, calculation, computation; bill; cf. akano; number, cf. dodow, ano. — ak. seŋkyerene, cipher. — (ye or) bu ak., to cast up an account, to calculate, compute, reckon. Mt. 18, 23. — fa ak. no hye ŋhomam', put down the account on paper; fa ak. no hye wo tirim, na wokɔ a, woakà akyere no, keep the account in your mind that, when you go, you can tell him. — ode n'ak. nyinaa ba pepeɛpe, he pays his bills very regularly. — afe or afrihyia ak., annual account or bill. — akóntaa-hyéde, number. Rev. 15, 2. — akóntáà-kyèrɛweɛ, figure, numeral. Rev. 13, 17.
[bu ak.] reckoning, ciphering, arithmetic; account. - ak.-tie, audit.
akónta. pr. 295; 2814 is a pun: akónta gye, brother, take!
a large tree with edible fruit.
1. a matter (palaver) between or concerning (two) brothers-in-law. — 2. intercourse between them; asɛm a ewɔ akónta nè akónta ntam'.
[ekɔŋ tenten]: obɔ ŋk. hwe, he stretches his neck to look.
[ekɔŋ, tia] a species of small black fly.
club; cf. asabaa, aporibaa, apotibaa.
[tet. kwentiwa] a species of gourd used in tanning leather. pr. 1711.
kɔntoŋ, q. v.
ŋkàntɔŋ.
a certain tree.
the young tender leaves of the kokoo plant. pr. 1713.
[usu. only plur.]: mmarima ak. baasɔŋ, seven strong men.

falsehood, falseness, unfairness; insincerity, duplicity, double-dealing; dishonesty; hypocrisy; slanderous lie, calumny; perfidy, treachery; syn. ŋkɔŋkɔnsá, nnabrabá; cf. nseku, ntwiri, nyàatwom. pr. 754 f. 1025. — twa (no or no hɔ) ŋk., to be false, dishonest; to tell lies, bear tales; to slander, calumniate; to deceive, delude; to act or deal perfidiously, treacherously. pr. 3402 f.

slanderer, liar, calumniator, backbiter; talebearer; hypocrite; perfidious or treacherous fellow, traitor. pr. 1714. — ose asɛm bi na ɔye wɔ nnipa anim, na onyé no kokoam'; syn. ɔtɔrofo, kɔŋkɔnsáni, dabrabáfó, fátwafó.
brag, boasting, pretension, ostentation; ɔye ŋk., he brags, makes a show as if he possessed riches which he has not.

[red. kontɔkɔntoŋ, kɔntɔŋkɔntɔŋ] to bend, curve, make crooked; to be bent, curved crooked; to be perverse. Mt. 17, 17; okwaŋ, duabasa no ak.; dua, ɔfasu no mu ak.; asu no kontokɔntɔŋ piij.; syn. kɔm, kùntũŋ, kùrum, kyea, pono; cf. kontɔŋkyẽ.
kontɔŋ, to lead about. Ex. 13,18.
bay, bight, gulf; ɛpo abu k., the sea forms a bay; cf. dɔnnɔn, braka.

that which has numerous curves and windings, or forms curious complicated figures, or is entangled, intricate; arabesques, ornaments of furniture, garnish; flourish (in writing); dua no abãa nyina aye yk. = akyeakyea pii.
kɔntɔŋkɔntɔŋ, red. v. s. kɔntɔŋ.

kɔntɔŋkrɔŋ, a. circular, round, in the shape of a ring; diff. korokorow, kurukuruwa, puruw. — n. a round, ring, circle, circumference, circuit; cf. dantabaŋ, haŋkare, katraka; - linea fusca (of pregnant women). — bɔ k., to make a circle; bɔ twa.. hɔ k., to go round a thing; cf. twa.. hɔ hyia or si.
1. the halo or luminous circle round the sun or moon, pr. 1712. 2844. — 2. sickle; syn. kãntãŋ-kráŋkyi, kãnikyi.
kɔntɔŋkyé, a. 1. crooked, curved, bent, wry, tortuous (dua, poma, okwaŋ), pr. 998. 1014. — 2. distorted, perverted, perverse (Prov. 2,12), dishonest (nneyɛ); untoward, froward, refractory. pr. 2626.
iniquity. Mic. 3,10. Zeph. 3,13. — ɔ-kɔntɔŋkyéŋí, ɔ-kɔntɔŋkyéfo, pl. a- -fo, a perverse, froward, unjust person. 2 Sam. 22,27. Ps. 18,27. Zeph. 3,5.

akɔntɔŋkyé-sɛm, intrigue; trick, artifices, machinations, crooked ways, i.e. dealings, crooks (of the heart &c.); frowardness; perverse things, perverseness, wrong-doing. Prov. 2,14. 23,33. Jer 9,4; ak, ano, a perverse mouth. Prov. 8,13; n'ak. a obekekae ny. abɔ no so or abua n'atifi. — di ak. = twa ŋkɔntɔmpo, ye ade a entɛe.
Akw. = ŋkɔntɔmpo.
abe hɔ biribi, the inner bark of a palm-tree, bast.
okwasea.
a species of beaver.
ŋ- [akɔm, atoro] a deceitful oracle, lie in soothsaying; di or hye ak., to prophesy falsely. Jer. 20,6. 27,10. pr. 1697. 2949.
a beetle with crooked legs.

a species of monkey, chimpanzee; other names: obiade-wɔno, [G. adu], adu-onnɔ-mma, akɔnsɔŋ, eku, ekú-mɛrɛme, kwagyadu, kwagyate, kwaforɔ-amotakyi, kwafea, kakaewadwe, kwagyenana, akyɛmfoo, oniŋkwaa, ampokuru-sũmsre, asesãboa. pr. 154. 195. 237. 1445. 1715 ff. 1875.
(pl.) messengers, ambassadors; syn. abɔfó. [tina.
accordion, harmonica, concertina; ŋkɔntwékɔntwé, adv. limpingly, totteringly; nam k., to walk lamely, to totter, stagger (from infirmity through sickness or old age).
-bée, in a state or condition of infirmity; oyare no gyaw me pk., the sickness has left me in, or reduced me to, a feeble condition.

Ak- ŋwa, pl. ŋ- [akɔŋ, agua] the common stool of the natives, a low stool neatly carved out of one piece of wood; also the king's stool, throne, s. aheŋŋua. pr. 1710. 2603. 3376. [When a man has his stool carried after him, it is carried by his attendant not on the head, but on the shoulder, at the neck (kɔŋ) or nape, prob. from some superstitious notion, cf. butuw]. Wotu ŋkɔŋguam', they turn their stools (in honour of a respectable person or of a fetish); aye akoŋŋua nè kyem, now we are in a great difficulty (or strait)! e.g. owing to unforeseen expenses. kɔ.. ŋkɔŋguakyiri, to die (said of a king or chief).
pl. ŋ-, a carrier of the king's stool, s. gyaasefo.
[the 7 principal stools] the 7 elders who form the council of the king or chief.
okónum, 1. a kind of shrub; cf. fofráhã. — 2. a large tree; ɛhɔ fitaa sè.
a mean, vile, paltry, worthless, despicable, miserable = bŭrohono.
akɔnnyóm [akɔm dwom] id. a fetish-song.
f. ŋkongya(a), miracle, wondrous miraculous act; - yi ŋk., to perform a miracle. — inf. ŋkonyãá-yí, ntafowa-yi.
s. ŋkonyobi.
a miraculous act or ace ye ŋk.; cf. aŋwɔnywãde.
a performer or worker of miracles; cf. osumanni.
[akɔm, gyigye] training in the performances of a "komfo".
1. a certain amulet; suman b: wode pe ɔdo ana mmea; wode bibi nè ahene nè aboa bi ŋhwi na eye. 2. water-melon (?). pr. 1778.
ŋkonnyábí, the thorn apple, Jamestown weed; Datura stramonium. Hos. 10,4.
Ak. = eko, buffalo.
pl. a!, a warlike man; ahe ak., warlike kings.
pl. a-, a mound of earth or embankment thrown up for fighting or defence, bulwark, rampart, fortification; palisade, stockade; cf. pem.
pl. ŋ- [s. ɔkɔ] a single fight, battle, action; wakɔ ŋk. du, he has fought ten battles.
a place for defensive fighting, bulwark, fortification, entrenchment.
pl. a-, defender, champion.
F. [Eng.] cup.
the last struggle (of life), agony.

pl. a- [con. nè k’ra, nè kàra] 1. the soul of man, pr. 11. According to the notions of the natives the kàra of a person exists before his birth and may be the soul or spirit of a relation or other person already dead (cf. bra, v. 3) that is in heaven or with God and obtains leave to come again into this world (cf. Ababio). When he is thus dismissed in heaven, he takes with him his errand, i.e. his destination or future fate is fixed beforehand; from this the name ɔkra or abra-bɔ, q. v. The kàra, put by God or by the help of a fetish into a child, can be questioned while it is yet in the mother's womb (cf. hweŋ). In life the kàra is considered partly as the soul or spirit of a person (cf. sunsum, hoŋhom), partly as a separate being, distinct from the person, who protects him (me kra di m'akyi), gives him good or bad advice, causes his undertakings to prosper (pr. 83) or slights and neglects him (cf. ɔkrabiri), and, therefore, in the case of prosperity, receives thanks and thank-offerings like a fetish (cf. asumguare). When the person is about to die, the kàra leaves him gradually, before he breathes his last, but may be called or drawn back (cf. twè kra). When he has entirely left (whereby the person dies), he is no more called kàra, but sèsà or ɔsà-māŋ. — 2. destiny, fate, lot, luck, fortune; nè kàra yé, he has good luck (can be said even of game that escaped the shot of a hunter); ne kra ye a eye nti..., nè k’ra yiye (yieyie, very), fortunately, happily, luckily; ne kra nyé = ne hò ade nyé. pr. 1760; cf. ehò B, ɔkrabiri. — 3. Of asáŋka, a dish, wide (open) and less deep, we note: abeyâ, aboyâ, Ak. = asáŋka; abuabuogyásó, akyem-asaŋka, kwãnséŋ, ananánówa, oposi, asaŋka-sãnyãã, asáŋkasoŋ (has a foot), taapoasaŋka, ntrɔtrówá.

v. Ak. kū [red. kuŋkum] 1. to kill, slay, put to death. pr. 26. 126. 339. 1673. 1806 ff. 2192 ff. 2444; wɔakum no, euph. wɔayi no hɔ, they have executed him; hyperbolically, to denote a strong sensation: awɔw, okɔm rekum me, the cold, hunger, is killing me, i.e. I am very cold, very hungry; bɔrɔ rekum me, I am suffering from scabies. 2. to defeat, overcome, vanquish, destroy; k. dɔm, to beat the enemy, conquer, gain the victory. pr. 1990. 3. to cause to cease: ókùm mé-kóm, he stills my hunger; but: ókùm-me kóm, he kills me with hunger, i.e. he starves me; k. sukom, to quench the thirst; k. kuru, to heal a sore. pr. 1038. 4. to tire (out), weary, wear out: wokum nnipa nẽ kasa, nseŋhunu, serew = wɔde kasa... kum nnipa, they tire one out with talking, with nonsense, make one die with laughing. 5. to silence: mikum no aniwu, I silence him with shame, i.e. I stop his mouth, make him ashamed to speak. 6. to disfigure: okum n'anim = omuna n'anim, he darkens his face, makes a dark, angry, or sad face; wak. n'anim, he is sullen, vexed, moody. 1 Kg. 20,43. 21,4. 7. to defile, pollute, desecrate: obi kum fi mu a, wɔde ŋyuan mogya n.a. na wɔde dwiram', if one defiles his dwelling, it is purged or purified by the blood of sheep &c. 8. (k. ano) to hinder from using, to stop, prevent, obstruct: okum ɔbosom ano, he prevents the fetish from eating the new yam offered to him, by transgressing a fetish-law. 9. (k. ano) to prevent the effect or efficiency of, to render ineffective, inefficient: wakum aduru no ano = ɔde nea aduru no kyi akã no, he has made the medicine ineffective (by adding to, or eating with it, some other thing incompatible with

to surpass, go beyond, exceed, excel, be larger than. pr. 2939; syn. sɛŋ, cf. tra. It is used for the comparative form of Eng. adjectives and the conj. than; after another verb it is translated by more than, better than, rather than, when negative, by not so .. as, not more .. than. Dabodabo yɛ kyɛŋ akokɔ, a duck is larger than a fowl; ɔkyɛŋ no akyene-ká, he outdoes him in beating the drum; Onyame ghyira ye kyɛŋ sika, God's blessing is better than gold; metumi mayɛ kyɛŋ nea wosusuw, I shall be able to do more than they think; moanyin seŋ me, enti mutu mmirika kyɛŋ me, you are older than I, therefore you can run better; biribi ŋkyɛŋ ogya kɔkɔɔ, nothing is so red as (or more red than) fire. pr. 413. 467. Gr. § 73. -- kyɛŋ so (without an expressed object of comparison), to be eminent, excellent, superior; nnéema à ékyɛŋ' so, extraordinary things.

a. & adv. very hard, dry, stiff; cf. kyɛŋ & kyɛŋkyɛŋ, v. — nām no ayɛ kyɛŋkyereŋ, the fish (or meat) is well dried; asase no mu (or so) ye kyɛŋkyɛnɛŋ (or kyɛŋky.) = emu akyɛŋ or awo, the land is hard and dry, arid, meagre, lean (Nu. 13,20), barren; ne ntama no aṣeŋ ky.; ne nsa seŋ ky. or kyɛŋe kesee, 1 Kg. 13,4. — wàkyɛŋ kyɛŋkyereŋ, he has become stiff (in his body or joints, and been so for some hours): eyé akɔsé àbiribiri-twa, syn. ade atɔ no so, ahunmu ato (or asi) no so.
a kind of hurdle placed on rapids to catch fish.

F.; kyere, Ak. = kye, v. to last, endure; waŋkyere so, he was not long (e.g. in speaking or preaching); F. mambekyer', I am not to remain long; ɔbekyer ahɛ, how long will it last? bekyer ahɛ ŋkɔ, how long (wilt thou stay away)? Ps. 90,13; - ŋkyère oó! (do not stay out long!) I hope to see you again.
[kye, v. to last &c.] a delay, lingering, prolonged stay; mephyé-wò kyére, I do not detain you, will not cause you a delay or detention; wan-nye ky. yɛe ntɛm kɔɔ ho, he hastened there without delay.

[red. kyekyere, q. v.] 1. to catch, lay hold on, seize (by pursuit); to take captive (ky. or fa dommum), apprehend; to detain; agyinamoa ky. ŋkura, akrɔmā ky. ŋkoko; ɔkyère ŋkoko. pr. 86. 235 ff. 3111. 1954-57; ky. asem, Lk. 11,54; ahɔpopo kyere no, trembling takes hold on him. Ex. 15,14; cf. yketeŋkété. — 2. to bind, tie round (adare, the handle of a bill-hook). Cf. dwere. — 3. to become thick, to curd, curdle, clot, concrete or coagulate into a thick in-spissated mass; to crystallise; nufusu no aky., the milk has curdled. — 4. ..mu ky., a) to be narrow; ɔdaŋ yi mu ky., this room is narrow; opp. mu gow, to be spacious. b) to be hurried and indistinct in pronunciation: Aburi-fo kasa mu kyere, e.s. wókasa ntɛm-ntɛm na emu ntew a.s. emu nná hɔ. — 5. kyere mu, to interweave, (tissue), variegate; to embroider. Ezek. 27,7; woaky. mu = otamaŋwénefó adi mu adwini; s. ŋkyeremú. — 6. to be in great distress or straits: ne hɔ kyere no = ne hō hĩa no wɔ mmaa nyinaa, he is in great trouble; ne tirim aky. no (e.s. asɛm bi aye no ehü né awere-ho nyinaa), he has become distracted, out of his senses or wits. - hyéŋ akyère no, he is sea-sick. — 7. to press or be pressed together; kyere so, to throng, crowd: nnipa no aky. so, the people are crowded together; wókyère nó sò, they throng him. Lk. 8,45; wókye-kyeré tów, they huddle together into a cluster, swarm or crowd; s. ɛtɔw. — 8. kyere

(or kyekyérè) sá, to prepare for war (by collecting an army &c.); wákyère me hó sà-boné, he has planned, devised or determined evil against me. 1 Sam. 20,7.9. 33. — 9. to show or manifest ill will, hostility, animosity, aversion, to bear malice, to make one feel a grudge; s. ŋkyeree.

[red. kyerekyere, q. v.] 1. to show forth, produce, exhibit, present to view (often preceded by de, fa, yi, with the object that is shown): fa mfonini yi kyere no, show him these pictures! mede maky. no (or, maky. no mf.); - fa wo hó or yi wo hó kyere, show yourself! okyere ne hó (dodo), he is ostentatious, boastful, vaunting. pr. 382. 1318. - yi..kyere, to manifest, reveal, make known. John 1,31. 2,11; to profess, pretend, cf. 9. - mekyere-wo nsã, your health! Answer: énko wo yiye, may it do you good. — 2. to show, point out (to); to guide or lead to; kyere no kwaŋ, show him the way! kyere no oday a obedam', lead him to the room where he is to sleep! pr. 1617. 1653. — 3. kyere ase, to show the reason, meaning, sense, i.e. to explain, interpret. pr. 1950. 1908; to upbraid or abuse somebody by reminding him of his ancestors; kyere ano, to state or declare the amount, number, weight &c., F. to declare. — 4. to teach, instruct in: mekyeree no ghoma-kaŋ, I taught him to read (cf. red.); kyere..ade, to teach, instruct; cf. kyerekyere. — 5. to advise, counsel, exhort: okyeree no se óŋŋuaŋ, he advised him to flee. pr. 226. — 6. to be in the direction of or have a situation toward, to front, face, to look toward: adannim ky. apuei, the front of the house looks eastward; ne mfen-sere ky. abonteŋ so, his window faces or looks into the street. — 7. After another verb, ky. often shows the direction of an action and is rendered in Eng. by the prep. toward (Gr. § 223,4): oterew ne nsam' kyere osoro, he spreads forth his hands toward heaven; or it denotes the reference to a person and is rendered by to: kã..kyere, to speak or relate to, to tell, give instruction or information to, to inform: okãã ne dae kyeree no, he told him his dream; wányã asém no ŋkã ŋkyeree, he has often inculcated this matter; - to make known, reveal. John 1,18. — 8. kasa kyere, a) to speak to. pr. 513. — b) to instruct, exhort, admonish. pr. 911. — 9. to do for a pretence: wobo mpae tenteŋ kyere, they for a pretence make long prayers. Mt. 23,14; to profess. 1 Tim. 6,21; cf. 1: yi kyere. — 10. Phr. enyé obi nã ókyere, it is a matter of course. — 11. wotow tuo kyere borohene, they fire guns in honour of the governor; ode tuo kyere no, he aimed a musket at it (or him).
F. unless, except (= gye); till, until: modo wo ky. owu apa hen mu, I shall love thee till death us do part; cf. kyere-de.
inf. Ak. = okyé, long duration, time. pr. 1949.
the act of teaching; doctrine, rule, precept, instruction.
Ak. = akrakoŋmu; cf. the following.
precious beads and pieces (ingots) of gold, fastened round the wrist; s. okrakyere.
inf. catching &c.; woko no kyere, they went out to seize him. — binding, bonds. Acts 20,23. 23,29.

pl. ŋ-, a wretch worthy or destined to be killed. pr. 636. 1958; cf. a-kwaakyere; wode no too akyere, they sentenced him to be killed after previous torments while dragging him along the streets; sie (obi) aky. or ŋky., to bury a corpse with the slaves killed to accompany the deceased to the other world; cf. asiede.
aboso, the batten or movable bar of a loom.
v.n. [kyere, v.] example, sample, pattern, instance; syn. ŋhweso; ehõ ŋky. bi ni; - pl. ŋkyerekyere, q. v.
[kyere, v.] 1. manner of binding; state of bondage, bonds; ŋkyeree a womã wokyeree no yɛɛ no yaw sẽ. Philem.

10. 13. — 2. a grudge, ill will, animosity, hostility, malice, aversion; mede ne nã hɔ ŋkyerɛɛ (= ne hɔ taŋ, ne hɔ ahi) na mede merekyere no, I make him feel the grudge I owe to his mother; mfá m'agya hɔ ŋkyerɛɛ ŋkyerɛ me, do not make me suffer for the aversion you have conceived to my father. — 3. = duasee, kãasee &c. — 4. a weaver's spool; cf. dodowa. kyerɛ-pãnõ, F., shew-bread.
inf. F. answer, declaration.
inf. explanation, interpretation; discernment; cf. asekyerɛ.

plummet. Zech. 4, 10. Am. 7, 7; cf. prumo.
pl. a-, a species of snake; nickname: aduasare; ɔyɛ ahaŋtaŋ sɛ ɔky.
the queen of the white ants = mfótéhéne. pr. 1959.
a three-angled piece of wood or shelf fastened in the corner (or nook) of a room to put things on; s. kyereso, kerefua.
hardened dung, excrement; onipa, atɔteboa biara a, s. akokɔ biŋ = a ɛyɛ denneennen; syn. biŋ, sɛbew; cf. bintuw. Ezek. 4, 12.
F. (in order to see) whether = kyere-sɛ; or only: kyere (Mk. 11, 13). — kyere ɔbokũ no, hoping to kill him.
a. little, few; mako ky., a little pepper; ŋhoma ky., a few books; wɔbɔ ŋkɔmmɔ kakra ara ky., they held converse for a little while.
a little something to make a show; a small token.

a. only used together with kaŋ, s. kaŋky....

red. v., 1. s. kyerɛ; the red. form is used, with the meaning to teach, instruct, when the thing or matter that is taught is not mentioned; cf. didi, keŋkaŋ. — 2. kyerɛkyerɛ.. mu, to explain, expound, elucidate, illustrate.
inf. examples, instances; s. ŋkyerɛ; ɛhɔ ŋky. bi.
pl. a-, teacher, instructor, tutor; preacher, minister of the gospel.
lit. what shows the way; 1. the forefinger, index. — 2. in a ship the helm, or perh. better, the steering compass. — 3. way-mark, direction-post.

the king's drummers. pr. 477; s. gyaasefo.
white flakes of ashes (ɔbro-de-hono a wəahyew mu gyarensɔ mù apɔwapɔw à ɛdedam' fitafitaa no).
a play of a certain company; asafo bi agoru.

[obs.] Ak. green palm leaves formed into a triangle by tying them together at the angles. When this triangle was put on a necklace at the funeral of a king, queen or chief, it meant that the wearer was to be sacrificed to serve the deceased in the other world.
Kyiriamim, q. v.
ŋkyeremú, a children's game; s. agoru.
a precious cotton cloth, mixed

1. basket made of wicker (hama nẽ mpɔ̃pã), strong & coarse, used to cover fowls, chickens &c. - cf. kentéŋ, kyèŋkyèŋ (akotwẽ), sésèa, pirebi, tekrekyí. - 2. bird's cage.
an aquatic bird, said to build a mud hut.

swollen to bursting; ripe; ǝhyehyeẽ ǝsoboaso aky. kenten bi mã, he filled a basket with (middle-sized) ripe plantains.
F. shew-bread. Mt. 12, 4.
row, line, range, rank, file. Lev. 24, 6.7; wafua ode gya-wu ŋkõ kyerépéŋkyérépéŋ, he has planted yam in (several) rows consisting only of 'gyawu'. - F. aky. mu, in rows. Mk. 6, 40.
a common name for the townships of Abiriw, Ɔdawu, Awukugua, (Abonse), Adukrom, and Apirede. Cf. Guaŋ.
(F. -de) = sè ebia, whether or if. perhaps. Gr. § 141, 1. B; kɔhwe ky. ɔwɔ hɔ ana? kokã kyere no ky. ɔbetie ana? kɔ ky. wobenya biribi aba na yeadì. Isa. 36, 8.

listening to instruction; mekɔ ky., I am going to have a lesson; asubɔ ky., the attending of instruction previous to baptizing.
catechumen.
[red. kyerékyerew], Ky. twers, to write; to engrave; ky. kyeréw, to write on paper, to write a letter, deed, document, tract or book; cf. kurukyerew. - kyeréw.. diŋ, to register. Lk. 2, 3.
1. writing, written document; title. John 19, 20. - 2. Scripture. - kyeréw-asém, word of the Scripture. Lk. 4, 21. - kyeré(w)-fèfé, calligraphy.

the phrase 'gu ne ŋkyerew' is used when nothing is left of things portioned out successively; wokye ade bi mu wie a, wokã se: yeàgù né ŋkyèrèw' = yeawie koraa, we are at the end of it, we have done or finished, all is spent, there is nothing left; aduan a yede kɔe no, yesaŋ akodi bi a, na wɔagu ne ŋky. dedaw, we went again to partake of the victuals we had taken with us, they were already eaten (finished, consumed, used up).
sister = onuabàa, -béa.
screw; cf. mfewa.
screw-driver; cf. mfewakyimfo.
letter, character in writing (s. kyerɛwe) or printing (s. ntintimii).
a line, syn. nsaŋhɔ; a mark or character in writing; letter; s. kyerɛwde.

writer; scribe; clerk; author (of a book).
a species of bird, which catches snakes.
verse. - kyerɛw-póŋ, writing-table, writing-desk; ky. ketewa, writing-tablet. Lk. 1, 63.
catching and selling; wodii Krɔbɔfo aky., they took to catching and selling the Krɔbɔfo people.

eng: a present or gift for several.

Ak. ɛkyé, pl. id., F. ŋ-, hat, cap, bonnet, any cover for the head. pr. 1918f.; cf. bɔro-kyew, fo-kyew &c. - bu or yɛ kyew, to make a hat &c.; pɔŋ or tu kyew, to take off one's hat; pa.. kyew, lit. to take off the hat, to beseech, petition; to beg pardon; syn. kotɔ, sĕre, kotɔ sĕre [G. kpa fai]; mɛpa wo kyéw sɛ: fa firi me, I beg you to forgive me! wó kyéw ni! lit. your hat is this, i.e. I beg your pardon; syn. kyew ni, owura, bĕra (mu)! please, sir, come in! kyew nyinaa yɛ wo dea = fa firi me, na fafiri nyinaa yɛ wo dea, ɛnyé me dea, I have nothing to forgive, I crave only your forgiveness; mepaa no me bone hɔ kyew, I asked him to forgive the wrong done by me; - yɛŋ T...fo, yɛyɛ afetewa: obiara so n'aŋkasa ne kyew, we people of T. are like (the fruit called) afetewa: each of us has (wears) his own hat, i.e. we are independent; obiara so n'aŋkasa ne kyew, a) everybody is independent; b) everyman is satisfied with his own ways.
entreaty, supplication, asking for pardon.

v. to fry, bake, roast, parch (akokɔ, nām, ŋkyewa, kafe, abŭrow, pr. 394, ase n.a.), with or without fat, in a pan, on a roaster or potsherd, whereas tɔ̃tɔ is, to bake in an oven, or, as kisā, to roast over the open fire.

fried cakes, roasted meat, delicate food; cf. akyeduaŋ.
a pan for roasting or baking. Lev. 2, 5.
Aky. [abŭrow a wóakyew na wówɛ] parched corn. pr. 1944. Josh. 5, 11.

v. [red. kyikyi] to turn the back to; 1. to dislike, not to like, to loathe, have an aversion to, hate, detest, abhor. pr. 83. 239f. 832; cf. taŋ; to shun, fear, shrink from. pr. 417. 1190. 1517; neg. not to be against. pr. 1805; woŋkyi, it is not objected to, not found unallowable. pr. 1488. 1963; wokã no saa a, woŋkyi, you may say so, although it is not the right word or answer. - abosom nyinaa wó adé à wókyikyií. - 2. to abstain from, to avoid, to consider as forbidden (by the fetish) and unclean; mìkyi, I am not allowed to eat it; kyi ayam, to fast; kyi buadá, s. abuadá. - 3. kyi anim, to shun, keep clear of, beware of, get out of the way of; nea ɛsɛ se yekyi n'anim ne ɔbonsam, he whom it is necessary for us to shun is the devil. - 4. kyi ayi, to abstain from certain victuals for a month and up to a year after the death of a member of one's family.

v. [red. kyikyi] to press, squeeze, wring or crush out; wóhoro ntama a, wokyi mu nsu no gu, in washing clothes the water is wrung out from them; kyikyi atam no mu; - kyi nùfu, to milk; kokyĭ ŋŋuaŋ no nufu, go and milk the goats! - kyi ŋŋo, to press out oil; kyi bobe-aba, to press grapes. Gen. 40, 11; - kyi nsu, to trickle down. Lam. 3, 49.

[con. n'akyí] cf. akyiri, Ak. akyire, Gr. § 119. 120,4. 130,5. 1. the back, the hind(er) part, rear; the outer (outward) part, outside of a vessel or enclosure, of the hand. pr. 468. - 2. the space behind or outside; bɛpɔw no akyi nohɔã, beyond the mountain. Gen. 35, 21. - the time and events behind, the end. Mt. 26, 58. - assm yi akyi bewie dɛŋ? what will be the

result of this matter? - 3. behind (ɔwɔ m'akyí, he is behind me; dua bi si daŋ no akyí. pr. 2160; mewɔ n'akyí, I am on his side. pr. 2); outside, without (ɔpoŋ akyí, outside or before the door); after (of time); ɔprannaa akyí na osu tɔ daa, after thunder it usually rains; ɛno akyí (no). after that, afterwards. - 4. in specific cases or phrases: a) the property left at a person's death; b) the time of one's absence; c) one's supporters or relations. - di.. akyí (di akyíri), to follow, go or come after; to succeed; to accompany, attend, assist; to pursue, chase. pr. 300.893.895.898 f. - ògyina m'akyí, he stands behind me, backs me, supports, assists or protects me, stands security for me. - n'akyí tweri me, he leans upon me, s. aninsem. - waba m'akyí, he has come in my absence; obi aba wo akyí, somebody came to visit you whilst you were absent. - ɛdɔm abeŋ yeŋ akyí, the enemy has made his appearance in our rear, at our back, behind us. - wáfi m'akyí akó hɔ, he went there without my knowledge; - siesie m'akyí, provide for my coming home (that I may find something to eat)! ɔhwe n'akyí, she looks for the things which he has left; nea wode hwes m'akyí wɔ hɛ? what did you prepare for me whilst I was absent? - ohyehye n'akyí, he boasts of he has not with him (what is left behind or expected); - ɔwɔ bi wɔ n'akyí, he has a rich relation; n'akyí nyé dùru, he is not of a rich or renowned family. 1 Sam. 18,23; m'akyí bá, my younger brother or sister. - obisaa yeŋ akyí kwaŋ, he inquired for us, asked for us. - ɔde n'akyí gyaw yeŋ, a) he made us act in his place during his absence; b) he committed his property to our care (for the time of his absence). - he leaves his property to his children. - akyí ansi no yiye, a) he ended his life in poverty; b) the end of his life was unsatisfactory. - akyí ade, akyí asem, that which follows, consequence; ɔppwene akyí asem hɔ, he is reckless, careless, heedless. - n'ani ye no n'akyí n'akyí, he fears, apprehends, is afraid; cf. n'ani ye no akyirikyiri, ani 8 A.
adv. then, now, afterward. Mt. 12, 44 f. Mk. 1, 14 = ɛno na; cf. akyiri no, F. n'ekyir' no.
mewɔ ŋkyí, I have relatives; mmofra ayi fi ohene a owui no ŋkyí, these children are among the relatives of the deceased king; orekɔ nè-ŋkyí, he is going to his relatives. Cf. akyi, akyiri 6, ŋkyifo.
a species of ŋkate.

[inf. ŋ-, red. kyiákyia] Ak. dwa, 1. to shake hands, greet, salute, bid welcome. pr. 144.2998; kyia me nsam', shake hands with me! - 2. to give or send one's compliments; cf. mā akyĕ. - 3. to bet, wager, lay (a bet or wager), hold a wager, (As. to nsa); wokyia wo so, they hold a wager on it; me nè no kyia, I wager with him; kyia mé è! lay me a wager!
inf. joining hands, salutation, greeting. Mt. 23, 7; daa mekra no ŋkyia, I always send him my compliments; - bet, wager; suretyship. Prov. 11, 15.
pl. ŋ-, any animal not allowed by the fetish to be eaten.

a detestable or abominable thing; abomination; any food disallowed by the fetish; avoidance(s), taboo(s); wadi n'aky., he has eaten what was forbidden to eat. pr. 759; a thing belonging or dedicated to the fetishes. - akyíde-fó, pl. id. an abominable person. Rev. 21, 8.
inf. following after, pursuing, pursuit. pr. 300. - akyidí-fó, pl. id. follower, disciple, adherent; successor.
the rear, rear-guard, reserve of an army, reserve troops of the centre; wobɔ-wɔŋ ky., they are their rear-guard. Isa. 52, 12.58, 8.
backbone; the vertebral or spinal column.
a support, stay, prop; a defender; n'akyidua abu, the person in whom or the thing on which one relies is no more.
alms given to the family of mourners.
1. he who follows; a certain kind of follower. pr. 1965.
cf. akyikafó, akyidifó; akyifó a wobae yi, these who came, this rising generation; akyifó of others = akyidifó, akyifó mfo.
the relatives. Cf. akyi, ŋkyi.
inf. standing behind, assistance, protection.
a supporter, protector, counsel, defender, helper, comforter. John 14, 16; he who handles a gun or weapon.

pl. a-, 1. one left behind, left in charge of something by a departing person. - 2. heir (= owunnyafo, odedifo). - 3. straggler. - 4. one who remains behind, the last. Mt. 20, 14. 16. - s. okyirikafo, F. akyirdzifo.

telescope, spy-glass; cf. ahwede.

unrulines, rashness; óyè ky., he does not sit quiet; he is rash, unruly, turbulent, refractory.

umbrella; cf. kyinii.
wresting &c.; ógyè me kyím, he takes my word and wrests it, he doubts, disputes what I say. pr. 76. 2147. Cf. akyinnye.
a food prepared of blood and palm-nuts, spiced with salt and pepper; odefufuu a kyim gu n'ani akyi, kyim put on yam-foofoo. Cf. korabra.

to turn, twist; oky. ne kɔŋ, ne ti, ne nsa, safē. - 2. to turn aside: dɔm no akyima akɔfa ŋkwansiane abesi kūrom', the enemy turned and entered the town by a roundabout way; - okykyima, he goes to ease himself, to the privy, W.C. (pr. 569); F. he goes about. Mt. 4, 23; - he has withdrawn; b) he has eased himself (evacuated his bowels); cf. ye hō yiye, gya ne naŋ. - 3. = ye bra; okyima ne hō = ɔkɔ mīkyiri, he has withdrawn.

hō nni or ntó ky., there is no defect in him; ne hō tew or tɔ ky., there is something amiss or faulty with him; ne hō tew ky. (biribiara ye no a, s. ono ye biribi) a, wode bebisa wo, if anything goes amiss with him, you will answer (be answerable) for it. - shō ntɔ ky., in sincerity. Eph. 6, 24.

[Eng.] = king (in Europe); mesom ky.

[Ak. kyiŋ; red. kyiŋkyini] to circulate; to walk or go (round) about; oky. daŋ hɔ̃; oky. maŋ mu, ɔnyé hwee; ɔsebɔ kyini kwaem’, ɔwia ky. ẃim’; ókyini ayarefo sɔ kã asɛm kyerɛ wɔŋ, he goes round to visit the sick and speak to them; - to rove, ramble, roam, range, stroll, wander; kyini kɔ ba, to circulate, to be current. - o-kyíni, inf. going to and fro. Job 1, 7.
Ak. kyinié, pl. -, a large parasol of kings, also called katamaŋ & bamkyinii; cf. akatawia. - kyinii-kúrafó; kyinie-fúafó (As.), umbrella-carrier(s); s. gyaasefo.

inf. lit. a turning round and meeting; the revolution or rotation of a wheel, of the hands of a watch or clock; an hour, cf. doŋhwerew. - a whirlpool. - di ky., to turn round again and again, revolve; to wander about; mfèwá no adi ky., the screw turns without catching hold in its nut; ahum a edi ky., a whirlwind. Ps. 77, 19. Jer. 30, 23.
whirlwind. Isa. 5, 28; stormy wind. Ezek. 13, 11. 13.
[dim.] a small umbrella; cf. kyinii.

red. v. 1. s. kyiŋ. - 2. me hɔ ky. me, I writhe. Isa. 21, 3; m’ayam’de ky., my bowels yearn. Lam. 1, 20. - 3. to pervert, subvert. Prov. 19, 3. - 4. F. to tarry, Mt. 25, 5; ɔrekyiŋkim né bá, he delays his coming; cf. twentweŋ. Mt. 24, 48.
windings; atrapoe ŋky., winding-stairs. 1 Kg. 6, 8.

kyiŋkyíni, red. v. kyiŋ, kyini, to rove about. Gen. 27, 40. - akyiŋkyíni, inf.: ɔkra aky., transmigration of souls, metempsychosis. - akyiŋ-kyiŋ-akyíŋkyiŋ (or akyiŋkyini-akyin-kyini), inf.: akɔ amã mabrɛ se dɔte, my walking about has overdone me.
a place where somebody walks about or to and fro; fãkɔ a obi kyiŋkyiŋ hɔ.
bɔ ky., to be alarmed by terrible news; cf. bɔ twi.
inf. circulation, the act of going about or passing from place to place or person to person.
pl. id. a planet.
circular, circular letter or paper.

inf. [gye kyim] doubt, unbelief (F. Mk. 9, 24), disbelief, scepticism; dispute, controversy, debate; ogye no akyinnye, (better: ogye no kyim) he disputes with him, calls in question or expresses dissent or opposition to what he says. pr. 446. 2147. 2716. - óyè aky., he is a habitual disputer.
pl. a- [akyinnye-gyè, inf.] doubter, sceptic, controvertist. pr. 1966. - akyinnyé-sɛ́m, question, dispute &c. Acts 26, 3; oppositions, 1 Tim. 6, 20.
inf. - mpa-akyiri. - akyipáfó ŋkóntomofó, those who perfidiously depart (from God), i.e. the wicked. Ps. 119, 158.
a certain game, = ŋkyerem’?
a hard, dry, barren land; syn. asase ŋkyerekyerewa or kyeŋkyereŋ.
bɔ ky., to become a vagabond.

Ak. akyire, F. akyir, 1. = akyi 1-4. pr. 275. (In Ak. akyi is used with a noun or pronoun before it, akyiri without such). - akyiri ɛ? - bɔkɔɔ! how are things at home, or, where you come from? - all is well. - akyiri kwaŋ ware, s. wàre. - di akyiri, to go or follow after, pursue &c. - saŋ aky., to turn back, return. - 2. behind; at a distance, afar off: ɔnam aky., he walks behind, or, at a distance; - ka aky., to stay behind; kɔ aky., to carry far (said of a gun); - ŋkɔ aky., don't go far! - aky. trãbea, the lowest place. Lk. 14, 9. - 3. the time after; - akyiri no, F. n'akyir no, afterwards: kaŋ no ɔmpé se ɔkɔ, aky. no ɔkɔe, at first he did not choose to go, but afterwards he went; - akyiri yi, recently, lately; wo ákyíri yi ŋhóma, your last letter. - 4. the latter end: aky. besi yeŋ déŋ = ɛbewie yeŋ deŋ?

how will it be with us finally? aky. besi mo yiye, it will turn out well for you; misuro aky., I am afraid of the consequences; - ohü akyiri, a) he is far-sighted, long-sighted; b) he can account for it; oŋhü akyiri adé, s. hü. - 5. nam or fa akyiri, to do without the knowledge of another. - 6. m'ákyìri firi hé, my mother's family, my maternal relations are from that place. - 7. woadi afe nè akyiri, they are a year old and upward. Nu. 3, 15. - 8. de (asem or əkasa) si aky., to conclude a speech, conversation &c.

follower(s); F. akyir(dzi)fo, the last. Mt. 20, 12. 14.
the last. Isa. 44, 6.

po, the hinder or Western sea. Joel 2, 20.
a certain kind of razor [ekyi afasew, it does not agree with af., getting dull when used to cut af.]; s. oyiwaŋ.
1. a middle quality of sandal; s. mpaboa. - 2. leprosy.

kirikra.

-kyiri, far, distant, far behind, far away, (in, at) a remote distance; əkə akyky. asase bi so (or, asase bi so akyky.), he has gone to a distant contry; - ..ani ye.. akyirikyiri, s. ani 8 A. - mmä wo ani nnyé wo akyirikyiri se merebehye wo dà-ténteŋ bi, do not fear that I shall put you off very long. inhabitants of distant countries. Isa. 8, 9.
F. akyiri-akyiri, backwards; nam ŋky., to go backw. Gen. 9, 23; s. pini.
adv. blazing, in full blast, in or with a bright flame, lustily, vigorously; ogya no dew ky. = framfram, frafra, kitikiti.
F. (Akp. in songs) the rising or next generation = akyifó, nne-mma, mma a wòaka akyiri a wòwò ho nne-yi. Ps. 78, 4.
pl. a- [pa akyiri] deserter, forsaker, apostate, renegate. Mic. 2, 4.
inf. retreat; cf. pini.
inf. [saŋ akyiri] returning. Jer. 5, 3; turning back or aside. Prov. 1, 32; backsliding; cf. nsaŋakyiri.

inf. exit, final event. Ezek. 26, 18.
inf. going back.

pl., s. ɔba; mmaa, pl., s. ɔbaa, woman, abaa, rod, baa, place.

seems to be a formative suffix of verbs (buma, hima, kyima) and nouns (adwumã, mframa, aguma, hama, ahema, ŋhɔmã &c.)

v. [red. (mẽmã), mõmã, q. v.] 1. to give, hand, communicate, bestow, confer, impart, grant, present (cf. kye, de.. hyɛ nsa); to deliver, yield up; to allow. When the thing given is mentioned in the form of a single object, it is usually put after the personal object; otherwise an aux. v. (de, fa, yi &c.) is used: òmã me siká; ode ne sika nyina amã me; mã me nsu! fa wo ade no mã me! yi..mã, s. yi 28. Gr. § 206, pr. 1916. 3176. - de (asem) mã.., to put a question to, to ask; to add a short remark to, or continue a discourse; ... enna ode mã no: "Wompe se wo nè me kɔ a, trã ofie"... then he added: "If you don't like to accompany me, stay at home!" - mã okwaŋ, to give leave or permission &c., s. okwaŋ. - 2. to put, apply to: wode (asem no) mã nnipa nè mmoa, the word is used in speaking of men and beasts. - 3. to dedicate, s. mõmã. - 4. to address with a salutation, to wish one something (mã akyɛ, nnɔpa, akwaba, amo, due &c.) - 5. mã asem, to tell or relate a story; to tell lies; cf. mõmã (hɔ). pr. 1989. - 6. to let, cause, make, allow, permit or suffer one to do any thing (used as an auxiliary before another verb, s. Gr. § 91, 10. 107, 25. 255, 3. Rem.): mã entrã hɔ (Ak. mã no tẽnã hɔ), let it (remain) there; ɔmã wɔkɔkyeree no, he let them go and catch him, he had him caught; ɔmã wɔbekyeree no, he suffered himself to be caught by them; wɔammã hwee ara anyɛ no, he was preserved unhurt. pr. 403 f. 439 f. 1969 f. - 7. (used as an aux. after another verb, s. Gr. § 109, 32. 243 b. Rem. 1. 2) to perform an action or to be in some state or condition for the benefit of, out of sympathy with, or with respect to somebody: ɔye adwuma mã me, he works for me; odi ŋkɔmmɔ mã ne nua, he laments for his brother; ɔbɔ tuo mãã Kofi, he shot himself so that Kofi should do the same. - Sometimes mã shows a general and indefinite reference of the principal v. without an object following, cf. asɛmpa a Luka kyerew mãe; in F. it answers to the adv. very: ɔyè féw mã, it is very beautiful. - 8. mã..só, F. do, to raise, lift, lift up: mã adẽsoa no so, lift or take up that load. pr. 99; cf. kukuru; mã wo naŋ so, lift your feet, i.e. quicken your steps, be quick, make haste; ɔmã n'aní (ne nsá, ne tí, ne nántiŋ, ne nné) so, he lifts up his eyes (his hand, his head, his heel, his voice); - to hold up; - to elevate, exalt, elate; ɔmã ne hɔ so, he exalts himself; - to take and carry away, to remove; to take up: wamã n'asem so, he has again taken up his speech. - 9. mã, to plaster: wode abanto-atere mã ɔdaŋ hɔ, nsemso ani, they plaster the wall of the house, the ceiling, with a trowel. - 10. mã, to cause, occasion, serves also for the Eng. conj. so that. Gr. § 273, 1 c. - 11. mã mu = tẽsm', to shout; wɔmã mu. mã, mãã F. = amãnã, amõa. Mt. 15, 14.

pl. mãmã, amã-amã, full, filled up; cf. mãtɛŋŋ, mãtɔ; m'áhíná ayè mã, my water-pot is full; ye, hyɛ or gu.. mã, to make full, to fill (up); wɔhye-hyɛɛ ŋhina no amã-amã, they filled the water-pots; nsú ayè tumpáŋ no mã, the bottle is full of water; wakyerew ŋhoma yi mã, he has written this paper full.

n. fulness; ɛmã mu nni siŋ, full is full; - F. also adv. plentifully, very. àmã, lime, bird-lime; pitch; glue; coaltar; bitumen. Gen. 14, 10. Ex. 2, 3; cf. amãne & mãnnɔ. [G. id.]
a. slimy, ropy, clammy, glutinous; viscid, viscous, sticky; syn. mätãmätã, fãã, sãã, twãã &c.
[contr. of Amemẽnewa], F. Amba, pr. n. of a female born on a Saturday. Gr. § 41, 4. pr. 1509. - Amma Dapaa, pr. n. of a f. born on Dapaa, q. v.
childlike confidence.
nea wammã asɛm no aŋwɔ koraa, a quarrelsome person.
kúrow a ɛmmã ɔmaŋmu ŋŋwɔ da, a quarrelsome, seditious town. pr. 1987.
ringleaders of rebels.
[ababaa, bere] maidenhood.
di m., to be fond of dress or finery, to try to appear lady-like.
(mabóó), mabáóó, interj. [= mɛmã wo abá-óó] welcome! salutation to a stranger arriving; Aburi, (Amanteŋsofo na ɛtaa kã). Cf. akwaba.
F. = me ara; m. ŋkõ = me ara ŋkõ, I (of) myself.
mãde, a species of yam, s. ɔdé. pr. 1988.
interj. [mɛmã wo adwó] good evening!
inf. freq. [ba] wányá ha mmàe, he has often come here.
[ade a emmae da] something unheard-of, unprecedented, extraordinary; waye m., he has performed something unprecedented &c.; s. mmɛɛda.
[bae mu] enlargement, expansion, extension &c.; syn. nterɛw-mu.
pl. a-, giver, donor; speaker. pr. 1989.
[mmaa ag.] unchaste play with women, fornication.

mmágum', v. n. [ba gu mu] reinforcement. pr. 1990; increase; ɔdaŋ yi, sɛnea m. gugum' ara ni, this room is getting filled up (with people); ahoho pii bae anɔpa nè anadwofã mãã m. (be)kum dɔm, many guests (strangers) came in the morning, and their number was increased by those coming in the evening; afe biara sika m. (a ɛba gum') no nye adewa, the yearly increase of money is considerable.
interj. [mɛmã wo ahá] good day! a form of salutation used in the middle of the day.

the pepper-shrub and its fruit; consisting of pods with many small seeds, of a hot, biting taste, Cayenne pepper, Capsicum. pr. 1898. 2352; besẽ m., s. besẽ. - Diff. kinds: ntɔŋ'ko (the largest), nnyeraa & mmesẽwa (the smallest); mako kɔkɔ (with red pods), m. tuntum (with dark-green pods), m. fitaa (with whitish pods); m. àbɔráa, brɔfo m., ɔpapo m. - makó-dùá, the pepper-shrub. - mąkowá [dim.]: wabehye m'asɛm ani m., he has put pepper in the eyes of my palaver, i.e. has made it grievous to me. pr. 3409.
[baakó, pl.] one by one, one after the other, each by himself. pr. 789. 2548. 3258.
[s. bákómma] manners and dealings of high-born persons, imperiousness. - mmákómasɛm-pefó†, aristocrat, the aristocratic party, aristocracy.
palm-wine drunk in the morning after having chewed pepper corns and (meat with) salt; wonom nsã anopa na awow wom' a, na wowe mako nè nkyene (nè nam kakra bi) ansã-na wonom nsã gu so.
Aky. = kookosi.
inf. [ɔba] child murder, infanticide.
[kurúw = twitwa] a kind of leprosy (cf. kwata, piti); when it has cut the fingers and toes, it heals.
interj. [mɛmã wo akyé] good morning! pr. 1992 f. 3658.
àmma-kyewá: onipa ye am., man has not come to stay long (on earth); s. amme-kyewa.
pl. of bámma [baŋ, ba]. 1 Kg. 6, 6.
ɔmámma [ɔmaŋ ba] pl. ɔmámma, citizen; also a well-known, dis-
inf. citizenship. Acts 22,28.
[ɔmãŋ, dim.] a small town or state; cf. akürowa.
[amánɛ aba] the fruit of a tree called amánɛ.
asitifo nè mum no yɛ m., the deaf and dumb utter inarticulate sounds.
mmáa-mù, harem; cf. adafae.
red. v. mãŋ.
ammá-m'ání-àŋwú, a species of yam; s. odé.
= ɔmaŋfo.
a kind of sumaŋ; s. App. B.IV.
[ɔmaŋ afɔ] pl. id. a desolate, deserted and decayed dwelling-place or habitation, ruined town, ruin, the site of an ancient town. pr. 159. 2003, 2664. 3035; syn. akürofɔ.
a certain creeper, climber; wode gye baŋ, kyere adare.
inf. desolation, devastation.
desolation. Dan. 9,27.
pl. a-fo [nea əfra ɔmaŋ] settler, a person who has come from another place and settled in a town. pr. 2004 f.; s. amaŋfrafo.
inf. tapping a rubber tree or rubber plant; kɔ am., to go to tap a rubber tree &c.
[ɔmaŋ bɔ] destruction or ruin of a town, country or nation. pr. 2905. 2918. — amãmmɔe-sém [asem a sbɔ ɔmaŋ] a cause of mischief or destruction for a town or nation.
ɔ-mãmmɔ-nípa, one who brings mischief on a community or nation.
[ɔmaŋ bone] s. bu 28.
[boro ɔmaŋ]: di am., to destroy, ruin or exterminate a nation, tribe or people.
pl. a-, the guana, iguana, a very large species of lizard eaten by natives pr. 1997; a nickname: bɔ-àmáŋ-dùapúo.
pl. a- [or ɔmáŋ-mpányimfó] a chief, elder, alderman, chief officer or magistrate in a town, tribe or nation; senator, pl. senate.
mampòmmíre, a kind of cycadaceous plant, having the appearance of a low palm and bearing red (not edible) nuts; a species of Zamia.
pl. a- [ɔmaŋ = kürow] a (comparatively) large town, city. Mt. 10, 11.
harem; s. mmaam'.
[pl. of abaa; mu] s. abaá.

inf. [bu maŋ] deportment, comportment, demeanour, behaviour, conduct, manner of living together in a community. pr. 1181; déŋ' am. na wo nè me rebu yi? what sort of behaviour towards me is this? wo am. uyé me fɛ! your conduct in this town does not please me; wo am. mu ɛ? how are you doing in your situation? m'am. mu ye, I am doing well. - am, pa, sociableness, sociable disposition.
amámmú; mo am. = senea mubu no maŋ fa, your manner of behaviour; what behaviour! nnipa (or, abɔde) am, hɔ nsiesiei, the moral system or the invariable moral laws of the world. K. § 132 f. 189.
[nsem a wohwe so bu maŋ] statutes or regulations for a community.
[ɔmaŋ bum] disturbance or confused state of a country or town.

v. [red. mãm'mãŋ, (mãŋ'mãŋ)] to turn or go aside, to turn in somewhere from the way or journey; mãŋ ná menseŋ, go aside, let me pass! wamaŋ (wɔ) ŋkwanta so hɔ, he turned off from the maŋ road to the other way where it branches off from the former (opp. wafa tempoŋ no so); yeduu Mamfɛ no, yemaŋ kɔɔ ofi bim', when we came to M., we turned aside to a dwelling; otwam' a, ɔmaŋ me, when he passes through my town, he turns in at my house. - 2. to pass by, not to happen: eyi mmãŋ wò = eyi mparè wo! may this not happen to you!
Ak. ɔmáne, pl. amáŋ & amáŋ-amáŋ, 1. (Akp.) town, syn. kurow = a collection of houses larger than a village,
ethnography.

émmàŋ, a species of herring, more common and smaller than two other species called kokùrò & mpanéí. pr. 216; F. ebaŋ.

márá, v. to send (a thing or things) as occasion offers or at opportunity, to transmit; wàmăná mè aduaŋ', nãm, sika, he has sent me food, meat, money; merekyerɛw ŋhoma mamrã Abŭrokyiri, I am writing a letter for (i.e. to be sent to) Europe; nnera mede ŋhoma memănãã Ŋkraŋ, yesterday I sent a letter to Akra; mesomae mã wode ŋh, kɔɔ Ŋkraŋ, ... by an express messenger to Akra); mmurukuu yi fi Abŭrokyiri na wode mănãe (mănãã me), these books were transmitted (to me) from Europe. - Cf. soma. - Red. măná-mănã, Rev. 11,10.
inf. sending, transmission; - ɔmăná ŋhóma or -kyeréw, a letter.
F. = amonom, immediately &c.
ámàrà, ámòna, Ak, F. next younger brother or sister; ɔye m'am. = ɔye m'àkyi-bá; ɔye m'am. kūmaa, he is the brother or sister coming second or third after me.
Ak. = amõá. pr. 2886.
= mmărã.
[mănã, ade] pl. id. a present transmitted; †goods or letters conveyed by the post. - amănãdé-hwɛfó, postmaster; amănàdè-kùráfó, postman, letter-carrier.
post, post-office. - amănãé-hwɛfó, postmaster. - ɔ-măná-gyiraé, postage-stamp.
di m., to trade by sending for articles, instead of going oneself. pr. 884.
măná-hóma, ɔmănà-kyé-rɛw, letter, dispatch.
[ɔbaa, anaŋ] pr. n. f. given to a girl being the fourth child of her mother. Gr. § 41, 5.
F. husband of wife's sister.
s. ɔmaŋ. - amáŋ-amáŋ-mù-ní, pl. -fó, a gentile, heathen. Rom. 2, 14. Gal. 2, 14.
revolution.

disorder, disturbances of a town or state.
pl. ɔmáŋaniwafó, an important or principal man in a town or state (able to care for it and an honour to it); a noble, nobleman, peer; pl. the chief men, head men of the town.
mẽnãtofo = mmărãtofo.

deputy, representative of the people.
mayor, burgomaster. Hist.
= amammu.
F. = man(n)ei.
-hunu &c. F., s. amanne &c.

amãŋ, Ak, F., 1. lime, bird-lime; pitch; glue; resin, gum; any viscous substance exuding from trees and used for catching birds, to mend pots, some also (as kūrobow) for rubbing the body, in order to make it sweet-scented; cf. amã; - bɔ amãne (or aman), to tap a rubber-tree. - 2. a certain tree; cf. amámma.
Ak. a community &c., s. ɔmãŋ.

amãnne (amãnɛ́), F. amandze [ɔmãŋ ade] trial, trouble, affliction, misery, misfortune, calamity. pr. 381. 462. 567. 1224. 2008f. - hū am., to be unfortunate, to be in affliction, to suffer; óhū amãne; obí à óhū amané; nyã am., to get into a mess or scrape, into difficulties, to be prosecuted or
involved in a lawsuit. (The word in its primary sense probably was applied to the trial of a cause before the judges in presence of the people, and to the grievous results of such a trial).
public tax, custom, impost, duty, contribution; cf. tow, akwanne.
custom, fashion, habit, manner, ways or usages (also religion) of a people.
kases; bɔ am., to deliver a message.
mããnɛ́, quarrel, brawl; quarrelsomeness, quarrelsome disposition; syn. atutuw; óyè mããnɛ́, ɔredi mããnɛ, he quarrels, squabbles, wrangles, brawls.
quarreller, wrangler, brawler, quarrelsome person. 1 Tim. 3,3. Tit. 1,7.
a certain creeper, climber; wodi n'aba.

[hũ amane] suffering, affliction, tribulation, trouble, adversity, unhappiness, misery, wretchedness, torments; yegyina amandzehunum', F. we stand in jeopardy. am. kũrow, hell, Gehenna, the place of torment. amanehúnu mù boasetɔ, patience, endurance. Ja. 5,11.
a sufferer, one who labours under affliction.
30 cowries = ¼ farthing (in Akuapem); cf. ɔbaŋ, atomanei.
one who is in affliction, being without a friend or supporter.
getting into trouble, incurring calamity; exposing to inconveniences; danger. Rom. 8,35.
the people in contra-distinction to the king or government; the members of a community as distinguished from their rulers; the representatives of the people; cf. ɔmãŋ 5.
a ruin &c., s. amamfó.
sojourner. Ps. 39,12; s. ɔmamfrani.
mingled people, allied to or admixed with a ruling nation; cf. afrafrafo; syn. amamfrani. Jer. 25,20.24.
consul. Hist.
mãŋ'ŋo.
the king or chief of a nation; cf. ɔdekuro.
[baá, beá] everywhere.
omnipresence, ubiquity. K. § 165.
a kind of India rubber; bird-lime.
dictator.
parliament.
member of parliament.
an acquaintance (nea ɔbɛŋ wo abusũa hõ kakra a.s. obi hunu a wunim no). pr. 69.214; guest. pr. 284. 695. 2010 ff. — cf. ɔmaŋmuni.
a needle of native manufacture.
gag, bridle; a piece of wood put in some one's mouth to prevent his talking or swearing [wo manni gyina ho, nso wuntumi mfre no]. pr. 3616.
to gag.
[ɔbaniŋ] longing after men; yɛ m., to be longing a. m.
a nickname of the rat; s. okisi.
[ɔbaniŋ ade, mmarimadé] manful, valiant deeds.
ohũ me am., he recognises me.
[ɔbaniŋ awow] shudder, shuddering, when about to perform a daring feat; - mm. agu no so, he shudders, shakes with horror; cf. awɔsɛ, ayisɛ.
[ɔbaniŋ] any men's disease due to unchastity: ɔkramaŋ, bába, akronnoi, twow.
manliness, valour; power. 1 Chron. 29,11f. Ps. 106,8; virtues. 1 Pet. 2, 9; cf. abaniŋsɛm.
mighty acts. Ps. 106,2.
[omãnni] sociality; am. nti onyãã amannifo pii.
an edible root, coco = koókó; a small species is indigenous, a larger species was introduced in Akuapem
from the West-Indies in 1843; by-names: oyéŋ'-mmá, abofrá-gyàe-sú, koobi-siŋ-n'adàmfo. - amapkáni-mùá, a whole tuber of coco. - amāŋkani-sé, a sucker or shoot from the mother-plant, coco sucker.
[me àŋkása], Ak. me ara, I myself; my own. Gr. § 59.
Ak, a kind of state-umbrella; s. bamkyinii.
[ɔmaŋ akō] civil, intestine, domestic war; am., wokō a, wontwá tiri, wōmfá nnommum nso. - wokō mmátókwa, fighting with fists, sticks. &c.; abɔnteŋkó, fighting with guns in the streets.
inf. peace between neighbours or parties opposed to each other.
pl. a- [G. maŋkralo] the first in rank after the king in some of the small states or their capitals (leading towns) on the Gold Coast.
a species of tortoise. pr. 1927.
Ak. -o, a large species of beetle. pr. 2014.
Aky. -kuo, pl. a-, part of a nation; province. 1 Kg. 20, 14; people assembled. Acts 12, 22.
a certain bead; s. ahene. Amaŋkwátía, pr. n. m.
chancellor of state. Hist.
migration of nations. Hist. mmaŋkyíri [= báŋ akyi] = duasee, duaso, &c.
pl., s. ɔmaŋ-ba.
public law; constitution; cf. amānyɔ-mmàra.
constitutional party. Hist.
pl. (ɔ)-fó, countryman, townsman, one of the same country or town as another.
māŋ'ŋo, mango fruit; mango-tree (māŋo-duá).
māaŋ'ŋoó [Ger. bank] a European footstood; bench, form; cf. beŋkyi.

1. (sare so dua bim' amāne a wōde tàre ahina) the gum of a tree, used to plaster up leaking pots; gum-elastic, caoutchouc, India rubber; pitch. Gen. 6, 14. Ex. 2, 3; cf. amā. - 2. the tree yielding such gum.
[omaŋ &?] a foreign country; abroad. pr. 1496; (ahoho a, s. ananafo) kūrow bi a enyé wo kūrow-a. Am. asem ye di-nā.
pl. amāŋ-mpānyin, prince, chief. Ps. 119, 161; prime minister.
protector, defender of the commonwealth. Hist.
Mèn'sá [oba, esā] pr. n. m. of one born as the third child of his mother. - Maānsá pr. n. f. given to a girl being the third child of her mother.
[omaŋ, sāŋ, cf. sānteŋ] all people, all nations; the human race, mankind. pr. 455. 1712. 2844. 2942. - am. ahwee, international exhibition. - amāŋ-sānteŋ asāfo, the catholic (not the Roman) church.
calamity, ruin, destruction of a nation, state or town.
[omaŋ asem] state affairs, business of state, political policy, politics, public negotation; diplomacy; social life. - am. mu afe-fóro, civil New-year's day.
pl. a-, diplomatist.
pl. a-fo, secretary (or chancellor) of state.
organisation, reorganisation of the state; a setting right, successful arrangement of governmental or political matters. Acts 24, 2.
restoration of peace and order.

pl. a-, a subordinate, partly independent province of a nation; a province; F. an independent town of a country; wōaye wōŋ hō ɔm., wōde or wōada wōŋ m., they are a separate people for themselves. - ɔ-māŋsiŋ-héne, tetrarch. Mt. 14, 1. Lk. 3, 1. Acts 13, 1.
amānsimmaa, amansimmawa, pl. a- [omānsiŋ, dim.] a small province, district.
Akyém Mánsò (or Akyém Sòádúru, Western Akem), a district of Akyem, formerly subordinate to Akyem Kotoku.

discord, disagreement, variance, mutual animosity, hostility, enmity, strife. pr. 2015; - twẽ m., to be at variance. pr. 250; onè woŋ wo or twẽ m.; m. yɛnè Krɔbɔ ntam'. - ɔ-mánsó-boáfó, pl. a-, promoter of rebellion. pr. 2016.
pl. a-, a person offended with, or at variance with, another; quarreller, wrangler, brawler. pr. 2017; Prov. 24, 21; onipa yi yɛ ɔm., this is a quarrelsome, revengeful, vindictive person.
inf. government, rule; s. di 43.
minister or secretary of state. Hist.
people of other countries; heathens (Mk. 10, 33).
the government of a country; reign, regency.
pl. id. or a- or ɔmáŋsò-ahwέfo, a man at the head of a government, regent, ruler, consul.
policy, politics.
the head of a state; am, na yesõm no, we serve him as his subjects, not as slaves (ŋkoasõm).
quarrelsomeness, quarrelsome temper or disposition, litigiousness.
pl. a-, a quarrelsome, contentious, litigious, seditious person.
[mánsó-asɛm] a cause of disagreement, contention or hostility; controversy, litigiousness.
demagogue. Hist.
inf. discord, strife, quarrel; hostility, sedition, open rupture, disruption. pr. 2018; diff. atùatew.
pl. a-, a quarrelsome, contentious, brawling person, seditionary. pr. 2019.

v. to bind, tie, fasten, tether, make fast, a cow or sheep with a rope, a ship with an anchor, so that some liberty is left for movement. pr. 1003; intr. wakomantam, he (the dog) has been entangled in his chain or rope. - cf. kyekyere, sã. - red. mantám-mãntam: ne ntini m. abó-kúw hɔ, its roots fasten themselves to, are entwined about, a heap of stones. Job 8, 17.

pl. a-, a populous district or nation; a people forming a distinctive political body, a state. Akyem nè Akuapem, am. abieŋ yi, Asantefo tumi woŋ; a district; om, mù panyin, the president of a district. St. III, § 10.
part of a state, province.
pl. a-, prince, satrap. Dan. 3, 3.
pl. a- [omaŋ, otaŋ] a primitive people; a mother-state or country; an independent state; omaŋ a esõ, omaŋ kokũroko a ne ŋkõ da hɔ; tribe. Ps. 74, 2.
[mãntám, v. & dua] a parasitic plant; general name for creeping plants. Cf. nyaŋkõnnuru.
pl. amantease-ŋk. [kũrow a efi teteete te ase se omaŋ] a nation of long standing or existence; woye om. pa, they are a very ancient or old nation. - ɔ-mãnteasé-máŋ, id.
amántemaa, a gossip; nea n'ano ye bɛtebete.

[amaŋ a etoatoaso kɔ pii, cf. teŋ] a series or succession of towns. Amántɛŋ-sò fi Akũropoŋ kosi Berekuso, the towns between Akropong & Berekuso; mpoanofo am. da po hɔ. - amanteŋsofó, the inhabitants of such towns.
double-dealing, duplicity; odi am., he is double-minded, halts between two opinions or parties, shifts or turns from one side to the other, shuffles, prevaricates; s. di. 7.
pl. a-, province.
subordinate towns, dependent on a leading town (as the coast towns from Osu to Niŋo are dependent on Ŋkraŋ pa). - amantiásefó, the inhabitants of such towns.
[omaŋ atifi] the northern or upper part of the country, the high country. - am, asase, highland.
[omaŋ atoro] high treason; di am., to commit h. tr.
inf. disturbance of the good relations between two (or more) countries.
(pl.) [ɔmāŋ, tow] single states, tribes or districts, towns, townships or communities; Akuapem am. si 17.

[baŋ, fence & tweaa] the place between the wall of a house and the mark made by the water dropping from the eaves; asase a eda ofasu nè ntɔnoa ntam'; mã me wo m. baabi mentrā, give me somewhere to live in your house.
[ɔba, ɔbaa, enu] pr. n. m. & f., the second child of a mother. Gr. § 41, 5.
pl. a-, or mannūafó, a neighbouring people; wɔanyé-wɔŋ mannūafó pa bi, they were no good neighbours to them.

a byname of the five Kyerepong towns Abiriw, Odawu, Awukugua, Adukrom, Apirede. [fr. amannūa-anum, five brother-towns, or fr. aman-aduonum, fifty towns, so many being said to have existed once]. Gr. Introd. § 5.

Mannúro, name of a certain fetish, also known by the name of Aberewa. It consists of two parts, the male being called Mannuro or Būrogya, the female Aberewa. Egu ahorow abien a eye ade koro no ara: ɔbarima nè ɔbaa. Obea no de Aberewa, na ɔbarima a oye ne bārafo nè kunu no de Mannuro anase Būrogya. Womfá wɔŋ abien no nyinaa nsi fākō: se Aberewa si hɔ a, na Mannuro seŋ hɔ.
Otwīi am., a pure Tshi man.
-ŋwéé [ɔmaŋ, dwo] peace, tranquillity of a people.
a species of yam, s. ɔdè. [Ewe lang.]

(n., a., adv.) disorderly, in a confused state or manner; scattered; crowded, teeming, swarming. Gen. 1, 20. 21; cf. hwanyaŋ mu, sakasaka; - nnipa nennam hɔ m., people walk there in a crowded, confused manner; mpaŋ nennam dagmu m., the house or room is swarming with bats; wɔaye m., they have been confused, jumbled or huddled (together); they are dispersed (wɔŋ nyinaa ŋkɔ fākō, oyi afa ha, oyi afa ha).
[ɔmaŋ gyina] welfare of the (whole) people; firm establishment of the kingdom or commonwealth. pr. 3010.

amányɔ, inf. [ye ɔmaŋ] social relation, demeanour, behaviour, deportment (in living with others). pr. 1181; syn. amāmmu, abrabɔ; wo ámányé or wo ámányɔ n'yé mè fe! óyè amanyɔpá = obu amammuipá, he observes decency. K. § 349.

[ade a wode ye ɔmaŋ na aye yiye] good manners; morality, civilization. - ɔ-mãn-yɛfó, a good, quiet, considerate citizen, onipa a oye ɔmaŋ yiye, ɔpe asem a emã ɔmaŋ mu dwo. pr. 2020. amányɔ-mmãrá, constitution; b ye am., to give or agree upon a constitution. - amanyɔ-sém, politics.
(siká àmàpá), native, pure gold that has not yet undergone any operation and is unmixed with dross; wode amapá ŋkō gu petea a, enyé yiye, gye se wofram'.
[he who grants satiation] an appellation of God.
[he who gives rain] ditto; s. Amosu.
[he who gives the sun] ditto; s. Amowia.
inf. [pe, ɔbaa] love or fondness for women, courting of or going after women, fornication. pr. 2021.
= apɛde 3.
pl., s. ɔbapɔmma.
m'ada, F. = me ara; mara a! it is I. Mk. 6,50.

v. n. [bāra, bra] law, commandment, order, decree, edict, regulation, rule, statute; ɔbra hō mm., moral law; asɔre hō mm., ceremonial law; ɔmaŋ hō mm., political law. - hye (or di) mm., to make, give (or issue) a law; cf. di 48; - di mm. so, (or ye mm.) to observe or keep a law; - tō mm., to transgress a law; - hye.. mm., to give instructions or commandment; cf. ahyede. Gen. 26,5.
pl. -nsem, commandment; cf. ahyede. Gen. 26,5.
mrá, v., s. mãnã.
s. amãnã.
s. amōnă.

s. mmrabram'.
[mmăra a eda hɔ] an old law, a standing rule.
= amănăde.
s. amrădo.
legalism, 'legality'; s. frene.
inf. the act of giving laws; legislation; s. mmăra.

slime of snails.
= mměraŋ.
adv., denotes the wriggling of a serpent in motion; ɔwɔ nantew m.
lawyer. Tit. 3, 13.
pieces of bronze or brass for abrammo &c.; syn. gúde.
pl. id. doer of the law. Rom. 2, 13. — mmăra-téfó, hearer of the law. ib.
inf. transgression (of a law). — mmărăto-adé, -de, iniquity. Rom. 6, 19; transgressions. Ezek. 18, 30 f.
fine for the transgression of a law; wòbegye ne hɔ m., he will be fined.
pl. id. transgressor (of a law), malefactor.
pl. mmănăt., pl. id. nea ɔtow mmără a, s. ɔpra ɔhene hɔ, a bearer of an elephant's tail before the king; syn. ɔhōprafo, q. v.
pl. m-fó, mulatto; better: omurătóni.
-yófo [nea ɔye mmăra] a fulfiller of the law.
a certain kind of cloth; ntama bi a snam ahorow beye se 4 a woapam afra; s. ntama.
[bare hɔ] the hoop of a cask.
[bare, hyia] circumference, area.
the Tshi name for Hausa and other countries on and beyond the Niger.
[ɔbarima ade] = mmaninné;
= ɔye nnam, he is manly, behaves like a man.
= mmarima-so; monyɛ mo hɔ m., behave ('quit yourselves') like men!
= abaninsem.
[not Akp.] = basabasa. side of the human body (between the armpit and the hip-bone); also armpit(?)
[basă ase] the right or the left side of the human body (between the armpit and the hip-bone); also armpit(?)
[ɔba, sigyaw] the state of being without children; di mm., to be childless, deprived of children; s. bas. & 1 Sam. 15, 33. 1 Thess. 2, 17.

Ak. -o [nsu a eba, efi nsu ani-wam' ba] living water, spring water, issuing continually from the earth. pr. 1056; running or flowing water; ɔde mm. bi a ɔkohũi ɔkwaŋ mu kum ne sukɔm, he found some spring-water on the way and quenched his thirst with it. Gen. 26, 19. — kyere mmasuo = bɔ or si baŋ wɔ nsum', to make a fence in the water for catching fish.
inf. [bata..bɔ mu] = ŋkǎbom'.

inf. [bata hɔ] 1. the act of adding or joining one thing to another. — 2. the cooking or roasting of different things on the same fire, which is superstitiously avoided. — 3. appendage, appendix, accompaniment; cf. ŋkǎhɔ, ŋkekǎhɔ. — 4. woaye no n'adwuma hɔ m., they have hindered him in his work. — mmatahó-kyí, the act of avoiding or shunning promiscuous cooking or roasting.
ŋkūkuraha, a species of climbing plant or creeper. pr. 1167. 2022. 2828.
a. slimy, clammy, cloggy, glutinous, lubricous, viscous, mucous (e.g. hwenɔre); syn. măă, prǎprǎ; cf. săă, twǎă; dote no yɛ m. (enyé sămsam); okásá mătămătǎ, stammering speech. K. § 318; s. tekrema.
a. brimful, full to the brim.
Ak, batiri [ba, baw, basa, & ti, tiri] shoulder. pr. 130. 1279. - mátò ne
I have empowered (authorized) him, s. to 17. - okä ne m., he shrugs, gives a shrug. Zech. 7,11.
inf. authorization, commission.
má-tətətə [mä, G. to, tətətə] chock-full, topful, crammed.
mmaatókwa [abaa, abaw, ntɔkwaw] scuffle, fighting with fists, sticks &c.; wəkő m. = wəkő amaŋkő.
ɔkw. = awotwëaa.
interj., said to a leaving visitor.
s. wu, v.
s. əbaye. - mmá-yéŋ, inf. education.
inf. fulfilment, fulness. - mäyetrəső, infinite fulness. K. § 225.
pron., F. eme, I, me, my. When prefixed to a verb having close sounds (i, u, full e & o, gya, nyä, twa, dwa), it is written mi; the e is dropped before the prefix a-. Gr. § 53-59.
mint, Menta, an aromatic herb used as a medicine. Mt. 23,23; ebinom due sumaŋ a, wode fra akokő nőa na wodi.

pl. a-, the palm of the hand or a stroke with it; wəabə no amë. pr. 3030; F. Mt. 26,67. - cf. ntentemmë, bə twere, kotromüa, kutruku, sőtore; bə fe, pl. afe; biram, guram; ohwe ne hő amë, she beats herself (out of pain, grief, misfortune &c.) with the palms of her hands.

v. [red. mëëmëë] tr. to feed to the full, to fill, satisfy, satiate; - intr. to eat so as to be satisfied, to eat enough. pr. 509; perf. to be satisfied or satiated, to have enough; aduaŋ yi nnim mämëë, s. nim 1. pr. 243 f. 260. 3666. - wamëë së, he has eaten his fill. - didi mëë, inf. the act of satisfying &c. or of eating enough; the state of having eaten enough, so as to be satisfied, satiety, fulness. pr. 863. 2030. 2191.
interj. come in! said in answer to àgoo, by which word one's coming (in darkness &c.) is announced.
[beabea mu] (several lines, sticks &c. lying) lengthwise, or parallel, or across (each other); nsensagee m., a cross (in any form).
mmëáé-mmëáé, pl., s. bea, beae, place.
s. akyeŋkyenä.
[bea mu] bar, cross-bar, cross-beam. Ex. 26,26.
F. mb., mberemu-dua, pl. m.-nnua [dua a ebi bẹa mu] a cross.
pron. even I, just I, I myself. Gr. § 59; F. mara, mada.
= mmaeda; nea waye m., an inventor.
name of the cat in fables, from its voice; s. agyinamoa.
[abe efë] the refuse or trash of the palm-nut, the fibres from which the oil has been extracted.
a. fine, finely woven, smooth; ne kente or ketɛ ani ye m.; ŋhoma or atuduru no ani ye m.; watwitwa nãm no m., better: ŋketeŋkete.
myself. Gr. § 57. pr. 242.
[abe ŋkwaŋ] palm-nut soup, a greasy soup, prepared with the pulpy or mealy and oily substance of palm-nuts, a favourite dish of the natives.
not having come to stay or last long; onipa ye am. = amma ammekye koraa; yeŋ de, yeye am.; ye aba am. Cf. ammakyewa.

v. [red. memmem] to sink (down, nsum', in water, asase mu, in the earth); to be sunk, swallowed up, absorbed; nsu no amëm, the water has been sucked up, absorbed in the ground; to disappear, hide or lose oneself, be lost (wuram', in the bush); to (cause to) sink, put under water, immerse in a fluid; əsrämäŋ, amëm fam', the lightning (thunder-stone) has entered the ground.
s. bëmma & ebɛŋ.
red. v., s. mä.
the slimy (alvine) discharges of children, stools.
a certain animal. pr. 523.
red. v. mëë; - to swell; n'anaŋ ase ameemee, her feet are swollen.
leech, blood-sucker, Hirudo, Sanguisuga medicinalis.
F. red. a., s. meŋ.
F. redness.
Ak, brain; s. hoŋ.
red. v. mene, to swallow up several things. pr. 2694; wamèmmène ne mfẽ tweŋ wo, he dislikes waiting for you. — red. a. meŋ.
Memèrèda, Saturday. Gr. § 41, 4. pr. 244. 1088. — Mem. Dapaa, s. dabone & dapaa.
(one who swallows up kings) a vaunting appellation of a king; ohene biara a oye otumfo, ohye ahene yh. so. pr. 2031.

[wamèmmène né mfẽ, he has swallowed his side] disgust, displeasure, dislike, distaste, vexation, indignation; èyè no am. = ompene, enyé no de, enyé no abodwo, eye no awereho; ode am. saŋe, vexed or fretting (at his mistake) he returned.
pr. 2109, = ebiŋ?

mene asé, menewáase, the under or lower part of the throat, gullet or esophagus; the heart as the seat of suppressed resentment; a grudge; woŋ menĕase nni pow, they bear no grudge; ode mè m., ode me ahye m., he bears me a grudge or spite; - nè mènaasé retew pe biribi adi, he has a good appetite, is very hungry; woŋ m. retow nè sukom, they pant with thirst, their throats are dried up with thirst.
or -daá (dawá), the uvula in the throat; ne menaase-daa ayi, ahoŋ. — mènaase-kotokú, maw, gizzard.

1. the prominent part of the throat, Adam's-apple (the projection formed by the thyroid cartilage in the neck). — 2. a grudge, hindrance of cordiality; owɔ no m., he owes him a grudge; óyì ne m., s. epow 1.
goitre.

v. [red. memmene] to swallow (up), suck up, to gulp (down), devour; to ingulf, absorb, to consume. Ex. 32;10. pr. 523. 2242. 2694. 2949; mmènè nãm sa, na wosaw ansã-na woamene, do not gulp down the meat like that, but masticate it before you swallow it!

menewá, the throat, gullet, esophagus; wotwaa né mène, they cut his throat. pr. 387. 2032. — okosɛŋ ne mene, he went and hanged himself. - ɔkã ne menem' or ne menewam', he utters the sound 'hem', he hems; agyinamoa kã ne menewam', the cat is dried up; he is thirsty; cf. menaase, amenewá.
òyè om., it (the enini) swallows the whole of a beast or man without tearing it to pieces; ade biara onyã no, omemmene no prɛkɔ sore so.

[bɛŋ] nearness, neighbourhood; obɛda mmɛnee nne, he is to sleep in the neighbourhood to-night.

v. to swell, e.g. of the virile member; of a river: nsu amenem so = nsu asram so, the river overflows its banks; nsu atwẽ am., the water decreases; fig.: otwẽ amenem (hyewe), he withdrew or disappeared (as if consumed by fire).
red. v. to swell, of a river; - nsu no ani m. = ye hurutu-tutu, q. v.

inf. strangling. — menetwá, inf. cutting of the throat, slaying. Isa. 22, 13.
