sore throat. - menewam'-síw, inf. strangling, strangulation. Job 7, 15.
pl. a-, a bird of the savanna, as large as a turkey, in form like a raven, black with a white breast; a species of heron? cf. dawakyafa.
inf. sounding a horn or horns; playing on a flute; music.
(I alone shall eat or enjoy): yɛ m., to be selfish, self-interested. pr. 2029. 3571.

mmɛŋkyɛŋéé [beŋkyɛ(ŋ)] = mmɛŋee; mefre wo akyirikyiri a, gye me mmɛŋkyɛŋee, if I call to thee as from afar, answer and save me as one being near. - mmɛŋkyɛŋéé-fó, persons in the neighbourhood, neighbours; cf. ofipãmfo.
Mansã [oba, nsã] pr. n. (= the third child).
-sá, ménsá pá, a species of yam, s. ɔdé. pr. 2033. 2261. 2559.
bensere, basin.
a wind-instrument; seven horns blown together (mmeŋ asoŋ na wəde gye dwom biakõ so). amensɔŋ, F. = amansaŋ.
imper. of ba; mã yeŋ hõ m. yeŋ hõ bio, restore us again. Ps. 60, 3.
mmăraŋ', Ak. mmäranne, surname, byname; attribute; wəbə no or wəpae no m., they give him or cry out his (honouring) bynames; gye m., to acquire a(n honourable) byname; cf. ɔbĕraŋ, nsăbĕraŋ.
[aberante, bere] youth, the part of life between mmofraase and ŋkwakoraabere.
exuberance of youthful gaiety, arrogance. pr. 88.
óyè ne hõ m., he walks in an affected manner, behaves proudly; cf. kyĕa. - mmĕrante-sém, s. dòŋŋ. mmĕrantiwa-sém [aberantewa, asɛm]
boast, vaunt, ostentation; ɛda adi wə kasam' nè nneysem'; óyè m. = óyè ahăntaŋ; ŋkwaŋkwaasem (flaunting) da adi wə nantew n.a. mu.
enní mmĕre-énní, so it is everywhere.
mmĕré, mushroom, fungus; ŋkatum, akotroko, mmĕwĕre, s. ananse-utaamma 4. pr. 373. 399. 603. 2034.
= mmerew

[obsol. = bere, bea, nea] place or manner (in which); where; amere (= amere a) wúfi ɛ? = nea wufi ɛ? - fãkõ mere ogyinae na ohúú saa no, ommekyere na yentie! - amere wóyé ni! = senea woye ni! F. mbɛye m'adwima de-mre n'asɛm kyere n' ara, I shall do my duty according to his word.
a tree (ofram kokɔɔ) used as a medicine on sores (pr. 2035), and for making shingles. - 2. s. amiri.
ahɔbĕrease, humility &c.
a disease of the skin; éyè onípa hõ kɔɔkɔɔ; - a blotch on the skin.
a small kind of mushroom.
liver. pr. 3667.
a species of ant, small, of a reddish colour, having its nest upon trees; ntétéa bi a wəwə dua so keka onipa.
ahɔbĕrease.
saw-dust; owaŋ anase sradaa ano m.; cf. ntetew-tutuw. - 2. the finest part of gold-dust. pr. 885.
a kind of rum or brandy.
a species of fish (caught e.g. at Kasunyã, on the way from Batɔɔ to Sandɔ).
a flock of goats. Cant. 4, 1.
= mmeamudua, cross; cf. asɛŋdua.
the young, light-green shoots or blades of palms; s. ŋkoŋmu; the straight shoot at the top of a palm-tree.

(a piece of) armour or dress. pr. 3114. 3195. — armed host. Job 39, 21; adornment (pr. 3114).
armoury. Neh. 3, 19.
armed men. Isa. 15, 4.

a name for leprosy; s. kwata.

well then! good speed! good luck! hail! all hail! It may be said twice, thrice &c. - mó nè kɔ́! mó nè adwúma! mó nè yó! - mã.. mó nè kɔ́ (adwuma, yɔ), to congratulate on account of fighting (work, doing). pr. 2039. Cf. amo.

rice, Oryza, the plant and the grains; gu mɔ̃ (in Kyerehí: saka mɔ̃), to sow rice.
a kind of resin or gum, used for waxing thread.

Job 18, 7; ontumi ntwẽ ne naŋ mu se kaŋ no bio.
pl. id. = mmũá.

Gr. § 248.
mmóbɔ-hű, inf. pitying, commiseration; cf. mmɔbőrɔhunu, pity.

a. & adv., miserable, pitiful, in a miserable state or condition; n'anim ye m., he looks wretched, miserable, has a sad countenance. Neh. 2,2; ónam m., he walks about in a sad condition. — mmóbɔmmóbɔyé, inf. sadness. Eccl. 7,3.
Ak. a scroll = mmobɔwe.

[bobɔ mu] 1. a white cotton cloth interwoven with red threads in squares; kente no ye m., wode adidi sika apwene mu ahigaŋaŋ-ahigaŋaŋ. — 2. a collection, accumulation, mass, heap, assemblage; opp. aŋkoraŋkoro. — 3. roaring (of a lion). mmofrá-bere, [abofra, ase, bere] childhood, the time from birth or infancy to puberty [con. ne mmófra-ase, ne mmófra-bere].
a siliquose plant.
-akókóáá, -kòkətè, different kinds of plants.
childish talks, dealings or concerns; s. ykisiwasɛm.

a certain tree; sareso dua bi.

[bə hố] doubling, duplication; double; pair (anantwi m. anaŋ, four pairs of oxen); multiplication by two or more than two; wəadə m. abiesã, their number has trebled; mitua no kaw m. anaŋ, I pay him or restore it to him fourfold.
[mmore a akaw] leaven, leavened dough.
F. = mako, pepper.

[red. mommom, q. v.] to roll or wrap up, furl, envelop; to squeeze together (that the hollow space appears): dorobəŋ no amom; mom akatawia no ano, shut or put up the umbrella! wakã ne nneɛma nyinaa amôm ano, he has packed up all his things.

[or mmóm', fr. bə mu] 1. ordinance, injunction, decree; interdiction, prohibition, prohibitory law; cf. mmãra; wəahye môm se obiara mmə so, they have decreed that nobody should mention the matter; every one is forbidden to speak of it. - 2. agreement; cf. mmom'; wəakəhye m. = wəapàm.
inf. [bə mu] joining, reconciliation; agreement, convention, contract, stipulation, treaty; communion, peace.

adv. (s. bef.), F. mmo (= mpo, Ak.) rather, in preference, more properly; mepe eyi m., I like this better; mepe ha-yi m. kyeŋ hə, I like this place better than that one; ɛno m. na ényé koraa, that is rather not good at all, that is even worse.
(mẽmã), red. v. 1. s. mã. - 2. to dedicate, devote to; əde asəredaŋ (sika, ne ba) mômã Onyame. - 3. to praise, extol, exalt, glorify; wəmômã ohẽne
inf. (s. bef.) circumlocution; discussion, explanation; expatiating on, (idle) talk; ɛhō m. ni.

pl. of abompɔrɔ.
v. F. (= mō, mŭ?) to be unrighteous. Heb. 6, 10.
mmɔŋ' (cf. bɔŋ v.) a neigh, neighing, whinnying; — bɔ m., to neigh, whinny (of horses). Jer. 5, 8. 8, 16. — ka m., F. to wail. Mk. 5, 38. — mmɔŋ-bɔ, inf. neighing. Jer. 13, 27.
s. bonnaa; — tɔ m., to intrude upon women by night, to ravish. — inf. m.-tɔ, the ravishing of women, rape. — ɔ-mmōnnaatɔ́fɔ, pl. a, = ɔbōnnaatɔfɔ.

a., n. freshness; rawness; me yam' wɔ no (ɔ)m., I bear him a grudge.

Gr. § 70, 1-3; ɔdé mòmóno, ɔdé-amóno; anǎmmóno (wodi anǎmmono, they eat meat, wodi nǎm mòmóno, they eat raw meat); ɔdé no yɛ mómóno; cf. ahabàmmóno. — àmóno kǎŋwɛë, quite fresh or new, used also of persons, as, a blooming youth; cf. buŋ. — àmóno also = sika.
= nǎm momono a wɔa-how dakoro pɛ, meat smoked only one day.
[amono mu, lit. in the fresh] directly, immediately, forthwith, on the spot; ɔbo no bɔɔ no no, amónom' hɔara na ɔtoe, when the stone hit him, he fell dead on the spot; F. amonm hɔara, suddenly.
red. mónommonom, mórōmmōrōm, a. smooth; opoŋ no ye m.; cf. ɛso ye torotoro.
mmonsé [ohoŋ ase] valley, lowland at the foot of mountains.
mmonséfó, inhabitants of the lowlands. Judg. 1, 19. 34.

(u = ū), the interior. 1. the inner or middle part, inside; any part or point within the limits of a line, surface or body. cf. pr. 148 f. — 2. the inner parts, cf. anom', asɔm', mfɛm', yam' &c.; the space within or inside. — 3. the interior of a country: emú nohɔ (no-hɔa) tɔŋŋ, far in the interior. — 4. As a postposition after nouns & pronouns it stands for the foll. prepp. & advv.: in, at, into, through, within, inward, inside; between; of time: in, at, during, within; of a plurality of things: among, amongst; connected with certain verbs (as fi, to proceed from): out, from; - di mu, s. di 24. 25. - See Gr. § 119 & Rem. on the tone of mu, which is high after a preceding low tone, and low after high tone. When used as a postposition or complement, the vowel u is often dropped, and the remaining m' connected in pronunciation with the noun or pronoun to which it refers, or with the verb. — 5. In some phrases emu forms the grammatical subject (instead of the thing to which it refers), as: emú dà hó, it is or lies open, is manifest, plain; emu dɔ, it is deep (abura, asu no mu, ɛpo mu dɔ); emu gow, it is spacious; emu tɛrɛw, it is wide; emu yɛ deŋ, it is difficult; ne yarɛ mu yɛ deŋ, his illness is severe; emu ntew me yiye, it is not quite plain to me. Gr. § 215. — 6. When compounded with nouns, mu expresses a manner of doing = after the manner or fashion of; e.g. mmàrìmàm', nnìpam', brɔfɔm', s. Gr. § 131, 4. — 7. In composition with verbs, mu has the power of an adverb, meaning in, between, together; cf. bam', bom', dam', gum', wom', nnim', hyiam', tiam' &c. — mu or m' influences the pronunciation of preceding vowels, making the open vowels (a, ɛ, ɔ) half-open (ə, F. e; e, o), and the half-close vowels (e, o) close (i, u). e-mú, the interior or middle part of the body, the chest, thorax, rump, back; espec. the upper part of the back, cf. akyi; ɔyare né mú, he has a disease of the chest or lungs; né mú bŭ fɔŋŋ, his (rump) back is flexible; ɔpono ne mú, he is bending his back; ɔtɛɛ ne mú, he stretches his back; ɔbɔ ne mú ase, s. bɔ 68.

The eye and its look being expressive of understanding, intelligence and prudence, of affections, of moral qualities &c., ani (or ani so) is used with the following verbs (which are alphabetically arranged). In A) ani or ani so is the grammatical subject; in B) ani, ani so, ani akyi, is the grammatical object of the sentence. A) n'aní bà mé sò, he remembers me; n'ani ba asem no so, he recollects the matter; n'aní bà ne hɔ so, he comes to himself, recovers his senses. Acts 12, 11. Lk. 15, 17. - n'ani abere, 1. he is in a passion, impassionate, strongly affected, in a rage, angry. pr. 2290. - 2. he is grieved, sorrowful, mournful, in a fit of grief or melancholy. pr. 2292. - n'ani bere ade (sika, mmea), he covets, desires, eagerly wishes for, lusts after something (money, women). pr. 2298. 2291; n'ani bere adwuma, he cannot rest satisfied till he gets something to do. - n'ani so biri no, he is giddy. - n'ani bɔ me so, his look falls on me; n'ani bota me, he has a glimpse (look) of me. - n'ani abu, he is tired of waiting, or, with expectation, impatient; yeatwɛŋ no mã yeŋ ani abu (mã afono yeŋ) = yeatwɛŋ no abĕre, we waited for him till we were quite tired. - n'ani (so) da hɔ, he is modest, unassuming; he is sober, temperate, moderate, cool, considerate; he is awake, in his (sober) senses, in his right mind; he is wise; ani a ɛnna hɔ, intemperance, incontinence &c. 1 Cor. 7, 5; n'ani so da hɔ, he is awake; n'ani da hɔ kăŋ, he is fully awake, lively, brisk, cheerful, quite clear. - u'ani da kwaŋ (so), As. he expects, is in expectation; n'ani da sa, so is his intention; sɛ m'ani da ni, so is my intention, thus I have purposed; - n'ani da me so, he hopes, trusts, confides in me, relies on me; n'ani da so, he hopes, expects; it is his intention; n'ani daa so sɛ meba, he hoped I would come; n'ani da so sɛ ɛdaŋ deŋ ara a, sare no bɛsee, he expects that the grass will be certain to spoil; n'ani da akatua so, he hopes for a reward; m'ani da Nyagkp. so, I trust in God. - n'ani da ne hɔ so, he is cautious, circumspect, considerate. - kŭrow no ani da yiye, the town is undisturbed, calm; kŭrow no ani nna yiye, the (whole) town is disturbed, in alarm, agitation, excitement, - yeduu hɔ no ani nna yiye, when we arrived there, the town was in a state of excitement. - ani adaŋ (ani = surface, appearance), the matter has changed, circumstances have altered, the aspects are different; ɔmaŋ no ani adaŋ = mansɔtwẽ aba ɔmaŋ no mu, the people or public affairs are in a state of disturbance. - n'ani dɔ ŋkrăŋ, he rages, is furious, frantic, rabid, infuriated. - n'ani dwo, he is quiet, peaceable, calm, tame, soft, mild, gentle, meek; ɔyɛ n'ade komm komm; aboa no ani adwo, the beast has lost its wildness; cf. n'ani ye merɛw; opp. n'ani abere; n'ani adwudwo, he has been softened, appeased, pacified. - n'ani afa so, he has overlooked it; cf. n'ani apa so, ne wɛre afi. - n'ani afi, he has arrived at the age of discretion, is cunning; cf. n'ani apae, atew; - ani afi, the surface is clean; s. fi 3. 7. - n'ani afura (Ak. afira), he has become or is blind. - n'ani (a)gye, he rejoices, is joyful, glad, cheerful. pr. 2208. 2296f. - n'ani gyina (ne nã, ne kŭrom'), he longs after or for, earnestly desires, is homesick for (his mother, his country), syn. wafe (ne nã); cf. n'ani

(= afi, atew), he is cunning.

water, i. e. tears have filled his eyes, his eyes are swimming with tears, - the tears standing in the eyes;

he is in consternation, alarm, confusion, perplexity = ɛye no aniani. - n'ani so ye no yaa, he is astonished. - n'ani so aye yiye, (ironic.) he is tipsy, flustered &c. - n'ani so nyé, he is tipsy, muddled &c., cf. bow (nsã).

he becomes intoxicated. - wode ábàre ani, they have engaged in battle, have come to close quarters, are fighting hand to hand; cf. bare; ani = face, front, face to face; bɔ ani, to join battle. Gen. 14,9; ɔkɔ no abɔ ani, the fighting has begun, both fronts meeting together, encountering each other. - obu no ani, he winks at him; cf. anikyew; obubu n'ani, he winks, twinkles; obu n'ani gu .. so, he winks or connives at, overlooks, does not take notice of. - da (n')ani, to sleep soundly; cf. abofra no daa n'ani, the boy slept soundly. - ódà or ɔdedá n'áni akyì, odwudwo n'ani akyi has wanton eyes (nea wode ye ne sɔ: mmarima de frefre mmea, na mmea nso de frefre mmarima). Isa. 3, 16; ɛda m'ani akyi, I take no notice of it, I don't mind it. - odan n'ani, he turns his eyes somewhere; ɔdaŋ asɛm bi ani (= surface), he changes a matter (e.g. a word said yesterday); wɔadaŋ abusũa (or ɔmaŋ) no ani, the family (or nation) has (got) a new head; wadaŋ n'akoa ani, he has changed his slave, i. e. sold one and bought another in his stead. - di.. ani: ne kese, ne fɛ (n. a.) di wo ani, its greatness, beauty (&c.) is extraordinary or beyond description; kũrow no bɔɔ twi, ne ŋwɔŋwã di wo ani, the town was in a stir beyond description. - odwo n'ani, he moderates his haste, his demand. - ohwe m'ani akyi, he observes whether I make a sullen or cheerful face. pr. 343. - ogow n'ani kãe.., he said in a low or soft voice, gently.. - ogyeŋ n'ani hwe .no, he looks sharply or closely at him. - ahɛŋhaŋ n'ani so, it has become unimportant in his eyes, -s. hãŋ. - akã n'ani, he has got to suffer for it, has been served out for it. - ɔde kãã m'ani se memfa nsu mmã no, he asked me for water. - ɔkã n'ani gu so, he shuts his eyes in sleep or death. - omia n'ani, he squeezes his eye, i. e. he exerts himself, he tries, endeavours; memia m'ani maye prekɔ, I will try and do it at once. - omũa n'ani tew, he twinkles. - wanyã me hɔ ani bone, he has bad intentions towards me. - enni ani, s. ɛwɔ ani. - enni n'ani so bio, he no more remembers it or thinks of it, he has no longer the sight of it; he does not mind it. - ɔpa n'ani akyi, she draws up her eye-brows. - opupuw n'ani kyerɛ woŋ, he spoke roughly to them. Gen. 42, 7. 30. - esi n'ani so, it presents itself before his eyes, i. e. it enters into his thoughts, mind or head. - ɛsɔ n'ani, it pleases him, he is pleased with it, has complacency in it. - wode asɛ ani, they have fallen in with the enemy, are engaged in battle or close fight; cf. wode abare ani. - susuw wo ani gye me kakra, lit. measure your eye take from me little, i. e. moderate your demand, do not overcharge me! - ɔtane woŋ ani, he disquiets, disturbs, teazes, troubles, annoys, deranges them; ɔhye nè hĩa nè awɛrshow tane nipa ani. - otew n'ani, 1. he opens his eye (from sleep); ɔtetew n'ani, he opens his eyes; 2. he is cautious, cf. n'ani atew. - nsã atew n'ani so, he has become sober after his intoxication. - to wo ani hwe ha, look here! - to wo ani kyerɛ Sidon, set your face against S. (cf. Ezek. 28, 21)! - ɔtoto n'ani, he casts his eyes or looks in different directions, he looks about. - ɔde n'ani to me so, he confides or puts his trust in me; ɔde n'ani to m'anim: a) he respects me; b) he has confidence in me; ɔde n'ani -too m'anim yee, in deference to me he did it; fa wo ani to m'agya anim yɛ mã me, for my father's sake do me this favour! - watɔ n'ani aŵe, he has deadened his conscience. - wɔatu(tu) n'ani, they have put out his eye(s); - wɔatu woŋ ani de rehwe no = wɔrehwe no diŋŋ, they cast their piercing looks on him; ɛdeŋ na wututu wo ani rehwe or rekyerɛ
preface, introduction; kā (asɛm bi) n., to say (something) by way of introduction.
1. headlessness, regardlessness. 2. one who respects or esteems nobody.
a species of jumping insect.

1. the cheek; nsen-sane abien twa n'an., two lines are cut across his cheek. pr. 1847. 2. the side or slope of a hill: bepɔw no ani ase fã yɛ kũrɔŋkũrɔŋ, na n'an. fã de, esĩaŋ ŋkakra-ŋkakra; sũare bi aniase, s. sũare.

1. desire, longing, lust, concupiscence, cupidity, covetousness; sika yɛ no an., gold excites his cupidity; cf. yɛ 11. pr. 2374.3555. 2. excitement, irritation, exasperation; desperation. pr. 1597. 3. grief, sorrow, distress, bitterness. 4. hot displeasure, animosity, anger, wrath, rage. 5. F. (anyibir) violence. Mt. 11, 12. - atɔ an., it has come to the extreme, to the highest point or pitch; they proceed to action; cf. pɔmpɔŋ. ani-berebéré, covetousness; ani-bereberɛ, Ak. rage.

the state of being aware or conscious of some matter; ɛye an. na ɔyee, he was well aware of what he did; opp. nsapa.

[oni = onipa, dɔ] humanity, gentleness, affability, kindness, amiableness; ɔye n., he is humane, kind, benevolent. — ani-dwó, inf. [n'ani dwɔ] calmness, mildness &c. of temper.

a right-handed person.
[nifã, enu] s. nĩmfãnu.
inf. an oversight, error, mistake, inadvertence; ɛye an., it was done inadvertently. Gen. 43, 12.

inf. sharpness of sight, quicksightedness, penetration, sagacity, acuteness, cunningness, skillfulness, slyness; > anitew; ɔye n., he does every thing cunningly, in a sly manner; commonly in a bad sense, sometimes in a good sense; woye an., a nuipa nsa ŋkã wo.
pl. a-, a keen-, sharp-, quick- or clear-sighted, sagacious person or animal; ànɔmaa nif., a quick-sighted bird. pr. 2491.

[n'ani gye] joy, gladness, delight, happiness, pleasure, gaiety; syn. anikã, ahɔsãŋ, ahɔsɛpɛw, ahɔmekã, ahɔtɔ, abotɔyam'. — ànígye-béa, a place of joy; an. seŋ awɔbɛa, ubi bene ibi patria, where it is well, there is one's country; 'where it goes well with me, there is my fatherland'. pr. 2310. — ànígye-de, a pleasure, pleasurable thing or performance, enjoyment, amusement, sport. — ànígyefó, pl. id. one that rejoices. Rom. 12, 15. — ànígyesé: bɔ .. an., to give (one) a shout of joy. Deut. 32, 43; s. ose. — ànígyetrásó, excessive joy.
F. anyigyeŋ', soberly.
homesickness, longing after, desire for. - anígyina-de, desire, desired thing. Prov. 13,12. Job. 6,8.
staring eyes; ohwe no an., he stares at him; pl. wəhwe no ànihãã-hãã, they stare at him.
sloth, laziness, tardiness. pr. 2314f., syn. akwadwero, werehunu (Ak.). - óyè an. (or an. akã no), he is lazy, idle, inactive.
a species of fly.
one too lazy to do any thing except eat and chat; sluggard. pr. 2311 ff.; syn. okwadwofo.
outward, -ly; an outward sign. - aníani-ha-yi, id. K. § 125.
a thing or place belonging or accessible to common people, profane. Ezek. 42,20. 44,23; s. the foll.
a fetishman or priest, one of the laity; layman; stranger. Nu. 18,4; (= onipa hunu) cf. akwa(ni)hūmani, ayemfo.
wanyã akõ nni, onyãã ŋkõnim nniĩ, he often or repeatedly gained the victory; s. nyã.
joy, gladness &c., s. anigye.
modesty, carefulness, quietness; wisdom; de an. kaŋ, to read quietly or carefully.

F. covetous desires.
remains of eatables; diff. nnekae.
being of a bright or clear eye, i.e. alive, living; syn. animono; wosiee no an., they buried him alive. - ŋkàsagũaa-nĩkãŋ, deliberate slandering.
F. nyikanfo, a living soul; pl. a-, the living. - a. live, living. Ex. 21,35. 1 Kg. 3,22.
property given to a son in the father's lifetime; opp. awunnyade. M'agya amã me an. ansã-na orewu. anikã-wá, a little or short pleasure or joy.
homesickness; cf. anigyina. pr. 2316.
the person concerned or in question, the particular or respective person.
sleepiness, drowsiness, inclination to sleep.
bewilderment, anguish, anxiety; desperation; owu an., agony, pangs of death, mortal fright. pr. 3041.
a wry look; obu no an., he eyes him askance, askew, he squints at or leers upon him.

to know. pr. 263-82; minnim no, mighũu no peŋ, I do not know him, I never saw him; nim dè, or dè, to know things; pr. 103: nim ade; ònim dè sèŋ me, he has more knowledge than I; nim nyansã, to have wisdom, to be wise, learned; nim.. mu, to understand, to be versed in. 2 Chron. 34, 12; nim ŋhomam', to have book-knowledge, to be instructed, educated, learned; aduaŋ yi nnim' mamẽẽ, you do not refuse this food though you have eaten enough of another good food; oye adwuma a, onnim awĩa, he always works in spite of the heat; nsu baa adaŋ no mu, ennim se woatoto apoŋ mu, water penetrated into the houses, although the doors had been shut; ŋkã nsem a wunnim yiye, do not say things of which you are not quite sure! obi a onim ne hõ ase, (pl. woŋ a wonim woŋ hõ ase), a citizen; a member of the royal family. - 2. to know or understand how to do a thing, to be able, can (denoting an acquired ability or skill, depending on knowledge and exercise, Fr. savoir; cf. tumi); wúnim déŋ yé? what can you do? what acquirements or accomplishments have you? onim ayaŋ or akyene-kã, he can beat the drum; onim aseŋkã, he can deliver a speech, is a good speaker; onim nantew, he is a good walker; minnim' kõ, I cannot fight; minnim' di, I do not know how to make it; minnim' di, I have never eaten it, do not like it. Gr.
nni mu, not to be in, (without. pr. 581); not to be true.

praise, honour, laud, approbation; perh. acknowledgment, recognition, recognizance; pre-eminence; victory, triumph; cf. ŋkõnĩm. Ne hɔ nyé nĩm bi, he is not respectable. Meye ade yi mamã me wura, na manyã n'anim nĩm; nĩm ne ade a woaye so aye a woyi wo; wode abaninsém na eye, enyé adow n. a.; ohene nso kõ a, odi nĩm. - gye nĩm, to gain the victory; di nĩm, to triumph.

[anĩ mú] 1. The face, visage, countenance; n'anĩm' apõmpono, his face is wrinkled. pr. 2352ff.; yeŋ wura anim ni! there comes our master! se m'anim hɔ, an uncertain number of; ŋkyene-boa se m'anim hɔ, a troop or number of monkeys; ebeye se mfe se m'anim hɔ ni, some years ago; mfrihyia ara se m'anim hɔ, for years. - 2. The front, frontside, forepart; cf. adannim.

3. The space in sight, in front of, before, pr. 413, = (prep.) before, in front of, in the presence of; abofra hwe nsum' wo n'agya anim a, oŋwú, pr. 1319; - of time: before; Kristo awo anim mfe du, ten years before Christ. - (= adv.) forwards, on, onwards. Gr. § 119. - 4. The face, surface, top, upper part, e.g. of the stump of a tree. pr. 403; of a wound, pr. 180; cf. ani. - 5. The surface of the earth within the horizon, together with all the things visible by daylight; s. the first phrases under 7 A. - 6. m'anim', my paternal relations; cf. m'akyiri. - 7. Phrases in which anim is A) the grammatical subject, B) the grammatical object or locative complement: A) anim (5) baebae, bõebõe, bue, it dawns, the day breaks, morning twilight sets in; anim aye fõntãfõntãŋ, ŋwánĩŋwánĩ, sesàsesa, it dawns, becomes twilight; anim' tètẽw, the sky clears up, it becomes daylight; anim aye wee, it is full daylight = ade akyẽ koraa, about 6 o'clock. - ãnim te asé, it is still daylight. - anim akata, the surface (of the earth) has been covered soil. by the shades of evening or of night, = ade sã, the night sets in, it is growing dark; anim abiribiri, amũa, amuna, aye kusuu, it has become dark. - anim gye twom, darkness sets in. - n'anim gu ase, lit. his face falls down, i.e. he is ashamed, put to shame. pr. 2644. - n'anim kisã, sĩãm, bɔ tuo, tow tuo, his face changes, loses colour, grows pale, perf. he is pale from anxiety, he is anxious about past or impending calamities; he is ashamed (n'anim asĩãm = n'ani awu). - n'anim amuna or asse (Gen. 40,7), he looks dark or gloomy from resentment (anger) or sadness, he is sullen or sulky. - n'anim tew, he looks kind, friendly, affable, cheerful. - n'anim tweri = mi-nyãã anuonyam. - n'anim awo, s. n'ani awo. - n'anim ye duru, he is grave, dignified, venerable (ɔwɔ anuonyam, wodi no ni, wuntumi ŋkã n'anim mmofráasem). - n'anim ye férè, he is venerable, has a solemn, majestic air, inspires or commands respect. - n'anim ba or ye nyam, he is illustrious, dignified, honourable, honoured, respectable, respected. - n'anim ye hare, he is lightminded, fickle, frivolous; he is a mean, base, vile, disreputable fellow. - n'anim ye taŋ, he is ugly, repellent. - anim tua anim, face to face. Phrase: nyã..okɔ, I have a question to conflict with him; 5. nyã..nnyã, I and he shall fight with him; examples of: nyã, nyã, nnyã, I and he; nnyã, I and he; ményã no nnyã, I and he shall get (it); me nnyã, I and he; me nnyã no nnyã, I and he with him.

v. [red. nyínyà] 1. to get, receive, obtain, acquire, find, gain, come by, come into possession of, win; to receive as a reward. 396. — in the perf. tense: to have, possess; daa ɒsram wu a, onyã n'akatua, at the end of every month he gets his wages; minnyã dabere, I have no sleeping-place. pr. 2298. — mányà! I have found something! ményãm' (= ményã mɒ), I shall get you (i.e. I will avenge myself on you)! pr. 693. 1198; 2509-34. 2816. 3251. 3407. 3677; manyã wo maye! would I were in your case or place! — 2. nyã ade, to get things, grow rich. pr. 975. 1371. — nyã ne hɒ, to get oneself, i.e. to become a freeman. pr. 1623, also to become rich; in the perf. to be free (cf. de ne hɒ), to be rich. pr. 2524. — nyã ne hɒ bá, to become rich; wɒrényã wɒn hɒ bá, they are becoming rich; cf. ba, v. — 3. Phrases in F.: nyã (obi) abufu, to be angry, vexed, indignant. Mt. 21,15. — nyã afodi, to receive condemnation. Mt. 20,15. — nyã anyitan, to be envious. Mt. 20,15. — nyã (obi) yam'gya = de (obi) hye ne yam', to have a quarrel or grudge against. Mk. 6,19. — nyã ayamhyehye, to be moved with compassion. Mk. 6,34. — oyer nyã okun hɒ fekwu, mboa na awerekyekye, the wife enjoys the husband's company, help and comfort. — 4. Phrase: me nè no anyã (scil. okɒ), I have got into a quarrel or conflict with him, we are at variance, I shall fight with him. — Cf. the foll. examples of 1 & 4: me nè no ntumi nnyã, I and he cannot get (it); mintumi nè no nnyã, I cannot get (it), though he get (it); me nè no rennyã, mintumi me nè no nnyã, I cannot be at variance with him. — 5. nyã, put as an aux. v. before another finite verb, denotes the setting in of the action expressed in the latter: onyã bá, béfré mè, as soon as he comes, call me; wanyã abà, he has come now. pr. 3. When both verbs are negative, it denotes that the action has up to the time present or in question not been performed, and must accordingly in Eng. be rendered by not yet: onnyã' mmae(-ɛ), he has not yet come; onnyã ŋhũi no, ose, ɒrennye nni da, when (or as long as) he had not yet seen it, he said, he would never believe it. Gr. § 107,14. 230,3. pr. 642. — 6. nyã with the freq. form of the infinitive denotes repetition, frequency or acquired habitualness of the action expressed by the inf.; wányà saá ŋkàe, he has become used to say so; mányà ntee, I have often heard (it); mányà no fó ntùi, mányà no ŋkà-kyerɛe. Gr. § 104,5. 105,1 c. 107,22. 230,2. pr. 2219. — 7. onnyã ne hɒ akáyé, he cannot move as he likes; nyã adayé, Eccl. 5,1, s. adayé.

dwɔmmá, [edwo, dwow, F. yam, ba] cooked or stewed yam. pr. 708. 1462.
oye ne hō aŋw. = oye kwasiamankwaa; cf. mparu-ŋwóma.

[edwom, koro] 1. = ɛbá-dwóm, a song, love-song of females; dwom a mmabaa hyia anadwɔfā to de bobɔ wɔŋ adɔfo diŋ. pr. 2062. — 2. a satirical song; 'street song'; dwom a obi to de saa obi anase wɔto kā ŋkwaseasɛm.
inf. = dwonto.
s. dwoasuru.
[dwow] corn which is roughly ground.
ayimāfó; kua aye ne hō aŋwumafo-dwuma a atetekwaa nnim', farming is an occupation to which everybody without exception can devote himself.
[oŋwíni, bere] the evening, espec. from about 5 to 6 o'clock, between mfaretu-bere & anadwɔfā; - aŋw. fomm, late in the evening when it is getting dark.
(F. in the arms [abaw] of evening) the time from about 3 to 5 o'clock.
[abɛ] 1. lit. evening oil-palm, evening palm-wine. — 2. the time from about 5—6 o'cl. p. m. - Cf. anɔpa-bɛ.
supper, a meal taken at the close of the day.
Aky. = ŋwíni, v. & a. — ɔdaŋ no ŋwuŋ sosɔ gu fam', the roof of the house is leaking, the water is trickling down.
(As.) = oŋwíni, shade.
in our books represents both the full o & the narrow ọ; cf. Gr. § 1 Rem. 2 & § 2.
prefix of nouns in the sing., s. Gr. § 29, 2. 35, 1, of pronouns, § 60, 1, of numerals, § 77, 1. 78, 5 — is often dropped in close connection with a preceding word. Gr. § 49, 1.
a pron. for a person, which is prefixed to the verb, s. Gr. § 54. 58; in F. also for a thing, § 58 Rem. 1.
interj. an enclitic sound after an expression containing a salutation, or after an exclamation or a sentence addressed to a person from some distance or with emphasis. Gr. § 147. 145. 144.
interj. expressing indignation or regret.
interj. expressing admiration or surprise. Gr. § 145.
(ô..ô), conj. whether..or. Gr. § 139 f. Rom. 14, 8; 1 Co. 10, 31.

v. [red. popá, (pepa)] to move or remove in a gliding or superficial way: 1. intr. pa..hõ, to pass by, move along: wapa me hõ (kɔ) = wabɛsɛŋ (wo) me hõ, watwa me hõ (kɔ). - F. pa..do = pa hõ, twam, Mt. 26, 39. - nnoŋ abieŋ apa hõ simma dunnum, it is a quarter past two. - 2. refl. to take one's self off: pa wo hõ! take yourself off, go away! - 3. intr. pa..hõ, so, to slip or glide over: ne nsa apa, he has committed an unintentional error or fault (a slip); ne nsa kopaa no hõ, he inadvertently committed something amiss concerning him or her; cf. sạkwáŋ, nsapa; n'ani apa so, he has forgotten or overlooked it; n'ano apa, he has blasphemed (the king or God). - 4. tr. pa..so, to plane: ɔde apaso dua no so. - 5. to take off (ani-ani na wopa, na enkom' ana ɛŋkɔ ase): a) to take off the surface: abŭrow a wosiw so mmŭro-fua, the uncrushed grains of corn; syn. po so. - b) to skim, scum, scoop off: abe ani ŋŋo, the oil from the boiled mash of palm-nuts; atɛl ani ŋsã, the liquor from the mash of malted corn. - c) to scrape or shave off: ŋhoma so, the flesh or hair of a skin; wəyere ŋhoma a, wopa so nãm na awo ntem; to peel off, loosen from: dompe hõ nãm, the meat from a bone. - d) to take or strip off (one's clothes): wapa ne ntama, he has thrown off his (own) garment; cf. 1 & yi ntade. pr.: 2578. 2 Pet. 1, 14. - wapa me hõ, he has stripped or divested me of my clothes. - e) to take away: poŋ so ntama, the table-cloth. - F. to take down: ne daŋ so, the roof from his house; pa hetsew, F. to uncover the roof. Mk. 2, 4; pa ahyiae-ntamadaŋ no, to take down the tabernacle. Nu. 1, 51. - pa daŋ, to pull down a house. pr. 1714. - g) wapa wəŋ ase (a̋wie), he has found out their secrets (completely). - 6. pa..so, to shove, push to: to exonerate oneself from.. by throwing it upon..; wapa asɛm no ato ne yɔŋkɔ so = wayi asɛm no ahye ne yɔŋkɔ s. mpátoso. - 7. to draw up: n'ani akyi, the eye-brows (from vanity or conceit, in order to appear lady-like = di mmabaasɛm?) - 8. to withdraw from (akyi, behind), forsake, deny; F. Mt. 27, 46. 26, 34 f.; mapa no, I will not be concerned with him any more; ɔpa ne hõ akyi, he denies himself. 2 Tim. 2, 12 f.; - to refuse, (ɔpà = əmpɛné), reject, cf. po. Ps. 118, 22. Mt. 21, 42; to forbear (e.g. to keep the Passover). Nu. 9, 13. - 9. to draw out, get out in a sliding or slipping way: get out (of a snare), pr. 424; ɔpa ne to ase fi adi, he manages to get out (of a snare), pr. 424; ɔpa ne to ase, he retracts; ɔpa ne to ase wɛɛ, s. wɛɛ. - 10. to draw off: abaw, the arms, to give up in despair; wapa
he has desisted from it, got tired (of it).
to make or to become or be bare or bald; oyare apa ne ti, a disease has caused his head to become bald; ne ti apa, his head is bald; asẽ nti oguaŋ hɔ pa, from the itch a sheep gets bald.
to fade, go (of colours), to lose the colour; ntama no pa, that cloth does not keep its colour; ani apa, it has faded.
to disappear (like stains or spots); ŋekãe no mpá, the stain(s) cannot be removed, won't go.

to be wanting, missing, lost; nsã mpa ne fi da; wəŋ hɔ mpa mu, they are never absent or wanting; 'kotodwe abə dua, ɛyaw mpa mu', when you knock your knee against a tree, it will hurt you (prop. pain is never absent for a long time, pr. 94. 490. 596, 3194. 3426.

to wipe (off, away), to blot out; popa poŋ so, wipe or dust the table; popa nsu a egu so no, wipe away the water spilt on it! əpopa n'ani, pr. 2714. - əpopa n'anim fifiri, he wipes off the perspiration from his face. pr. 595. 3054; mɔmpopapa mɔ srɛti so, wipe off the writing on your slates; wapopa me mfomso, he has blotted out my iniquities. Acts 3,19; wapopa ne diŋ afi soro ase, he has blotted out his name from under heaven. Deut. 29, 19 (20); cf. kita & pra, to sweep.
to take off the hat in reference to some one (cf. 5 d), i.e. to beg submissively, to beg pardon; s. kyɛw.

to fling, to pelt with stones (perh. without hitting, diff. bo..abo); pa butuw fam', to lie flat on the belly; əpa daa fam', he laid himself flat on the ground; mepa m'afuru too bepɔw no so sɛ merekɔhwe, yeŋ sha, here we were badly treated.
to strike fire (cf. apagya, fire-steel); to beam, dart or sparkle fire; cf. əbáyifo.
to flash (as lightning), to lighten. pr. 510; anyinam pa (pl. popá), lighting flashes. Ex. 20,18.
to allege, pretend, feign, simulate; ɔpà payàrɛ, he simulates a sickness. pr. 2579, cf. boapa.

(to let pass over the vocal cords in the larynx, to let slip or escape a sound, to emit or utter a slight noise), to snarl, growl, grumble (as a dog); to rattle in the throat (cf. hwane); onipa seŋ ne mene a, ɔpá so sɛ ɔsebɔ, when a man hangs himself (lit. his throat), he growls like a leopard; akwaoonsuro, wuyi no a-firim' a, opa so sɛ ɔsebɔ; kotie opá à ɔsebɔ no repa so!
to part, put asunder; owu pa hen mu, death parts us; cf. pae.

(wɔ) no so, na antow, he levelled (pointed, aimed) a musket at him, but it did not go off; ɔde ne tuo paa no so, (levelling a musket at him) shot at him; ɔpaa me so tuo, na antom', he shot at me (with a m.) but did not hit me (missed the aim).
to postpone; wopaa asem no guu mu nnaanum, the matter was postponed 5 days; wopa guu mu, they postponed it.
v. Ak. s. paw; F. to choose, elect, select. Mt. 20,16. 24,22. 13,49; pa..fi hɔ or mu, to sever from among.
F. added to an affirmatory clause, conveys a negative idea; ɔye fɛw pa (this would be in Akp. = it is very fine); in a negative clause pa conveys a contrary idea : ɔnye fɛw pa. Mf. Gr. p. 137.f.

a. [red. pápa, q. v.] 1. good; it is always, as it were, compounded with the noun to which it is joined, so that the noun usually has a low tone throughout: onipa-pá, a good man; nsã-pá, good palm-wine; kōma-pá, a good heart, i.e. joy, gladness; ahene-pá, a good, i.e. precious coral; also opp. glass bead, cf. the foll. - 2. proper, properly so called, true, real, genuine; cf. potẽẽ; bise-pá, the proper cola-nut, opp. bise-tóro; nna-pá, sleep in the common sense of the word. John 11,13; ɔye-pá, a proper, lawful wife.
F. 1. borders, frontiers, region, district. Mt. 15,22. - 2. = apaw.

1. a scaffold of sticks erected near the houses of the natives, to put plantains and other fruits on, in order to keep them secure from the goats. pr. 3025; a similar scaffold erected by the wayside near a town or village, on which the corpse of an unknown stranger is put, in order to give opportunity to passers-by to ascertain his identity; cf. apata. — 2. trap; afiri bi a wosūm de yi akura ana wuram' aboa biara, na wode abo gu so, na wode abūrow, ŋkate, kwadu, brōde n. a. hye ase, na se aboa no ba na ɔbeyi aduan no afi ase a, ahūaŋ abo no. — 3. Ak. = apaw, q. v.
couch, bed, anything to sleep on, mat, mattress, cloth, board &c., F. = kete; siesie mpa (so), s. siesie 1; cf. mpáboa, mpadúà, mpatiá, owupá, oyarepá.

adv. & interj. really, truly, indeed; earnestly; to be sure, certainly; undeniably, not to be refused or rejected (cf. pa, v. 8). pr. 1106; asɛm yi wom' ampa, it is really the case; áyè me ampá, I am persuaded. Rom. 14, 14. It is frequently used as an elliptic confirmation of what another person says, for: so it is, you are right; - also as a question: ampá? indeed? is it really so? - or as an expression of surprise: ampá-à! indeed! — Cpds. ampá-ara, very truly, ampa-(a)mpá, ampa-nè-ampá.
pl. a-, a curved iron closing round the wrist of a prisoner and fixed in a block; (diff. adansa, handcuff, manacle;) woabo no pá = woabɔ no duam'.
F. ripe, mature.
an old, aged, long-lived person, beast or tree; akoa no ye àpà pá ara = ne so apà biara nni baabi; bɔ apá, to grow old; cf. ɔpànyiŋ, dupã.

mpá, pãm', the lower part of the back, where the ilium is joined to the lumbar vertebrae; loins, reins, rump. pr. 145. 3173; syn. sisi, sisiakyì. — katá mpá, to bring up the rear, to conclude (or be hindermost, be the last in) a train of persons; wakata bo agya(w) pá, he is badly dressed. Cf. mpāmdeŋ, pi, pi, pim'.

v. 1. to strike, smite. pr. 2230; paa so = bɔ só na ɛnye deŋ! ɔpaa n'ani so, he strikes him in the face; ɔpaa n'asōm', he gives him a box on the ear; s. pae 1, pa 17. — 2. to split; [wapaa, better:] wapae poŋ no hō, he has split a piece off the table; s. pae. — 3. to hit: apáa no sò = asɛm no abo no, the matter has been decided against him. — 4. paa so, a) to continue in a struggle or any action, to go on: me nè wifo no apaa so (= adi) ara magye m'ade ny. wo ne nsam'; paa so = bɔ so mã ɛnye deŋ! - b) to add; s. pae 14; - (perf. apáa so = 'moreover, in addition to'): wadi me amim ahwe me apáa-so, he has cheated me and beaten me besides. — 5. F. = pae, to burst. — 6. pae, to curse. — 7. me ti paa me (pr. 611) = pae me, s. pae 10.
adv. [red. pàapaa, q. v.]: bɔ paa, to pat; ɔbɔɔ n'atifi pàa, he patted him on his head.
adv. forthwith, with all haste; paa woguage = tɛrem woguage; cf. hwii; - pà hwíi, s, hwíi, paatwee.

pl. id. a contract or agreement by which the services of a person are engaged for another person; ódi (me) paá, he serves (me) as a hired labourer or carrier, carries loads &c. for payment. — óbò me paá (pl. ɔbɔ yeŋ paa), he hires me (us) as a labourer, carrier or for any service; mabɔ a-dwumayefo paa, mabɔ apaafɔ, I have hired labourers. pr. 3003; gye paa, to enter an engagement as a labourer or carrier for pay; wagye ntamaŋwene paa, he has received cotton to be woven into cloth by him for pay.
F. curse. — mpáá, F. prayer; cf. mpáè.

1. a mat plaited with narrow strips = ntómmaa. — 2. a stroke with the flat hand; wodi mpaa n.s. wosi ntew mã obi twa (kum) ne yɔŋkɔ a, onnyé no hɔ ntrama, ŋkate n.a., na ɔbɔ (otwa) no mpá, a stroke with the senea wotoáé; cf. paá.
pl. m-, a mat made of palm-strips.
palpitating; ne koma pãá, his heart smites him, throbs, palpitates, beats or sates violently.
a bird which cries or throbs, palpitates.
paápó, a large kind of sandal.
mpa mu 1328.

sandal, a shoe, cf. ntokotá, pr. 2194; to make sandals. 1. mpa-ma (Nnoŋkofo na wode mpa (Kodiabɛfo na eye), kyɛãwkyɛãw; ŋkutu, mpaboá-boafó, sandal-bearer; mpaboa-pámfó, sandal-maker; mpaboa-túo = 2 sandals.
inf. the act of hiring a man or carrier.
hire, wages, reward, performance.
the act of walking in the rain, by a man or beast, through the bush; cf. padec, pr. 1240, s. ɔdɛ.
hire. Isa. 23, 18.
pl. a-, worker for hire; cf. ɔpaani.
[Guan: pãlɛdɛ].
F. porch (Mt. 26, 71).
pl. m-, a cross-beam of wood, used instead of a bed.
the log or piece of wood on which the iron 'le' is fixed for the hand of a prisoner.
pl. m-, a bedstead, a long-legged bedstead, tiaá (mpaduatiá or mpaduá) or long-legged bedstead.
v. [red. paepae, pae] to burst, smite; ɔpae n'asōm' = ɔpaa n'asōm', pr. 160. 400, 1328; to split, rive, cleave, burst, e.g. split a piece of wood.
pl. m-, a mat plaited with broad strips.
adv. palpitatingly; ne kōma bɔ no pãá, his heart smites him (1 Sam. 24,6), throbs, palpitates, beats excitedly, pulsates violently.
a bird with red eyes.
paápó, a large male atwáboa.
[mpa mu aboa] (bed-)bug. pr. 1328.

sandal, a pair of sandals = ntokotá. pr. 2194; bu, pam or ye mp., to make sandals. Diff. kinds: ahènemma (Nnoŋkofo na eye), kyiri-ahemfí (Kodiabɛfo na eye), gyapatiá, ŋketewá, kyɛawkyɛaw; ŋkuróŋŋúa. - mpaboafó, sandal-bearer, s. gyaasefo. - mpaboa-pámfó, sandal-maker. - tow mpaboa-túo, to walk with clapping sandals.
inf. the act of hiring a workman or carrier.
hire, wages or pay for some performance.
(bubu), the noise made e.g. by rain, by a man or an animal running through the bush; syn. kitikiti.
pr. 1240, 23, 17 f. - ɔdampadeɛ.
hire. Isa. 23, 17 f. - ɔ-paadífó, pl. a-, worker for hire. Isa. 19, 10; cf. ɔpaani.
[Guaŋ: pãlele] = siwabiri, sowa. pado, F. porch (Mt. 26, 69). Mk. 14, 68.
pl. m-, a cigar-shaped log of wood, used instead of a canoe.
the log or block of wood in which the iron called pã, securing the hand of a prisoner, is fixed.
pl. mpa-nnuá, bedstead; mpaduɛŋ, (mpaduatiá or mpatiá), a short-legged bedstead.

v. [red. paepae, paapae] 1. to strike, smite; ɔpae n'asɔm', n'atifí, ne mpampam', pr. 160. 400, s. paa. - 2. tr. to split, rive, cleave, break; p. dua, to split a piece of wood; p. gya, to cleave wood; p. mpuran, ntáboo, to saw beams, boards; p. abo, to break, cut, dig or take stones from the earth, from a quarry, to quarry stones; pae asase, to furrow the earth. Ps. 141,7. - 3. intr. to split, rend, burst, crack; ɔprannaa duru duam' a, ɛpae, when the lightning strikes a tree, it bursts; duá no apáe, the tree is riven; kora no apae, the calabash has a chink. pr. 614; ɔdodobeŋ, pr. 947. - ne tuo mu paee, his gun burst, flew into pieces. pr. 3389 f.; emu apae abieŋ, it has burst in two; to cleave asunder. Nu. 16, 31. - 4. to part, divide; ɔpae (ɔpaa) ne tirim, he parts his hair on (the top of) his head; ɔpae sa, he cuts or opens a path through the bush; wòbepae ɔkwaŋ foforo afa wura no mu, they will cut a new path through the bush; wòpae asase no ahye, they mark the borders of the land (by cutting the undergrowth). - intr. to branch: ɔkwaŋ pae abieŋ, the road branches off into two; - pae ..mu (tr. & intr.), to divide; mapaem' pɛpɛɛpe, I have divided it exactly; me nè wo bepaem', both of us shall have equal part in..; nsu no mu paee abieŋ, the water divided; nnipa apaapae woŋ hō mu aye amaŋ pii, mankind is divided into many peoples (nations); - wòpaem' ahɔɔdeŋ mu, or ɔnè no na ɛpaem' ah. mu, they are equal in strength. - 5. pae..mu, a) to cut open, rip up. 2 Kg. 8, 12. pr. 3264 f. - b) to lay open, display; pae mú se, say it plainly, frankly! pr. 2580. Gr. § 234. - c) pae (biribi nè biribi) mu, to make a difference between, distinguish between. Lev. 11,47; ɔnè yeŋ pae mu, he differs from us; he leaves us, we part. - pae ntam', to put a difference between. Ex. 11,7; ɔnè yeŋ ntam' apae, he is at variance with us. - 6. to exclaim (thereby rending the air), to cry out; esɛŋ pae: ti'oo! the herald cries: Attend! - pae mmãraŋ, to give a surname; ɔpae ɔhene mmãraŋ, to cry out the titles of the king (in his praise); pae diŋ, s. 15. - wòapae guaŋ no, they (by the town-

crier and his bell, s. dawuru) have made publicly known that the sheep has been lost; - wopae no sanebene, they want him to say the watch-word, to make himself known as a friend or enemy; - p. hum, to announce or proclaim the ohum custom or festival; p. ghyia, to proclaim a convocation. Lev. 23,2. 37. - 7. to cackle; cf. kwane. - 8. to burst or break forth as a flood of light, to shine, to flash, espec. in the perf.: ōwia, osram apae, the sun, the moon, shines; osraman, oprannaa pae, the lightning flashes; akado bepae fitaa, (the) lime will become white (when dry). - 9. to ferment, effervesce; to become sour; nsā or ahai no apae = akaw, the palm-wine or beer has undergone fermentation. - 10. to pain, ache: me ti pae me (= beg me), my head aches; me ti mpae me, nothing ails me, I am quite well. - oboa kasa pae ne ti, he takes much pains in speaking. - 11. n'ani apae = n'ani atew or ań, he or she is a cunning person; n'ani apae se ogya, he is much displeased, very angry. - 12. ne kōma apae or repae ne yam', he is utterly terrified; ne kōma ye apae, he is very uneasy, terribly frightened. - 13. to get angry = bo fuw; métee no na merepae, when I heard it, I became angry. - 14. pae so, to add; fa pae so = fa paa so, fa bo so, fa kā hō. Isa. 56,8; yeanyā odōm apae dōm so, we have received grace upon (in addition to) grace, cf. John 1,16. - 15. pae diŋ: opae ne diŋ, he separates, i.e. forbids his name and gives him another; kaŋ no wofre no se: Dannya-me, na ne wura apae ne diŋ ato no Fasaadamase. (Gye wo akoa ŋkō na wobetumi apae ne diŋ.) - 16. to call the name of a person, at the same time invoking the power of a higher being for good or bad; to curse; wa-kopae me amā Kyeŋku; cf. mpae 2. - 17. aduaŋ apae, dinner is ready; sika apae opon no so, the money lies ready on the table; mā wo nnesma mpae, keep your things in readiness! mā wo tuo mpae, fetch your gun at once! - 18. pae..si hō, to pay or charge 50 per cent. interest.
inf. explosion &c.
pl. m-, a bag matted or plaited of a kind of grass (uton) for carrying salt, dried fish &c., smaller than tekre-kyi. pr. 2239.

v. n. [cf. pae 6] 1. invocation, prayer, supplication; bo or yi mpae, to pray; ɔbɔ Nyaŋkp. mpae amā ne nua, he prays to God for his brother; sometimes: ɔbɔ Nyaŋkp., he prays to God. Osofo na oyi mp., e.s. wosore asēre biribiara; se wokasa bērɛso oo, wokasa denneŋ oo, ne nyinaa wofre no mpae; mekaŋkye ma-bɔ abosom mpae; mede nsā merebɔ me nena samaŋ mpae na me hō aye me deŋ. Obiara kobo mpae a, na bɔhye wom' (according to P. Ket., others deny it). Múnyi (or mómmaɔ) mpae mmā no, na ne hō ye no deŋ a, wobemā no aboade (abohyedē); - ɔbɔ me ti so mpae, he prays for me. - 2. impreca-tion, curse, execration; cf. nsew; mpae ŋkā no! F. let him be cursed!
mpáé-yí (Jer. 11,15), inf. the act of praying; prayer; munnynae mp., do not give up prayer, pray without ceasing!
pl. mpaapáé, cleft, crack.
inf. a short, simple celebration of the yam-festival; cf. odwiratwa.
v. n. [pae]: esono were ye mp., an elephant's skin is rough; bɔre hō ye mp. (nè) adamadám, the skin of the snake called bɔre is rough and speckled.
inf. division &c., cf. mpaa-paem'.
inf. open confession.
s. paapae.

pr. n., s. asafo; Apagyafó, the members of the Apagya.
fire-steel, steel for striking fire. pr. 3288; matches; pa ap., to strike fire: wope ap. abo akonhama, they seek embers to make fire for preparing their meal.

Ak. pagya, v. to lift up, take up, raise; p. ahamanka, otuo; woabep. me abesi won ahennua so, they have placed me (as king) on their throne; op. abofra no too n'akyi de no boo mirikatente, he put the child at once upon his back and ran quickly away with it; mekasa miwiei pe na op. ne ho pankran se.., no sooner had I done speaking than he rose up suddenly, saying..; pagyaw..anim, to honour, to praise; - p. asem, to bring forward a motion, to move; - p. ne ka, to increase one's debts. - to inflate, puff up, elate; ne nimdee ne n'ade asum no afiri na n'adwene ap. no, ensnared by his knowledge and riches, he is lifted up in his own conceit; - to act regardless of others. pr. 2263.
F. passover, Mt. 26,1, = twam'.
(bi wo gwa na wugye akyinnye wo tirim?). - otuu won fo se wonye papa nanso (eye) ap., he exhorted them in vain to behave well.
pâ-hwíi, an exclamation at the breaking up of an assembly; acclamation, to the laws published.
strong drink or liquor = mmosa, nsa a eye den, engye nnipa bow. Isa. 28,7.
v. = paghin.
wages, port(er)age; adesoa biako ap. nko na obetua, he will pay the porterage for one load only.
[apakan]: mp. oha, a hundred baskets full. pr. 3024.

Ak.-kane, 1. travelling-basket, a long basket in which kings or chiefs are carried. pr. 2021; for European travellers the hammock has supplanted it. - 2. basket for carrying palm-oil, palm-wine (in pots), salt and other things; cf. bedew, akotwe, kyɛnkyɛn. - Esono apakan kese a wode soa nnipa, ap. a mmarima de soa nyo ne nsa, asante-ap. a wode soa ŋkyene, nè apakoko-ap. a mmaa de soa adesoa.
-fo, pl. mpakaŋfó, a king or chief carried in the apakan.
ɔpakaŋsóafó, pl. m-fo, carrier of the travelling-basket.
a cloth spread inside the travelling-basket.
(Kuk.): ye p. = bo mpatabiri-biri; epo no ani yee p. kese, cf. Mt. 8,24.
a basket in which women carry loads; s. apakan 2.
cold, catarrh; oyare p., ɔp. aye ne hwene, ɔp. abo no, he is affected with catarrh; cf. ɔpapu.
bed-room, any room in a native house except the hall where the meals are taken (s. asá-sò); cf. pia, pumpunu, dabekyiri.
1. lameness; to or yare ap., to halt, to be lame. - 2. pl. m-, a lame person; oye ap., he is lame; cf. na oto dwonku a, s. gyawa, ósi síi. Cf. sii, osiifo, hũaŋ, dwonku.
inf. [pa akyi] denial, desertion of somebody; backsliding. Hos. 14,5.
Ak. apakyie, pl. m-, a broad calabash with a cover. pr. 228. 1849. 2582 f.; cf. kora. - also the gourd from which the calabash is made.
pl. m-, cover or lid of a broad calabash. pr. 1151.
pl. m- [dim.] a small calabash with a cover. pr. 1842.

a man or woman possessing a soothsaying fetish in a calabash, which, when asked, he or she takes upon the head, and without holding, lets it slip forward or backward, to the right or left. Cf. ɔkɔmfo.

v. [red. pam'pam] to drive or chase away, to disperse, dispel; to put to flight, rout; to expel, dismiss, banish; pam ŋkoko. pr. 1532. 1644. 2584-87; p. dom, cf. yi dom, gu 15; s. ɔpanyifó. (F. pãm, Mk. 10,14, to forbid to come).

[red. (pempám), pompám] 1. to join, to make by putting together pieces of wood: p. adaka, to make a box; to sew (together), to make by sewing: p. ntama, p. atade. pr. 2590. 2592; p. mmatakari, wono, nsɛbe, foto &c. - to mend. pr. 1372. --- 2. red. a) to join, bring together, unite, organize; eyi na yerempempam asafo no foforo bio, we shall (now) no more reorganise the company. --- b) to repair, restore. 2 Kg. 12,6-9 (ofi no mu adannow). --- 3. intr. to be joined together, to close; asú no ani apàm, the surface of the river is frozen. Job 38,30; ŋkwáŋ no ani apàm, the eyes on the soup (broth) have joined, i.e. there is fat or oil all over; n'ábògye apàm, he has a lock-jaw; p. hɔ, to be doubled. Ex. 26,24. --- 4. pam afuw, to clear the place destined for a plantation, by gathering the remnants of the burned trees and brushwood in order to complete their burning; ópàm n'áfúw, pl. wopempám' woŋ'mfúw, e.s. woahyew afuw na wota-se so nnuaa nè nnubãã mmiakó-miakó siesie. --- [Inf. apàm].
pem', F. = pa mu, pae mu, paw mu.
[Gã], pàm, adv. very much; totally; cf. papaapa; - wábòw pam, wawe (nsã) atò pam, he is (completely, or) dead-drunk; s. tàm.
the report of a gun; otow tuo pam.
F. 1. = pam', Mk. 10,14. --- 2. = pàm; pãm ntar (ntade), to make clothes.

[inf. apãm, red. põmpãm] to enter into a confederacy, to confederate, unite in a league, join in a covenant. 1146; ɔmaŋ yi nè maŋ yi apãm, these two nations are confederate, allied by treaty; woŋ baanu pãme; me nè wo bɛpãm ato hɔ, Gen. 6,18. 21,27; cf. apãm. --- pãm..tiri so, F. pãm..do, Mt. 12, 14, to conspire against, hold a council against.

inf. covenant, confederation, alliance, league, treaty, agreement; wo-wɔ apãm, apãm da woŋ ntam', they are confederate, there is a league or covenant between them = woápãm; cf. Gen. 9,9ff. 14,13. 17,2ff. --- kɔ apãm or mp., to enter into an agreement; s. mpãm; - mpãm wo yoŋkɔ hɔ ap.-mone. - F. fa apãm, to take counsel. Mt. 22,15. 27,1. - kɔ apãm, F. to hold a consultation. Mk. 15,1.
inf. s. pàm, v. 4.
a (thorny) tree, the bark of which is used to prevent abortion.

pl. id. (cf. pam, v. 4), a stick put in the ground by the side of a planted yam, a stay, stake; dua biara a wode si odé mã sforo kobua so (wode dé no fá hɔ); worekotwa saa nnua a, wuse: mekotwá pám anase mekobó pám; cf. apammɔ, pamfĩ. pr. 1298. 3595.
= pã mu, s. pã, mpã.
apãm; mpanyimfo kɔ mp. na woadi mmãra, - na wonè asiamasi akɔkɔ, the elders have gone to unite in issuing a law, - have agreed to enter into hostilities against some one.

pl. id., pricks, sharply pointed pieces of wood or palm-branches, thorns, nails or knives put in the ground to wound or pierce the feet of a thief who is going to steal palm-wine or other things from a plantation; wahye me mpãm = ɔde nsɔe akɔhyehye fam' se mekofa so, ɛŋwowɔ me.
[nea ópompam' ade a ɛyɛ agow-agów], nea ɔye ade a asɛe yiye, restorer, renovator; repairer of the breach. Isa. 58,12.
firmness of the back (s. pã); hye wo nuanom mp., comfort, support or strengthen your brethren, encourage them when they begin to faint; syn. hye..baniŋha. --- mpãmdéŋ-hyé, inf. encouragement.
seam; joining. John 19,23.

pl. m-, a bundle of sticks (s. pam); any large bundle, a heavy load of yam &c.; wakyekye ŋhoma no p. asoa me, he has given me a large pack of books to carry; yeŋ bone a woa-kyekye no p. de asoa Iesu no, ensé se owu ana?
pl. a-, sewer, seamstress, tailor.
mpe...
= mpawmu
pl. n- (s. pãm), artisan, party-man; Osee nè ne nkurɔfo yɛ Osee ne king and his people; mpamfo, mpamfo, mpamfo.
F. confederates.
covenant; the New Covenant.
a plant.
inf. (e.g. of oxe: mpãm-hyé-de, adommãnãde).
pl. a-, associate; cf. apãm-mó, inf.
sticks or stakes.
a certain shell of white (ping-glass).
pl. n- (sma kó. 1. a plant.
= mpampá, a thick kind of corn mixed with oil, boiled with water [G. pampa, a].
apámpaa, a round, flat basket, one piece of which women carry plantations. pr. 1298. cf. apawá. - s. so, Ak. (& over the plantation disorder; - 1. na mp. gu a received his.
carelessly; wa-hye him; pa-pãm, adv. 1. p. mpeŋ adu, abo anaŋ akɔduru makɔdaŋ ka: woŋ saŋ no woyɛn du, came near excessively.
red.
F., the elect, Mt. 24,31, = mpawmufo.
pl. m-, confederate, ally; partisan, party-man; associate, companion. Osee nè ne mp. (= ne ŋkoa), the Asante king and his subjects; cf. apămni; mfefo, mpraprafo.
F. council. Mk.-13,9.
apăm-fófóro, a new covenant; the New Testament.
a certain tree.
junction; a pair or yoke (e.g. of oxen).
-hyɛ̀dè, sacrament(s); syn. adommănăde.
pl. a- -fo, confederate, ally, associate; cf. ɔpămfo.
inf. [bɔ apam] the cutting of sticks or stakes for the yam.
a certain tree and its fruit, the shell of which serves as a cup (cupping-glass); s. kaŋkua.
pl. m-, hill, hillock; s. pémpé (smaller), kókó (larger). pr. 1017.
ampa-ampa, ampa-nè-ampa.
a thin pap or soup of ground corn mixed with water, sieved and boiled with red plantains or bananas. [G. pampa, aflata].

apámpaa, (F. apampá), pl. m-, a round, flat, hollow vessel, made of one piece of wood; a bowl in which women carry provisions from their plantations. pr. 128. 1963; shovel, Isa. 30,24; cf. apawá. - mp. gu afuo (Akp.: afuw) so, Ak. (& Akp.), bowls lie scattered over the plantation, i.e. there is much disorder; - ne nsa aŋkā n'akatua nti na mp. gu afuw so yi, as he has not received his wages, he is in difficulty.

bo-, to trifle with, use carelessly; wòbo no mp., they trifle with him; onipa-pa wu a, wòmmó no mp. pàm-pam, adv. successively; me nè no abɔ anaŋ akɔ kŭro no so p. mpeŋ 3; makɔdaŋ ka no p. mpeŋ 5, wantua me; wɔŋ saŋ no mu no aŋkā ɛremene wɔŋ p. mpeŋ du, on their way back they came near drowning ten times successively.
red. v. (s. pam'), F. to persecute.
the crown of the head, vertex, top = atifi. pr. 400.
a certain tree. pr. 2588f.
pămpăŋ, exhalation, evaporation, damp, effluvium, scent; biribi hŭā a ŋiframa de ba; duasee no p. bɔŋ bɛfaa me so.
a long knife or sword to cut plantains; Ky. = kăntăŋkrăŋkyi.
a (low) fence or obstruction over the foot-path near a town or village, to prevent the entrance of evil spirits; stile. pr. 3309; palisade, stockade.
a certain tree used for fuel.
trucebreaker; implacable. Rom. 1,31. 2 Tim. 3,3.
= mpampŭró.

[red. pempàŋ, pomp.] to pluck, pull off or out; to crop (off). Ezek. 17,4; wokopáŋ òdé, they are going to take out yam (of the first crop, pr. 827; tu is used of the 2d); śpàŋ dubăā; wópem-pàŋ ahaban; obi ntumi mpaŋ wɔŋ me nsam' (John 10,28 f.). Syn. pɔŋ, tew, hŭam.

v. [red. pōmpàŋ]: p. mu, to leave a void, an empty or blank space, a distance between; wòde ntumpaŋ sisi hò a, pompàŋ mu na ammɔbɔ! - mu pàŋ, to be distant from each other: Akyem ŋkŭrow mu pàŋ, Akem towns are at great distances from each other; wɔŋ ntam' pàŋ = wɔŋ ntam' pōmpàŋ, s. pōmpàŋ; - pàŋ.. ntam', to separate between. Isa. 59,2. Syn. tăŋ, tēntăŋ.

m-, a. 1. empty, void; odáŋ hŭnu. F. Mt. 12,44; espec. in cpds., cf. ɔdámpàŋ, nsàpàŋ, yafumpáŋ. - da mpáŋ, to be empty, void; abura no da mpáŋ, Gen. 37,24. - 2. adv. wɔŋ ádáŋ sisi pàŋ pàŋ, their houses are built at considerable distances from each other. - 3. = kwa, hunu: menyé wo biribi pàŋ ŋkō a, woyaw me, though I have not committed even the least offence against you, you scold me!
adv. imitative of the sound of firm,
heavy steps; firmly, heavily, boldly; onam páŋ páŋ kɔɔ asu nom', he stepped boldly into the water; ɔnam tɛ̃ɛ, wan-nyina baabi, nso ɔnne hũ na ɔkɔe; cf. piŋ piŋ.
adv. imitative of the ringing sound of a bell: ɔdoŋ no bɔ or bom' p.
a pole used in punting boats; wosi amp., they punt a boat.
Ak. ápànè, pl. mp-, a species of bat; cf. hwenakrɔŋ, ahwérede, ɔpán-twèènìni. pr. 231.
pl. m-, F. a species of snake. ampáànà, Akp. Okw. a (large) tree like a beech.
s. pră...
F. lightly. Prk. Awar p. 29.
s. ɔprămiri.
pl. m-, needle. pr. 758. 2590ff. [pam ade] cf. abūi, G., dorowa; - p. aniwa, asɔ̃, hwene, tò kwáŋ, the eye of a needle.
s. ampá.
apánnèdaw [apăm dedaw] an old covenant; the Old Testament.
a species of herring (middle-sized); s. mmaŋ, kokuro.
a. long, tall; ɔpoŋkɔ anim p.; dua p. bi si hɔ; onipa yi naŋ ye p.; ogyina ho p. = oware tenten; cf. tenteŋ.
v. to excite, rouse, stir up = hintiŋ; me bo ap. me, my heart 'is excited &c. to anger.
pl. a--fó, a person who works for wages, hired labourer or carrier, hireling. pr. 1330. 2593; s. paa; bɔ apaafɔ, to hire people, labourers; syn. ɔpaadifo. Isa. 19, 10.
mpaanní [not Akp.] palm-oil used for food; abe ŋŋo a wodi.
F. = asréne.
Aky.: bɔ p., to kneel on one knee, cf. kotow; sε wo naŋ biakɔ si hɔ na wokɔtow wo naŋkrɔma biakɔ so.
a. tall, slender, slim; ɔbéa p.
n. quickness, agility; bɔ p. (behwe)! get up quickly! be lively! = sɔre ntem! ye wo hɔ hare; cf. ahɔ-twẽtwẽ. — adv. suddenly.
pl. a-, m-, a small barrel or cask; cf. hase, G. kpùm'kpãã; akótowa, ɔkwádùm, atentení m'.
pl. a-, cooper.
(so), v. to turn aside = mãŋ. Joel 2, 7. Nu. 22, 23. — ɔp. ne nan-tew (ne kwaŋ) so = óyi akwá, ohima ne nantew. Cf. pare.
páãñóõ [Port. pão] European bread, wheaten bread, marchpane; biscuit(s); cf. abodoo, dɔkono. — mpáã-nówa, small biscuits.
= pãmpãŋ', exhalation.
Aky. = pãmpãŋkwa(w).
v. 1. to scatter; strew about, disperse. Deut. 30, 3; syn. sampam, petẽ, hwete. — 2. to search through or all over; map. me daŋ nyinaa mu, maŋhũ.
inf. [si apam] the act of putting in the stakes for the yam plants.
a species of grass.
v. to be wide open; ɔpoŋ ano pantaŋ hɔ, the door is wide open; ŋkŭrow abieŋ no ntam' pantaŋ, those two towns are far from each other.
a. plain, open, wide; ɛhɔ ye p'.; syn. tẽtree, hãhrãã; high and wide; ɔdaŋ nom' ye p'.; cf. kàutãŋ, kùntãŋ.
Okw. the jawbone; cf. abogye.
hovel, shed, poor cottage, miserable hut, decaying house.
ɔpántene, ɔpanténe, Ak. pl. a-, the largest species of snake found in Western Africa = enini. pr. 219. 2975.
a certain tree; wode ye gyedua. pántu, pl. a-, a large bottle.
= kese.
a species of plantain; s. ɔbrɔde. — apantũrɛŋ [obs.] id.

Akp.; opántweènìŋ, F. Aky., pl. a-, a species of bat, a little larger than ampaŋ, with a long snout. apantwewa, Aky. 1. = ɔpantweenini. — 2. a beast resembling a snake; it cries 'paŋ twrrr', which sounds like the hammering of a blacksmith. pr. 2594.
very far, very distant or remote; ɔkɔ p. (nóhɔ), he went to a very distant place.
mpãn-yee, Ak. ɔ-pán-yi, inf. [7, 26.

pl. a-, one expelled or banished; exile, outcast; nea woapãm ayi no.
[ɔpanyiŋ, dim.] a subordinate or subaltern officer; syn. adiakyiri.

- aa, pl. m- [= ɔp.] a half-grown boy or girl (of 7-12 years); a young person (that has attained to, or only) arrogates the rights of an adult; a pert, assuming, forward, impudent child, girl, fellow or person; òye ap. = odi mmerantiwasɛm; onipa a ɔnè wo nsɛ panyiŋ no na woyaw no se: woayɛ wo hɔ ap. - also a person of 30-40 years.
[ɛbere] the age of an adult person, manhood, the time, age or period of a man's life after his having grown to full maturity, between mmerantebere (mmabaabere) and ŋwakoraabere (mmerewabere).
a worthy, respectable, reputable man.

ɔpanyini [apã, nyiŋ] pl. m-, 1. an old person; an adult, a grown-up person, opp. abofra, [con. ne panyiŋ]. pr. 194. 382. - 2. a gentleman, respectable man, person of rank, senior, alderman, senator, elder, grandee; a superior, chief, master (is also used of kings and of God, pr. 164. 2542). pr. 564..586. 2595-2625. - pl. mpanyimfó, the elders, grandees of a town, who form the council of the chief or king, each of them having his particular charge (ɔsafohene, military commander; ɔyotɛsãŋfo, ɔsannaani, treasurer; ɔkyɛame, speaker, reporter; ɔbófo, ambassador &c.). - 3. panyiŋ, pl. m-; adj. old (of persons, cf. dedaw), aged; adult, chief; mé núapanyiŋ, my elder brother, opp. akũmaa. - 4. n. the chief (part), principal (thing). pr. 1421. - 5. ɔp., eldership, magistracy, office. pr. 576; odi p., he is entrusted with an office; wodi mpanyiŋ, they are ent...; onyãã ɔp. bi dii, he obtained an office to perform. - 6. mèsɛŋ no panyiŋ, he is younger than I.
a poor or indigent, old and decrepit man.
chief seat. Mt. 23, 6.
adv. after the manner of aged, old, elderly persons, considerately, prudently; odweŋ asɛm hɔ mp., he has sound judgment.
things or doings befitting adults or elders. pr. 576.
inf. eldership, office, government. Isa. 22, 21; - mp..., principalities. Col. 1, 16. 2, 10.
= mpanyiŋ anim.
an aged, old person = akwakoraa.

1. the word, talk, speech, mode of talking, manners and dealings of a man advanced in years or occupying a reputable place in society. - 2. what an old man relates, legend, history; cf. atetesɛm. - kã mp., to talk like an old man, wisely and gravely; to relate an event that has happened in by-gone times; di mp., to arrogate or assume the air of an adult or an elder, to be presumptuous, forward, arrogant, haughty; cf. apanyimma.
adv. according to age; wode woŋ atrātrã mp., they were seated according to their age.
a costly kind of cloth or stuff (as nsaa &c.).
trãbere, the uppermost place, highest seat. Mt. 23, 6. Lk. 14, 7. - mpanyiŋ-ŋwúma, eldership, office, charge. - mpanyiŋ-yɔ́, inf.: ye mp. = di mpanyiŋsɛm; cf. dwae.
mpãnyee [pãm, ye] inf. previous agreement, preconcerted matter.

1. red. a., s. pa; Gr. § 69. 70. - 2. n. good, good things, moral good; goodness; good action; benefit, favour, kindness; welfare, well-being, prosperity; good luck; syn. yiye. pr. 2626. - ne papa nè ne bone, its advantages and disadvantages.
adv. 1. very good, very well. - 2. well, very, much, very much, too much. pr. 1239; syn. dodo,

pii, yiye; ɔkásá papa, he talks too much; ɔkásá papaapa, he speaks very well; opɛ se ohyehyɛ ne hɔ papa, she is too fond of finery; wahwe no papa, he has flogged him well or severely; mikyiá nò pápaapa, I salute him most heartily. Gr. § 133, 3.
cf. ⨍itae; kube ahaban na wode yɛ p. a wode huw woŋ hɔ, fans are made of the leaves of the fan-palm to fan oneself with.
okw. = bàsabasa.
pl. -nom, pope. - p. hɔ trãfo, cardinal. Hist.
red. v. F. = paapae. Mt. 25, 32.
red. adv. pàa: bɔbɔ paapaa, to pat; ɔbɔbɔɔ n'atifi p., he patted him on his head.
bɔ .. ap., to divide, part, separate; wɔbɔ wɔŋ ap. de oyi kɔɔ ha, they were separated and taken to different places.
papã-dénkɛse = mpopã...

red. v. pae, to cleave, split, burst multifariously: tr. to split into many pieces, to split many things; p. sika mu, to change money; intr. to burst asunder, to fly into pieces, to get many chinks or cracks. — p. mu, to speak out freely; to separate, divide; s. pae.
v. n. 1. the creaking or squeaking of soles (of the shoes) in walking; the cracking of a newly daubed wall. — 2. a bursting of the skin of the heel and the back of the foot.
fissures, clefts, cracks of a rock, of a dry soil.

mpaapaemú, inf. division, disjunction, disunion, separation; abruption; rupture, schism. John 7, 43; sika mp., change (= small coins). - di mp., to be divided, disunited, at variance with each other. Mt. 12, 25. - mp.-di, inf. the act of separating, separation &c.
pl. F. good men, saints; ap. woŋ koryɛ, the communion of saints; - the good. 2 Chron. 19, 11. Prov. 14, 19; s. papani.
pl. m-, 1. a private man, a common citizen; ɔnyé kũro a ɔte mu no mu panyin, onni diŋ bi wɔ mu. — 2. bachelor, unmarried man; cf. osigyafo, unmarried woman, & ɔhõkwafo, pr. 1189. 2627.
a tree with spongy pith; wode yɛ sukudɔŋ; - Paapaaku, wosow ntrama, nanso wudi hĩa (wunni sika), P., you carry cowries, yet you are poor (have no money). pr.
a good, righteous person; cf. papao, ɔtrẽneeni.
pl. -fó, papist. - paapâ-sém, popery. Hist.
s. pápa.
pl. m-, As. a species of fish found in the Bosonotwe lake.
a disease similar to dwɔkɔ, kukurume-tawiam', ataatá; it causes tottering and inability to stand upright without support; s. horobɔbɔ.
1. well-doing. 1 Pet. 2, 15; syn. yiyeyɛ. — 2. moral goodness, virtue. - pápayefó, well-doer. 1 Pet. 3, 17.
adv. flat and lengthwise; dua yi atɔ p., opp. atɔ mã akyea.
tight, fast; wɔkye(kye)ree no (ne nsa) p., they bound him (his hands) tight; mĩa mu p.! tie it fast; syn. dasii, denneŋ.

[Heb.] paradise; orchard, pleasure garden. Cant. 4, 13.

v. [red. popare] to pass by, go by; to go or be far from, recede from, not to come to pass, not to happen, to be spared to. Eyi mparè me, be this far from me, may this not happen to me! Onykp. mmã empare se (aŋkã) dua yi bebu abɔ me, apáreè! This tree break (off) and fall on you! Aŋkã dua yi re(be)bu abɔ me, apáreè! Ɛpàre wo a, wo hɔ beto wo! pr. 2628. — Ade mpare ade a, aŋkã..., if it had not been fortunately avoided...
inf. the act of passing by or sparing, exemption; a threatening but averted danger (cf. asĩane). Apáre mparé me se aŋkã dua yi bebu abɔ me! — apáre! an exclamation of disgust or terror.
a place covered with thorn-bushes; ap. atiti me hɔ nyinaa, my whole body bears the pricks of thorns.

1. a rib, one of the bones enclosing the thoracic cavity; kyinii mp., the ribs of an umbrella. — 2. a spoke, the radius or ray of a wheel. — 3. spar, rafter of a house, cf. dampàré. — 4. a stripe or streak on the body, e. g. the marks which one gets from trees or branches in running through the bush: hwɛ ne hɔ ap.! oguáŋfó hɔ mpa ap. da. pr. — 5. F. an enclosure (as the ribs are one of the chest): wəabɔ me hɔ ap., F. they have encompassed me; cf. bɔ hɔ dantaban, kontonkron, twa hɔ hyia.

[pariw, red. pariparuw, inf. a-] 1. to cut off small particles from a surface, to notch, edge; to rough or fresh-cut (a millstone); əp. ne ẅiyam-mó = əde bobá bobə oẅiyammó a. s. oẅiyammóba no so; əpariparuw mpu-raŋ no hɔ de ayɛ apóŋŋuá; pariparuw əbo (abo) hɔ, to hew or dress stone(s). — əparuw soo ne tuo mu, he took up his gun quickly. — 2. to make a remark, to utter one's sentiments, give one's opinion; əparúw' asem no bi, he expresses his opinion concerning the matter; wapáruw' mè asɛmmóné, he has made bad remarks about me; əp. me mparuw-ŋwóma, he makes malignant remarks about me = əkã m'asɛm hɔ asɛmmone. pr. 431. — 3. red. with hɔ: to occupy oneself preliminarily or superficially with: wodi asɛm a, wəparipariw hɔ ansã-na wobu nteŋ; əpariparuw bone hɔ, he trifles with sin, he acts or talks with levity concerning sin, is not serious in his repentance and in praying for deliverance from sin.
hailstone. Osu betɔ na amp. agu a, aberewa bi na əparuw ne ẅiyammó wə soro, na nea əparuw na eturútùruw (wə) əbo no so gu no ne amp. yi.
preliminary speech, introduction, comment.
unfavourable or malignant utterance about some person or matter, s. paruw 2 & ŋwoma, bitter.

in a most miserable condition (cf. Lk. 10, 30); wayɛ p., he is in a woeful plight; he is utterly undone; he is desolate, destitute, starving, perishing, pining away. Lam. 4, 5. Rev. 18, 17; kũrow no aye p., the town has gone to ruin. Cf. sampam.

fraud, deception, falsehood, lie, roguery, extravagance; cf. atoro, ŋkontompo, ŋkoŋkonsa. [G. guile, John 1, 47; hypocrisy]; bɔ ap., to be extravagant; to behave as a liar or rogue; wabɔ ap. nti, wokã asɛm bi kyerɛ no a, ontie, because he is an extravagant fellow, he does not take any notice, if you admonish him.
pl. a-, a rogue able to do every kind of mischief, in the way of theft, lying, extravagance; akoa yi yɛ ɔp. = ɔyɛ n'ade sakasaka, odi ŋkwasasem, ɔyɛ onipa a ɔbɔ ka, ɔtorofo, ɔhohwini.
a certain animal. pr. 2629.
As. a certain kind of drum.
ragged, paltry; ɔde kente-gow mp. bi akoŋkwaŋ n'aseŋ, he has put a meagre piece of cloth round his loins; ɔnam mp., he goes about in ragged clothes. Mic. 1, 8.
twa mp., to make a short tour.
s. pása.
pásaprapaa, stark naked; ɔnam hoara p., he walks about st. n.
a thorny tree, used for building purposes & fuel; s. ɔpesare.
v., apásáw, F. = pase, apase.
inf. destruction. Rom. 3, 16.

v. [red. pasépase, Port. passear-se, Germ. spazieren, It. spazziare] to walk (for amusement or exercise), take a walk, promenade; mekɔpásé, mékɔ apásé or mpásé = mekogye mframa or mfare, mekotẽstẽe m'apowmu; mekɔpásépáse kakrá, I am taking a short walk.
mpásé, inf. ambulation; mekɔ ap., s. pase; kɔ or tu mp., to take a walk.

1. the lower part of the bed = anafɔ, nea wo naŋ kyerɛ hɔ. — 2. mpáasé, adv. unawares (prop. from under the bed); cf. mpaso; Asantefo abefi yeŋ mp., the Asantes have come upon us unexpectedly; ɛdom biara rentumi mfa wɔŋ mp., no enemy can take them by surprise; wɔahyew no mp., or mpaase-hyéw, they have burned the bush, which he had cut, before he was ready for it, fig. in his absence they have done something at which he ought to have been present.
[serewá à wɔápáw] small cowries, held in preference to large ones and therefore purposely selected.
hire, wages.
adv. [red. mpàso-mpàso] 1. by chance, accidentally, unawares. — 2. unadvisedly, inconsiderately, thoughtlessly, without thought, carelessly; óyè n'ádè mpásompàso; s. sèsekwàsòm.
1. plane; a joiner's tool; s. pa, v. 4. — 2. As. = akape.

pr. n. a town in Akwam & in Pae.
hire, wages.

the line(s) of battle. pr. 165. 2630 f. 3482; rank. 1 Sam. 17, 22f. — baa or bae mp., to extend the lines of battle; wobae kūrow no hō mp., they set themselves in array against the town. Jer. 50, 9. 14; twa mp., to arrange or array the battle, to set the battle in array; wɔatwa Akwam so (m)p., they are encamped against or ready to fight with Akwam; ohyéŋ' (m)p. so, he had the lines of battle formed [G. gba ta]; waw mp. ano, s. waw 5. — mpasúá-sò-fó, the soldiers forming a line of battle. — m-pasúatwá, inf. arranging the battle &c.

v. 1. to ward off, keep off, prevent; wɔp. wo ka, you are kept from debt. pr. 1571. — 2. to quell or quench the fire of a burning house. — 3. (to make straight, plain, level) fig. to adjust, settle, compose; to assuage, appease, allay, soften, sooth, quiet, pacify; to reconcile, conciliate, propitiate; to expiate, atone for; pata asɛm, to adjust a law-suit; mepataa wɔŋ mãnsɔ, I reconciled their difference; wapata ol ed the king; v fom a ɔfom ɔhe expiated his tra king. pr. 2635.

v. to put together, to join, to connect with; p. ... de, implies the place where things meet at the same time. pr. 314. 2425. 2631. — ŋkaŋ, do not run away at the same time! wɔapata, it is comprehended, understood. Rom. 13, 9.
pl. m-, a sort of shed on which plants or fruits are preserved; pata ase, under the town without a house. pr. 2632 f.
pl. m-, a partition, a hall, vestibule, porch, entrance; odan ketewa bi, a small room. [The word is mostly used for ntwirono F. 1 Kings 6, 3. Mt. 26, 71.
inf. 1. the act of (a dispute), pacificati-on, reconciliation. pr. 427. 1138; pr. 2636; atonement. — 2. reconciliation, pacification &c.; wɔmá no mpátá; indemnification. pr. 2636; ransom. Pr. 6, 35.
ransom.
— mpátá-aguá, expiatory sacrifice.
1. a scaffold, a stage, the building or roof of a house, a wókyère no ɔdan no, a. s. wotare daŋ no, the building frame (wɔye no, a. s. funu a, s. nãm). — 2. ère mp. isu, a roof.
1. no, a. s. wode nnúá gú so à wòyè mp., a raft.
slovenliness, dirtiness; daŋ mu ap., he is dirty and order in his house.

Rom. 13, 9.
pl. m-, a scaffold made of sticks on which plantains and other fruits are preserved; shed, hut; syn. apa; əsese. - pata ase wə hene, there is no town without a king. pr. 702. 792 f. 2632 f.
pl. m-), patám', portico, entrance-hall, vestibule, porch, covered entrance; ədaŋ ketewa a wusi mu kaŋ no. [The word is more used in Gã = Tw. ntiwonoá]. F. porch, common hall. Mt. 26, 71.

inf. 1. the act of settling (a dispute), pacification, (re-)conciliation. pr. 427. 1138; propitiation, expiation, atonement. — 2. the means for pacification &c.; wəmā mp. = wəde biribi pata; indemnification, indemnity. pr. 2636; ransom. Prov. 6, 35.
ransom. Ex. 30, 12. — mpátá-afəré, expiatory sacrifice, atonement.
mercy-seat. Heb. 9, 5.

1. a scaffold to stand upon in the building or repair of houses; dua a wókyère no ədaŋ hō gyina so ŋwōnā a. s. wotare daŋ no. — 2. litter, carrying frame (wəye no se apakaŋ de so funu a. s. nām). — 3. a bridge; wóakyère mp. wə asu yi so, e. s. woasísi nnúá gú so à wónam' so; - nsuani mp., a raft.
slovenliness, sluttishness; óyè ne daŋ mu ap., he neglects cleanliness and order in his room.

a. level, plain, open, free, denuded of trees or bush, bald, bare; wadəw hə (mā aye) p.; kūrow no hə ye p.; sareso ye p.; bepəw no atifi da hə pátaa, the top of that mountain is bare; mmepəw atifi nyinaa ayeye pataa-pataa; koko p.; bətan p., a bare rock. Ezek. 24, 7.8, cf. ferefere; dua no so ye p. = kwatii, without leaves, barę. Cf. pāradadada.

pl. m-, fish. pr. 444. 3091; cf. ɛnām, nsunām. commotion or agitation of a sheet of water; nsu no bə mp. = nsuani him bebree. Mt. 8, 24; cf. pakapaka. - mp.-ye, inf. Ps. 89, 10.
comprehension. - mp'. mpåebó, general prayer.

a rush, rushing motion and noise, rustle; boisterousness, turbulence: əde p. fi adiwo aba ədaŋ mu, əde p. fi dua so abshwe ase; adv. boisterously, tumultuously, noisily &c.; with a crash (Ps. 35, 8); óyè n'ade nyinaa p., he does everything impetuously.
day of atonement. Lev. 23, 27.
F. -dze, satisfaction, propitiation. 1 John 2, 2. - a propitiatory thing, gift or sacrifice. Rom. 3, 25.
expiatory work. K. § 232.
pl. a- [con. né pát. & ne pát...] pacifier, appeaser, peace-maker; mediator, conciliator; reconciler; propitiator; cf. kyeedwo. pr. 2424. 2637 f. 3076. Mt. 5, 9.
pl. a-, sloven, slut, slattern; cf. obufo, buru.

pl. m-, hyena; wolf; nicknames: kuntuŋ, kuntumpãā, obonu, obonukyerɛfo, ofui, agyanee.
a climbing plant; sareso hama a wodi n'aba.
macaroni, made of a paste of flour into long, slender tubes
pl. m-, F. an ant.

expiatory death.

v.: ɛmpatèrè dé = ɛŋkwati de, it is not without an agreeable taste; odɛw mpá mu.

a short-legged bedstead; s. mpadua.
red. v., s. patiriw.
mildew; mould.

a species of bean; s. asɛ.

Ak., by way of introduction.
an (unforeseen) accident; ɛyɛe me (wɔ) ap. mu = mpatuw mu, it happened to me or it befell me accidentally.
[mpa tiri mu] the upper side of a bed.
inf. [paa, pae, tiri mu] the parting of the hair on the top of the head.
v. [red. patipatiw] to glide, slide; slip, trip; to lose one's footing, to miss a step; op. hwee ase; fig. to commit a fault, pr. 2461; also watiriw.
=odampaŋ, a house or room with an open front; patom' hene, the head (overseer) of the king's cellar.
a slippery; osu ato nti ɔkwan mù ayɛ p., through the rain the road has become slippery.

inf. imputation; shift; wodii asɛm no mp., they conducted the lawsuit in a shifty way (shifting off the charge upon the innocent party); ɛ.s. wopa asɛm bi to wo yɔŋkɔ so, wuyi asɛm bi de hyɛ wo yɔŋkɔ sɛ ono na oyɛe, you shift off a charge and put it upon another person, asserting that it is he who committed the deed; cf. pa..to..so, under pa, v. 6.
pl. m-, owl; ne mmɛraŋ: aduammɛŋ, agyammɛŋ. pr. 533.
=patu ani, the eye of an owl. pr. 2304.

unexpected killing.
a sudden death; cf. awusíŋ. pr. 2544. 2646. — ɔ-patuwú-yàré, a disease causing sudden death.

v. to surprise, overtake, to do something unexpectedly, suddenly, at once, without warning, unawares, unlooked-for, undevisedly, ɛnyé mpátúw ɛyɛn, it does not befall us unprepared; mepatuw na mebaa ha yi, I came here without having previously designed it; dwom yi de, ɔp. bɔ ne tirim na ɛyɛe, it is this song that she improvised; ade repatuw asã, the night falls in all of a sudden; wap. abuagyɛŋ, he died all of a sudden; nnipa nyinaa remp. ŋwu, all men will not die at once. pr. 315 f. 401. 2408. 2430. 2544. 2643 ff. 3336; - F. to pretend.
inf.: yɛ -, to be in a great hurry, to be urgent; ...akoyɛ mp. nti, because it required speed, - was urgent... Job 9, 5.
unexpectedly; unawares.
a certain bead; s. abene.
inf. F. telling lies &c., s. apàw.
di p., to laugh at, make sport of.

v. [red. popaw] to choose, select; to pick out, more than one or as many as possible of a plurality of things (or persons), whilst yi is used of one object or of more; - mépàw nea mepe, I choose what I like; opaw ntrama fufu, he is picking out fufu; opaw ŋkɔri, he is picking out the large fowl. pr. 1373. 1625.
a certain bird; s. apàw, F. falsehood; s. apàw.

twi: boa, di atoro, t' ap. = wommoa, you are right, you are not lying.

peacock.

a certain game; s. agoru.
F. falsehood, lie; twa (a)paw = boa, di atoro, twa ŋkontompo; wuntwa ap. = wommoa, thou dost not lie, i.e. you are right, you speak the truth.
[= paa, q. v.] pl. (dim.) mpaawá, a work or engagement for hire or wages; job; eye a, odidi mpàwá-mpàwá, occasionally he undertakes a job.
pl. m-, Okw. F. plate, platter (Mt. 23,25) = apaawá; cf. abeyeaa.
Akp. F. a round, flat or hollow vessel, made of one piece of wood, used also for winnowing; fan. Isa. 30,24; əkorow tratraa bi a mmea de woŋ nneema-nneema gum'; s. apawá, apampaa.

pl. a-, elector, one of the princes of Germany formerly entitled to choose the emperor or king. Hist. mpaw-mú, inf. selection, choosing, choice; syn. nyiyim'; nnipa mu mp. biara nni Nyaŋkəpɔŋ fãm'. Cf. Rom. 2,11. Eph. 6,9. James 2,1. [hãã].
peacock. 1 Kg. 10,22. (diff. koopáwpaw: bə p. to do a thing quick and carelessly. pr. 2308.
As. apaaso, on the plain.
a mat made of the leaves of the fan-palm. [apaw.
inf. telling lies &c., s. twa
