inf. [yɛ ampa] reality, sureness; true knowledge, sound wisdom; safety, sincerity. Prov. 2,7. 8,14. Job 6,13. 12,16. 2 Cor. 8,8.

[red. pepe] 1. to seek, pr. 818, to search, for procure, provide, to try to get; (ópɛ..., he seeks; òpɛ..., he desires); pɛ bōrō-ŋhoma bi mã me, get me a piece of paper! orepɛ me asem, he seeks an occasion against me, picks a quarrel with me. 2 Kg. 5,7. - opɛ me see nɛ animguase, he seeks to bring ruin and disgrace upon me; - pe..ano, to search for the cause of..; - pɛ ani bɛhwe (lit. come & see with your own eyes), it is marvellous, wonderful; senea əbə saŋkū fa 'pɛ ani bɛhwe', it is wonderful how he plays the organ. - pɛ ade, to seek riches, try to become rich; pɛ ade nyã, to gather riches, become rich, make a fortune. pr. 317ff. - 2. to desire, wish, want, will, be willing, intend, followed by an objective complement and a verb in the consec. form or by the conj. se. pr. 2647 ff. 2661. Gr. § 256 Rem.; òpɛ mó ayé, he would like to be in your place; əpɛ se ohū ade nyinaa kroŋkroŋ, he wants to know everything clearly; mempe wo agoru, I do not want to have you for my play-mate or friend. pr. 415. 2225; kōma a ɛpɛ, a willing mind. 1 Pet. 5,2. - 3. pɛ ntém yɛ, to be quick in doing, to do quickly. pr. 418. 3204. - 4. repɛ followed by the consec. form of another verb, to be going to; afei na ɛrepɛ adaŋ atutuw, now it would probably have come (or, it nearly came) to a quarrel. - 5. to like, love, be fond of. pr. 29. Gr. § 203 Rem.; mempɛ no, I do not like him; ampaŋ pɛ sūm, the bat likes the dark; mèpɛ n'asem, I like him, lit. his word, i.e. his conversation, I am fond of him; - mempɛ n'asem, I will have nothing to do with him; - pɛ atutuw, to be quarrelsome; òpɛ atutuw dodo nti obiara mpé n'asem, because he is very quarrelsome, nobody will have any thing to do with him; - pɛ adifude, to be greedy. - 6. to love a person of the other sex. pr. 2666; wapɛ əbea = wafa əbea, s. fa 9.

a. 1. like, alike, same; ye pɛ, se pɛ, to be alike, to be the same; nnipa abieŋ no se pɛ, those two men are like each other; nsem abieŋ no ase se pɛ, the meaning of these two words is the same. pr. 3255. - 2. complete, perfect; - ne hō nyinaa pɛ; onipa yi te hō pɛ, 'he sits there in such a manner as to arouse neither suspicion nor comment'. - 3. ne pɛ a əwie yɛ, his perfection; cf. peye; ne pɛ a ənye yɛ, his imperfection. K. § 166.

adv. exactly, accurately, precisely; just, even, but, only; completely, thoroughly, perfectly; adaŋ anaŋ pe wɔ kūrow yi mu, there are but (or only) four houses in this village; wosi nnipa oha pεpε, there are exactly a hundred people; wasiesie ne daŋ mu pεpεpε, he has put his room in excellent order; ohũũ me ara pe, oyaw me, as soon as he saw me, he scolded me; woye ade pe, you act quite rightly.

inf. 1. will, desire. Ja. 1, 18; wó pé a wopε nye, thy will be done (Mt. 26, 42); ope na mepεe se mehũ wo anim, I have heartily desired to see thy face (Lk. 22, 15); cf. apεde. - ɔpέ-sɔ, of a free will, willingly. 2. love or affection for a person of the other sex, amorous passion; opε fi dompem', love comes from the inmost heart, the heart's core, prop. from the interior of the bone. pr. 2671.

the harmattan, a dry and cool north-easterly wind from the interior of Africa, which blows in December, January and February toward the Atlantic ocean, and is usually accompanied by a haze which obscures the sun; it withers vegetation and shows the effects of its excessive dryness in the skin, lips, nose &c. of the human body, in things made of wood, leather &c. - opέ asi, the harmattan has set in. pr. 288. 2672f. - 2. the dry season, from Dec. to Feb., marked by the harmattan-wind, the haze and fine dust accompanying it, extreme drought and a cloudless sky. Cf. opebere, ofupe, ɔpenimma, ɔpepɔŋ. Ope afe adu. Ope mu a. s. ofupe mu wobu abŭrow tu dé (mpɔwm'), ntɔmmɔ, kooko... pέ, night-watching; si pε, to sit up at night. pr. 2155.
Aky. a certain game; cf. agoru.
adv. thickly; mme ŋkɔ na ehye ho pe; cf. pépe, bé.
(pl. mpέ), a nickname of kontromfi. [G. ekpe, baboon].
a nickname of the dog, s. ɔkramaŋ.
a kind of jumping game.

= mpokyere, iron fetters.
a dish of mashed bananas (green or ripe); pɔtɔw kwadu buŋ a woanɔa no p.!
after-pains; cf. kagyi-rãmã.
dispute, contention, quarrel; di ap., to dispute &c.

twi: piŋtiŋŋ, a. & adv. firm, -ly, fixed, constant, completely; steady. Ex. 17,12; wusi dua bi na ɛyɛ p. a, wuse: átim; àwia gyina p., the sun has exactly its highest position; àwiá p. = àwia ketee; me hō ye p., my health is excellent, unshaken, constant. - piŋtiŋŋ-yé, inf. firmness &c., health.

eng: a kind of tabor, tabret, tambourine, timbrel; toa ko-kŭroo a woatu ano na wəde ŋhoma ayere na wəsɛ wəy kəŋ mu de woŋ nsa kã; gye ahene nè asikafo na wətaa yɛ ade no.
a certain kind of drum.
very much; mikyia wo p., my hearty greetings to you; cf. pii, pá.
the sound produced by gnawing.
= pibibi, kitikiti; osu tɔe p., it was raining hard; mframa no bɔe p., the wind blew vehemently; wode pipibibie baa yeŋ fi, they rushed towards (or into) our house.
thick; dense; dua, p., a thick stick; mmĕrete yi (mu) yɛ p., this board is thick; omuŋuŋkum p., a dense fog; usu p., muddy, miry water; akwatia pipripi, pr. 3233.
thickness; density.
dwarf.

to knock; to hurt or be hurt by violence, to wound; be wounded; mapira me nsa(m'), me nsa apira, my hand has been wounded; mapirapira me nsa hō anum, I have received five wounds in my hand; cf. bə afe; - wopiraa no pira-bone, he was mort. w. - Phr. wókà woŋ ti pirá, they lay or put their heads together, i.e. they troop, gather or collect together for a common undertaking, for an evil purpose; they combine, conspire, plot. Isa. 54, 15.
ne p. fi mogya, his wound bleeds; n'apira-kuru fifi mogya, his wounds are bleeding.
a wounded person.
a wound, i.e. a breach or separation of parts by violence, as by a cut, stab, or, bruise; diff, akisikuru, an open sore, ulcer; s. kuru.
pyramid.

twi: pirápira, red. v., 1. s. pira. - 2. p. mu,
eng: to knock together; to jostle one against another. Nah. 2,5; wopirapiram' = wobobom', wopempem woŋ hō; cf. wodi atipira.
wounds without cause. Prov. 23,29.
whip, scourge, cut from the skin of an elephant, hippopotamus, buffalo, wild horse, bɛw, tóróm &c., twisted, sometimes three or fourfold, and fasten-
mpere, F.: si emp., to run a race; syn. tu mmirika.
a basket with a lid, made of kubé leaves, used for carrying provisions or containing clothes; cf. séséa, kyerɛŋkyɛ.
a certain game; s. agoru.

twa ap., to come to an end, to cease; to fail, be spent or exhausted before the time; adwuma no atwa ap., the work was given up (as the people were incapable of completing it); atúotów betwa ap. ntem, the shooting will soon be over (from want of powder); n'ahõɔdeŋ twaa ap. ansã-na owiee n'adwuma, his strength failed before he finished his work; nsu a mise mede mereguare no atwa me so ap., the water with which I intended to wash myself was used up before I had finished.
1. a hunting-bag; kotoku a wode ŋhoma pam; abɔmmɔfo de aboba nè atuduru gum'. 2. the pouch of certain birds.
F. piro, v. to roll (hãse, a cask. pr. 2967, abo stones); - red. piré-pirew, F. piropiro, to roll, wallow, welter. Mk. 9,20.

v. to make or grow hard, to harden; to parch, scorch; ne hõ apirim, his skin is getting hard, said of a baby of 3 or 4 months; ɔdé, ntɔmmɔ no hõ ap., the outside of the yam or the sweet potato has become black (in the ground); ɔdé a ɛda gyam' na ogya pii nni hõ pirim; ɔdé no ap., the yam has become hard over the fire (in boiling or roasting). pr. 1550. - ɔdé mmeŋ yiye a, epirim, wotõtõ-a, ɛmmeŋ bio, if the yam is not well roasted in the beginning, it remains hard, and does not become softer by continued or repeated roasting; aduaŋ a wɔnõ nõa na ɛntumi mmeŋ, wose: apirim; ekuru a wotõtõ a ɛmmeŋ, wuse: ap. --- Phrases: ne kõma ap. = ne k. ye deŋ na ontie asɛm biara ŋkɔm'; opirim ne hõ or kõma, he hardens himself or his heart, so that he does not listen to advice; nea op. ne kõma, the courageous man. Am. 2,16; opirim' ne tirim, he took courage; pirim wo anim, take heart or courage, do it manfully! opirim n'anim tu no fo, he boldly (or earnestly) admonishes or forewarns him; op. n'anim pɛ ne ŋkwãgye akyi kwaŋ, he earnestly strives for his salvation. K. § 257.
[obsol.] = piriw, birim.
F. perfectly: mã yendɔ w' p.

pírimm, prím-prim, prím-prim, hard, strong, healthy, lively; ne hõ (yɛ) primm = ne hõ yɛ dɛnnɛnnen-neŋ, ɔnyaré neŋ; onipa yi, ɔyɛ mũ primm, this man is not sickly, but primprim, he is quite nimble = ne hõ ye deŋ, ɔnyé fõuɔfõnɔ.

bɔ p., to be struck with fear or terror, to be startled. Mk. 16,5; tr. bɔ..p., to strike with terror, to startle, frighten, terrify; - syn. bɔ birim, bɔ pitiri; yi..hũ, yi..ahii. - píriw-bɔ, inf. terror. Isa. 17,4.
si mp. to shout with joy; to play. - inf. mpiriwa-si, shouting with joy &c.
red. piropiro, v. F. = pirew. Mt. 27,60. Mk. 9,20.
= sipiripii, confused; dull &c.
[obsol.] a kind of frumenty or pap; abũroduan a woyam na wɔamã ahono na woasɔŋ so na wowie (so sɔŋ) a wɔakã [G. aflata].

swoon, fainting-fit; to p., to become weak, fidgety, restless, senseless, to swoon away, faint, espec. from hunger. pr. 2067. 3223. - to cause to faint: ɔkɔm na ɛtɔ nnipa p.; cf. to beraw, tware. -- píti, leprosy = kwata, fa-wohõ-kodi, mi-fua-duam'.
a jumping insect.
the name of a small bird; anõmaa ketewa bi; ne hõ ŋwraŋ-ŋwraŋ, ne hõ kaŋkaŋ, nanso wodi.
ebiti, F. apitsĩ, unleavened bread; abũrow a woyam no mmɔre na wɔnõa na wɔbɔ no ap.
the day of unleavened bread. Lk. 22,7.
o-pitiní, pl. apitifo, leper = ɔkwatani, pr. 2194.
pl. apitifo, leper = ɔkwatani, pr. 2194.
the sound produced by pounding fufuu.
a certain plant; s. otokotaka.
thickly crowded, thronged, close together; syn. pepe; ŋkŭrɔfo no aboaboa wɔŋ hɔ ano p. Lk. 11,29; ŋk'ráŋ yi, wòfore só p.
adv. much, continuously; wòhwe no p.
bɔ p., to be struck with terror, to startle, shrink; cf. piriw.
pl. a-, a species of river-fish. pr. 2694.
inf. falling in a swoon, fainting; op. nyinaa fi kɔm (?).
pl. a-, a starving, fainting person. pr. 2695. Job 22,7.
pitsipitsiw, F. thick (of fluids); cf. pìtipiti & piw.
F. thick (of fluids); cf. pìtipiti & piw.

v. 1. to become or be thick, inspissate(d); ŋkwaŋ, aduru no apiw. — 2. to be dense, stand thickly or close together; kwae yi mu piw, emu nnua n.a. (bemmeŋ hɔ) pìw só, kyere só; mmrûkuu yi, emu mpiw. — 3. to make thick, hard; p. dote = mà dote ye pẽto-pẽto. pr. 1596.
inf. stubbornness; asɔ̃deŋ, asɔ̃wui, kōmapirim; s. mpì.
por, v. F. to strip (off), atar, one's clothes; s. pore.
v. F. to strip (off), atar, one's clothes; s. pore.
v. Ak. s. pow.
Aky. = osɔ́wá.
or pó po, expressions imitative of the sound of beating, knocking.

v. [red. popo] 1. to push; ɔpò me táw = osum me, ɔwɔ me ŋkɔnsiaw, holding me by the neck, he pushes or thrusts me forward. — 2. to shake, tremble [inf. apo, q.v.] - red. ɔpopó, ne hɔ popo, ne hɔnam popo he trembles; mframa popo nnua, the wind shakes the trees (syn. him, posow, wosow); nnua no apopo, the trees have been shaken. — 3. red. ɔpopo ne ti, he shakes his head, refuses, declines. — 4. po, to refuse, decline, set aside, make void, frustrate, Gal. 2,21, reject. pr. 1555; F. Mt. 21,42. Mk. 7,9. — to forsake, leave. F. Mt. 19,27. — to disdain, scorn, despise; to repudiate; to spurn away; F. to renounce; to deny. Mt. 10,33. 16,24. — syn. pa [G. kwa]. Phr. woapo ne bra amã no, they have left him to himself. - po so, to refuse, decline (a present, an invitation to eat); to simulate refusal (me-mã obi biribi na ɔpe, na ɔboapa se ɔmpé a, na ɔpó so neŋ). — 5. po abŭrow so, to sift, winnow or fan corn by pushing or shaking the vessel containing it; cf. huw so. — 6. to throw off or drop the leaves, to grow leafless; aka kŭmaa na dua yi apo, this tree will soon lose its leaves; dua yi apo, this tree is leafless; nnua no apopo; to fall off (of a flower), 1 Pet. 1,24. pr. 993. 997. Cf. po, to wither. — 7. to emit, discharge: n'ano po ahuru, he (much) talking. — 8. to utter words by repetition: po dódów, to stammer, stutter. Mk. 7,32. — 9. to emit other sounds: po waw = bə waw, to cough. — 10. to growl, gnarl, snarl (as a dog, leopard, lion, bear). Jer. 51,38; cf. pow. — 11. po so, to rattle in the throat in the last struggle before death; pl. wopopo so. — 12. to beat: po ŋhoma, to curry leather by a process of scraping, cleansing, beating, smoothing and colouring; mmoa ŋhoma na wodan ani mã shõ dwo (the hides of animals are dressed and prepared so that they become soft and pliant), na wode di adwini biara; etəd. wode hye fam' mã shõ dwo na woàpo só ŋhwí no, na wəahye no kɔkɔɔ a, s. tuntum, a, wode ayɛ mpaboá, ntoa, mmoha, ɛkyɛw, ŋkotoku n.a. — 13. po abrɔbe, to sever or extract the fibres from the leaves of the pine-apple; wəpo (or woboro) abrɔbe-ahabaŋ na wəwəre so na' woyi mu abrɔbe-mfuturu no. — 14. po..hõ, to clean; po amapkani hõ, cf. pow 1. — 15. to abandon; obi mpo ne ti mmã dwiw, 'nobody gives up his head to be cut off', i.e. nobody will give up his life if he can help it; troubles connected with it.
v. to wither; cf. po, to grow leafless; this leaf is withered, cf. apopo.
pl. id. fetters, chains; = pokyere, m-.
Gy. Aky. a sea, ocean. pr. 1023.
inf. abnegation, refusal.
v., inf. wither; cf. po, to wither.
inf. trembling; the state of a firm or old person who cannot stand on his feet and head; ɔpó, trembling.
pl. a-, a bale of goods; ntamá pó o nta, a bundle of cloth, ntamá ara ntwaa so bi.
a-, a dish made of clay. pr. 3017.

sea, ocean. pɔm, in the sea; ɛ-pò no, the sea; kɔ pɔm, go to sea. Mt. 21,3. — viri, the tide is coming in, it is rising; twẽ, the tide goes out, it is ebbing water. tẽaa, ɛpo bása, a gulf, bay. D. As. Cf. pɔ, sea. pokwantẽaa; po-m-pó, (full of water).
m'po, (full of water); madi awu a, anka me mpo, if I had committed murder, I would not deal with you in this manner, mpo (Judg. 8,19). —
adv. entirely; te hɔ pòɔ a woyɛ, these people are always in the same place; woye nnipa pòɔ, they are people who are always there.
the sound of a heavy fall; otuo tow pòɔ; cf. pɔ́ pɔ.
adv. expressing a heavy fall; in walking: n'anamon pòɔ (= kó kɔ) n'anamon pòɔ, he walks heavily; ɔsore a, pɔɔ pòɔ, he rises heavily; preŋ na ɔkɔ, m'póɔ.
adv. expressing the sound of beating, striking.
v. to wither; cf. how; ababaŋ yi apo, this leaf is withered; pl. ŋhabaŋ yi apopo.
pl. id. fetters, shackles for the feet = pokyere, m-.
Gy. Aky. a lizard; ɔte afasu so. pr. 1023.
inf. abnegation &c., cf. po, v. 4.
ɛ-, inf. withering; cf. ɔhow.
inf. trembling, tremor of weak, infirm or old persons; trembling of hands, feet and head; ɔyaré apó.
pl. a-, a bale of cloth (= 12 yards); ntamá pó or ntamapó = ntama a obiara ntwaa so bi peŋ ɛ.
a-, a dish made of some herb. pr. 3017.

sea, ocean. pr. 1449, cf. bosonopo; pom', in the sea; po só or pò ani, on the sea; - kɔ po, to go to fish. John 21,3. - ɛpo yiri, the tide flows, sets in, is coming in, it is flowing water; ɛpo twɛ, the tide goes out, ebbs, falls, it is ebbing water. pr. 670. - po nom' tɛaa, ɛpo bása, gulf; po nom' tetrete, bay. D. As. Cf. kɔntɔŋ, dɔnnɔŋ; pokã, pokwantɛaa; po-fãm', pom'.

(full o) adv. even; nay; mpo madi awu a, aŋkã wɔnyé mè sɛ, even if I had committed a murder, they would not deal with me like this; me nuanom, mpo me nã mma ne woŋ (Judg. 8, 19). - Gr. § 75, 3. 134, 3 b.
adv. entirely; permanently; ebi(nom) te hɔ pɔɔ a wɔŋkɔ baabiara bio, some people are always living in the same place; woye nnipa a wote ha pɔɔ, they are people who live here permanently.
the sound of shooting or drumming;
adv. expressing the sound of steps in walking: n'asepatere no si fam' pɔɔ pɔɔ (= kɔ kɔ) na ɔde kɔ; ɔno de, daa ɔsore a, pɔɔ pɔɔ na ɔkɔ, e.s. mprempreŋ na ɔkɔ, mprempreŋ na ɔkɔ.
adv. expressing the sound or act of beating, striking or cutting; mabɔ no poó = bum; wotwa ogya (poó poó) or pɔo poó.

v. [red. poopoo]: p. ani, to cast an angry, piercing, intimidating look at; opoo n'ani, opoopoo (opupuw) n'ani kyere me, opɔɔpɔo me, he threatens, frightens me, addresses me harshly, flies at me, speaks roughly to me, rebukes me sharply, 1 Tim. 5, 1, = otutu n'ani kyere me, ɔtɛstɛ me hunabuna me, ɔye n'anim kyere me se, ɔnyã biribi a, ɔbeye me (Gen. 42, 7. 30).

mpoó: ɔbɔ me mpoo or apoo, 1. he ill-treats, ill-uses, abuses, maltreats me = óyè me sakasaka, ɔye me pupɔpúpɔ, oboro me, ɔghwe me so yiye. - 2. he cheats, deceives me = ɔdaadaa me, osisi me; F. he robs me. - bɔ apoo or mpoo, also to commit burglary; cf. twa dwow.
m-, inf. ill treatment; cheating, deceit; burglary; F. highway robbery.
burglar(s).
pl. m-: twa..poa, to challenge, defy, with words, espec. by the use of debasing or vilifying expressions; otwa me poa, wotwitwa yeŋ mpoa.

(pl. mpoatwitwa). inf. challenge, setting at defiance; defamation; dwom yi mpo ye mp. (mp. ne sɛ: ɔhene bi wɔ hɔ na wo ani nsɔ no na wokasakasa senea wo nè no sɛ, se ebia wobese sɛ: oyi a, minsurɔ no, ontumi ŋkum me, mewɔ sika mekyen no, ohĩani no nsɔ, wɔde no ye deŋ?) pr. 1096. 2698 ff.
1. = hyeŋmuni. - 2. naval hero.
sea-shore, strand, beach, shore; sea-side, coast, sea-coast. pr. 1107. 1291. 2697.
pl. m- -fo, a dweller on the sea-coast; people living near the seashore.
gulf.
= apowapow, s. ɛpow; bump &c.
Aky. = mpoatwa.
a nickname of the fly. pr. 2572f. mpobi? pr. 2701.
pl. m-, a black boil, very painful and enduring longer (perh. 6 months)
pr. n. 1. an ancient king. 2. a brook, G. Ogboli.
the itch.
[pɔw b.] wabɔ me hɔ p., evil is determined against me by him. Esth. 7,7.
pl. a-, a large pot to keep water in. pr. 2702; cf. ataahina.
s. faka.
south. Ps. 107,3; cf. kesee-fám, pɔfiri, a medicinal plant.
unexpectedly, unawares; suddenly, on a sudden, all of a sudden; cf. mpaase, mpasompaso.
pl. (a- fo), apofo, fisherman. pr. 2703.

[ɔpɔw foforo] assumption, forwardness, pertness, flippancy; cf. nsoá-fóro; "ɔpɔw anaa mp.?" is it "politeness or pertness?" abofra a ɔrefiti ase asũa kasa na ɔde mpanyinsém nè mmɛrántiwasɛm afra ne bram'.
[foro, v.] pl. id. = antweribe.
yam, plantains, potatoes &c., boiled without having been cleaned.
v. F. to be soft, flabby (of the flesh).
a. F. soft, not hard.
asem no bɔɔ wɔŋ nyinaa p., the matter puzzled all of them; asɛm no abɔ no p., he is at a loss.
= apagyá.
[pa ogya] glow-worm; cf. obogyá, apagyá.
[ɛpom awuru] sea-tortoise, -turtle; ap. bɔŋ, tortoise-shell; cf. apowuru.
channel, strait, narrow sea between two portions of land.
pl. m-, lump, ingot or nugget of gold, bullion; mpɔkɔwa, i.e. mpɔw akɔkɔɔ akɔkɔɔ.
pr. n. m. pr. 2704f.
a species of white heron, aigret.
a draught of a fluid; cf. few.
s. kontromfĩ.
pl. m-, the full round breast of a young woman; cf. nufu, nufuten; diff. mpekua.
pl. m- -fo, a full-grown girl.
a strait of the sea.
v. 1. to crumble off; to pluck off. [G. kpoke]; ɔp. akutu hɔ, he peels an orange; ɔp. n'ani hwɛ no, he stares at him, casts an evil look at him. — 2. to defer, delay, linger, tarry.
pokye-pɔkyè: n'ani (yɛ) p., he has piercing eyes, a piercing look.
pl. m-, fetter for the feet; F. mp. (no sing.); cf. apo, mpinkyeraŋ, dawɛmfoɔ. — to. p., gu. mp., de.. to mp. mu, to fetter.
pl. a--fo, a prisoner in fetters, in jail; diff. odeduani, one arrested (in his own or another man's house) on whom the sentence is not yet passed.
[ɛpo mu] F. in the sea; to sea; southward. Cf. nifã 4, po-fãm'.

v. 1. to stick, be fastened, be held back somewhere; me sika a aka no pɔma mú nne, the rest of the money due to me is still retained (in their hands, withheld from me). - tr. ɔpɔmá ne kyɛw, he puts on his hat; ɔp. ne ŋkrante, he puts his cutlass into its handle; de dua p. adare, to furnish a bill-hook with a (wooden) handle; - wode asɛm no pomá hyɛɛ ne nsa, they put the matter into his hands. — 2. to charge or load a gun; ɔpomá ne tuo. — ɔhene nè ne mpanyimfo gye p. so, the king and his (elders) councillors are confederated, i.e. determined not to yield.

pl. m-, (F. poma, Mk. 6,8) stick, walking-stick. pr. 388; cane, staff (of the speaker of a jury, of a messenger or ambassador); wòkosi mp. wɔ ɔhene anim = wòkoyi nteŋ wɔ ɔh. anim; s. si; aŋkã bo aŋkã p., s. ɔbo.
pl. a-, m-, 1. cane-bearer, messenger, ambassador. Isa. 18,2; syn. ɔkyéámé, ɔbɔfó. — 2. pl. a-, persons sitting on the scaffold of poles serving for a W. C.: mekɔmã ap. akyẽ = mekɔ dua so.
ototo me a regardless, unconcerned thing at all about nsɛm ap., do not neglect slight his words!
inf. contempt, regard.
[si mp.] a plant.
[a plant, a stick] fig. a footing.
a byname of a god.
so or kind of use of a messenger to address an assembly, asɛm. pr. 3283.
pl. m- [ɔpɔmma] toto mp. no mu!
pl. a- [pɔu, pɔmã].
too much room.
red. v. pàm, Ezek. 27, 2.
red. v. prune (a tree), to a pɔmpáŋ, red. v., pãm, there is a distance are separated.
pl. m-, boil, tumor; p. tu ntɛm pobiá; - ɔyare mp.
inf. vain haughtiness, pɔmpɔ́ ɔyè ap., he is puffed up, swaggering, vaunting, obu ne hɔ kɛse, ɔhwɛ Ps. 131, 1.

v. 1. pɔmpɔŋ, the highest asɛm or ɔyare no: the matter (law-suit) has reached the highest, much more difficult than it was in the pɔmpɔŋ mú or p. come to extremities, the highest pitch; pɔmpɔŋ, pɔnpɔŋ, ch. so called from the uncorking of the bottle.
ɔtoto me ap., he is careless, regardless, unconcerned, he cares nothing at all about me; monntoto ne nsem ap., do not neglect, disregard or slight his words!
inf. contempt, neglect, disregard.
[si mp.] a public transaction.
[a place in which to put a stick] fig. a footing.
a byname of Tannɔ, s. App. B.
so or kura mp., to make use of a messenger's cane, to go to address an assembly = di ɔhene anim asem, pr. 3283.
pl. m- [ɔpoŋ, dim.] shutter; toto mp. no mu!
pl. a- [poŋ, v.] F. redeemer.
too much rubbing of the teeth, so that blood comes, pr. 2645.
red. v. pàm. - ɔ-pompamfo, pl. a-, mender, repairer, caulker. Ezek. 27, 27.
red. v., s. pàŋ; p... hɔ, to prune (a tree), to dress (a vine).
red. v., pàŋ; wɔŋ ntam' p., there is a distance between them, they are separated.
pl. m-, boil, furuncle; caricous tumor; p. tu ntem (opens sooner) kyeŋ pobiá; - ɔyare mp.
inf. vain pomp, vain-glory, haughtiness, pomposity, arrogance; ɔyè ap., he is puffed up, vain-glorious, swaggering, vaunting, a braggart; obu ne hō kese, ɔhwehwe nneɛma akese. Ps. 131, 1.
pom'pɔŋ, v. red., s. poŋ. Joel 1, 7.

the highest pitch or degree; asem or ɔyare no ato (no) pómpɔŋ mú, the matter (law-suit), or his sickness, has reached its highest point, and is much more difficult to be overcome or cure than it was in the beginning; ato pómpɔŋ mú or p. só, matters have come to extremities; it has reached the highest pitch; cf. apenteŋ-so.
póŋpoŋ, champagne, lemonade; so called from the noise made by the uncorking of the bottle; s. póŋ.
[poŋo] wrinkles; curves.

pomp'rɔ, red. v. 1. to bend; s. poŋ; to crumple up; p... nsa, to fold one's hands together. Eccl. 4, 5. 2. to wrinkle. pr. 3490. 3492; to get (perf. to have) wrinkles, to be wrinkled: akwakoraá no anim' apóm-pɔno, that old man has a wrinkled face; ɔpompónɔ né mòma, he knits his brows. 3. to writhe with pain or agony. 4. to bend or wind in manifold curves: asu no ap. = akontoŋ, akyeakyea.

2. to strip or deprive some one of property given to him at some former time (said of persons who impoverish one previously enriched by them): Owusu Yaw apɔŋ ne yere Maanu, Mr. R. has taken back from his wife M. all he had given her.

7. to dismiss from work or from a meeting, as-

sembly or congregation; owura M. apoŋ n'adwumayɛfo, Mr. M. has dismissed his labourers; ɔkyerskyerɛfo no ap. ne sukuufo, the teacher has dismissed his scholars or pupils; wɔapoŋ asafo no, the congregation has been dismissed. — 8. to call people out of or away from their homes: wapoŋ ŋkürɔfo aboa ano, he has called the people to assemble. — 9. to call back, recover, win or bring back (fugitives, under the assurance of their not being hurt, from the place to which they fled perhaps from fear of being killed): wopoŋ akobafɔ a, wo ntama ano yɛ duru. pr. 493; cf. poŋo, F. — 10. to redeem, recover a pawn. pr. 770. — 11. poŋ so serew, to burst into laughter; ɔkãa saa no mepoŋ serew twétwetwe, when he said that, I laughed heartily.

a certain animal (fish?) living in the water. pr. 2727; s. apúpúw. apúpũa, a medicinal plant; akrámãnnuru. pupú-púpú: me yam' yɛ me p., there is a noise in my belly; s. yafum-yare.
a certain sound or noise; p. wə hə à, aberante ntə akü (mu), if one were warned, one would not fall into a pit.
Aky. apúpúo, pl. id. the smallest species of fish; s. apúpú.
v. s. puw.
s. asunsoŋpúpúw.
pl. a., one who frightens another, nea oyi bi hũ.
F. mpunaŋ, a large piece of timber, beam.
mpúru, a game in which short pointed sticks are thrown into soft ground; tow mp., to play such a game.
adv. imitative of the sound sometimes heard when food comes into an empty stomach, - or of a foot knocking against a stone.
a certain tree; wəde seŋ abonnua.
p'roku = nea ne sẽ apõrow, one who has bad teeth; òye p., he has bad teeth. pr. 2725. 3582.
very deep; òkoe ara p., he fell down very deep (sc. into a shaft); cf. bũroŋŋ, kūroŋŋ.

v. 1. F. Akp. to stumble = hintiw. - 2. to snap one's fingers at one, to challenge by a stroke with the finger; wapurow me or wap. m'ano, he has challenged me to fight by striking me over my mouth with the tip of his finger; - to knock; to throw about. - 3. to disgust one, provoke one's dislike, excite aversion in some one; asem yi ap. me = afono me, I am weary of or disgusted with this matter, it has become loathful or an abhorrence to me. Isa. 1, 14. 66, 24.
pl. a., a species of small squirrel; òp. pã, op. aŋkasa, ne hɔ̃ kəkɔɔ; cf. apetebi, apeterebi, akwantea, akwantwea, kwaame-tabi, akyerekye(ree); amoakuwa, pr. 1101. 2566. 2728.
a white species of opurow.
the noise caused by swallowing; cf. puro.
mpúri.
that which is roughly or coarsely ground or pounded; that which is rough instead of being soft and smooth; ade biara a wəayam sẽ wəasiw na amfe no.
bùrum; cf. prum, pum.
the rustling noise of an antelope in the bush. pr. 3516.

Aky. puduo, 1. a. round, circular, orbicular, globular, spherical, cylindrical; cf. korokorowa, kurukuruwa. - 2. n. a round, disk, cylinder; òsram atwa p. = kròkũmã, the moon has formed into a disk, i.e. is full; wəahyehye kyínii no, e.s. wəde ne mparow no ahyehye ne p. mu; akatawia no p. abu.
naŋkũm, pr. 3026.
globe. D. As.
òsram p., the becoming full of the moon.
yam boiled with the peel; Akwam kūrom' wontwa p.
pùsiripii = òkwà, hwèe(?).
As.: asase p., earthquake; cf. opusuw.
a kind of play or dance.
red. v., to shake; s. poso-poso & pusuw. pr. 1599.
opete.

v. 1. to shake; wugoru me hɔ̃ a, mep. wo mpreŋ, if you want to make sport or game or a fool of me, I shall just shake you! - 2. pusuw wo anom, wash your mouth (before or after eating) by shaking water in it! - Cf. posow, wosow. - o-pusúw, inf.: asase p., earthquake; cf. opusuo.
F. cork.

a certain food; aduaŋ bi, wəde e-pútu, a hut for bi a wəde dé sie wəde nnua na afei wəde dé no wəde akobaŋ p. 1261. - F. Isa. 57, 20; Jude 13; p. anu violence. Ps. 27, scil. the cud fro

a hut for storing yam in; asese bi a wode de siem'; wosi no se odaŋ, wode nuuaa na ede wurawuram', na afei wode de no abay mu; wotu ode wode akobaŋ putum'. pr. 213. 326. 1261. — F. (pl. m-), a yam fence.

a sudden or unexpected occurrence; surprise; eboo woŋ putupüru, it came on them unexpectedly = mpofirim; oguaŋ na abekå aseaa nè aduaŋ no ahwe ase p. so; - bo putu = bo twi, to be alarmed ec., s. twi 3. - adv. suddenly, at once.
the sound of drumming. pr. 1938.
struggling, forcible and violent efforts, as of a captured bird; wuyi anömaa a, oye p. = kìtikiti(kiti); wuse: opere.

[red. pupuw] 1. to throw out; p. ahuru = fi aburu, to form, gather or throw out spume or foam, to foam, froth; nsu a esey bebree no puw ahuru; to eject or throw out from the mouth, to spit, spew; ópùw nsu ana aduaŋ gu = oyi or ogyaa fi n'anom gu; yeŋé mmofra na yeadi ade a wopuw, 'we are not children that we should eat what has been spit out by others', i.e. a matter that has already been settled, must not be taken up again; yenni ade mpuw, 'we do not eat something and vomit it again', i.e. we are not able to pay it back. - to cast up. Isa. 57,20; puw gu, to foam out. Jude 13; p. anuodensem, to breathe out violence. Ps. 27,12. — 2. to throw up seil. the cud from the 2d stomach of ruminants to the mouth; puw wesaw, to chew the cud, to ruminate. — 3. to come up, come forth, appear; dua aba no ap. = apue; to come forth in a crowd: küromhofo nyinaa puw (= boaa woŋ ho ano) behwes no, or, kopuw ne ho hwes no, all the inhabitants flocked together to look at him; anäm-mono repuw nsoae no mn, living raw flesh appears in the rising (swelling). Lev. 13,10. — 4. to raise the surface of the ground; s. puduw 2. — 5. to bring forth; asase puw mmere, abürow, ode, Isa. 61,11. — 6. red. to stand out, project, be prominent: n'ani apu-puw, he has large eyes. Ps. 73,7. — 7. red. a) to cause to stand out, to thrust forth; opupuw n'ani kyere me, he seeks to frighten me, speaks roughly to me. Gen. 42,7.30. - b) to frighten. — 8. to puff, assume importance; to threaten; osuro woŋ puw a wopuw no (1 Pet. 3,14). — 9. p. wusiw (= puŋ wusiw), to smoke, i.e. to be angry. Ps. 80,5.
sediment, lees (Jer. 48,11), dregs, espec. of palm-wine; nsâ fufu ase poto-poto no; - remainder of any thing (?); cf. nnikae; asunsoŋpupuw.

m-, something thrown out from the mouth; yeŋyé kòsa-aŋkóméé na ye-adi ade apuw (cf. puw, v. 1), lit. we are not people who go to war and suffer hunger so that we must eat again what has fallen out of our mouths, i.e. we are not cowards. Cf. adi-apuw.
osu to p., s. osu.
[puw 2] ruminant, an animal which chews the cud.

(F. ada), is a particle of either particularizing or generalizing power, chiefly added to, or compounded with, pronouns, or following after verbs, often combined with other adverbs: 1. even, just; self, same; ever, -soever; this very...; cf. meara, woara, onoara, enoara (F. mada, wada, nada); yeŋ ara, moara, woŋ ara. Gr. § 59; shena-ara, oyiara, obiara; deŋ-ara, ebiara, biribiara; she-ara, shaara, sha ara. § 60. 61. 133,1; - beŋ-ara, yiara, noara, biara. § 74. 75; sesee-ara, mprempeŋ-ara; - enó ara ni or enó ara neŋ, that is all. — 2. even, just, merely, only.

[red. sesá] 1. to cut in or into, incise, make incisions; sa ŋkãmãà, to cut marks in one's body; woasa n'ani ase, he has a cut on his cheek. pr. 2843. — 2. sa..mu, to prick, pierce, lance; mesa ne pompom', I shall prick his boil; mesa ne mfã mu, I shall open his skin that the guinea-worm can come out. — 3. red. sesá, to scarify for cupping, to cup; mésesá me nãŋ, I shall have small incisions made into my foot so as to draw blood from it; cf. sũaŋ. — 4. to take or apply a clyster, to make an injection, to syringe; mekɔsá = mekɔbɔ bentoa, I am going to take a clyster; mekɔsa no = mekɔbɔ no bentoa, I shall give him a clyster. — 5. to geld, castrate, emasculate; woasa no sae, they have gelded him. — 6. to scrape (with the paw), to dig up, scrape out; ɔdemerefũa, wusie funu a, ɔde ne nsa sa (= funu) fám'; s. ɔsaa funu. pr. 1023; wosaa funu no kɔɔ K., the corpse was (exhumed) disinterred and carried to K. — 7. to dig out, take out; mekɔsa sika a (mede) mehyee, I am going to dig out money which I hid in the ground. — 8. sa abe, to pick or take out the palm-nuts from the pulpy substance formerly covering the shell and separated from it by smashing; in order that the pulp containing the oil may be boiled; s. ŋŋóyé. — 9. sa mu, to pick out, cull, select, to choose, elect more than one out of many things or persons; syn. paw mu; of one single thing selected, yi or tu must be used; wasa ɔde no mu nea eye nyinaa afa, he has picked out all the good yam for himself. pr. 3434. — 10. sa yare, to take away (cut off) or cure a disease, to cure, to heal; masa no yare; adúru ŋwèneŋwéne sà yáfúnum' yare. pr. 356. 394. — 11. sa..ano, to steel or harden iron tools; wósà abonua (adare, asow, ososow) ano, e.s. wode komã ɔtomfo na ɔye ano yiye bio. — 12. sa boa, m-, F. to mend a net. Mt. 4,21. Mk. 1,19; cf. sã 1. — 13. sa, F. to be partaker with, = bom'. Mt. 23,30.
v. Ak. s. saw, to draw, scoop. pr. 2729; s. asatoro.
v. Ak. F. = saw, to dance.
= saa, to mix, weave.

(subst.) dem. pron. (adv.) so, thus, (in) that manner or way, degree, quality or quantity; (in) such a manner, same way &c., equally, still so, always the same. pr. 68; without anything in addition: yede mpããnowa no kekãã yeŋ ano saa ara, we ate the biscuits without anything else. Cf. see, se. Gr. § 60, 5. 61 (ne saa nye; saa onipa yi) 133, 1 (ete sa, ete saara). - Saá nã eye, so it is right; wose sa, wòkà sa, so they say or speak, so the word is used; ewom' sa, s. ko 2; saa fã, half as much (Ex. 30, 23).

[red. sesã] general idea: to bring into, or be in, or aim at connection. 1. to tie together, bind, mend, repair, patch, cobble; sã me mpàboá mã me, mend my sandals for me; cf. sa 12. 2. to tie, fasten (a rope &c.); ode hama kosã dua kese bim' na ode asã dua tiatiaa a wasi no nso, s. sereŋ; ósã me, he ties me to a stick; cf. mantam; de aponkɔ sesã teaseenam, to harness horses to a carriage. 1 Sam. 6, 7; aponkɔ abieŋ sēsã teas, no ano, two horses are harnessed to that carriage. 3. to be tied or fastened somewhere. to hang down; hama bi sã or sēsã hó, the rope or runners of a climber is or are hanging down (from trees) or across; odopko sã hó, a swing is suspended there. 4. to stretch, be stretched; asu bi sã ho, a river runs along there. 5. red. sesã, to cast forth rays, to radiate. 6. to strain: sã ani, to fix one's eyes upon something, to regard attentively, observe closely: nea osã n'ani kakraa sê tumi hũ se eye asisi ara ŋkɔ, one who looks at it a little closely, can see that it is nothing but deceit; de n'ani sã dɔɔ, to stare or gaze; s. dɔɔ. 7. to be bent upon or directed to, to aim at; ani sã (s. ani B), to direct the intention or purpose to; to have in view; to have an evil eye upon or intention against; akokɔ ani sã bũrofua, the hen's eye 'points' at the grain; asafo ani sã akuraa, the troop have set their eye on (seek for) a plantation-village (to obtain food from). pr. 1652. 2754. obonsam ani sã Onyame mma, the devil aims at the children of God. 8. to run after; osã me = otaa me. 9. to hit, to enter and stick fast; bemma (or agyan) a otowe no akosã dua no mu, the arrow shot by him has struck the tree and sticks fast in it; otow agyan sã no, ósã no bén, he shoots him with an arrow. pr. 1473. wanõ bore asã ne hō, he has boiled poison to his own hurt. 10. s. red. sesã, to change, exchange. 11. sã so, to be connected, uninterrupted, to follow in a train. K. § 244.

[G. tã] to end, come to an end, pass away, die away; to be spent or consumed; perf. to be at an end, to be ended, finished, past; me taa resã ŋkakra-ŋkakra, my tobacco is gradually diminishing, coming to an end; me ntrama nyinaa asã, minní bi bio; dabi, ensãe e, ebi wò wo adakam'; all my cowries are spent, I have no more; no, they are not (all) spent, there are some in your box. pr. 3371. wotɔŋ wo tu' a, me nè wo bedi na asã (from a song), if you sell your gun, you and I will eat it up, i.e. we will spend the money in feasting; pr. 689. 812. 821. 986. 2638. 2874. 3371. asem asã, the matter is over or finished; now it is enough! stop it! ne nyansã asã ne tirim, he is at his wit's end. Ps. 107, 27; tr. to cause to cease. pr. 2795. ekuru sã = wu, the wound heals. pr. 1857; ne yare asã (better: ne yare agyae, ne hō agyae = ne hō aye no deŋ bio; cf. ne hō asaŋ), he has recovered. Phr. adé sã [G. dše na], things come to an end, i.e. the day closes, evening draws near, it grows dark; ade resã, it draws towards evening; ade asã,
the day is spent, the night is at hand or has set in, it is night; ade besã yeŋ, it will be night (before we arrive somewhere, finish our work &c.); cf. anim A. pr. 458. 810. 3058.
pl. a-, a path cut through the bush, okwaŋ ketewa bi a ɛda wuram', abommofo kwaŋ; twa sa (pl. twitwa asa), to cut a path; twa obi sa, to give some one a hint = yi asitiw.

[G. ta] war; (pl.) osá bèbree, (many) wars. Gr. § 44, 2; ko or tu sa, to go to war, make war, take the field. pr. 196. 2438. 2730 f.; wotu no so sa, they make war upon or wage war against him; ye or ñoa sa, to prepare for war. pr. 2469; kyere sa or sa-bone, s. kyere 7. 1 Sam. 20, 7. 9. 33; gye .. sa, to engage allies, s. gye 7; gu-yeŋ sá = mã yeŋ asáde, a) give us our share of the booty! b) make up for our expenses!

adv. then, again; else, besides; but; therefore; ɛdɛŋ' ásá? what then? ɛdɛŋ na wchwehwe asa? asa wohwehwe deŋ? what else do you seek? asa ɛhɛ na worekɔ na woboaboa wo hɔ? but where will you go seeing (or since) you are preparing yourself? ásá woykɔ? therefore you don't go?
Ak. s. asaw.
inf. [sa 4] making an injection.
the largest room in a native house; drawing-room, assembly-room; salon;
loom = asadua.
warp in weaving, the threads which are extended lengthwise in the loom and crossed by the woof; cf. dwese, mfa.

[con. ne nsá] 1. hand. pr. 2733 ff.; finger(s); cf. nsateaa; arm, cf. basa; forefoot of quadrupeds, cf. naŋ; - obo ne nsam', he claps his hands, smites the palm of the hand; (sc. ade), property. pr. 402. - nsá-akyi, the back of the hand; - ɔde ne nsa aso adwumayɛ mu, he has put (his) hand to work; ɔyarefo pe ɔkɔmfo nsa, a sick person seeks the help of the fetish-man. - 2. hand, index or pointer of a dial, watch or clock. - 3. handle of a jug or similar vessel; - axle-tree. 1 Kg. 7, 32 f. - 4. branch (of a climber); cf. basa. - 5. otúo-nsa, a) the spring of a gunlock; b) the lock of a gun. pr. 257. - Phr. nsa kã, (lit. the hand touches,) to receive, obtain, attain; to reach; me nsa akã ŋhoma, I have received a letter; wo ŋhoma no akã me nsa, your letter has come to hand. pr. 1484; ne ɔhwehwee no, ne nsa akã, he has obtained what he desired, or, attained what he sought for; mahũ mmepɔw yi, na minim sɛ me nsa akã me kũrow, having seen these mountains, I know that I have reached my home; cf. kã 28. - ne nsa hyia ne hɔ, what he earns with his hand suffices (is sufficient) for his wants. - ne nsa hyia ɔmaŋ no so, lit. his hands meet over, i.e. he is able to manage the people, (to keep them in due subjection,) to rule the country. - ɔmaŋ annyɛ ɔhene hɔodeŋfo a, ne nsa ŋkora woŋ, if the king is not a strong ruler, he is not able to manage his people. - nsa ko n'akyi, to menstruate (for the first time). - ne nsa nná, lit. his hand does not rest, lie idle or sleep, i.e. a) he is busy, active; b) he is bustling, not quiet; c) he is industrious, diligent = ɔyɛ nsì, ɔyɛ ɔdeyɔfo. - ne nsa apa, his hand has left off holding, i.e. he has desisted (from doing something), he has grown tired, given up in despair; syn. wapa abaw. - ne nsa kɔpaa no hɔ, he hurt him unintentionally, by inadvertence; s. pa 3 & sãkwaŋ. - me nsa nséŋ woŋ hwenem', they are too high for me, I cannot reproach them. - ne nsa si fam': wɔa-mã ne nsa asi fam', they have caused him a great loss; ɔde ne nsa si fam', ohyira ɔhene, he curses the king's life. - ne nsa sɔ, lit. his hand reaches, is (strong) enough, i.e. he is able for, ɔbetumi. pr. 2373; ne nsa sɔ.. so, his means suffice for (buying &c.), he can afford or is able (to buy &c.). Lev. 5, 7. - ne nsa bo, ne nsa sɔŋ', ne nsa tɛs, he is a marksman. - ne nsam' tɛe, he is open-handed, ne nsam' tɛe, he is bountiful, munificent; me nsa wom', s. 1. nsa yɛ deŋ, he is lent. pr. 2736; 1. is illiberal, ne nsa 2740. - ne nsa yɛ too ready to flog, is well off. - 1. dwow, his hand, i.e. he is docile, cf. wapa abaw, n or odaŋ'nàŋ ne n 'ne nsam', a) = 1. slack in working, to give in charge, care; to surrender, hye.. nsam' ade, pr. 573. - ɔbo ne he snaps his fingers, pressive ager nsa ano, á ne his hands &c., s. to 27. - ɔwɔ me power; he is in my charge,) I take him. - ɔwɔ ne biribi = ɔwɔ sika nsam' ye duru, s. nsa, a) he withdraws is at his meal, 1. me nsa maba mpi.
n-, three; cpd. § 77.

pl. a-, (F. n-), larva; ɔsã a ɔŋw nsã, strong drink, s. nsãfúfu, palm-wine. 46. 2761; mmorɔsã: merekeri nsãfúfu, ahai, ate mmorɔsã: merekeri kobi, kumpraka; wĩn a.s. bobesã; n nyĩnyã, asìŋ, mfĩ boro nsã, to be into - ɛbebow wo nsã Tshi-English Dict.
he is a sharp-shooter, a good marksman.
he is open-handed, liberal towards us.
he is liberal, generous, bountiful, munificent, open-handed.
s. to, to meet (with).
he is rigorous, severe, violent. pr. 2736; he is not generous, he is illiberal, near, close, miserly. pr. 2740.
he is too ready to flog.
he is well off.
his hands have become slack, i. e. he is discouraged, disheartened, cf. wapa abaw, n'abasam' atu.

twi: ɔdaŋ' or ɔdan'aŋ ne nsa, s. daŋ'
eng: ogow ne nsam', a) ne nsam' tɛɛ; b) he is slack in working.
to give in charge of, commit to one's care; to surrender, deliver (up).
to satisfy by giving. pr. 573.

twi: ɔbɔ or ɔhwe ne nsa ano
eng: he snaps his fingers, a gesture expressive of eager desire.

twi: omũa ne nsa ano, ɔkã ne nsa mũa ano
eng: he folds his hands &c., s. mũa.
s. to 27.
he is in my power; he is in my charge (given in my charge), I take care of, look after, him.

twi: ɔwɔ ne nsam', ne nsam' wɔ biribi
eng: ɔwɔ sika, he is wealthy, opulent, in good circumstances.
s. duru 5.
a) he withdraws his hand; b) he is at his meal, he is eating; mekoyi me nsa maba mprempreŋ ara.
n-, three; cpd. abissã, mmiensã. Gr. § 77.
pl. a-, (F. n-), caterpillar. pr. 2732; larva; ɔsã a ɔŋworow ne hō ɛ.

strong drink, intoxicating liquor; s. nsãfũfu, palm-wine. pr. 65. 287. 2742-46. 2761; cf. mmósã, mpahyewa, beŋano, mfrásã; - nsã ahorow pii wɔ hɔ: nsãfũfu, ahai, atokosã, kubesã; beso; mmorɔsã: mereken, gyiŋ (G. aolende), kobi, kumpraka; pótɔrɔ, brɔfo-ahai; wiŋ a.s. bobesã; nsãkawee (nsã nyinyã nyinyã, asiŋ, mfinigyer). - bow, bo, boro nsã, to be intoxicated with liquor; - ɛbɛbow wo nsã wo asɔm', it will offend your ears; - gu nsã, s. gu 23. - aberante no asi ababaa no ti nsã, the young man has brought the palm-wine for his betrothal or affiance to that young woman; cf. si 38; - nsã ato no atɔ-pam, s. to 26. - Phr. nea mekãe no, misee [or mase] saa a, eye nsã, I recall, recant, revoke, take back what I have said. - interest; sika a ɔde fem me no, ogye me ɛhō nsã ɔha so anum (5%) on the money he lent me; cf. mfemtom'; sika a ɛhō nni nsu ɛhō nni nsã, money lent out without interest. - contribution.
[ɛsã, three]: Opóku A., Op. the third.

adv. first, at first; in the mean (time), meantime, meanwhile; trã ha ansã, stay here in the mean time! - ansá-nà, before, usually followed by the consec. or imp.; wobskyerew eyi mã ansá-na woagyae? will you write this full before you leave off? to mfensre mu ansá-na esũm nnuru, shut the windows before it gets dark! pr. 390. 1195. Gr. § 266, 1. - na .. ansã, till, until; tɔ wo bo ase na (or mã) meŋkyerew me ŋhoma ansã (na me nè wo ŋkasa), have patience till I have written my letter [then I shall speak with you]. Gr. § 266, 2.
saá ara, s. sa.
F.: wɔ saa = di nokoro, to agree. Mt. 18, 19.

v., red. saasaa (mu), to mix; to be mixed; to weave in different colours; syn. fra, frafra; - nsãfũfu no asaa = wode nnera nsã afra nne de mu amã ne nyinaa aye de; ɔde nsã-bone nè nsã-pa asaa saa mu; mmorɔsã sàasaa nsã-pã mù; ɔsaá ne ntama = ɔde bibiri nè hoa nè asawa fufu frafra (saásàa mu) ŋwene ne ntama; cf. nsaasaa.
F. = saw. - asaa, inf. dancing, dance.
v.: to dwom (de) saa.., to mock or ridicule by satirical songs; cf. nsaadwom.

palm-wine. Three weeks after felling the palm-tree and lopping its branches a hole is cut in the trunk to the core, from which the gathering sap runs through a reed into a small pot which is emptied every morning and afternoon, and the opening is each time cleaned and made fresh by cutting and burning. The palm-wine continues to flow out for about six weeks and is called by different names, according to the different qualities it assumes during this time: 1) wokokã no gya a edi kan a, na n'adekyee no na worekoyi ntétéasã a.s. nsúsã; 2) ebeye se ne nnannum so na wokofa ntúŋkúm, ntunkuntíri; 3) na ebeye ne nnaawotwe de-reko dadu-nnannum na adan nsãpá, odómono; 4) na ede-reko sram nè fã a, na adan kókúró (àmpon). There are, according to the belief of the heathen Negroes, three different kinds of departed spirits: a) those who fell in battle (or by an accident, such as by a falling tree); b) common spirits; c) lingering spirits. The last are not admitted to the world of spirits, where the others are, but hover about behind the dwellings; - the spirits of those who were killed do not associate with the common spirits; they walk about, rubbed with white clay and in white garments; they are not afraid, whilst the common spirits flee when they see a man, and do not wish even to be seen.

In negro Mythology it is said: In the realm of the dead there are kings as well as subjects (slaves). If you were sick in this world for a long time, you will be restored to health there after three years; but one who died in battle or by accident will be well again in a short time, perhaps in a month or so. It is said: the realm of the dead is below (in the earth); some say: it is above (in heaven); about this there is no surety. Where one is taken to, when he dies, there his spirit is; when you die and they take you to the spirits' grove, there your spirit is in the grove. The town (or country) of the departed spirits is not in the grove, but in the earth; it is a large town (city), a long way off, and in going there a mountain has to be ascended. The way of one who died a common death is dark in heaven; but if one who died in battle or by accident takes that way, some of the white clay, with which he is rubbed, drops down, therefore his way (the milky way) appears white. - In the spirits' grove the departed spirits do not stay always; only on certain single days they come and assemble there for drinking or eating or playing.

1. to fail, be wanting or lacking, be cut off, cease to present itself; - ohia nsàrè da, poverty never becomes extinct, always sticks to one destined to be poor; adwúmayé n'sàre = ensã da, work is never wanting, is never out of reach, never fails to present itself, after every hindrance we can yet find opportunity to do our work (only lazy people excuse themselves: I have tried it 3, 4 times, it is of no use); - bere nsare ɛ, it is not yet so very late; wogu so de kã ara mã odasu saree, they went on talking into the dead of night; àsàre, it is too late, the time is over. - 2. to be prevented, intercepted and stopped. - 3. to prevent, intercept and stop, hinder, thwart: oyare nti m'adwuma asare me or oyare asare m'adwuma, sickness has prevented me from working, put a stop to my work; aduannõa nti afumkɔ asare me, on account of cooking I have not been able to go to the plantation; ade no, ésàre me afumkɔ, that prevents me from going to the farm; mésàre-wo nná, I keep you from sleeping. - 4. to forbear, refuse, decline: akoa sare asukɔ, the slave has ceased to go for water now, having attained or assumed a condition in which he deems himself above it or too good for it. pr. 1627. - 5. to forbear, abstain from: wòsàre nná, they forbear sleeping, do not sleep, keep awake; m'ani asàre dwé, lit. my eyes have withholden mucus (s. dwe), sleep has been withheld (has departed) from my eyes. Gen. 31,40.

sere, esére, 1. [F. ehono] a long grass, used for thatching. pr. 1048. - 2. [F. sare] also sare mu, sareso, Ak. serem', serem', sereso, sere-so, a plain covered with grass, as that between the sea, the lower Volta, and the Akuapem mountains, or that in the north of Asante; savanna, prairie, steppe, heath, wilderness, desert. - sàre päradaa, päradadada, perededede, tãtrãã, an extensive open plain, mostly destitute of trees and covered with grass.
[ade a esare adwuma] hindrance, impediment, obstacle in working; asem ketewa ba na woaŋhwe anni ntem a, edan' s. pr. 370.
used espec. of the steppes or grassy plains in the north of Asante.
the atrocious king of the steppe or wilderness, i.e. the lion, s. gyata & osse.

1. [asase obonsam? As. kàsampẽre] an imaginary monstrous being, conceived as having a huge body of human shape, but of a red colour and with very long hair, living in the deepest recess of the forest, where an immense silk-cotton tree is his abode; inimical to man, especially to the priests, (osẽsẽ nnipa nnompe nè ade; woko wuram' na o-kyere wo a, na wafa wo nnompe), but the friend and chief of the sorcerers and witches. pr. 2782f. Isa. 13, 21. - 2. [sésá mu bonsam] a human spirit which on account of its quarrelsome disposition had to leave the asaman and is now living in the depths of the forest; onipa a wawu na n'asem ye deŋ no, na wadwu na okotrã wu-ram' akyirikyiri; "woŋká dõdo, they are not very common". - 3. a kind of bat? aboa a otu se ohã; okyere'nnipa.

beings under the earth. Phil. 2, 10.

pl. nsáwansiafó, a child with six fingers; the sixth finger may consist only of a very small globular excrescence at the little finger, yet having a nail; such children are held in abomination by the heathen negroes and are usually killed immediately after birth; s. nsã-nsia, asìafo.
a place where water is drawn.

striae on the abdomen of pregnant women.

a certain bark used for tanning leather.

a braid of hair; the dressing of one's hair after a certain fashion ('I don't-care-fashion').
insolent, impertinent behaviour.
the palm of the hand; de nsa to ns., to put one hand on the back of the other. Cf. nsa, yam', nsam', nsákyì.
osaŋoa, inf. mobilisation.
easiness of curing or healing; enni as., it is incurable. Jer. 30, 12.
v. Ak. to crack (open); syn. sa; ósè. adwé, kube, e. s. ade bo a, s. dua bi bɔ adwe a, s. kube-aba no so na oyi mu aduaŋ; kokosi de, wòbo.

v. [red. sesè, sesèe] 1. to equal, be equal, to be the same in quantity or degree. pr. 63; òse no ahɔɔdéy, he equals him in strength. Gr. § 235, c. [G. ye egbo]. - 2. to be or look like, to be similar, to resemble; neg. to be unlike, of a different kind &c.; òse n'agya, he is like his father; òse no, òné no se, wòsesɛ wɔŋ hɔ, wòsese, wòsesse, they are like each other; wòse diŋ nà wonsé hōnam, their names are alike or similar, but not their bodies. pr. 1545; ne nipadua ye ase oyi, in (bodily) appearance he is rather like that one; òsè n'agya = owiewie n'agya: se ebia òréyè ade bi a n'agya ye a, na wose: òsè n'agya = e. s. ónsé n'agyà pɛɛpɛe, na oyé akòsé nò. - 3. to be fit, proper, becoming, rightful, right, just, equitable, fair; to be due to, to be deserving, meriting, worthy of; to become, behove; to be meet, due, seemly, befitting, behoving, incumbent on; cf. fata, di; èse wo se wunyà akatua pa, you have deserved a reward; owu se no or òse owu, he is worthy of death. pr. 2215. [G. sa]. - èse (nó) sê òkó, he must go; cf. twa 36. Mt. 16, 21. 17, 10. Lk. 2, 49. - èse wo ani, it is beyond description. - 4. to concern, touch: èse wo ara! that is your concern, is in your hands, is your own fault, you have to answer for it. - 5. se só, to be alike (cf. bɔ so, to be of like dimensions, to be equal); èse só = èse pé, edi 'nse; - wòsè só nàm, they walk together, go side by side (by the side of each other); wofi adi a, wòse só, when they go out, they walk side by side. - mã .. se so pe, to accommodate.
inf. equality, similarity, fitness &c.; ne se a ònse, his unworthiness.
v. Ak. = sɛw, q. v.

conj. [fr. se, to be like] as, like, denoting a similarity in manner or degree; ebere sɛ mogya, it is as red as blood. pr. 293. 471. 1182. 1312ff. - as (much as). pr. 3666. - as if, as though; how, as far as, just as &c. as (much as). pr. 3666. - as if, as though; how, as far as, just as &c. Gr. § 141, 2. 10. § 255, 1 c. d. 5. 268-271. - da sɛ nné, a week to-day (prop. the day that is like to-day). pr. 696ff. Gr. § 248, 6; ete sɛ, it is as though, it appears as if. pr. 1104; cf. senea, sê. - sé éte ni or neŋ, ne no, so it is; se woye no ni, it is made like this - this is the pr. 2800f.

conj. [fr. se, to say. F. de; G. ake] 1. that (introducing a noun-sentence that supplies the subject or object or other complement of a preceding verb); whether, if (when the accessory sent. is interrogative); nea ɔkä no ase ne sɛ, ɔreŋkɔ, the meaning of what he says is, that he will not go; etwa se ɔkɔ, it is necessary that he goes = his going is a necessity, he must go; metee se ɔresü, I heard that he was screaming = I heard his screaming, I heard him cry; kohwe se waba (ana), go and look if he has come. pr. 2323. 2343ff. Gr. § 255, 1b. 2. 3b. 4. 6b. 265, 2. 273, 2. — 2. se, Ak., se AKP., is often used to introduce the words spoken = saying, also to introduce an explanation = namely, videlicet (viz.), or as a mere mark of quotation. Mt. 21, 13. 15 f. 26, 61. Lk. 7, 8. pr. 189. 192. 205 f. 323-26. 2367. — 3. so that (introducing an adverbial sent. of manner or extent; Gr. § 273, 1b). — 4. that, in order that (he might &c.) or to, in order to (introducing an adverbial sentence of purpose. Gr. § 279, 1); mabo obi paa sɛ ɔnnyigyè me bá, I have hired a person to nurse my child; otuu no fo sɛ ɔnye papa, he exhorted him to behave well; ogyigyee no sɛ ɔnye bone, he seduced him to do evil. — 5. if (being put at the head of an adv. sentence of condition or concession. Gr. § 276, 3. 278, 2); sɛ ete saa a, aŋkä eye, if it were so, it would be well. pr. 2603. 2624f. Whenever sɛ stands at the head of a sentence, sometimes in an interrogative way, as in Mk. 9, 11. 28, some ellipsis has taken place, e.g. [eba] sɛ wokɔ a, befre me = if or when [it comes or happens that] you go, call me; [ɔkä] sɛ ɔmma a, mehye no na waba, if [he says that] he is not coming, I will compel him to do so. — 6. because (standing at the head of an adv. sent. of cause, or connected with efi or esïane with Tshi-English Dict. nti or ntia at the end of the sent. Gr. § 275, 1. 2, 248, 5. Mat. 16, 7. — 7. sɛ, (sɛ gye), gye sɛ, except, but; anihaw mu nni biribi sɛ ohia. pr. 2315; onni biribiara sɛ dua aba ŋkɔ, he eats nothing but fruit. Gr. § 277. 235b. — 8. sɛ, anase, or, e.g. in disjunctive questions, s. ana (Gr. § 253, 2). — 9. sɛ ebiá, as for example.

adv. 1. thus, so = se eyi, sɛé, sa; ebinom rebom' see, na afoforo rebom' sɛ, some were shouting one thing, and some another. Acts 19, 32; ogyee me apensä sɛ, s. apensä. — sɛé, for instance; ade bɛŋ na eyɛ hü? owú sɛé, what excites fear (or, what is frightful)? death, for instance. — 2. sɛ, very; otu 'mirika sê, he runs very fast; ɔye koküroo sɛ, he is very tall; aka kakraa sɛ na woawie wo adwuma ye, there is very little wanting before (or till) you have finished your work. — 3. about (before numerals): wobsye sɛ du, they will be about ten; mato ŋko kɔ beye sɛ aduonu, I have bought about twenty fowls.

v. [red. sise], Ak. F. se, 1. to say; to tell; to command; cf. kä (pr. 1492), kasa, bɛ 78-82. — se no yiye, say it right; wanse biribi, he said nothing; osèe sa, so he said; kose no sɛ ɔmmëra, go and tell him he must come; òsè (often instead of osee; Ak, osee) ɔbɛba mprem-preŋ. pr. 30. 54. 95 ff. 323 ff. 403-19. 575 f. 1717 ff. 2803-26; mise saa a, minsé sa, I retract my word(s), I retant &c., cf. nsä & otuo; ade yi nsé hwee, this is worth nothing, is good for nothing; sho awow de, minsé wo sa, the cold of that place is excessive. — 2. to mention, speak of. pr. 982. — 3. to say within oneself, to purpose, intend, design. pr. 35. 94. 2825.

after a previous v. se, kä, frɛ, bisa, bua &c., introducing the words spoken, Ak. se, F. de, or rather sê, dê = saying, is often not to be translated, and serves as a mere quotation mark; s. se, sê 2.
v. Ak. = sew.
v. [red. sēsẽ] 1. to hang or gird round

or about; to wear about one's body, ŋkrante, odonno &c. pr. 1226. 1283. 2827; cf. sĩane. — 2. to bear, (carry) something hung up; e.g. ɔfasu se ŋkotoku, 'the wall bears bags'; bags are hanging on the wall. pr. 328; - to carry something heavy. pr. 1389. 2828. — 3. to follow in a train or procession; to stick or cleave to.

Akp, a mass of clay in a roundish elevated form, a small pillar; a platform; dɔte bi a wode ahɔre hɔ na woaboro so a, s. wode aye biribiara (ebia woaye se wotra so oo, se wogyina so oo); dɔte bi a wode musuyide bi ahye ase. Syn. sũmpí.
inf. a saying, utterance, remark, word. pr. 2802; ɔde ose yɛɛ ɔyo, he carried out his intention(s).

a shout, loud burst of voices, vehement and sudden outcry of a multitude, expressing joy, triumph, exultation, animated courage, or exhortation; war-song, war-cry; dom no nyinaa bɔɔ se = wohuroe (huro is also said of a single person); wobɔɔ no se, they gave him a shout.
father; Ak. the father of another person, not of the speaker himself; cf. agya. pr. 7. 2106.
con. m'ásé, pl. asénom, the wife's or husband's father, father-in-law. pr. 690. 2823. 2835; cf. ɔsew, ɔsewa.

Ak, ase. 1. The lower or nether part, end or beginning (opp. ɛso, ɔsoro, the upper part or end; cf. ano, the fore or upper end, to, the hinder part); bɛpow ase, the foot of a mountain; ɛsɛ ase, the gum; - s. bewase, the way down; s. 6. 11. - 3. (adv.) down; s. 6. 11. - below, beneath, downward; (prep.) under, beneath; at; - of time: in, at, under, during. - 4. The place or time of, cf. ayiase, mmofraase. - 5. The end: me nɛ wo bɛpaa so akosi ase, we both shall go on to the end. pr. 2392; nea nɛ kwáŋ ase akosi ne ha, here his way ends. - 6. asěrene, a mat used instead of a door, being fastened above and rolled down, pr. 2910; a door or shutter made of thin slips of (the bark of) palm-branches tied together with strings (mfiriwa); cf. berapae.
[serew, asem] joke, jest, witticism; fun; cf. asɛŋkwaa.

red. v. sěre, to beg (much, constantly), to mendicate, to ask alms, going from one door to another; s. hũa; onipa a ɔs. nneema, wofre no hũafo. - asěresěré, inf. begging; ɔde as, ara na ɛkoduu hɔ, he begged his way thither.
pl. a-, a beggar. John 9,8.
one ingratiating himself by friendliness, but stealing or secretly doing other mischief; onipa okontomponi, atiko-yisá-anim'ŋkyéne, cf. atiko & ŋkyene.
aserede. ɔ-sereséréfo, pl. a-, laugher, pr. 2911.
aseresem.
red. v., s. serew.
[Eng.] a slate.
bɔ s., to smile.

[red. sereserew] to laugh, smile. pr. 127. 191. 2830. 2852. - tr. to laugh at, deride, mock. pr. 332. 2199. 3564. - ɔ(sere)-serew n'ano, he smiles. - poŋ so serew, s. poŋ 11. - sere(w), inf.: oto ne hɔ sére(w) or séré(w), he exposes himself to laughter. pr. 3312.
cowries = ntrama; di s., to use cowries as coin; woatew ne ti s., they have sold him; cf. tew 13. - recently also: serewá, pl. n-, a cowry; s. biakɔ, one cowry; ns. anum, five cowries.
playing for cowries.
a player for cowries.
a small bird. pr. 2912.
drollish, funnily, laughably; akyekyere kɔ s., the tortoise moves in a droll manner. pr. 1912.

sa; to scarify, make small incisions in, so as to draw blood from the smaller vessels; to cup; to bleed; mes. me naŋ. pr. 2913; wos. woŋ ano, they make incisions in the corners of the mouth (for embellishment).
red. sésàsèsa.
= sesaw; cf. saw, v.

(1. to mend, 2. to tie, 3. to hang, 4. to stretch &c.) 5. to radiate: ɔwia sesá m'ani so, the sun-beams strike upon my eyes (cf. sã 9: ɔtow bemma sã me); ɔwia sesá a esesá sika the reflection of the sun upon the golden city was extremely glorious.

= sakra, to change, commute, be changed or altered; ne nné as., his voice has changed, he has (got) a hoarse voice; ɔdoŋ no nné as., the clock no longer sounds well; enné a esésã, a trembling voice; n'anim as., her face has changed, e.g. on account of a guilty conscience. - 2. = sene, to exchange, give or receive in exchange, pr. 157; to interchange; to barter, truck; sesã dare yi mã me, change me this dollar! mepe dare (gold-dust &c.), I wish to exchange cowries or gold-dust for dollars, I wish to obtain dollars in exchange for cowries (gold-dust &c.); cf. nsesã. - 3. to redeem. Ex. 13,13.
barter, exchange; di nsesã(-gua), to barter.

= osámáŋ, the spirit of a deceased person, supposed to work mischief on survivors (only if the corpse is burned, this can no more be done); n'àsésãfó rekùm no, his deceased relations are troubling or killing him. - 2. the effect or mischief wrought by a spirit (in this sense osámáŋ could not be used): meye wo s. = miwu a, meba mabɛye wo bone; ɔ(re)ye no s., he is inflicting some disease on him; s. akita no, ɛ.s. osámáŋ aye no bone; s. sesãyare. pr. 1808.
a species of black pepper, Piper nigrum; dua bi aba a ɛye yaw sɛ yisá; esow (wo) dutaŋ hɔ sɛ ɔdɔmá. Cf. sãwusa.
= kontomfi; ɔte sɛ onipa; tetefo se: asamanfo na ɛdaŋ saa aboa.
onipa nantu nè ne sère hoŋ na ɛhɔ baabi tu kuru na efi nsu daa, na daa nso ɛhoŋ; cf. ntaatâ.

twi: asesá-dé, a foolish, unwise, immoral thing, action or conduct;
eng: syn. asesasɛm.

twi: sesã-duá, a shrub attaining man's height, with a stinking sap, white flowers, and small round fruit; the root is used as a medicine against tooth-ache; s. sesã-yare.

eng: cf. sesã, nsensaŋee. Hab. 3,4.

twi: ɔ-sesafó, pl. a-, ɔ-sesaní, pl. a- -fo, a loose, dissolute, disorderly, wicked (Prov. 11,7), unreasonable (2 Thess. 3,2) person; rogue; a crazy, crackbrained, shatter-brained person; idiot, simpleton,

eng: disorderliness, ill conduct; immorality; n'as. nti wanseŋ adwuma no mu.
(trade of) barter, exchange, truck; s. nsɛsã.
nsɛsã.., merchandise. Ezek. 27,27.
adv. disorderly, out of order, deranged, confused; syn. basabasa; ɔkwaŋ no so yɛ s.; ayɛ n'ade s.; ɔnam s.; anim ayɛ s., it dawns, s. anim 7. A.
pl. = asesafó, loose men &c.
a disease inflicted by a departed spirit. Obi yare s. na wode sesãdua ahaban gu gyam' a, ɔsamaŋ bi ntumi mma ofie hɔ mfa ne nsa mmɛkã ɔyarefo no.

red. v. saw, 1. to take up a collective quantity from the ground, ŋwɛ̃a, sand, ŋwura, sweepings, ŋkyene, salt. pr. 322. 1941; sesaw .. kɔ, to sweep away. Jer. 8,13. — 2. to draw (nsu, water) repeatedly, to draw a great quantity. pr. 3197. — 3. to draw in folds; wasesaw sirikyi atade ahyɛhyɛ ne hɔ kusuu, he is gorgeously and pompously dressed in silk. — 4. mfã na esesaw no hwee hɔ, having a Guinea-worm, he is confined to bed.
shovel. Ex. 27,3.
Ak. red. v. se, = sise. pr. 2914.
subsistence = akwaŋhyede.
red. v. sē.
red. v. s. se, v., to be equal, right, straight; wòsese, or wòsese, they are equal, like each other. - ade a esesse, equity. Prov. 2,9; nea or nsɛm a esesse, right things. Prov. 8,6. 23,16.

sesɛ̃, seséɛ yi, seséɛ (= seséɛ yi) adv. [sɛ sɛɛ, liter. as thus] 1. = afri, mprempren, just now, till now, as yet, still: woye dɛŋ wɔ ha sesɛ? (when the word stands at the end, the ɛ is short), or, sesɛɛ woye dɛŋ wa ha? what are you doing here now? sesɛ woda so te kwaŋ mu? what, you are still on the way? - immediately, instantly: sesee na mereba; sesee de, wada; mprempren na mihũũ no, na seséɛ wàyɛra, I saw him just now, and he suddenly disappeared. — 2. sesɛɛ ebia: perhaps, probably, likely: s. wada, perhaps he is asleep; s. ɔkɔ, he is probably gone; s. wawu, he is likely to be dead.
adv. [sesee emph.] just now, this moment, instantly, immediately, in a trice, in a twinkling. — sesebére, seséé-bére: ɔkyɛna s., to-morrow about this time.
pl. a-, hut, cottage, small house. pr. 2915f; pavilion. 1 Kg. 20,12. 16; shed. Isa. 1,8. - bɔ ɔs. (pl. bobɔ asese), to make a hut &c. — s. asesewá; - ɔsese-kóro, a solitary, lonely hut.
feast of tabernacles. Lev. 23,34.
pl. a-, a certain tree; dua fitaa bi a wode seŋ akoŋŋua, wode pam poŋ n. a. (dua-pa sē); plane-tree. Isa. 41,19.
a noise produced e.g. by shaking a calabash containing pebbles, cowries or seeds of abürobia; wowosow mfũaa sésesese. - bɔ sése, to walk fast, quickly.
wɔ..s., to stitch (something) equally; to backstitch.
pl. n-, a round basket, plaited out of a species of reed (go), with a flat cover, wider at the bottom than at the top; cf. kentɛŋ, kyeréŋkyé.
ósẽsẽã, a certain tree; dua ketewa a wode yɛ mparowa. pr. 2917; cf. akurampoŋ.
F. rebuke, reproach. Ps. 39,11.
[s. abɛŋ] a kind of horn or wind instrument of music; abɛŋ a wode bɔ ɔhene mmraŋ na wode kã asɛm nso kyere no; mmɛŋ abieŋ a nnipa baanu hyɛŋ na wɔŋ nyinaa kã asɛm biakɔ pɛ.
ɔ-, inf. [sesew, foforo] reformation. Hist.
pl. a-, a stool made of ɔsɛse-wood.
adv. 1. perhaps, peradventure, perchance, by chance, possibly; likely; cf. ebia, sesee; mekɔ wo afuw mu a, s. bi menyã ogya matwa ana? when I go to your plantation, am I likely
a superficial or an uncertain, doubtful matter, a mere probability; n'asɛm nye s. = n'asɛm nye asɛm bi a wonnim no yiye.
a perfunctory, careless, negligent service; ɔsom no s. = ɔsom no mpaso-mpaso, ɔŋhwɛ so nsom no yiye.
[asɛm a wose] a mere saying, rumour, talk, hearsay; syn. atésɛm; asɛm no nyinaa ye as., na ŋkontompo wɔ mu; cf. ayésɛm.
red. v. sère, 1. to poll, shear, clip; ɔsesére ne ti sɔ, he polls his head. Ezek. 44,20. 2. to flutter (said of birds); cf. sère.

a word without any meaning, used to mark the end of a tale; yeŋ tipeŋ, se ebia yerebɔ səmɔde na yeŵie na yese: as., saa asɛm na yɛkohũi na as., that's what we saw, and now (we say) basta! (wontaa ŋkã no pii; womfá ŋko guam' bebrebe).
ebi-nè-bí.
gyigyà-gyigyà.

red. v. 1. s. sew. 2. to put or set in order, put or set to rights, reduce to order, restore: wosesɛw kũrow no (mu yiye), ɔmaŋ mu; ɔs. ne fi (ofie), syn. siesie, ye yiye. 3. sesew so = taa so, (Akan) te so, level, make level. 4. s. ntam', to restore peace and harmony between parties at variance; c. siesie 3.
red. v. 1. s. sew. 2. phr. ɔde n'anim s. fam', he disgraces him or himself.
[osese, dim.] a shed, covered with palm-leaves.
time of reformation. Heb. 9,10. ɔ-sesɛwfó, pl. a-, reformer.
v. n. [sesɛw] regulation(s), institutions; arrangement, adjustment, settlement, pacification.

[ade a ese so, biribi a ese] a thing having the same figure or quality as another: ntama yi s. wɔ hɔ, there is cloth of the same quality; wotɔŋ kuru-wa yi s. wɔ ŋkraŋ, other jugs of this kind are sold (or, may be bought) at Accra; né sèsó hene bi anni n'anim, such a king as he was had not been before him. 2 Kg. 23,25.
[s. before] likeness, similitude, analogy, comparison: ns, bɛŋ na yɛde besusuw (hɔ)? with what (comparison) shall we compare it?
F. an under-garment.
inf. [te or tie ose] obedience, submission to authority; ɔsete na eye = wòsè wo ná wutié à, na eyé; os. ye seŋ afɔre; cf. asɔ̃merew. - ye os., to be obedient, dutiful.
inf. understanding; cf. asehu, ntease, ŋbũmu.
diff. species of beans; s. asɛ.
inf. certainty. Prov. 22,21.
inf. s. to ase & ntoase.
inf. [to .. ase] neglect.

inf. [trã or te ase] 1. life, the course or time of life [= βιος, cf. ŋkwã = ζωη]; existence; condition or circumstances of life; manner of living, conduct, deportment; - ɔbaa as., he came to take up his permanent residence (anywhere). - 2. met. = asetrãde. Mk. 12, 44. Lk. 8,43. 15, 12, 21, 4. - asétrã-bére, time of life.
the means of life or subsistence, livelihood, living.
sekyedua, a bench made of poles by the wayside, the seat of the toll-gatherer.
inf. gnashing of teeth. Mt. 8, 12.
v. [red. sesew] to spread, spread out (kete, a mat, Mk. 11,7.8, ntama, a cloth); sèw kete means also to make the bed. pr. 249. 2930; sèw abo, to pave, e. s. wode abo tintim fam'.
v. [red. sesew] to sharpen, whet, grind any cutting tool. pr. 882; cf. serebo, hì.
mother-in-law, the husband's or wife's mother; cf. asé, ɔsewá. - F. asew, mother-in-law, daughter-in-law. Mt. 10, 35.
Ak. nsée, curse, malediction, imprecation, me ns., h.
adjuration. Prov. 29, 24.
F. = nsow, mark, note; hye nsew, to make secure. Mt. 27, 65 f.

(Ak.) aunt, the father's sister (m'agya ne nuabea); niece; female cousin: the father's sister's daughter (m'agya ne nuabea ba = me nà-kakrá bá); cf. wofasewa, ase, osew; - uncle (the father's brother). Jer. 32, 7. 8. (- sewaa, the uncle's son? Jer. 32, 12).
[asẽ, dim.] a small vesicle, scurf, scab: s. antì no = biribi ampira ne hõnam baabiara. - nsẽwá, the itch (with small vesicles).
lentils. Gen. 25, 34; cf. asedua.
s. mfowanini, ɔdehye 4.
Ak. nseee, v. n. [sew, v.] inlaid work, tessallated, checkered, mosaic work; abo ns., pavement.
the (very) picture or image of your father. pr. 127; cf. osé.
a certain company of warriors in Akem; cf. osé-awuo. pr. 3288.
inf.: wɔwɔ os. koko, they have the courage to carry out their word or promise; cf. əseadeɔyə.
duty; syn. asede.

[red. sisi]: 1. contin., to stand, be fixed in an upright position (chiefly of things that are placed; cf. gyina, of man and animals, taa of things extended more horizontally than vertically): dua bi si hɔ, a tree stands there; nnua pii sisi tūrom' hɔ, there are (or were) many trees in the garden; abrogua si hɔ, there stands a chair; tumpaŋ si poŋ so, a bottle is standing on the table; adaka si poŋ ase, a box is standing under the table; ɔhene daŋ si kūrow mfinimfini, the chief's house stands in the midst of the town; asrãfó no sisi hɔ kyerebeŋ, those soldiers stand in a straight line. - 2. to stick, to be stuck or fixed: ntakara si ne kyew akyi or ne kyɛw so, a feather is stuck in his hat; cf. hye. - 3. to sit, to perch: patu si duabasa so, an owl is perching on the twig; - to sit in state, in a stately manner (of a king): òsi hɔ kusuu, he is sitting in grave or solemn majesty; cf. te, trã, bum. - 4. caus., preceded by de, fa, kā, twẽ..., to put, place, set: fa agua no si hɔ, put the chair there! fa kanea no si poŋ so, put the light on the table! ode honi asi ne daŋ ano, he (has) placed an idol before his door; òde aduan sii n'anim, she put food before him. 1 Sam. 28, 22. 25; òtwẽe abofra no sii ne serem', he took the child between his knees; ade no sii wɔŋ so hene, or osii no wɔŋ so hene, he made him king over them; wòde no sii agua so, they placed him on the stool (throne); òde no sii asase no so. Gen. 41, 43; - de (asɛm or ɔkasa) si akyiri, s. akyiri. - 5. (also without a preceding verb) to put, place, set &c.: si baŋ, to place (plant, post) troops in a strong position, s. baŋ 4. - si àwɛnfo, F. to set a guard. Mt. 27, 66. - si awowa, F. ahoba, to give a pawn or pledge. - si nsore, s. nsore. - si adakaní or apratwõm, to fasten a lock. - 6. contin., followed by a numeral: to be, amount to: nnipa no si ahẽ? how many persons are there? wòsi dú, there are ten; (wosi bebree, better: wòye bebree = wòdɔsɔ); mmofra ahẽ na ɛwɔ hɔ? wosi anum pɛ, how many boys are there? there are but five. - 7. to rise, come up: a) to appear (of an elevation on the body): pompɔ asi me koko so, I have (got) a boil on my chest; - b) to grow well, flourish, thrive: dua no asi, the tree has become stately = ɛrenyiŋ yiye; kan no de na aŋkã erétò apẽ, na afei na asi yiye; - of persons: wasi so yiye; - abofra a wasi so, a grown-up child (aged 9-14 years); cf. frɔmm; - mmofra a wòasi so yi ye nsì, the rising generation is industrious; cf. before & 43.

to stand (together): woŋ nsã a worenom yi yenè woŋ na yɛbesi afram' mpreŋ, lit. their liquor which they are drinking, we shall stand with (or to) them and mingle in it (or, among them) at once, i.e. we will at once join, share or participate with them in their proceedings.
to step, set foot (into, upon): osii bonto mu, he entered into a boat. (pr. 263); osii ne kwaŋ so kɔe, or osiim' kɔe, he departed.
to step, in, interpose, mediate between contending parties.

to lead (of a way): woŋ kwaŋ nsi ha, their way does not lead them through this place; woŋ kwaŋ nsi kũrom' ha, their way does not lead (them) to this town; ne kwaŋ asi me mu, his way falls in with mine. pr. 134.

to descend, come or get down, light (down), alight (off, from, expr. by fi): ofi dua so si fam', he descends or gets down from a tree; ofi hyeŋ mu si fam', he disembarks; ofi ne pɔŋkɔ so si fam', he alights from his horse, dismounts.
to descend into, to strike: ɔprannaa sii duam', the lightning struck a tree; cf. duru.

to come down, set in: omunuŋkum resi, a fog is coming; ɔpɛ asi, the harmattan has set in; awia asi, a great heat or drought has come; awia si bebree a, ɛkyere ɔkɔm = ɛde kɔm ba, much drought brings famine.
so, to come down upon, take possession of: ɔbosom asi no so, the fetish has come upon him.
to turn out: asɛm no asi me yiye, the matter has turned out well for me; woye saa a, ɛrensi wo yiye ara da.

to stop, stand still, make a stand: n'ano asi = n'ano atɔ, he has finished his speech; ɛha na m'ano abesi, here my mouth has come to a stand, i.e. with this I have finished my speech; metrã mu makosi ase, I shall remain in it or endure unto the end. si often serves as an aux. v. for the prepp. to, unto, till, until, cf. Gr. § 117, 227, 2. 229; (de) besi, (de) kosi, cf. ɛfam & Mt. 1, 17. 25.
to push or knock against: efunu asi no or ne kãra, the corpse has pointed him out as the murderer, cf. afunsoa.
to strike with the head, push with the horns, to butt: aberekyi de ne mmeŋ asi no, the goat has butted him; mpapo si, the he-goats are butting each other; cf. 28.
m'agya wu a, ɔbesi me, when my father is dead, he (i.e. his spirit) will trouble me. pr. 2322.
to give shocks, to cause the convulsive motion of sobbing: osũ asi no, he sobs.
to stick (fast): aduan no asi me, the food sticks in my throat (ete sɛ me menewam' kwaŋ asiw); - to stifle, choke: asi me, my voice fails, ste sɛ biribi asiw me menewam' kwaŋ a mintumi meŋkasa bio.

to raise, erect, build: si daŋ, to build, esp. a house of sticks (cf. to abaŋ or fádáŋ, to build a stone-house or mud-house). pr. 2920f.; si ntamadaŋ, to pitch a tent; osii trãbea no, he reared up the tabernacle. Ex. 40, 18; wasi fi amã no; also with de (cf. 4): bɔrɔŋ yi so na mede me daŋ mesi.
to institute, set on foot, set in operation, make, arrange: si agoru, to commence a game; cf. tutu agoru; si kane, to arrange or set on foot a competition, to vie, contend, to do in competition.
to raise, lift up: si fraŋkaa, to hoist a flag; si abrannaa, to set a sail; cf. 43.
to cause to hang down: si mmɔhɔɔ, to hang a curtain; si adurade, to put on a robe or garment. pr. 1547. Ps. 35, 26.
to prepare or hang up a snare. pr. 520.
to wash clothes. pr. 1136; cf. horo.
to fill into bags or bundles: si ŋkyene, ɛmɔ, to tie loads of salt, rice; Ɔkwawufo si ɛmɔ no mmoaa (du a, s. ɔha) na wɔnam tɔŋ.
to plan beforehand in card-playing, cf. toa 7.
to strike one's (own) breast in an ostentatious, boastful, or bragging manner, i.e. to boast, to venture, undertake: wasi ne bo se ɔbekɔ nè no akɔkɔ, he undertakes to fight with him.

a) = si kwaŋ mu (cf. 9), to step into the way, i. e. to set out on a journey, to start, depart, gener. followed by kɔ: osiim' kɔe, he went off; s. sim'. b) to put in, i. e. to repeat: ɔkã sii mu, he said it repeatedly; cf. ti mu, kasa saŋ mu; c) to put in, i. e. to add, to give into the bargain: matɔ nãm mmaŋ du, na si me mú = tò me só! cf. nsimú.
hye anagmu, to put instead of, to repair, restitute, restore, compensate.

a) to push, put, join or fit the ends together: kã ntãboo yi si anim, fit these (two) boards together! fa apoŋ no si anim, push those (two) tables together! pr. 653. 766; ne sẽ kã si anim, his teeth are slightly clenched. b) to put, place or set before; s. 4. c) to charge with, upbraid with: mede masi wo anim: wo na woyɛe ade no, I have set it before your eyes, say it to your face, declare it plainly to you, charge you publicly with it, that you have done the deed. d) F. mframa asi woŋ anim = hyia woŋ, the wind is against them. Mk. 6, 48. e) to fight; syn. kɔ.
to stay up, sit up at night, over a game, attending a sick person &c.
to practise extortion; s. apempem.
to set or place the canes of the speakers in public assemblies, i. e. to transact or discuss a public or judicial matter; to credit slaves; s. poma.
to fix or tie a knot; cf. si nsemma, s. 24.

wasi ne ti nsã, he has placed palm-wine before the elders of his town, declaring that he now intends to marry a certain woman, i.e. he has declared his intention to marry her before the elders (in putting palm-wine before them).

to put down, make low: osi ne nné ase, he lowers his voice, speaks with a low voice; wutwa ŋkontompo a, wusi wo nné ase; osi n'aŋi or ne ti ase, he sinks his face or head, from shame, grief, modesty, humility, he casts down his eyes, droops or hangs his head, is dispirited or desponding, flags; cf. ase 11; wakoyɛ ɔhene nti wontumi ŋhye no denneŋ bi na woasi woŋ ti ase = wɔamuna te ho komm, because he has become king, they cannot, as it were, force him, but must contain themselves, restraining their indignation; ɔkwaŋ no si ne ti ase, the road is sloping = (quickly) &c., s. 7.
to hobble, limp, halt; s. sii.
to grow (quickly) &c., s. 7.
a) to promise a woman (in early childhood) in marriage; b) gye aware, s. gye 9.

a) to increase in growth, to grow fast, thrive: abofra &c., s. 7; to grow up in reputation: ɔhéne yi diŋ si so, this king has become renowned; b) ne home si so, his breath or his pulse is regular (beats in a proper way, in its due time, follows in regular succession); ensi so, it is irregular (the duration being shortened &c.); c) to fit, be suitable or appropriate: ensi kasa so, it does not fit, or agree with, the language (sɛnea ŋkũrofo no kã, as it is spoken by the people); to agree to. Acts 15, 15; sɛnea wakyere ase yi, ensisi so, his interpretation or explanation has no proper connexion, or, it is wrong; kã si so! say it out! (say what is wanting to complete the sense!) finish the sentence! d) to accompany (in continued & full activity): wɔreyɛ eyi no, na ŋkyene nè . mmɛŋ nè abubuw si so; cf. da mu. e) to add, repeat, in pouring liquor; to pour in addition: si (no) só! (e. s. woahye obi nsã na woasaŋ ahye no bio) serve him (with liquor) once more! f) wasi so dua = wahye mu deŋ, wamã atĩm; cf. hye 11. Col. 2, 2; si so dua hwe, lit. fix on it a stick, i. e. mark it and look (whether it will not come as I say) = depend upon it! you will see! g) si so, s. 15. h) to be built up. Ps. 89, 3. 5. i) to be hoisted (of a flag); cf. 23. pr. 2901. k) to last, remain, continue; syn.

Fanteni bi kāe sɛ: Sɛ abibifo se: onipa wu na ɔnsore a, asɛm no nnim', na yɛŋ ara yɛŋ kasa yi na skyerɛ sɛ ɔbesɛre ampa, eness yese: wòkosie no a, s. wòkokora no: nà ade a wokosie no, - gye sɛ wosaŋ kɔfa bio, na ɛŋka hɔ korakora. - wòde no sie funu, he is buried with the corpse of his master. pr. 1614. - 6. to put things in order (s. red.): me nè no sie a, ensɛŋ, 'if I and he arrange (things), there is no place for them', i. e. we cannot agree or live peaceably together. - 7. asie me yiye = asi me yiye, it has turned out well for me. - 8. sie is used as a supplemental or aux. v. for the adv. beforehand, previously: kā sie, to foretell; maká masie, I predicted it; I told of it beforehand; kasa sie, di sie, to arrange or settle beforehand. pr. 2885. - also for the prepp. for, against (an event); obi nnom nsu nsie ɔps. pr. 288; ɔbɔaboa abūrow ano sie ɔkɔmbere, he gathers corn against the (expected) time of scarcity; wónsiesie wɔŋ hō nsie nea ɛbɛba no, they shall prepare themselves for (or against) the things that are to come! mint; nea wogu sika.
