[si (kwaŋ) mu] to set out, start on a journey; sim' kɔ, to depart; sim' ntem kɔ, set off quickly! wuŋsim' ntem a, wunnú ntem, if you do not set out in time, you will not arrive in time; ahemadakyɛ na misiim' wə Dkraŋ, early in the morning I set out from Accra; s. si 31.
nsí-mú, inf. 1. what is given into the bargain when a large quantity of any thing is bought; besides nsim', an ntɔsó, Ak. ŋŋuso (q.v.), is given; cf. ŋkwányé. - 2. the stump of a tree. Job 14, 8.

[siŋ ba]† minute = miniti; aka s. dunnum na dɔŋkoro abɔ, it is a quarter to one; dɔŋkoro apa hɔ s. du, it is ten minutes past one; dɔŋkoro apa hɔ s. dunnum, it is a quarter past one. - simma-síŋ,† second.
pl. of simma [siŋ ba]: nnua ns., small pieces of wood. - wokã asɛm no ne-nsimma-nsimma mu, they relate the story in portions or sections; cf. mmobom' 2.
F. = asiamasi.
a certain cotton cloth made in Europe.
[the man who is responsible for the boats]: woye me S., you exact something impossible from me, you demand what is out of my power, you overtask me; you make a fool of me. [Simpã = Winnebah].
simpíní, Ak. = sūmpī, syn. ɛse.
F. a weight of gold-dust, equal to threepence; cf. pɔwa.
a tamarind.
pl. n-, 1. a pillar = odum; cf. nsim'. - 2. fig. = otitiriw.

pl. asigasiŋ, 1. remaining piece or part of any thing, fragment or remnant of a whole, stump; duasiŋ (ɛnyé dua-mū no, na ɛyɛ né siŋ); siŋ is not used of broken vessels (gyirase, ŋkora, ŋkuruwa, of which gow, fã or fɛre is used, except of the scattered pieces: woabɔ no asigasiŋ; n'asigasiŋ gu hɔ; ɔpoŋ no na ebui no, ne siŋ ni); but it is said of other things, e.g. hamasíŋ, and of fluids in a vessel: nsã ye tumpaŋ mã na wuhwie so bi a, nâ aka siŋ; ŋŋo a mehyɛɛ no mã kosii hɔ no so atə siŋ, the oil no longer fills the vessel as it did when I placed it there; - əsekansiŋ ye əsekaŋ a'nano ye siŋ; cf. dunsíŋ, nnyansíŋ;

básíŋ, hwénsíŋ, akónsíŋ, nánsíŋ, anosíŋ, asósíŋ; ɔmán-síŋ; - asem no siŋ ŋkɔ ni, this is only the half of the case or matter; - sika no, ɔmãa me asin-asig, he paid me the money by instalments (and has not yet paid all). - (twi)twa .. asinasig, to cut (in)to pieces. Ex. 29, 17; tetew .. as., to tear (in)to pieces. - 2. fathom, a measure of two yards or six feet of cloth, when bought from the European merchant, but of five feet only among the natives; ntamasig; matɔ ntama-síŋ asĩa, I have bought three yards of cloth. - 3. siŋ anim, the front line of an army where a sharp fight is going on & a number of soldiers have already fallen; - a place where a serious accident has happened.
[G. asíŋ, Ger. Essig] = mfinigyer, vinegar. Prov. 25, 20.
[red. sínásína] to perforate, pierce; to thread (a needle); to string, to file on a string (nãm, ŋwaw, ŋhene, meat, snails, beads &c.). pr. 443. 2881. 2899.
inf. s. bɔ 108.
= sēnãmeŋ.
-abá, -fua, mustard, mustard seed. Mt. 13, 31. Lk. 17, 6.
pl. of (e)siŋ. 1 Kg. 18, 23.
[Eng.] shingle(s); bɔ .. so s., to shingle.
a certain European cloth; s. ntama. [G. ogbale].

1. red. v. seŋ, to cut, carve; to cut off, peel (yam; a fruit, e. g. a pineapple, by cutting away its rind by small pieces); cf. wae, hũaŋ. - 2. to grow hard, stiff &c.; ne naŋ as., he is lame (in his feet). 2 Sam. 4, 4. - 3. o-sinséŋ, inf. cramp, convulsions.
red. v. síam.
red. v. síaŋ.
red. v., s. síane, 4-6 & botohuhuw.
[siw a ɛpɛ nt.] a small ant-hill. pr. 2965.
a large chair.
colon(:).

a. dizzy, giddy, confused; dull, torpid, insensible; - n. dizziness, dullness &c.; trembling; fearfulness, terror. Isa. 21, 4. - me hɔ ayɛ me s., me hōnam te sɛ ahonhoŋ, biribi bɔ me a, mentɛ, I am stunned, petrified, awestruck, horror-stricken, I shudder, I have become insensible, apathetic; cf. awɔsɛ, ayisɛ.
inf. dullness, heaviness, gloom, sadness; apathy.
a species of sea-fish, caught frequently in the month of August = oyáká.
s. síriŋ.
a certain charm, amulet.
Ky. = siw; siri nsuo no ano = siw or waw nsu no ano, dam the water up (in or out), obstruct the flow of the water!
[Eng.] silk; cf. sedaa.
better: sireŋ [Eng.] a shilling. F. sideri.
s. sipìripì.
semicolon.
red. v. to approach, draw near hesitatingly or reluctantly; ɛ. s. se obi reba wo ŋkyɛŋ na ontumi mma.
better: sesẽ, subsistence.
red. v. se, to say repeatedly, talk much of; mate sɛ wosisese sɛ wəbɛkɔ baabi.
inf. talk, sayings; rumour, report. pr. 1600 f.
[asem a wosiw so] a 'talk' (topic) or matter to be concealed from general knowledge, to be kept secret, a secret; enyɛ as., as. biara nni yeŋ sōm mu.

red. v. si: 1. s. si, 1.2 &c.; nnōmaa bebree sisi dua no so; kɔkɔsakyi s. sūmãnã so, pr. 1680, the vulture often perches on the dung-hill. - 2. sisí atwẽ, s. atwẽ. pr. 2968. - 3. to cheat, deceive, impose upon. pr. 12. 139. 154. 767. 2238; cf. gyigye, daadaa. - 4. Phr. otutu m'ano sisi, s. ano.
inf.; ye as., to be wont to butt. pr. 1060. Ex. 21, 29; to cheat.
inf. the act of cheating &c., deceit, imposture.
pl. id. [& a-] a bear; other names: sisi(e)-kwàbrafo, osisìrè, osisìmo, ɔto-
she-bear.
the constellation of the Bear. Job 38, 32.
the lower part of the back, from one thigh-bone to the other. pr. 2966 f.; syn. pã, pãm, pim; cf. akyi. Phr. so me sisí, support me, help me to pay a debt! sisi-akyi, backside.
the rump, end of the backbone of an animal, with the adjacent parts; the loins. Lev. 3, 4.

bower, arbour; a shelter in a thicket of trees and shrubs. pr. 1852; ɔdɔtɔ bi a ayɛ se ɔdaŋ a mmóa dả asé; mekɔ or mehyɛŋ s. ase. o-sisíám’, in the dense and dark bush; ahabaŋ mu a ɛhɔ ayɛ ɔdɔtɔ na ɛhɔ ayɛ sũm no.
s. siaw; phwireŋ sisiaw woŋ mu biara koko so, all of them wear flowers on the bosom [lit. flowers stick on..]; wode nnamrãm as. apakaŋ no hɔ; cf. damrãm.
a thing or things acquired by cheating or deceit, unlawful property.
medicine to cure pains or disease in the lower part of the back. pr. 367.
Ak., a bear.
a cheat, deceiver, impostor; syn. ɔdaadaafo, ogyigyefo.
arrangement, institution; cf. ŋhyehyɛe, nsisiei.
ntaboo-adum, boards (of the Israelites' tabernacle). Ex. 39, 33.

1. the calyx of the flower (of a pomegranate-tree). Ex. 25, 31. 2. setting (of jewels). Ex. 28, 20. nsisi-mú-adúm, pillars at the entrances of the Israelites' tabernacle and its court. Ex. 39, 33. 40, 18.
osísirè, s. sisi, bear.
mpieŋgo.
a tasteless, from want of salt & pepper; syn. wóo. numb, torpid, dull; me naŋ yɛ me s. te se ananse akita me, my foot is benumbed as if it were asleep; cf. sipiripii.
s. sipiripii.
pr. n. of a strong man = ɔhɔɔdeŋfo. pr. 2969.
osisiriw, a certain tree bearing red flowers; tulip-tree? pr. 3624; ɛbere kɔɔ a, na wodua abũro; wɔnɔa ɛhɔ hono nōm se ayamkawaduru; wode ye afa a wode tono.
a deceitful matter or act; deceit; error. Isa. 32, 6; feigned words. 2 Pet. 2, 3.
assistance, support, help; cf. sisi, ɔboa.
ɔkanea ns., chimney of a lamp. sisiw, F. sisu, red. v., s. siw.
yàré, lumbago, pain in the loins and small of the back; cf. emuyare, sãmẽẽ, oséŋmù.
a species of (small) fern = sibe, q. v.
v. n. 1. repeated pouring in of liquor, s. si 43 e. 2. the complement of a verb. Gram.
ɔkanea ns., chimney of a lamp. nsisó-náŋ, a foot standing upon its axle. 1 Kg. 7, 30.
a person with abnormal legs, so that in walking only his toes, not his heels, touch the ground; onipa a ɛnam ne naŋ abieŋ ano; cf. sii, osiifo.

asōtiw, deafness; yi.. as., to give one a private hint, to warn, acquaint with, make known; yi me as., give me notice (of it)! wɔayi me wo hɔ as., I have been informed concerning you. 1 Cor. 1, 11. Cf. nãm, v. 4; asō 15, hwĩtĩ, v.
a deaf person. o-sitíyífó, a. warner, informer.

red, sisiw, Ak. si; 1. to pound, stamp, bruise, beat, thrash; wósiw kɔkote de ye dɔkono; ósiw abũrow = ɔde abũrow gu woadurum’ na ɔde womma wów (de ye amoagyanewa). 2. to stop; to be stopped. pr. 2985: osiw n’asō, he stops his ears. Acts 7, 57; owú si(w) asō, death stops the ears, i. e. one will not believe that the sick person can die (always hoping for his recovery); n’asō asiw, his ears are stopped, i. e. he is disobedient, s. asō. - siw kwaŋ, to obstruct one's way, to bar, barricade, block or shut up

the way, to stop, check; to give a check to; to put a stop to (cf. sàkwaŋ); to prevent, obviate; to hinder, impede; to resist, oppose, withstand; to prohibit; ósiw me kwáŋ sɛ mennye adwuma or osiw me adwumaye hō kwaŋ, he hinders me from working. — siw ano, a) = siw kwaŋ, to withstand, resist, Heb. 12, 4, &c. [G. tšii na]; b) to shut up, close, seal: wasiw kotoku no ano, he has sealed up the bag. — siw so, to conceal, to hide or keep from, keep close or secret, hush up. 1 Sam. 3, 17. 18. Acts 20, 20; nsiw me nea wakā no biara so, do not conceal from me anything of what he has said! — osiw ne hō so, a) he disguises himself. 1 Sam. 28, 8; b) he suppresses his emotion = ohye ne hō so. — emu siw, it is hidden from, it is not clear, unintelligible, obscure to: emu siw me kakra = emu ntew me yiye, it is not quite intelligible to me. — 3. to stand in the way, to hinder: ɛdɛŋ nti na esiw fam' = agye asase no akenteŋ so, why does it cumber the ground? (Lk. 13, 7), — emmā ennyā biribi afifi-yē. — siw sūm, to stand in one's light: me wura, tafarakye, woasiw me sūm! — siw awia, to stand in the sun: nsiw me awia! (Diog. to Alex.) — 4. to let grow (cf. si 24, to let hang down); osiw ne ŋhwī, ne 'ti, osiw atimum' = ɔmā ne ti ŋhwī fuw ware, he lets his hair grow long, wears long hair, a sign of mourning. pr. 1445. — siw bogyese, to let the beard grow. — 5. siw nténne, to suppress or hold back the voice of complaint. pr. 335.
Ak. sie, ant-hill, the conical structure of the white ants, made of a reddish clay and from 8 to 12 feet high. pr. 371. 373. 2926. 2970f.

1. = siyere; si .. as. = si siyere. — 2. (Aky.) a certain game; cf. agoru. síwabiri, sowa, pādêdê (= Guaŋ: pālele), an herb or grass with fibrous stalks, very frequent at the sides of the footpaths in the bush; perh. a species of Rhēa, China-grass; Boemeria puya? — flax. Isa. 19, 9.
Akw.: ɔye assm no mu s., he is not honest in the matter = otwa mu ŋkontompo.
F. = ntuaano.
pause, stop; fullstop.
ɔdag no sibea wə asiye, that house is built in a good place; cf. sibea, bə 108.
inf. [yɛ nsī] diligence, industry, close application to one's business. — nsíyɛfó, pl. id. = osīfó; pl. men of activity. Gen. 47, 6.
pl. a- [con. ne siyère] a woman demanded (in early childhood) in marriage; a betrothed woman, fiancée, bride. Lk. 2, 5; syn. asiwá. — si .. siy., s. si 42.

v. [red. sosə] 1. to drop, drip, trickle, distil, fall or discharge itself in drops: nsu (nsä, ŋŋo) sɔ fam'; tr. to pour or let fall in drops. Deut. 32, 2. 33, 28. — 2. to light, kindle, inflame (ɔkanea, ogya, a candle, a fire). pr. 185. 336f.; masə gya = makoyi nuyansrama wə obi gyam' makogu me dem'; yeasə nnyansin ano, we have kindled two logs of wood opposite each other; intr. to catch (fire), to be kindled, to blaze, flame, to flare up: ogya no asə, the wood has caught fire, the fire blazes; hence: — 3. afāhye no asə, the festival is celebrated with gaiety, has reached its pitch; n'ayeforo-hyia sɔe dodo; agoru no sɔe, the play was merry &c., grand; agoru no nsə, the game is not merry, joyous, gleeful, pleasant. pr. 1216f. — 4. to be tough, clammy, sticky: me fufuu sɔ (hūāā), my dumpling (of pounded yam or plantains) is tough. — 5. to apply, examine, taste, try, exercise: sɔ .. aduru, to apply or let medicine; ósɔ ne. tuo (wə) dua no mu, he tries his gun at that tree; espec. with hwe: sɔ .. hwe, Gr. § 110. 220, 1; mesɔ aduaŋ (nsä, taa) no mahwe, I am tasting the food (liquor, tobacco), cf. kā .. hwe; mesɔ me hō mahwe se me hō ye deŋ ana, I shall try whether I am strong (enough for it); əsɔ ne nsa, he exercises his hand (in shooting, throwing

6. sɔ dade mu, to weld iron. - 7. sɔ..ano (cf. 1) to seal, orig. by dropping sealing-wax on something; mede dãgeré mesa ŋhoma ano. pr. 2978. John 6, 27. Rev. 5, 1. - 8. sɔ..ani, to satisfy or gratify the eyes of, to please, to content; to be acceptable in the eyes of; biribiara nsɔ difudepɛfo ani, nothing satisfies the discontented; ani a ensɔ ade, discontent(edness); ɔsɔ m'ani, I am well pleased in him. Mat. 3, 17. 12, 18. - 9. n'ani sɔ me, he respects, esteems, honours me; wo ani sɔ wo hɔ, you are pleased with yourself, are self-satisfied; n'ani akɔsɔ ne hɔ atra so, he is supercilious, overweening, insolent, presumptuous, loose. - 10. sɔ, to endure. Mt. 24, 13. - 11. sɔ (pl. sɔsɔ) obi kwaŋ = hyia obi kwaŋ, to meet some one on the way.
v. 1. to drop &c., s. before.

v. [red. suso] to seize, catch, take (lay) hold of or on, lay hands on; sɔ me nsa, take hold of my hand! pr. 338; múnso no mú! lay hold on him! pr. 2972: - sɔ pɔŋ no mu, take hold of the table! sɔ ŋkrantem', to put one's hand to the sword; ɛdɔm nnyã mmae no, yesɔ yeŋ akɔde mu, before the enemy approached, we took up arms; cf. kyere, kita. - Phr. sɔ..mu, to give or lend a (helping) hand: bɛra bésɔ mè mú, come and help or assist me! Gr. § 214.1 b; misom' a, ensɔ, when I try to go on with it, it will not (or no more) do, I try it in vain; cf. bɔ 54: mebɔ sɔ a, ɛmmɔ. - sɔ mu, sɔ ano, to stop, check, stay (a thing); to give a check, put a stop (to a thing); to withstand. - ósɔ ne nsá mú, he holds up his hand. Ex. 17, 11; sɔ n'asɛm mu, to seize on his words (with a hostile intention); F. to lay hold of his word, receive it word; - sɔ mu, to appropriate to oneself; to confess. K. § 8 ŋk. 9, 11.

v. contin. [red. sɔsɔ] 1. to be carrying on the head, to wear; cf. sɔa; òsɔ adesoa, he carries a load. pr. 25. 45. 64. 2755. 2973-77. - òsɔ kyɛw, he wears a hat. pr. 3262. - sɔ bosom, s. under soa. - 2. Phrases: òsɔ ne hɔ, he is his own master, he is independent; òsɔ ne ti, he is wayward, wilful, stubborn, obstinate, unruly, without restraint. Ezek. 16, 30; òsɔ asem no nyinaa ti, he is the principal person (head, chief, leader) in the matter; meso asem menam, I am sent on an errand; òsɔ no nam, he carries him about; mesɔ amannehunu menam, I walk about in great affliction. - 3. Phr. òsɔ no soro, he carries him up or about, i.e. abuses him with words; wòsɔ no hɔo, they speak indignantly of him. - 4. red. sɔsɔ, to arise, get up.
Ak. = sow & sɔw.
F. = sow (aba). Mk. 4, 7 f.

[red. sɔsɔ] la. to reach, arrive at. pr. 529; ɛnsɔ fam', soon nothing will be left of it; ósɔ Ab., he goes as far as Ab.; kɔsɔ, to go as far as: mere-kosɔ Abiriw maba, I will go as far as Ab. and then come back; mokɔsɔɔ hɛ na mosaŋ bae? how far did you go before you turned back? pr. 403; nea yenim kɔsɔ, as far as we know; nea nnipa te kɔsɔ nyinaa wɔ asase so, as far as there are men dwelling on the earth; de kɔsɔ sɛ, as far as, inasmuch as. K. § 152. - mã ensɔ ha ara, let the matter rest here, do not go any farther; ɛno ansɔ hɔ ara, it did not stop there, that was not enough. - F. mber no asɔ = ɛbere no adu, the time is fulfilled. - 1b. to attain to. Prov. 2, 19.

to overtake. Am. 9, 10. - ne nsa ansɔ n'atirimpɔw so, he could not carry out his intention. - 2. to suffice, be sufficient or enough: ɛrensɔ yɛnè mɔ, it will not be sufficient for both us and you. pr. 2489; ɛbesɔ, it will be sufficient, it will do; yɛyɛ asafo a yɛnsɔ ɔkaŋ, we are few in number. Gen. 34, 30. - cf. dɔ, dɔsɔ; sɔ ano, to be sufficient; syn. du ano. K. § 232. - 3. to be able (for): mesɔ me satu, I am able to go to war without the help of another; merensɔ kaw nom' = ɛkaw no dɔsɔ seŋ sa medu ano, I cannot afford, to take up debt. - 4. yé, it is fulfilled. pr. 2979; sɔ marry, be married; asɔ sɛ wɔbɛware, it is judgment. sɔsɔe, Gr. § 152, much. pr. 2979; or kɛse, he is very much. hɔ nsɔ mni, it is not large enough. ne nnɛ sɔ, it is enough. nné asɔ, he has come (at his entering, today); ne nné sɔ, it is not enough. - precious, of value, it is of great value. Mk. 14, 3; (Akan) valuable. sɔsɔ adae. 9. ɛbɛsɔ n'ani, it makes you satisfied. me he wo, we are under him.
a shark; cf. ŋkɔbɔ; - ɛ-sɔ, inf. the act of an interrogative. o-sɔ, a fine, heavy expression. 1166. osɔ = ɛyɛ fɛ, expression.
F. aso, in. F. Mt. 26, 40.
Ak. sɔɔ. 1. the upper part, the upper place; what is in, on, over, c'e, e, in, at, rin, at, concerning, kaŋ da pɔŋ ano hwɛ abɛn, abɔnteŋ no so. 1680. 2427. 28 hwe sɔ, mã sɔ nye, this.
a shark; cf. fũrefũre. [G. ogboolele]. pr. 1166.
(u-) a fox.
kokɔbɔ; also a bush-cat. - F. (pl. ɔ-sɔ, inf. the soldering. Isa. 41,7.
a fine, handsome person or thing; ɔye osɔ = ɔye ɔhɔɔfɛfɔ, he is gay; ɛye osɔ = ɛyɛ fe, that is fine! a favourite expression.
F. aso, interrog. particle at the head of an interrogative sentence. Gr. § 142. F. Mt. 26,40.

Ak. soɔ [cf. ɔsoro & Gr. § 118-120] 1. the upper part or surface of. - 2. the upper parts, the space above, and what is in it. - 3. on, up, upon, over, above, upward, on high; of time: in, at, during; of other relations: on, at, concerning, in, from, with; - osekaŋ da pɔŋ no sò; ogyina n'abobowano hwe abonteŋ no so; etwene nni abonteŋ no so. pr. 40. 373. 592. 883. 1427. 1680. 2427. 2708. 3025; - cf. dweŋ so, hwe so, mã so, se so &c.; ɔkwaŋ yi so nye, this road (way) is not good;
eso, F. = nso, also, besides.

adv., conj. [Gr. § 134, 3b. 140] also, too, likewise; besides; but, yet, however, moreover; nňo wo yɔŋkɔnom ŋkɔ, na dɔ wo atamfo nso, love not only your friends, but your enemies also; ɔdeŋkyɛm da nsum', ɔmampam nso da wura', the crocodile lives in the water, but the guana lives in the wood. pr. 622. 628. 859. 1848. 1924. 2287. Cf. usoso, pr. 522, nanso, pr. 12. 506. 512 &c.

blame, reproach; culpability; guilt; - obua no sɔ, he reproaches or upbraids him; cf. asɔbua; esɔ da no so = asɛmmone da no so; syn. efɔ da no so, odi fɔ; - odi sɔ, he is blamable, culpable, deserves blame or censure; odi mogya hɔ sɔ, he is culpable of the shedding of blood (by omitting what he ought to have done to avoid or prevent it); cf. odi mogya hɔ fɔ, he is guilty of blood, by a deed committed; - wode sɔ yi tɔɔ no, they brought this reproach or accusation against him; watɔ no sɔ, he has falsely blamed him, declared him culpable. pr. 1710; (in blind-man's-buff:) he has seized the wrong person. Cf. asɔbua, asɔtɔ.
(pl. id.) the ear; auricle [con. n'asɔ]; asɔ abieŋ, two ears. pr. 1312f. 2980-89. - páane asɔ = p. aniwa or hwene, the eye of a needle; ɔkwaŋ asɔ, the

edge of the path. pr. 1893; otuo asɔ (or asɔm'), the pan of a flint-lock; awo-wa asɔ or asɔ ano, the edge or rim of a brass pan. - asɔm' = asɔ mu, the cavity or inner part of the ear; m'agya asɛm da m'asɔm', I am mindful of my father's word. - Phrases: 1. n'asɔ yɛ dɛŋ, he is disobedient; n'asɔ anyiŋ, apew, aṣeŋ, asiw, awu, id.; n'asɔ asorow, id. = wayɛ ne hɔ sɛ osɔdenfo, wokã asɛm kyere no a, ɔntɛ wɛ n'asɔ akyi (or n'ani akyi), na ɔnte wɛ n'asɔm'; - asɛm no to n'asɔm', he understands the matter. - 2. n'asɔ nni so he gives no heed to it, cf. asɔ-bi-anna-so; n'asɔ gu so, he listens. - 3. n'asɔm' nni agua, lit. there is no seat in his ear, i.e. he soon forgets what he is told. - 4. n'asɔm' adwo, he has peace, rest, tranquillity, is undisturbed; wo asɔm' dwo a, enna wo hɔ ato wo; Maŋkata amã yeŋ asɔm' adwo yeŋ na yeŋ hɔ atɛ yeŋ; n'asɔm' ŋŋwo no, he is not at rest, he is distressed or disturbed, e.g. by a bad conscience; syn. ne hɔ ŋŋwo no. - 5. ohuw n'ade no asɔm' = ɔtoŋ n'ade no. - 6. ɔkyea n'asɔ, he bends his ear, i.e. perverts judgment. - 7. opra n'asɔ akyi, he will hear nothing of it, does not at all care about what is said to him: asɛm a meka mekyeree no no, ɔprapraa n'asɔ akyi (de guu so) na osiim' kɛɛ; wobo woŋ diŋ baabi a, na wɔpra woŋ asɔ akyi, their name was mentioned everywhere, (but) only with terror. - ɛnam n'asɔ akyi, it makes no impression on him, he takes no notice of it; egu woŋ asɔ akyi kwa, it makes no impression on them. - 8. ɔkɔsɛree n'asɔ kɔtee = ɔtee no abansosɛm, he has it by hearsay. - 9. ɔsɛreŋ n'asɔ, he pricks up his ears, listens to a distant sound. - 10. wotu no asɔ, they persuade, induce, inveigle, seduce him, prevail on him, win him over, get him to do anything good or bad; F. yɛbotu n'asɔ asoma, we will persuade him. Mt. 28,14. - 11. wotwɛ ne asɔ, they draw him by the ear, i.e. he is punished. - 12. ɔweŋ n'asɔ, he wakens his ear, i.e. he is attentive, pays close attention. - 13. oye asɔ, he gives ear, lends an ear, pays attention (to), listens; mɔnye asɔ! = múntie! hearken! attention! give heed! - oye n'asɔ demm or komm, he listens attentively. - 14. ɔde ye n'asɔ so ade or asɛm, he takes the hint, takes warning, bears that in mind, lets it be a warning to him, is mindful of it; ɔmfã n'yɛ n'asɔ so asɛm, he does not care about it. - 15. ɔyɛ no asɔ = ɔyi no asitiw, he gives him a private hint. - 16. oyi n'asɔ, he withdraws his ear, i.e. he is careless, heedless, unconcerned; secure; nnipa a wɔayi woŋ asɔ te ase yi, womfrá koraa, these men, living so carelessly, or passing their life in over-confident security, are worthless people, good for nothing fellows. (D. As.). - 17. Wo asɛm a wokã yi nni asɔ, this word of yours has (deserves) no ear, i.e. attention, i.e. what you say is not worth hearing, is not acceptable, cannot be true, is a foolish word, is absurd, nonsense. - 18. ɔkeŋkaŋ guu maŋ no asɔm', he read (it) in the audience of the people. Ex. 24,7.

inf. difference; ne sono a esono noŋ ne nea ɛwɔ he? in what is it different? os. bi da yenè woŋ ntam', we differ from them; we are at variance. Cf. nsōnoe.

v. [inf. a-, red. sosəre] 1. to be careful about; treat carefully; sɔre wo hō oo! look after yourself, take care of yourself! ósòre ne bá no sê = əhwɛ no so yiye, əntoto no ase; əs. ne mma hō; əs. ne ŋhoma yi sε eye ŋhoma pa bi. 2. to worship, adore; əs. Nyankəpɔŋ; əs. ne bosom. 3. to perform official religious duty or service, devotional exercises, religious rites; to say the prayers in the family or congregation; wósòre, they are worshipping, have divine service. 4. to baptize: wósòre. no, wasəre ne hō, (pl. woasósəre woŋ hō), he has been baptized; better: woabə no asu, wamã woabə no asu. 5. sɔre se ŋŋó, to be handsome, beautiful (said of young men & women).

v. [red. sɔresəre] 1. to rise, arise, get up (espec. from a seat or bed &c.; sɔre fi me trãbere! ósòré fi ne kete sɔ); mónsəré mmã yeŋkə! arise and let us go! pr. 323. 325. - to rise (in rebellion), rise up (in arms): əmaŋ besəre. (wə əmaŋ so. Lk. 21,10; sɔre hye.., to rise up against. Gen. 4,8. - ówia sɔre = pue, the sun rises; - to rise, swell (mmore, dough; əpo, the sea; asu, a river). - mã yeŋwie yeŋ adwuma prɛkə nsəre so, let us finish (complete) our work at once; nini menee adowa (prɛkə) sɔree so, the nini swallowed an antelope completely (at once). - 2. to part or depart; to leave, go away; to cease: ne kãra (sunsum or hoŋhom) asəre [wə] no so, his soul or spirit has left him (this is said even before the person has actually expired); mesəré b'rá yim' à, hwe me mma so mã me, when I depart this life, take care of my children! woŋ a woafa woŋ hō adi nyinaa asəre ha, all those who have become free, have left this town; - ɛno ansəre mu a, woŋ yiyeye wə akyiri, if that does not cease (is not given up), it will be a long time before their circumstances change for the better. - 3. to revive: ŋhabaŋ a ɛbəwe no asəre bio; ŋhabaŋ no sɔresəre.
v. F. to be conical, to rise to a point; cf. sɔŋ.
a. F. conical, pointed; high, lofty, steep; cf. sɔrɔnsɔrɔŋ.

[red. sorósòrow] to grow or make stiff; to take or cause fright; to become or make shy, coy, timid, stubborn, obstinate, mostly used with asõ: n'asõ asorow, he is disobedient (s. asõ), stubborn, refractory; wasórow, id. = wáŋwèŋ, n'ani abere; wòkã asem kyere no a, ɔnte; aŋkã ese se ɔba, na ɔmma; - was. akoa no (asõ) = watu akoa no asõ.

(after poŋkɔ), rider. Ex. 15, 1; (after asase) inhabitant. Lev. 25, 10.

[tu .. asɔ̃] persuasion, enticement, seduction. - asótú-sém, a seductive word or piece of advice.

v., Ak. sɔ, [red. sosow] 1. to catch, catch up, snatch up, with the hands or mouth: metów mesòw, I throw up and catch (a ball); obi foro dua bi na ɔtew n'aba no bi a, na nea ogyina ase na ɔsow; s. mframa, to snuff up the wind. Jer. 2, 24; cf. 14, 6 & sɔ̃m. - ósòw or n'ano sɔ abohom or ahupmu, he gapes, gazes, stands agape, stands gaping or idling about; - to catch with the ears and mind; wosowe se śiadesɛm, they took it as a good omen. 1 Kg. 20, 33. - 2. to pick up; to pick, peck at, of birds with their bills: apiti ye anomaa ketewa bi, əsow nnipa sê. - 3. to catch (up) or receive in breaking a fall or blow, to intercept, ward off: aŋkã merehwe ase, na oyi na əsow me, I should have fallen, but this man (boy) caught me; aŋkã Persini bi de ŋkrante rebɔ ne ti, na Klito kəsow ano, Clitus warded off the blow. - 4. to receive into a vessel, to gather, collect: əde ahina sow nyaŋkɔnsu, he gathers rainwater in a pot; de.. sow .. ano, to place a vessel for that purpose = sũm; - wo ani bɔ aduaŋ yi so ara pe a, na wo ano sow nsu, one's mouth waters at the (first) sight of this food. - 5. sow gu, to flow or trickle down from one place or object upon another: nsu sow guu me sɔ me daŋ mu, the (rain-)water, that had fallen on the roof, trickled down on me in my room.
v. [red. susow] 1. to hatch (eggs): akokɔ no ansow ne ŋkesua no, na wanom ne nyinaa; ósòw ŋkesuá. - 2. to cut into pieces (yam, for planting): wósòw ədé.
v. [red. sɔsow] 1. (with or without aba) to produce or bear fruit; ésòw abá. pr. 1476. Mt. 7, 17. 21, 19. - 2. sow mu, to set, stud, e. g. a cloak with precious stones.
pl. n-, hoe, mattock. pr. 729. 3042; cf. soduro, sokum, səbakura & əsosow. - əbɔ əbea no asów, he gives the bad advice to that woman to leave her husband; cf. asɔy.
sɔw, ɔsɔ, pl. n-, F. fox. Mt. 8, 20.

sign, mark; hye adé yi nsòw mã me, mark this for me! mahye ne nsem no bi ns., I have marked (taken particular notice of) some of his sayings or expressions; da nsow, s. da 26. Cf. agyirae.
a plant, s. siwabiri.

beautiful; abawa os., aberante os.; - osówá! an exclamation of lascivious women at the passing of a handsome young man, or vice-versa; syn. epɔ.

asɔwiá [ade a esɔw awia] umbrella, parasol = akatawia.
As. = fefeefɛ.
inf. hearkening, hearing. 1 Sam. 15, 22. 1 Kg. 18, 29. 2 Kg. 4, 31.
= asepáteré.

särá, v. [red. srasra] 1. to stroke, rub; to daub, plaster; to smear, besmear, grease, oil, anoint; osrá odaŋ, he washes the house, daubs the house with white clay; osra (ne hɔ), əde ŋkũ (srade, bɔrɔ-ŋŋo) sra ne hōnam, he anoints his body with shea-butter (fat, oil). - 2. to spy (out), search, watch, guard, lie in wait for; sra dɔm, to watch or reconnoitre the hostile army;

asɔ, to pay attention to something.
to arrange or array the battle; cf. twa mpasua.
to visit somebody; mabɛsrà wo; pl. yeabésrà mo [prop. I (we) have paid you a visit], a salutation at parting after a visit.
the act of rubbing, daubing, anointing &c.
the act of visiting, spying (out), watching &c.; - ɔkɔɔ (ɔbaa) hɔ nsra, he went (came) there on a visit &c.
àsàrà, snuff; som as., to take snuff.
ɔsẽnã. - ás'rãã = asẽnãã.

camp, encampment; bɔ (..so) ns., to pitch a camp (against), to encamp (against); to be drilling (of soldiers); bɔ nsra kyerɛ, to parade. - nsra-báŋ, 1. camp, encampment. Gen. 25,16; wɛbɔɔ ns. ahorow abiesã, they pitched 3 camps successively. - 2. = mpasua.

(military) parade.
parade-ground, drilling-ground; place for encampment.

pl. (n)sráfó, scout, spy. 1 Sam. 26,4.
nsram'fo, the people in the camp, encamped warriors. pr. 941.

n-, F. sorãfo, sorodãfo, soldiers; s. osrãni. - nsrafo atrãe, cantonment; asr.-daŋ, nsr.-fi, asr.-yeŋbea, barracks, casern. - asráfó-dí(-dwùmá), military service. - asrãafo-kúw, band, cohort of soldiers. Mt. 27,27.

inf. abandonment, neglect &c.
overseer &c., s. osrabehwɛ.

Nu. 16,33. - wasrám wɔŋ ani so, he has besmeared their eyes. Isa. 44,18.
osárám, pl. a-, a tall person, giant; giantess (ɔbea ɔs.); cf. ɔtẽnteŋ, tentensram, ɔbraŋ, ɔbrantetɛtũ.

Ak. osrãné pl. a-, 1. the moon. pr. 2552; syn. hyeŋ, ɔbosóm'; ɔs. afi, the new moon has appeared; ɔs. apae, the moon shines; ɔs. gye so, the moon rises (over the horizon); ɔs. gye so, asi no sɔ, the moon has smitten him, Ps. 121,6 (amã ne tirim aye no sakasaka, so that his head is deranged and he is lunatic or moon-struck); ɔs. atwa
or kòròkúma, the moon is full; ɔs. awu, the moon has died, i. e. its disk is without illumination. pr. 3043f.

2. the moon-light, moon-shine; s. sram'sò. 3. month, syn. ɔbosóm; ɔs. fi, the month begins; ɔs. wu, the month ends; daa ɔsram wu a, onyã n'akatua, at the end of every month he receives his wages. pr. 2810; ɔ-sram sram akatua, monthly pay or wages = asranne. According to Kofi Akwatia of Akropong the natives have 4 months of 28, 3 of 30, and 5 months of 32 days; and other informants differ concerning the names and succession of the single months. We give the names in the most probable order, adding the numbers of the corresponding European months (1. January, 2. Febr. ... 12. December): obubuo (2), 9, 10, 11, 12; openimma (mùmɔ?) 11, 12, 1; onyamewia? ogyefuo 1, 2, 3; ɔbenem 2, 3, 4, 5; o-forisuo (ogyenko) 4, 5; otwanyokoŋ? ɔpraworam 5; aye-wohɔ-mumo 5, 6, 7; 11, 12; akita-wo-nsa 6, 7; kɔtonimma 5, 6, 7, 8; hũhũhũhũ 5, 6, 9; nyãnyãã 7; ɔsannaa 8, 10; odweŋpwane 9, 10? kɔkosukwakwawea(m), osiapansam 9, 11; ɛbɔ 9, 10; ahĩn(e) 9, 10; ɔpese 10 or 10-12 & 1.
yellow fever; atiridii kɔkɔɔ.
Ak. = yafumpaŋmu: ɔda ns., he sleeps with an empty stomach.
live coals, glowing coals = nnyansrãmma; cf. sramsram & gyabiriw.
fire-pan.

(pl. a-), 1. lightning; ɔs. apae, the lightning flashes, it lightens, cf. anyinam; ɔs. si (or duru) duam', the lightning strikes a tree; ɔs. apae asi no so, the lightning has struck him. O-nyame m'pae s. nsi me! may God strike me by lightning! (if my statement is not true &c.), cf. gũa. Oprannaa bom' a, na nea eduru duam' no na yefrɛ no srãmãŋ, thunder-bolt = Nyaŋkɔpɔŋ abonua, cf. abonnua. Ɔs. duru duam' a, spaem' na dua no hyew, nsó osu tɔ gum' a, ennum; na ɔs. no apkasa mem fam araa, na ano kɔkã (kɔto) nsu wɔ fam' a, na esan ba bio; nanso wose: wode aɛowa si sum' a, na ɔs. apae asim' na atu to na amem fam'. 2. swivel, rocket. 3. pr. n. of a fetish at Akropong. ɔ-srãmãŋ-bo, F. thunder-bolt.
pl. a-, crescent. Isa. 3, 18.
s. srãfó. 1 Sam. 14, 12.
unawares.
in the moon-light or moon-shine; wɔnam s., they travel by moonlight.
ad. emitting sparks, sparkling, -ly, glittering, with twinkling or vivid brilliancy; dade no adɔ sss. the iron is red-hot; nnyansrãmã tu sss.; cf. ɔsram, srãnsrãnsrãg.
a women's disease; eye wɔŋ ani kɔɔ, mpafɛ nso wom'; cf. atiridii.
[osram, ɛda] the days of a month - as. ŋhoma, almanac, calender.
night-watching; bɔ as., to sit up at night; syn. si pɛ. [ɔsram' & neg. of da, to sleep]; ɔsram fi a, wonnã.

pl. a-, a pile of yams (consisting of a dozen tubers) bound together and stowed in the putu from bottom to top until taken out for sale; ɔs. biakɔ kura ɛdɛ mpów mmaakɔ-maakɔ 12, ɛtɔd. wɔye no 15; esono ɔdɛmú 3 a, s. 6.
Ak. s. ɔsram'.
[osram ade] monthly pay or wages; yi.as., to pay (one) his m. wages; cf. gye 1 & ɔsram 3.
[ɔsram] month of vanity. Job 7, 3.
Akp. srawni, F. sorãnyi, soro-dânyi (q. v.), soldier; cf. pl. asrãfó & srãfó, asafó, ɔsafoni, ɔkɔfo, ɔkɔfoni; di srãni, s. di 42.
[osram diŋ] name of a month; pl. a-, the names of the months.
pl. a- [ɔsram] monthly debts (expenses); monthly pay or allowance; tua ..ɔs. or as., to pay (one) monthly or by monthly instalments.
adv. sparkling, glistening, glittering, -ly; ogya no tutu ss.; dade no adɔ ss.; ɔtam yi ani, sika, kɔbere nè aɛowa hɔ ye ss. - ɔwia
anointing. Ex. 30, 31.
red. v. sra; to stroke, caress, flatter; ɔsrasra agyinamoa hɔ, he is stroking the cat.
pl. a- [sra 4] a visitor; nea ɔsra obi.
glossy, smooth and shining; onipa, ɔpɔŋkɔ hɔ aye s.; cf. hràhràhrà, sràmsràmsràm.
inf. the act of snuffing, taking snuff. — di as., to have close communion (with). pr. 3456. — ɔ-srasómfó, pl. a-, one who takes snuff, snuff-taker. — asra-toaá, snuff-box.
inf. service as a soldier; cf. srà. — ɔ-sráw'ní = osrâni.

[usram' or srafo yere] the proceedings and ceremonies of the women for the supposed benefit of their husbands away at war; mmommomé; di as., to perform such ceremonies: wodi as. ne se: mmarima kɔ 'sa na mmea te wɔŋ akyi wɔ fie to dwom na wɔsaw na woyi mmusu na wɔbɔ asumaŋ.
v. = sère.
in a straight continuous line; asrâfo no gyina hɔ (toatoa so) sr., those soldiers stand in a straight line.
sérèŋ', v. to become, grow or be lean and white or pale; wasréŋ = wahóa fitaa; ɔyare bi bɔ wo na woasreŋ fitaa a, woreŋkye wu, wo sunsuma asɔre wo so.
2. to comb: ɔsréŋ' né ŋhwí, nè tí, she combs her hair, her head.

3. to direct the climbing of the runners (twigs or shoots) of the yam-plant: ɔs. ɔde, he causes the yam to climb up a tree; ɔs. bayere n. s. wufua bayere, na efí a, wusi dua tia-tiaa bi na wode hama kɔsà dua kese bim' na wode asã tiatiaa no, na bayere no aforo.
4. to prick up, asɔ̃, one's ears: ɔs. n'asɔ̃, he listens to a distant sound; to bristle: agyinamoa yi sreŋ (ne ŋhwí), this cat's hair stands erect or on end (prop. this cat makes her hair stand up).
pl. a-, one who cards wool, flax &c., a carder. Isa. 19, 9.
aloof from, in the or from a distance: ɔwɔ no ani abere nti migyina ns. na mehwe no, e.s. dekɔde no memwɛŋ no na migyina akyirikyiri mehwe; metee no ns., I heard it indirectly.
s. asĕrɛne.
[Eng.] slate.
Ak. = ásèréwá.
suro, F. to fear; s. suro.
nsroafo, F. = ɔsɔranyi, nsorafo.
[G. srɔlɔ] shavings brought off by the plane. Twi: nsensenẽẽ.
pl. n-, F. a sparrow. Mt. 10, 29.
nsrɔŋ, Ak. the fruit of the ɔsrono; Akp. ɔsɔŋ'(aba), q. v. pr. 195. 237.
ɔsɔróno, ɔsróne, Ak. F. a tamarind = ɔsɔŋ'; F. also the Locust tree.
sórɔŋ, v. to be high, lofty; - red. srɔnsrɔŋ; mmepɔw no s.

sórɔŋ, n. the highest point, summit of a mountain, tree, house &c., sharply pointed height; bepɔw yi s. ware seŋ yi de, the summit of this mountain is higher than the summit of that one; wadu bepɔw no s. so; anɔmaa si daŋ no s. so.
a. (pl. a-, Isa. 30, 25), high, lofty, steep (when viewed from below, cf. kũrɔŋkũrɔŋ); opp. taa; bepɔw, dua, ɔdaŋ no atifi ye s.
pl. srɔnsrɔm-méa, a high place. 1 Kg. 3, 2. 2 Chron. 1, 3.
a. high, lofty, stately: dua or abaŋ no si hɔ s.
asɔrɔtow, F. species, kind(s) [Mk. 1, 34].
stockings, socks.
sú, the sound of pounding fufuu in a wooden mortar. pr. 349; cf. tum, tum.
Ak. = suw.
v. 1. to weep, shed tears, cry. pr. 8. 365. 2199; woasũ, nà wo ani abere, you have been weeping, for your eyes are red; ósũ mmɔborosú, osú hèm, he

inf. 1. weeping; wailing, lamentation. pr. 2650. 3049. - osü asi no, he sobs. - tu sũ, F. to burst out weeping. - 2. cry; crying of a bird &c. pr. 1481. 1524; esono né sú ŋkɔ (= ne kasa), its cry is peculiar. pr. 2479.

species, kind, sort. pr. 1528; nature, property, quality; character; manner; cf. bay, subaŋ, sso, odasú. - ntamá yi su nte sa kaŋ de a metoe no, this cloth is not of the same sort as that which I bought formerly; wo sú n'yé! you are a bad character; wo sú nè wo báŋ biara nso m'ani, neither your character nor your manners please me. - esu a empörow (da), incorruptible nature, incorruptibility, imperishableness.

Ak. nsúo, 1. water; nom nsu, to drink water; bɔ or saw nsu, to scoop or draw water; nsu ba, water comes, i.e. a) water springs, comes forth, from a well; b) the river fills (ready to overflow its banks); nsu yiri, the water overflows. pr. 3097; cf. bɔ 3. pr. 3080-97. 3482. - also a body of water, standing or flowing; kɔ nsu, better: kɔ asu. Cf. asu; pr. 3083-86. 3092. 3094. - Phr. ne diŋ tɔɔ nsum' (his name fell into oblivion), he was no more mentioned; cf. ediŋ; de .. nsa gu nsu mu ye biribi, to try one's best or utmost; sika a shɔ nni nsu nni nsä, s. nsä. - 2. sap of plants, cf. asonsüaa; juice of fruits. - 3. some or other kind of liquid secretion from animal bodies: a) milk; nsu nni ne nufu mu bio; s. nufusu; b) sperm. Lev. 15, 32, cf. ahɔbaa; c) urine; gu nsu, to make water; cf. dwensɔ; d) cf. nta-su, spittle; e) matter, pus; cf. ekuru. - 4. the drink or potion taken in swearing an oath of allegiance or mutual fidelity; - the oath, or the alliance or covenant itself; onè no wɔ nsu, the two are confederate, associated by an oath, leagued together; also the water which two men pour on the heads of their nephews (heirs) under some solemn promise; gu nsu: nnipa baŋ hɔ ɔbosom bi diŋ, na wode nsu gu woŋ wofasenom atifi se wòbedi woŋ hɔ nokware; s. also gu 24; - tɔ nsu, to break faith; wátɔ nè nsú, he has broken or violated his promise, oath or covenant; wɔatɔtɔ wɔŋ hɔ nsu, they have mutually broken their covenant; cf. nom or di abosom, di nsew.
nsew, F. vow, solemn promise; hye (dzi) nsú, to vow, make a vow.

1. rain; cf. nyaŋkɔm, nyaŋkɔpɔŋ 4. - pr. 3051-65; osu reba, rain is coming; osu tɔ, it rains. pr. 1449. 2040; osu gu, it rains moderately; osu-pá, a usual rain; osu-kesé, a heavy rain; osu tɔ ŋwéséŋwésé, it drizzles, cf. nsuwɔnséaa; osu tɔ tràrara, tràdada, pibibibi, pipipipi, pibàbababa, púbàba, pú-wàa, ŵòo, yàa, the rain falls, descends, gushes in a heavy shower, in torrents; osú ká ha ká ká ha, it (is) was raining in every direction; Onyaŋkɔpɔŋ tɔ osu gu asase so, God causes it to rain upon the earth. Gen. 2, 5. - 2. cloud, rain-cloud, nimbus; osu amuna, the clouds have darkened; osu reseg, the clouds are passing; osu no apa, the cloud is gone.

[pl. s. asuasú] a place where water is fetched, any body or collection of water, standing or flowing, well, pond, lake, spring, brook, river; nsu biara a staa nea nsu fi ba. pr. 78. 3066-79. - cf. asum', nsu 2, asuwa, asuteŋ, asubɔnteŋ, ɔtare; kɔ asu, to go for water,
inf. the act of swearing, oath of allegiance &c., solemn promise; ns. nye ɔkɔ. pr. 3098.
inf. the act of learning, imitation. pr. 613: 2284.
pl. a-, a species of monkey; s. ahweŋhema. pr. 894. 3100ff.
a weight of or for gold = 9 dollars or ackies, £ 2. 6d. pr. 132.
-besé, a certain tree and its fruit; cf. bisé.
a place for learning, school; cf. sukuu.
pl. a-, a house for learning, school-house, school-room, learning-room.
adesũade [ade a wosũa] any thing to be learned, lesson; ene de woansũa wo as.; cf. asũasem.
s. ɔsebɔ. - asũáé = sũabea.

inf. experience, Rom. 5,4, successful learning; ade nyinaa dáŋ sũahú, all knowledge is. acquired by learning and only thereby. pr. 802. - asũahú-de,† knowledge, acquirements, accomplishments, (literary &c.) attainments.
an oath or solemn promise that is not fulfilled.
one who cannot fulfil his oath or promise.
a species of bird (hoopoe, hoop, dungbird?); anomaa bi a ɔreye akɔse akyéŋkyɛ̃ná, nso oŋwíé nò sé. pr. 737. 1948. 2569.
the other side of the river, beyond the river; cf. asuogya.

[red. sunsũaŋ] 1. to pull, to draw out, forth, or away; sũaŋ dua no fi tanaa a ɛrehyew yim' (syn. twẽ, koyi fim' bere me)! sũaŋ no fi nea ɔdá hɔ! mekɔe no, na aboa no da ɔkwaŋ-mu hɔ, na misũaŋ no mifi hɔ; kosũaŋ no asé, ɔtwẽ no fam', he drags him along the ground (much or little of the body touching the ground); kosũaŋ-guag no ase, take that sheep up by the feet! wosunsũaŋ' n'asé, s. tobẽ.

2. to bleed, let blood, draw or take blood from, by opening a vein or by scarifying and cupping, cf. sa, sesa; wásúáŋ me; ode sekaŋ s. no. — 3. to eat with a greedy appetite, voraciously; ósúáŋ aduaŋ', nãm = odi no pii.
a climber; the swelling caused by the sap of it; hama bi a ɛwo wuram'; emu nsu kã wo ara pe a, na ɛho ahoŋ; na egow na wumia a, aboa bi fi mu.

[red. sunsùane] 1. tr. to tear, slit, split, rend, rive, to separate thin and soft things into long pieces or strips, to make a long fissure; cf. tew, pae, twa; dadewa no as. me ntama, the nail has torn my dress; ósùane ŋ'ánò, he opens his mouth; cf. bue. — 2. intr. to split, rend; ntama no asùane. pr. 1419. 3413.
pl. a- -fo, learner, scholar, student, disciple; apprentice.
the surface of the water. pr. 1899. — on the water; ǫnam ns. kǫ hǫ, he goes there by water. — nsúani-fá, inf. sailing, navigation, voyage. Acts 27,9.
well, spring, the opening in the earth from which water issues; cf. nsuti, source.
bank, shore of a river, lake, or sea; cf. nsunòa.
pl. nsuanofǫ, a man from the coast; people living near a river, a lake or the sea.
a weight of or for gold = 18 dollars or ackies, £ 4. 1s.

[con. né sùáre] any spot or place in the bush, a piece, patch, tract, or plot of ground, bush, or other land; a beaten path, trace, track, vestige, mark; obi nnim sùare kǫ a ǫnam so, nobody knows where he roves or roams about; mihyiaa, no na ǫnennam s. bi so na mefaa no dwen, I met him strolling about in the bush and made booty of him; yèhùù sono anamǫn nè wǫŋ s. pii, beboro dakoro kwaŋ po, we saw many footprints and other marks of elephants for rather more than a day's journey; wǫŋhú né sùáre só, no vestige of him was found; wo de, woamfi sùáre bi aniase koraa, you did not come very far!
a weight of or for gold, 27 dollars or ackies, £ 6. 1s. 6d. pr. 132.
osúá-nsatéaa, a shrub with edible fruit.
the bottom of a river or of any other water. pr. 2716.
[asem a wosùa] any piece of instruction, precept or doctrine to be learned; catechism.
inf. imitation or mimicry in an excessive manner.
[pl. of asu], waters here and there; tu as., to walk in water.
red. v. sùa, to imitate, mimic.
inf. imitation; mimicry; ye as., to imitate, mimic.
pl. a-, imitator, mimic.
v. [inf. a-, red. susùaw] to lop a tree or its branches, to cut branches off a tree.
inf. [sua 2] exception, exemption; cf. nyiyim'.

súbaŋ, figure, form, shape, fashion; stature; constitution, condition, quality, nature; kind, pattern; cf. su, baŋ; ne súbaŋ (= nipabáŋ, nipaduá) te se oyi de; in his figure he resembles this man; ntama yi s. ye fe, this is a fine make or pattern of cloth; mihùù ade no, na maŋhú ne s. yiye.
nŋo, palm-oil.

inf. 1. [bo asu] the act of bathing in fresh water, of diving in water; of cleansing, wetting or dashing with water. [Obǫ ne hǫ asu, he dives; m'aŋkasa mekǫbǫ me hǫ asu; oo, ne hǫ ye fi, móŋkǫbǫ no asu; esono móŋkoguare no! woguare no, ɛ.s. woaso saw mu na wode reguare no]. — 3. an ablution, a religious ceremony connected with application of water, also without washing or diving the whole body; cf. ahǫdwira, asumguare. [Obǫ ne hǫ asu = obǫ ne kãra asu; wǫbǫ wǫŋ hǫ asu a, ɛnyé se wode nsu no guare wǫŋ hǫ nyinaa, na wode ka-.
pl. id., asúbòhwèhwéní, pl. -fo; asubó..., candidate for baptism.

(pl. a- -fo), baptist: a) one who administers baptism, specifically applied to John, the forerunner of Christ; b) an anabaptist, one who maintains that baptism ought to be administered only to adults by immersing the body in water.
pl. n- [nsu aboa] water-animal, i.e. a quadruped living in the water, espec. the crocodile or alligator; s. ɔdeŋkyem.
one who joins (lit. helps) another or others in weeping. pr. 3104.
osukraman, water-dog. pr. 3105.
guare as., to get drenched (by rain).
pl. a-, valley, with or without water; cf. oboŋ, oboŋhunu. - o-subóŋkã, channel or bed of a river.
Ak. = osukraman.
pl. n- [nsu, abɔnteŋ] river, stream; cf. asu, asuteŋ.
the bank of a river, cf. asukɔŋ.
inf. bathing in a river, lake [or sea.
pl. n- [nsu abura] well. place in the water, in a river.
-búnùm, [nsu, buŋ] a deep place in the water, in a river.
the Danes; Os. asase, Denmark.
s. usuhuru.
things (ade) that cause tears or deserve weeping about. pr. 2411.
sweet, i.e. pathetic or affecting lamentation. pr. 1163.
= suru.
s. keŋkaŋ, v.
v. Kuk. = sũa, susũa.
pl. a-, weeper, mourner. pr. 3106. Rom. 12, 15.
water dashed by the wind against something.
[Lat.] sulphur, brimstone; syn. adubẽn, atodu-dubẽn.
inf. drowning; (suffering) shipwreck.
inf. [guare asu] the act or art of swimming. (Diff. asumguare). - o-suguaréfó, pl. a-, swimmer. Isa. 25, 11.
[nsu, guare, osẽŋ] washing-pot. pr. 176.
pl. - nnaka, base or stand for the lavers in Solomon's temple. 1 Kg. 7, 27.
[asu, hare v.] ferry-man.
[nsu ahina] water-pot. pr. 3109.
pl. id. [nea osũ ne hō] murmurer, grumbler.
pl. a- [nsu, awuru] a species of turtle or tortoise found in rivers = osúdànná, sukyekyeré, sũpurupũ; cf. apohuru.
roof, espec. its outside or upper side; nea ekata dampare so; cf. ɔdamparé. - osuhyɛ-fá, one half of a roof. pr. 3110; os. wommua, audiatur et altera pars! hear also the other party! hear both sides!
n-, a hollow passage or fissure in the ground, caused by the water, gutter; channel or bed of a river or brook; canal; cf. obɔŋkã, subóŋ; - conduit. 2 Kg. 20, 20. [nsu.

n-, a large river &c., cf. asu, asu-kɔ, inf. [kɔ asu] 1. the act or duty of going for water. pr. 1627. - 2. dɔ as., to dive, descend or plunge into water, thrust the body deeply under water; hye (obi) as., to dive into, submerge or immerse (one) in water.
a drop of water; nsuko fua or biakɔ, one drop of water; nsukókó abieŋ, two drops of water &c.

the dark, darkness. pr. 33; esúm kàbii, kùntàŋ, kùsuu, tùmm, black darkness; esum aba, darkness has come, it has become dark; esum duruu asase no so, a darkness came over the land; òwia duru sum, the sun is darkened; - esum apatuw atu, the darkness has disappeared all at once; - n'abra-bɔ mu ye súm súm, her dealings are not straight and upright; - siw súm, s. siw 3.
esũm-asɛm, F. secret, mystery.
F. secret, mystery.

F. = hintaw, to hide, to be hidden. Mt. 5,14. 13,33. 44. Mk. 4,22. - nsũmam', F. = kokoam', in secret, secretly, privily, privately. Mt. 1,19. 2,7. 6,4.; nsumam' bon, secret sins; ns. asɔr, private prayer.

[dim. s. suman] an amulet of little significance (pr. 655) or worn only as an ornament; wɔye ebi few so; wode ŋhenewa nè akoo ntakara nè ŋkyekyeraa bobɔ toto wɔŋ hɔ; cf. ŋkufe. - sumãm-mó, inf. [bɔ suman] wearing of charms or amulets.

Ak. -ne, pl. n-, 1. charm, amulet, talisman, worn as a remedy or preservative against evils or mischief, such as diseases and witchcraft, consisting or composed of various things, as feathers, hair, or teeth of various animals, beads, scraps of leather or paper inscribed with mystic characters &c. and tied round some limb or hung about the neck; bɔ s., to make or wear an amulet; tu s., to introduce (or make) a new amulet; gye s., to procure or buy an am. pr. 117. 162. 655. 115. 1721. 2610; syn. dóhuwa. - 2. any protecting power, including the abosom: ókɔ n'ásúmãŋ (or n'ásù-maŋ') akyl, (euphem.) = he died; s. wu. A list of amulets, s. Appendix BIV.
[suman ade] magic arts; ye as., to practise magic. Acts 19,19.
pl. asúmãnfó, the owner of a charm; one who understands how to make amulets and sells them; sorcerer, magician; onipa a asumaŋ pii nè as. ahɔɔdeŋ wɔ ne nsam'; wizard. Lev. 19,31. 20,6.
Ak.: ɔkɔ n'as., (he died), he is dead; ɔkɔɔ n'as., he died; cf. sumãŋ 2.
asúmãŋ-sém, sorcery, witchcraft, magic, enchantment; di as., to use magic arts. Acts 8,9.
sorcery, witchcraft, magic, enchantment; di as., to use magic arts. Acts 8,9.
s. aduasã.

oath; the great oath of kings. pr. 1314. 3161. 3373; kã nt., to swear, to take an oath; kã ntaŋhunu, to swear falsely; wɔmã no nt., they put him on his oath; ogye nt., he desires to swear an oath; wode ntam gye no mã ɔkã, they impose an oath upon him, permit him to swear an oath. 2 Chron. 6,22; fa ntám gyè mé na meŋkã! = mesẽre ntám; upon this the kyẽame says: kã Wukúda è! and the defendant or plaintiff says: meká! - kwae nt., to dispense from an obligation undertaken upon oath; tɔ nt., to disregard or transgress an the neglect or transgression of an oath. pr. 3316. - On the nature and significance of an oath in the sense of a Tshi man, s. Cruickshank, Eighteen Years on the Gold Coast. vol. I. p. 256-268. When one swears by a king or chief, he mentions a place or day which refers to the most calamitous event in the life of that chief or his forefathers or his tribe, whereby the said chief, in order to avoid a similar calamity, is prompted to look well to the matter which occasioned the oath, and to claim the forfeit due by him who disregards or acts contrary to the oath. The great oath of the kings of Asante is "Méméneda Kòromantẽ"; that of the king of Akuapem "Wukúda nè Sókodéi"; in a similar way certain companies (asafo) have their peculiar oaths, e.g. Akũropɔŋ Asɔŋkofo ntam ne "Yawda". - Obosom nni ntam, gye se wofre no bɔ wo hɔ dua, a fetish will not answer to an oath unless the person invoking it curses himself. Cf. bɔ 81. - 'Agyá ntám' ne se wokã kyere onipa biara se: meká wo sé naŋ anasɛ wó sé amannehunu n. a, se di asem yi mã me; - na se wuse: "meká wo sé, meká wo ní" a, en'de na woayaw no, 'father's oath', i.e. you say to anybody: I swear by your father's leg or sufferings, &c., that you should help me to settle this matter; - but if you say (with thumbs stretched out): "I swear by your father or your mother", you insult him. [ta, asüaanu] a weight of or for gold = 1 1/2 peredwane, 54 dollars or ackies, 3 3/8 ounces, £ 12. 3s.
inf. the act of watching women to see their secret parts, a shameful deed formerly punished with death. Cf. tasú.
As. a two-edged sword; ŋkrante anofànu.
adv. imitative of the setting of steps: gye, gyigye or yɛ (abofra) t., to lead (a little child) by the arms or in leading strings.

red. v. taa, 1. s. taa 4. 11. - 2. to be filled or swollen with water; n'ani atáatàa (nsú), tears have filled his eyes; watáatàa, he has the dropsy [G. efufüi, he is swollen all over]; ne naŋ ase at., he has the dropsy in his feet.

ataatâ, n-, inf. dropsy; ɔyare a ɛmã onipa hoŋhon ne naŋ akwaa so a. s. hōnam nyinaa, na ɛwɔ ho wɔ ho a, na ne baabi atu kuru na nsu fim' (sẽwa bi tow wo hō a eseŋ nsu pii). - mmofra at., dropsy attacking children; it causes their faces or feet to swell; ɛmã woŋ naŋ a. s. woŋ anim hoŋhon.
ataatâ, inf. [taa]: di at., to run after each other in turns, in play or with hostile intentions.
ntaatá, Akp. = ntatáwá.
[obsol.] = tatrãä.
in succession; one after another; cf. atáatâ.
1. a. plain, level, flat; mfuwa t. so, open, cultivated land. - 2. ɛ, n. a plain, an open field, level land; t. mu, t. so, syn. apaa-so, apaw-so; t. yi, woadow mu; Asantefo nim t. mu kō.
ntaatáá [taa mu, Ak. tɛ mu, to patch] a patch; pieces of cloth of different stuff; waye ne ntama mu nt., ofura nt, ntama, he wears a cloth patched with pieces of other stuff.
[ata] male twins.
a. wide, extensive, large; syn. tètɛree, hãhrãä, koküroo, paradada; sare t., an extensive plain, prairie or wilderness.
a climbing plant from which blacking is made; kwae mu hama bi; woboro no de no kã mpaboá hō mã ɛye tumm.
a. 1. plain, level; asasetáw, a plain;
level land; s. tataw. - 2. worthless, unsatisfying; mere; without anything else; syn. hunu, - aduaŋ-táw, a meal without meat or fish.
v. Akw. = taa. - taw, Akw. = taa, tawa, tobacco.

a push with the hand by the neck (or any part of the body); ópò no táw, he pushes him by the neck; wòpoo no taw hwee fam'; po .. anim t., to disregard, slight; syn. tew ahĩ. ntaw-ntáw, quarrel, angry contest, brawl, altercation, contention, dispute; wodi nt. s. wonè bi nyã asɛm na morɛyaw na mope akõ; syn. (di) akamekame, (di) twẽ-mã-mentwẽ, (ye) akasakasa.
taá, atáa, ataá.
fire to light a pipe with; orebetew abofra no na wakofá no t., he is about to take away the boy to make him his servant.
taasɛŋ.
pr. n. a male or female born next after twins. pr. 3145f; cf. Ata.
tile; brick. - ntáyáá = ntannaa, a creeping (or trailing) plant. te..., ti..., is changed into tse..., tsi..., in Fante words.
v. Ak. = 1. tew; - wo ani bɛte = wo ani bɛbere. - 2. tɛ so = taa so, to level; sesɛw so.
tew, ntɛw. pr. 3210.
adv. imitative of the sound of rending, breaking or tearing (in two): hama no atew té; the string broke at once; cf. wa, wɛ. pr. 3037.

v. contin. [red. tète, tètee], F. tse, 1. to sit; to be in a place, dwell, live, to have one's regular and lasting abode in a place: cf. wɔ, da; correl. v. trã, ba, kɔ, betrã, kɔtrã (Gr. § 102,3); mète abŭrogua so, I am sitting on a chair; ote daŋ mu, he is sitting in the house; ote me nifã, he is sitting in the my right hand; ote pɔŋkɔ so, he is sitting on a horse, i.e. riding. pr. 2708. - ote teaseɛnam mu, he is sitting in a chariot, i.e. riding in a carriage; - anomaa te afirim', the bird is in a snare. pr. 2479; - kŭrow yi sũa, mmusũa abiesã pɛ na ete m(u), this village is small, only three families live in it; mmoa bebree te asase so, ebinom nso te nsum', many animals live on land, some also live in the water; onipa te asase so ketewa bi na owu, man lives a short time on earth, and dies. pr. 2065. 3195-3202. - te hɔ, te ase (pl. tete ase. 1 Thess. 4,17), to live, exist; Onyankõpɔŋ te hɔ or tɛ ase dáa; correl. v. trã, trã ase; - ote ne hɔ̃ so, ote ne hố ase, he is independent. - 2. to be with respect to quality, to be in a certain state; correl. v. ye (Gr. § 102, 4. 209, 1. 255,5); wote sɛ me, you are as I am; ohoho te sɛ abofra, a stranger is like a child; senea afõa te na boha te, as the sword is, so is the scabbard. pr. 1410f. 1837. 2893; - ete sa, so it is; ete sɛ amaŋ abieŋ yi tumi sɛ, the power of these two states is almost equal. - wo hố tɛ déŋ? how are you? mète yiyè, I am well; onipa a ote sɛ (or onte sɛ) na wawu yi such a man (who scarcely had his equal) is now dead! ade a ente sɛɛ, an unusual thing, something unusual. - 3. to be.. by nature, to be naturally..: ete sɛ ete ara, it is common, ordinary; it is unchangeable; enté sɛ ete bio, it has been altered, changed, perverted from its natural state, has degenerated. K. § 149f.; yɛbea a ete, the natural use; yɛbea a ente, the use which is against nature. Rom. 1,26.

v. [red. teté], F. tse, 1. to perceive by the nerves of sensation, to feel; to perceive within one's self, to be affected by; also to be felt or perceived by; wò abaa a woabɔ me no anté me, (or) mante koraa, the blow you gave me with your rod, I did not feel at all; otee ne hõnam mu sɛ ne yare no asã. Mk. 5,29. - aduru no ante no, or, wante ad. no, the medicine did not produce any effect on him. pr. 17. - asɛm no ante no = anyɛ no de, the matter did not please him. - te.. sɛ ase = yɛ de, to taste good; ètè wəŋ' sɛ asé = eye wəŋ de, they like

it &c. .. te.. mã, to sympathize with: métè wo yaw memã wo, I feel your pain with you, I sympathize or have compassion with you in your grief. - 2. to perceive by the taste: menté mako a ose ode agum' no, I do not taste the pepper he says he has put in (in cooking the food); also to be felt or perceived by the taste; ŋkyene antém' the salt is not to be tasted in it, it is not sufficiently salted. - nsã, mmekwaŋ no ate me dew mu, the palm-wine, the palm-soup, is palatable to me, tastes sweet. - 3. to perceive by the smell, to smell, com. used with ŋkã, hũã: opete te funu ŋkã, the vulture smells a carcass; mete aduan no hũã, I smell the food; mahũam taa no mate se eye, I have smelled the tobacco and found it good. - 4. to perceive by the ears, to hear: wote dɔŋ ana? do you hear the bell? gyeegye no nti menté n'asem; mete se akokonini reboŋ, I hear a cock crowing. In the imp. tie is used, pr. 2601. - 5. te asem, to obey; onté ne nã asem, he does not obey his mother. pr. 581. - 6. te, te asé, to understand; menté asém no ase, I do not understand the meaning of the word. pr. 347. 3205f.; the perf. mate is often said in reply to a command or request, involving not only that the person understands what is meant, but also his willingness to do what is desired: I have understood it and shall do accordingly. - 7. maté masie, I thought so beforehand, I anticipated that it would be or come so. pr. 3203. - 8. Phr. te mu dew, to enjoy the pleasure or benefit of. pr. 484. Heb. 11, 25. - 9. átém', it is well mixed (said of colours).
tew. pr. 1910.
a certain tree.

1. a film, membraneous covering on the pupil of the eye, a disease of the eye, cataract, perh. also glaucoma, amaurosis, leucoma (albugo); ade ku-rukuruwa bi a enyiŋ wo aniwa so; aboa a ewɔ wo ani so [kurutiayisi], ekum no wie na ne nyinaa ye fitaa a, na wo ani ŋhũ ade bio. pr. 2295. 2301. - ete asi (no so, or) n'ani so, he has (got) a cataract, has become blind with a cataract. pr. 3628. - ete atu afi n'ani so, he has been cured of his cataract. - 2. fig. woŋ ani so té(w) atew, the object of their contention has been removed, their quarrel has been settled.
a cushion, bolster or covering of leather, with various figures, e.g. for kings, to sit on; cf. sumii; - bu ate, to make or sew such a chair-cushion. - opoŋkó-até, saddle.
to make wide, open wide; watsɛ n'anom = wahãŋ n'anom. Prov. 13, 3. - s. red. tɛɛtɛe.
a beetle covered with small dots (emitting an offensive smell); bug? tē, tēē, teeē: ode sɔ tɛɛ (=twom) he snaps, snatches or catches it up or away. Cf. hwim.

a., adv. straight, -ly, -way; uprightly, honestly; ōnam tɛɛ, he walks straight on or along, straightforward, moves in a straight line; wonam tɛɛ reba ne ŋkyɛŋ, they moved on directly to him; they hurried up to him; dua no nyiŋ tɛɛ, the tree grows straight; n'asem nam kwaŋmu tɛɛ = n'asem tɛɛ pe, he is upright or honest in his dealings; me nè nokware apkɔ tɛɛ. pr. 3211; - immediate. K. § 6.
n. straightness; uprightness; frankness: né tɛɛ ye me ŋwɔŋwâ; cf. tɛɛ, trɛnee, tɛɛtye.
duaseé, duásò, kãseé, mãŋkyiri, teasee; cf. tia, tiafi.
tɛatɛaa, pl. ntɛaa, ntɛaa-ntɛaa, a. narrow, small; thin, slender, slight, lean; close, tight, strait; ŋkwaŋ, poma, tenã, atenã, tsɛaba, atsɛa. Mt. 7, 13. 14. Cf. hĩhĩa, mũamũaa, hwɛahwɛaa.
a species of cashew tree and its edible fruit; Anacardium occidentale. Cf. átɔaã.
[te, to feel] a cheerless, comfortless, dull, dismal place. pr. 1491; ɔkɔ ant., he is going to the dogs.
tiafi.
[nea wate na okose] tale-bearer; ɔye at. = óyè ófàkɔ nè fába, ohetie nsem kokã na okotie bi bekã. Ote-anaŋkã-nnuro, a nickname for Kwame.
inf. understanding. F. ntsease. Mt. 15, 16. Prov. 2, 3; cf. asete, asehū, ghūase, ŋhūmu.
pl. n- [wote ase a, ɛnam] carriage, wagon, coach &c., cf. kudɔɔ. - t.-kãfɔ, wagoner. - teaséɛnam-náŋ, wagon-wheel, carriage-wheel.
ɔye t., she is dead while she lives (1 Tim. 5, 6) = ote ho de, nanso te se wawu ara ne sa.

pl. a- [te ase] 1. an inhabitant of the earth, mortal, man, human being. pr. 1125. 2545 f. 2764. 2855; cf. odesãni, onipa. - 2. a living person; opp. owufo, osãmãŋ. pr. 3215. - in appos. living: Onyame teasefo, the living God. - 3. one sitting on the ground. pr. 3214. - 4. one living on his estate, tilling the ground, opp. onantefo. pr. 2104.
tebea 2. K. § 237.
1. a place of existence, abode; cf. trãbea, trãbere, trãbew. - 2. manner or quality; nature; condition; rank; appearance. Lk. 9, 29; cf. su, baŋ; dibea.
Ak. = tew-bea,
a certain tree good for fuel; dua kwadaa bi, eye ogya.

a food prepared of plantains (with or without palm-oil); obrɔde buŋ a wɔanɔa apɔtɔw nè ŋŋo anase ŋŋo nni so; akunafo nso, wósiw bi dì; wɔŋ de, wóde brɔdɛ̀ kòkɔɔ na èyè wɔŋ dè, wófré nò patiransĩaw. Cf. ntem-merefu(w)a, & osibaw.
a doughy, dough-baked, tough; né dɔkɔno ye t. = asɔ hūãŋ.

ntɛbɔ́, existence, manner of living, behaviour, conduct, = nneyɛe (wɔbra wo kasam' a, na wofre nneyɛe no se nt.); mahū wo nt. mu, I have seen through your dealings = mahū wo akyi, mahū wo nneyɛe a woye nyinaa; Onyankɔpɔŋ nim me nt. nyinaa mu, God knows all my ways (me trim' oo, me nneyɛem' oo). pr. 1119.
[dua a woatɛw] 1. a planted tree: asubɔnteŋ hō t. (Ps. 1, 3). Isa. 61, 3. - 2. sucker, layer.

v. red. [tɛ́tɛɛ], F. tsɛ, tsɛa, Ak. tene, 1. a) to be straight (pr. 998), right, direct, even, level; b) to be erect, upright, right; c) to be right, correct; d) to be plain, straightforward, honest, righteous, just; e) to be fit, suitable; to fit, suit; f) to seem or appear to be right or correct; n'asem tɛɛ pe, he is perfectly upright or honest in his doings; he is quite right in what he says; his cause is quite righteous one; etɛɛ (etené) se beŋ, it is as straight as an arrow, fig. it is quite correct; etɛɛ mè = ekɔ me ntep; n'asem a orekã yi tɛɛ me; what'he says seems to me to be right. - 2. to flow, take its course; nsū no atɛɛ, the water is flowing along (though perhaps in curves). - 3. to make straight, straighten. pr. 1011; to stretch, stretch out, extend: ɔtɛɛ nè nsá, he stretches out his hand; but: ne nsá tɛ́ɛ, he is a good marksman (e. g. in throwing stones), s. nsa; mesore matɛɛ me mu, I am getting up to stretch my back; mekotɛtɛe me naŋ mu or m'apow mu, I am going to take a walk for exercise (= mekopase) or do gymnastics; mekotɛɛ me mù, I am going to stretch myself, i. e. lie down on a bed or couch; cf. twè ne mu; ɔtɛɛ ne mu tu mirika, he runs with his whole body extended to its full length (cf. Phil. 3, 13); ɔtɛɛ ne hō kasa, he speaks adroitly, in an adroit manner; akoa yi atɛɛ ne hō akasa = wakã ne nsem nyinaa akwaŋso-akwaŋso. - tɛɛ obonto, to bring a boat into the right course. - tɛɛ mrɛtɛ ano, to cut a board straight. - 4. to cause to form straight lines; to direct, train, exercise, drill: t. asrãfo, to drill soldiers. - 5. tɛɛ so, to rectify, correct; to set right, lead into or show the right way; to instruct, advise, admonish; to chasten, chastise, castigate, discipline; ɔtɛɛ no só; mã 32*
mentɛɛ wo so, allow me to correct a misstatement! 6. tɛ́ɛm', red. tɛ́ɛ-tɛ́ɛm', to cry out (Gr. § 214); F. tsɛam, tsɛatsɛa mu, Mt. 27,23. Mk. 15,13. 14; cf. bɔm', paem'. 7. ɔtɛɛ no, he shouts at him.
Okw. a small grey bird living in a flock; cf. atiebia.
inf. cry, crying.
inf. correction, instruction, discipline, chastisement.
red. v. 1. s. tɛe 3-6. 2. to cry at somebody, to threaten, rail, reproach. F. tsɛa, to rebuke (Mt. 8,26), to chasten.
inf. threat, threatenings.
= ntɛɛm'.
pl. n-, cockroach, a beetle of the genus Blatta, Blatta orientalis; cf. kakaraka. tɛfere Yáá (said in fun). téfɛrɛ-yám, s. yam, ringworm.
one who hears, hearer.
s. sótefó, mútefó.
(pl. a-) a righteous, upright person; syn. ɔtrɛneeni.
brɔde, ode or amãŋkãni of the first crop.
okasa nè né ntégyaw, s. okasa.
the climber which yields the seeds called ntew, q. v.
F. ntohwire, 1. a gap between the teeth; cf. gyaw; t. da né sěm'; yare t., pr. 2279. 2. a gap-toothed person; onipa a né sě atu na ɔkwaŋ dam'.
F.; ntehyéwá, Ak. = tetê, asthma.
malt, malt-dust; abŭrow a wɔabuw mã afĩ na wɔasiw de nsu ahono de asi gya so de akosi hɔ, na ade bɛkyɛ na akaw, na wɔsaŋ nɔa bio, na wɔtɔŋ.
[nea ɛtewe or ɔtewe nti ɛkaa mu] omission; ɔkasa nè ne nt... , I have forgotten to mention ..; cf. ɔkasa.

[tɛw, kaŋ]: di..t., to prevent or thwart another person's secret intentions, insidious acts or waylayings; yɛadi no t. ammã wannyã nea ɔkohwehwee no (ɛ.s. obi pɛ sɛ ɔkodi asɛm bi hintaw yɛn na yeanyã ntɛm akosiw no kwaŋ), we have got the start of him to hinder him carrying out his purpose.
= takaa.
[G. short] a short-legged fowl.
F. = ntakara.
inf. [te, to hear, kɔ, to go] talebearing.
pl. a-, talebearer; reporter; ɔyɛ ɔt. = ɔyɛ tékɔ, he is a talebearer; cf. ateakosewa.
hickup, hiccough; t. asi me, the h. has befallen me, I have the h.; also: kɔkotékɔ. [G. fukofukɔ, hikohikɔ fele].
pl. n-, a bag or sack plaited like a mat, from a kind of grass or reed, larger than "pae"; wobobɔ ano a, ɛyɛ yiye, it may be rolled up. pr. 3216. - tekreyiwá [dim.] a small bag &c. Cf. kyerɛŋkyɛ.

Ak. F. tekyerɛmã, F. gyerɛmã, tongue (t. de sakramã). pr. 360. 769 ff. 2415. 3217-28. 3407. - abŭrow t. the germ of a grain (of maize). Phr. wɔde t. to abogyɛ(ɛ) mu, they bring the palaver to an end. - tɛkrɛmã-afɔá, -afãná: otwitwa me t., he rebukes me sharply, severely. 2 Cor. 23,10. - tɛkrɛmã-béré: ɔyɛ t., he has a soft, gentle, humble, modest tongue, speaks softly &c. - tɛkrɛmãbútúw, stammering; ɔyɛ a, s. oyare t., he stammers, mispronounces single letters = ɔkasa mătãmătã, cf. ópò dódów.
pl. a-, 1. liar, cf. ɔtorofo; braggart; flatterer; babbler. pr. 3229; man of evil tongue. Ps. 140,12; enchanter. Eccl. 10,11. - 2. a dainty-mouthed, lickerish fellow, lover of titbits; cf. ɔnomdewfo.
a wound caused by the tongue, i.e. by cutting words.
-kyére, [tɛkrɛmã a ɛye tongue, flattery; ɔto no t. (= ɔkã asɛm frɛmfrem kyerɛ no, nanso nea ɔrebɛye de, ɛwɔ ne tirim = wakoto no sɛmmãradã) he entices him by fair, mild, flattering words].
flattering speech, he decoys him with honeyed words; cf. anode, anodefedeɛ. - t-tófó, flatterer.
the root of the tongue.
lingual sparring. pr. 1581.

sudden anger, choler, violent passion: ósè ot. (ote asɛm biara a na ne bo afuw), he is passionate, so as to condemn at first hearing and, as it were, to kill in his mind without giving room for defence.
pl. id. plash, pool, puddle; morass, marsh, swamp, fen, bog; osu toto a, at Akyem kwaŋ mu bebree; cf. dontorí, dɛŋkyɛdɛŋkyɛ, tàkaa. pr. 2630.
Ak. F. = tɛkrɛmã. Mk. 7,33. 35. Ps. 39,1.

v. [red. tentɛm] 1. to become silent, still, quiet, to be overawed; me hɔ hũ nti wátɛm = osuro me nti wayɛ komm; ɔbene yerenom twam' a, Kumase atɛm diŋŋ. - 2. to be or stand on one's guard, in expectation of, in cautious readiness for; me nè no rekɔkɔ no na watɛntɛm dedaw ansã-na miduu hɔ, when I went to fight with him, he stood awaiting me in silent readiness, before I arrived there. - 3. to tread cautiously (on a slippery way): sɛ wonam ɔkwaŋ a eso yɛ toro sɔ a, wotentɛm a.s. wutintim wo awɛrew yiye na woanwatiriw aŋhwe ase (cf. tam tam).
te mu; - átɛm', s. te 9.
di .. at., to insult, abuse, revile; odi me (wodidi me) atɛm, s. di 70. pr. 1862. 2835.

quickness, swiftness, velocity, speed, haste, rapidity. pr. 102. 1210; ntɛm yɛ, nà ɔgõm yɛ, quickness is good and slowness is good, i.e. each in its proper time and place. pr. 622. 1931; pɛ ntɛm, to be in haste. pr. 127; ne ntɛm-bone a ɔkɔpe, his unadvised haste. - adv. with haste, in haste, fast, quick, quickly, swiftly, speedily, rapidly, early, soon, immediately; ntɛm! ntɛm! mɔŋkɔ mo tràbere! quick! quick! to your seats! bɛra ntɛm! come quickly; woaba ntɛm nne, you have come soon to-day; woama ntɛm, you are (have come,) late; yɛ ntɛm, mã enye ntɛm, make haste, be quick! gye ntɛm, to hasten. Eccl. 1,5. ntɛm ara, adv. id., with all speed; immediately, forthwith; ntɛm ara a woye-ebé'yé (= woye a ebeye yiye), with all possible speed, as soon as possible. ntɛm-ntɛm(-ntɛm), adv. id., with the greatest speed, hurriedly; cf. hwim-hwim. - ntɛm-pá, betimes, in good time, early, soon; ne mmusu reye nt., his adversity hastens fast. Jer. 48,16. ntɛm-pɛ, inf. haste, hastiness, speediness, precipitation. 2 Kg. 7,15. ntɛm-sò, hastily, speedily; in haste, in a hurry. - ntɛm-yɛ, inf. haste, speed, quickness.
Ak. ntommorofu(w)a, a certain food prepared of yam or plantains (with or without palm-oil); s. nteberefu(w)a.
a certain bead (of a red-dish colour); s. ahene.
[atɛŋ, fã, enu]: yi at., to hear and try or prove the statements of both parties.
= atɛŋ bone, false judgment, s. ntɛŋkyew.
[atɛŋ, pa] good judgment; wise counsels. Prov. 24,6. 1,5; obu at., he gives a righteous judgment; ɔwɔ at., he has a sound judgment.
pl. a-, highway, main road; a way or path frequented at all times, on which you always meet persons. pr. 1900. 2080. 3230.
atɛŋbú, inf. [bu ntɛŋ], F. atsɛmbu., atsenbua, the act of judging, judgment.
court-day; day of judgment. Mt. 10,15. - atɛmmu-dé, rights, manner. 1 Sam. 8,9; judgments. Ps. 119,7. Ezek. 18,9.
-akɔŋguá, judgment seat. John 19, 13. Mt. 27,19.
pl. a-, judge; umpire, arbiter, arbitrator, referee; cf. ɔsennifo.
jurisprudence, the science
v. [red. tentèŋ] 1. t. ani, to rest on the surface of any fluid, to float, swim, be buoyed up; wode dua to nsum' na eŋkɔ ase a, wuse: èteŋ ani. — 2. red. to sit in a kingly manner; akoá yi, wàtènteŋ.
a., adv. full to the brim, brimful; nsu aye ahina no mã teŋn; wòhyehyeɛ ŋhina no mã tenteŋn; wohye me nsã no a, mã énye tèŋn.
pl. a-, a species of stinging fly, conops, horse-fly, ox-fly, gad-fly; tsetse. pr. 596. 3231. = ohurii; cf. akekawere. [G. ofɔi].
a certain insect; ne hɔ seŋ nteŋ, ne hɔ ye hare seŋ nteŋ, he is very nimble or quick.

n., F. ateŋ, ntseŋ, 1. charge, accusation, imputation; statement; grievance, complaint, expostulation; yi at. or nt. (= woyi nt., e.s. nnipa baanu de wɔŋ asem abehyiam' na worekekà), to prefer a charge or charges against another or each other, put forth a case for transaction; to charge with or accuse of having done something amiss or neglected a duty; to remonstrate or expostulate with, to reprimand, reproach, reprove, censure; to convict. Ja. 2,9; oyi no nteŋ pe se asem a atɔ ɔnè no ntam' no, wokã na woyi fi hɔ; oyii no nteŋ se edeŋ nti na ɔmma ne ŋkyeŋ bio; nea oyi nteŋ no pe omaŋ-korakórá; cf. bɔ ŋkūro; - twa nteŋ, to have a long talk, to tell a long story. — 2. decision, verdict, judicial determination, judgment, sentence; bekyere ateŋ no mã yentie, let us now hear the decision! ateŋ no (ateŋ a wobui no) anye no' dè, this decision did not please him; - bu at. or nt., to decide a case, to pronounce judgment, to judge, give or pass sentence on; woabu no asem no mu nt., they have passed judgment on him in that case or concerning the matter; cf. di asem, bu fɔ, bu bem; Asantetéŋ, pr. 740; ananateŋ, nteŋkyew, atempa, ntentrẽnee.
a certain charm; sumaŋ a wode tɔ aduru; cf. sãbe. pr. 1663.

(in connection with twa), with one stroke; otwaa duaa no t., he cut the shrub with one stroke; asɛm no twaa ne yam' t., the matter grieved him very much.

[red. s. tenteŋ] only in cpds.; 1. long-stretched, long, high, tall; cf. banteŋ, ɔbeteŋ, abɔnteŋ, oguanteŋ, nufuteŋ, asuteŋ. — 2. right, regular, true, real, genuine, syn. trẽnee, trodoo; cf. obɔfotéŋ, abūrotéŋ, onipatéŋ, ntáteŋ. Cf. tẽe, tene, tẽe, trẽnee.

(straightness, straightly, straight, right &c.): 1. kɔ ntēŋ, to be straight, right, correct, convenient, agreeable: eŋkó nt., it is not correct, not good (e.g. to say 'ahunum' for 'ahuŋmu'); it will not do; èko me nt. = etẽe me, it suits me, I find it suitable, think it right; aduaŋ yi, nsu yi kɔ me nt. = eye me de, this food, this water is agreeable to me, I relish it. — 2. tu ntēŋ, F. ntene, to go (on) straight away, straightway, straight forward, to advance; ɔtrãã hyeŋ mu fi Roma tuu nteŋ kɔɔ Kartago, he sailed straightway from Rome to Carthage; woko yi, tu nteŋ ara hwe wo anim na wobehū, when you go, always look straight before you, then you will find it.

righteous judgment; bu nt., to judge righteously; s. atɛn.

[yi atɛn] 1. the act of remonstrating &c.; remonstrance, expostulation, rebuke, reproof (2 Tim. 3,16), reprimand; cf. ŋkurobo. - 2. = atanyi, a payment of money imposed as a punishment for an offence, a fine, mulct (sika a wogye wɔ ntama a ŋkurofo tɔ mu;) ŋheŋkwaá gyigye ŋkurofo hɔ at. dı (ŋheŋkwaa no, asɛm a ɛnye asɛm no, mprempren na woamã adaŋ asɛm 'na woagye sika adi).

a sterile or barren spot, place or tract of land; baabi a ɛhɔ biribiara nnyin yiye, ɛhɔ sare nyin tenteŋ beye nammoŋ pe, na enti wode to asase biara a aduan nyé yiye wɔ hɔ. Cf. ŋkuro-tɛpá, ŋkuraa-tɛpá.

stara, Ky. expression of consent = ɛte sa, se ɛte ara, so it is! true!
a species of singing bird of a yellowish colour, larger than the canary.

tèw, v. [red. tetew], F. tsɛw, Ak. te, 1. tr., to tear: dadewa no atɛw m'atadɛm' tokuru, the nail has torn a hole in my coat. 2. to tear off, pluck off: t. aduaŋ. pr. 3212. - t. hama, to (tear) pull off a (piece of) string. pr. 2530. - to break (hama, asawa, a cord, thread); cf. 13. - t. akutu, to pluck off an orange; to gather (grapes). Deut. 24,21; tew nsã, to take ('collect') palm-wine, removing the vessels from under the felled trees; when several vessels are emptied, tɛtɛw is used; cf. ɛbɔm', ɔdɔdɔbɛŋ; tɛtɛw ahaban. pr. 3242. 1909. - wotew akɔkɔɔ mã wo hō dodo, lit. you take the red (fruits) too readily for yourself (leaving the green or unripe to others), i. e. you talk big, you boast. - tew .. so, to deduct; to abate something from a price. pr. 3213; tɛw mè só kàkrá, sell it a little cheaper! make a slight reduction! - ɔtɛw anoma no ti, he wrings off the bird's head. Lev. 1,15. - wotew abofra no ti bɔɔ dua = wotew abofra no fi ne nã hō de ti pem dua mã owui, they tore the child from its mother and dashed its head against a tree.
3. to tear open, to open: metew m'ani, I open my eyes, cf. 7 & bue; tew nsɔano, to open a seal.

4. to rend asunder, break in two: t. akutu no mu, divide the orange into two halves! b) to break through: makɔ tɛtɛw mu, I have fought my way through (the enemy). Cf. 8. 11; ɔhweam tew faa ɔdaŋ no hō, the stream or current forced its way by the side of that house. Lk. 6,48f.

5. intr. to be torn, to break, rend, burst: me ntama atew or atetew, my dress is torn. pr. 3241. - ahene tew, the string of beads breaks. pr. 1319. - hama, asawa no atew, the cord, thread is broken; ɛso atew, a piece is (or has been) torn off.

6. to sever, become separated, break loose, run off: akutu at., stɔɔ me ti(ri) so, an orange has dropped from the tree, it fell on my head; ne guaŋ atew, his sheep has broken loose. pr. 1906. - tew hwɛ, to fall off (e. g. from a bicycle); tew hwe ase or fam', to fall down.

7. to open (pr. 1910), perf. be open (cf. 3); n'ani atew, his eyes are open, fig. he is sensible, intelligent, prudent, sagacious, cunning, subtile, shrewd (syn. waben); he is civilized. — 8. tew mu kɔ, to dissociate oneself, to part, withdraw, depart. 1 Cor. 7,15; tetew mu, intr. to part, separate, be disunited, fall out with one another; ɔnè wɔŋ tt. mu. — 9. to rend: of clouds; osu atew, the rain-clouds have cleared or passed away; hence: to become free from clouds or fog, to clear, clear up, brighten, to become fine; perf. to be clear; fig. to be serene; ŵim or ɔsoro atew, the weather or sky has cleared up; ɔdaŋ yi hɔ atew, the apartment has become light; ɛhɔ atew, the place has been lighted up. pr. 33. — 10. hɔ tew, lit. the outside is clear or clean, free from spots or blemish: oguaŋ yi hɔ tew, this sheep is without blemish (ne hɔ nye taŋ wɔ ɔyare biara hɔ, ɔnyare yare biara): ɔbaa yi hɔ tew, this woman is handsome; — hence: to be morally clean or pure, to be blameless, holy.
