to nt., to stagger; tɔ obaa hɔ nt., to be ravished or entranced with a woman. Prov. 5,20. — F. bɔ nt., to recoil. Cf. mĩmpã. — ntíntíŋ-tś, inf. staggering. Isa. 51,17.

red. v. s. tim, 1. to be impressed: n'asèpàteré ase nnàdewá tintim hó (mĩamía hɔ), the marks of the nails on the soles of his shoes are impressed or to be seen there; to become or be steadfast. 1 Cor. 15,58. — (de..) t., to establish. Ps. 78,5. 89,3.5. — ode n'aniwa t. wɔy so mã bone, he sets his eyes upon them for evil. Am. 9,4. — 2. (= tim 4) to hold fast, with or without one's consent; to force; to prevail against. Job 15,24. — 3. t.. so, to keep close together; wotintim' sika no so. — 4. t. ŋhoma (so), to print a book, to imprint. — 5. otintim' n'anim (ɔye n'anim biribi-biribi se ɔde yi obi hũ), he makes a bold or fierce face to frighten somebody, he tries to carry out his intentions in an arbitrary manner; ot. n'anim kɔe, he went presumptuously. Deut. 1,43; ot. n'anim se ɔye onipa-trẽnee, he feigns to be a just man. Lk. 20,20. — tintim yiye oo! = hwɛ yiye oo! take care!
inf.: (ŋhoma) t. a edi kaŋ, the first edition or impression of a book.
pr. 3385, = otuntumma.
stability; ɔyare no agye nt., that sickness has become epidemic.
di nt. = di asénníni, cf. di 53.
inf. arbitrariness, arrogance, violence, outrage.
printed letter(s).
inf. perseverance, persistance.
inf.: ot. na ɔretintim me without showing me a reason for doing so.
inf. [otintim no gye ne nsam' (sika), he holds him fast till he gets it from him] extortion, exaction. Ezek. 45,9.
a stupid person; cf. ototonto.
= tie oo, muntie oo! attend! listen to me! a call for silence when a person desires to address a multitude.
s. eti 11 c.
adv. suddenly, all of a sudden; ɔsoree ara t. na ognaŋ kɔe.
[eti a apa] 1. baldness of the head, bald-headedness. — 2. a baldhead; onipa t., a bald-headed man. F. o-tipaa, pl. a-. Cf. hɔpae.
inf. [ti pae] head-ache; syn. atibeŋ. pr. 3273.
a foolish person, fool.
a certain bird which feeds on ɔfontobiaa.
[con. ne típeŋ] equality in size. pr. 1018; wónnyinàgyina hó típéŋ sò, they shall stand out, line up, arrange themselves, according to size.
pl. id. [con. né típénfó] a person of equal size with another, or, persons of equal size.
inf. a fighting for, or defence of, one's own head or life, self-defence; cf. tigye; anyamesem ye at., by keeping to the word of God we save our own selves.
inf.: di at., to knock the heads together; s. pira, di 90.
wɔbo no at. = woyi ne ti koraa, they shave (the whole of) his head.
As. s. nti.
n'ani ye no nt. = n'ani ye no tɔtɔtɔ, he is in perplexity.
[atiri enu, two heads] a species of serpent, amphisbaena.
= nteresu, - tiri, s. nti.
pl. a- [con. ne tíri] s. e-ti; tiri hōnam, s. ɔhōnam.
pl. a-, a head of cowries, i. e. fifty strings of cowries, cf. ɔbaŋ, ɔtramatiri.

fever, espec. intermittent fever, ague; prop. the aching of the head, but cf. atibɛŋ, atipae, awɔw. [G. atridii, atúrùdíí]; at. abɔ no, he is feverish; he has fever; me hōnam mu yɛ me atiridii-atiridii, I feel (or am) feverish. — atíridíí-bárímá, at.-níni, at.-as(é)-rãŋ, malarial fever; a dangerous kind of fever; a severe attack of fever with delirium. — at.-barima n. a, abɔ no, he has an attack of malarial fever &c.
inf. [gye tiri] Ak. = atigye.

tiri mù, s. eti 1. 9. 12 & tsirim, ntisirim, F. - pr. 3274 f.; ɔdaŋ tirim, the gable-end of a house; wonyã kyeŋ odaŋ no anim nè akyiri (de) a, na wode rekɔ ne tírim' nè ne tirim; ne tirim nè tirim hōnom, its two gable-ends; - also of geographical situation: Nnoŋko tirim nohō na Saraha wo, Salaga lies far behind where the Donko-country begins. - ne t. a ɔbɔbo, his thoughts, plans, designs, devices. Ps. 146,4; woy t. mmaa adwene, they have not yet any judgment of their own. [con. ne tirim]. - tírim'-adwéne, device(s), inventions. Eccl. 7,29.
pl. a-, 50 strings of cowries = 1s.; cf. otiri.
(one who has) a scar on the head. pr. 589.
s. ɔkekaw 2.
vexation, irritation, mortification; ɛyɛe no at. = anyé no abɔdwo, it displeased or vexed him exceedingly.
inf. [kyere 5] perplexity.
[s. eti 12 Af] cruelty, inhumanity, barbarity; brutality; inhuman or pitiless treatment. pr. 1423; implacability; ɔbɔ me at., he is hard, cruel &c. with me; cf. bɔ 107.
pl. a-, a hard, cruel, inhuman person, barbarian. pr. 3276.
cruel and barbarous deeds, cruelties.
-sém, manners of a barbarian, inhumanity; violence. Ps. 72, 14. [plan, plot.
a design, device, scheme,

[tirim' asem] the (secret) thoughts. pr. 1773.3277; wodi at., they are on terms of intimacy with each other; they make an agreement with each other. 1 Kg. 1,7. - at.-di, inf. being on terms of intimacy with somebody, knowing his (secret) thoughts or plans; counsel, plan. Job 29,4.
inf. causing emotion; eye at., it would drive one mad.
Ak. head-money &c.; cf. ti-sika.
place of skulls; cf. nitiriso. Isa. 8, 12.
atiri-so-pám, conspiracy, confederacy. 2 Sam. 15, 12. 2 Kg. 11, 14.
pl. a-, conspirator.
pl. a-, F. an insane person, a madman.
price paid for a person, for goods &c.; cf. tiri-sika, ti-ade.
adv.: wabow (nsã) t., he is excessively drunk, dead-drunk, so that he cannot move; wabow nsã atra so, na ontumi ŋkã ne hō; wabre t., he is extremely tired.
s. ti, tiwtiw.

red. v., s. ti; 1. to scratch: agyinamoa títí me nsa (hō), the cat scratched my hand. - 2. to pick, to pull with the fingers, e.g. a hand closed on purpose to open it. pr. 468; to take out any pappy or pulpy substance with the fingers. - 3. to feel with the fingers, to grope: onifuraefo de ue nsa títí (kɛkã) fasu hwehwe ɔkwaŋ; ɔde ne nsa nè ne naŋ títí, he climbed up on his hands and feet. 1 Sam. 14, 13. - 4. to stroke or bedaub with the fingers: watítí hyirew, he has strokes of white clay on his body. - 5. ne hō títí no, he has a restless or constantly burning desire, is eager or impatient for something, is anxious;
inf. the act or habit of scratching.
one who takes part in this game. pr. 3280; - byname of the centipede?
byname of a certain insect.

a., adv., n., capital, principal, chief, main, essential; often in cpds., s. ɔsafohentitiriw, asent.; - chiefly, principally, especially; - né titiriw no, its principal thing, i.e. especially; above all.

a., chief, chieftain, headman, grandee, peer, lord, prince; "ot." kyers dwuma-kese a nea ɔde saa di. ntitíwá-ntitíwá, a. pl. (small), short, said e.g. of the ears; s. omúmɔ; of grass: sare nt., short grass.
a fine for offences against marriage laws.
o-títrání, pl. atitráfo, chairman, president; cf. tiban 2.
a. tasteless, insipid, dull; eye t., titri-kú, a mighty, influential person. atí-twá, inf. cutting of heads, decapitation. Mf. atsikware.
v. to run after, follow, pursue, with good or indifferent or hostile intentions; cf. taa, to persecute, sě, di akyiri. pr. 3338. 3202.
F. to be established = tim.
pl. a., F. = ositifo.
a. not tough nor tenacious; crisp, crimp, short; said of fufuu: waghú fufuu no wow, wamã aye tiw tiw = ensɔ, wotew a, enyé hũãã, eye téŋ teŋ or peŋ peŋ; cf. ti ti.
pr. n. of a certain company; s. under asafo.
better: ntwiwa, a byname of the fowl, s. akokɔ.

[eti a ɛwɔ ase] malice, maliciousness, malignity, rancour, spite; me tirim nni at., I intend or mean no harm; ɔyè at. (se obi ade resse a, eye no fe; ade a ne yɔŋkɔ ye a ɔbenyã hɔ biribi na odi no mu aboro), he is malevolent, malicious, rejoices in the calamities of others. pr. 3575.
[nea ne ti wɔ fam] a malicious, rancorous person.
pl. a-, pursuer, persecuter. Josh. 2, 22. Jer. 17, 18.
want of intellectual faculties, weak-mindedness. tiwui-ní, -fó, pl. tiwuifó, one who is not gifted, a weak-minded person.
a disease of the head; 'stink-nose', ozena; emã wo ti ye wo duruduru, epɔrɔw wo tirim hoŋ, wonam a, emã wo hwenem' bɔŋ wo senea nãm-prɔwe bi fãm wo hwene ano.

v. [red. totə]: 1. to fall, drop down, sink (cf. hwe, gu): akutu (atew) ato fam', an orange has fallen down; metɔɔ nsum', aka kũmaa se miwui, I fell into the water and sunk to the bottom. pr. 357. 2258. 3281. 3287; biribi a étɔ asɔm', good reasons (lit. something which falls into the ears). - osu tə, rain falls, it rains; tr. osoro tɔɔ osu, the heaven gave rain. Ja. 5, 18; ɔtɔɔ sufre nè gya guu Sodom so. Gen. 19, 24.

2. to set, go down, sink, pass below the horizon, of sun, moon and stars; ówia atɔ, the sun has set: - 3. to fall, be killed, be slain, die, perish, in battle, or by an accident, not by a natural death. pr. 238. 2259; cf. ɔtɔfɔ; wo de, gye se wotɔ! (Gr. § 248,5) I will not let you die a natural death! - 4. to pass (suddenly and passively) into a weaker or lower state or circumstance: a) tə beraw, to fall into a swoon, to sink into a faint, to faint or swoon (away) from blows or torments; b) tə dobosã, id. from a sun-stroke (Jon. 4,8); c) tə piti, F. to bitsi, id. from hunger and starvation. Mt. 15, 32. Mk. 8,3; d) tə ŋko or ŋkom, to fall or sink into a slumber, to fall asleep. pr. 996. - e) tə & tə mṻm(mu), to grow dumb, speechless. Mt. 22, 12. - 5. a) tə kɔ..hɔ, F. to be

v. [red. totɔ] 1. to lay down the price for a thing, to buy, purchase. 2. wato no kaw, he has paid him the money according to him in order to give him satisfaction for adultery with his wife; cf. akatɔ; - to ayefare, to pay for adultery. 3. to asɛm di, to take bribes in a law-suit.

v. [red. totɔ] 1. to throw, cast &c., Ak. = tow, q. v. 2. to lay or put somewhere, gener. caus. (preceded by de or fa) and followed by a locative complement: fa adé no tɔ pɔŋ sɔ, put this on the table! fa to hɔ, put it there! mede ahene meto me kɔŋ mu, I put a string of beads round my neck; ɔde ne ŋkrante ato (n'asɛŋ) = wabɔ ne ŋkrante, he has girt on his sword. 1 Sam. 25, 13; ɔde wɔŋ to afɔa ano, he gives them to the sword. Jer. 25, 31; - wamfa anto ne kɔmam', he did not take or lay it to heart. Ex. 7, 23. - mfa wo ano ŋkoto asɛm no mu, do not meddle in that affair, it does not concern you, you have nothing to do with it. - fa (or gye) .. to ne hɔ so, to take (an obligation) upon oneself, to make something one's duty; cf. gye 3. - to bi (sc. asãmãnãde) pɔŋ so = sãmãna, cf. apɔŋ. - to (ofi, kürow) mu gya, to set (a house, town) on fire. - to.. mu ŋkyene, to season with salt. Lev. 2, 13. - 3. to (ŋ-)kesua (Akp.: tow..), to lay an egg (eggs), also simply: to, to lay: akɔkɔ kwane, obɛtɔ, the hen cackles, she is going to lay.
pay 4s. in advance. - yɛpɛɛ biribi too ase, we tried to get something to eat.
ɔbɛre ne hɔ ase, he humbles himself.

to neglect, disregard, slight, treat slightly, throw aside: wato ne hɔ ase mã dɔm abefa no mpàasé, he was not on his guard, so the enemy was able to take him by surprise; ɔrekɔ ɔsa, nso wato (watoto) ne hɔ ase, he goes to war, but is not sufficiently prepared; monnto mo hɔ ase, be always watchful! monnto mo mpaebɔ ase, do not neglect your prayers, do not give up praying! - ɔntó m'ase, he esteems me, respects me = obu me.
to be the last: asem a ɛto ase a merebebisa wo ni, the final question which I am going to ask you is this.
lit. to lay down the breast, i.e. to have patience, be patient, wait patiently. pr. 3299-3303; s. ɛbo & tò 20.
a) to put or lay on, to cast in, to give over and above, to add: mato nãm pii, afei tò me só! I have bought much meat (fish) of you, now give me some into the bargain! cf. ntoso, ŋkwanys.
m'ani meto no so, I cast myself upon, commit myself unto him, confide or trust in him; wo asem no so a mede me hɔ to nti meba, I shall come relying on your word.

c) to so, foll. by a num., to be in number the.. th: ɔto so anaŋ, he is the fourth; ɛto so anum, it is the fifth; obisaa no too so abiesã, or, obisaa no nea ɛto so abiesã, he asked him for the third time; akoko bɔŋe ne mpɛrennu so, ne mpeŋ abieŋ so, or, nea ɛto so mpeŋ abieŋ, the cock crowed for the second time; cf. tia, Gr. § 83, 3.
10. to, to build, abaŋ, a house of stone; abantenteŋ, a tower; fadaŋ, a house with mud walls; ɔfasu, a wall. pr. 3306 (cf. si 21).
11. to.. bɛ = bu.. bɛ. pr. 3305.
12. to.. bo, to lay or make a bet or wager; to testify that the word, statement or assertion of somebody is true, s. ɔbo.
13. to.. bo ase.
14. to da, to appoint or fix a day: meto da na wakɔpe sika abetua me; syn. hye da.
15. to.. dade, Ak. to apply a deadly weapon to.., to kill, slay, put to death; woato no dade = wòakum no; cf. tow 5.

16. to.. dig, or simply to, to give a name, impose a name upon, to name, call: mato no (or ne) diŋ Bekɔe, I have given him the name B.; mato me ba Adow, I have called my child A.; cf. Gr. § 205, 4. 5. pr. 391. 691. 774. 789. 3304.
17. to dwom, to sing; s. dwom; - ɔto dwom so, he leads the choir; ɛ. s. ɔn'na ɔto dwom ansã-na wogye so. pr. 174.

18. to hama, to mark or lay out (a garden, piece of land &c.); koto afuw no hama! - to line (the sides of a house &c.); koto daŋ no hama, line (mark out) the sides of the house! stretch the cords to mark out, the lines for building the house! cf. kyeŋ daŋ.
19. de.. to hɔ, to leave to one's pleasure or disposition. pr. 413; de kwaŋ to hɔ = to..kwaŋ, s. 20.
19a. kä..to hɔ, s. kä 54.

20. to..kwaŋ, to give free way, grant liberty, accord freedom to; to suffer (Ex. 12, 23); mato no (ŋkɔ) kwaŋ, I have left him to himself, to take his own way; I have permitted him to do as he pleases; - to sraha, s. sraha.
21. to..mmati, to lay on one's shoulders, i.e. to empower, authorize, invest with (full) power; ɔpanyiŋ soma wo na ɔto wo mmati a, wudi asɛm a, wommɛre.
22. to anã, to give one's genealogy, to show one's parentage, to prove one's descent. pr. 358.
23. to anansesem, to tell (prop. spin) a tale, cf. 11. 28. pr. 359.
24. to or toto ani, to anyiwa (aprɔ) F., to look round about (Mk. 3, 34. 9, 8); ɔtoo n'ani hwes n'akyi, he looked back.
25. to.. pɛ, to asperse, slander, calumniate, vilify; cf. sopa, pɛ; to hɔ mpɛ, s. mpɛ; diff. to apɛ.
26. to or toto.. apómãfo, to neglect, disregard, be careless about; s. apomafo.

27. to nsa: a) to stretch out the hand (= tɛe nsa): to wo nsa fa ade no mã me, stretch forth your hand, take that and give it to me! - b) ɔto ne nsa, he waves his hand in anguish or anger. Zeph. 2, 15. - ɔto no nsa, he beckons him to come. - c) to nsa didi, to eat from the same dish me nè no didi.
d) to nsa, 28. to asa ŋkurukuruwa hyɛm' na wode hɔ, na wode wo bɔw wò dua no to tɛkremakyɛn &c., s. tɛkrema tafarakyɛ, to 1. apology. pr. 144. Ak. te or fe to spit. pr. 360.

(1810) one's self (to the sun, to th warm one's se to warm one avɔw, to expo mekoto ɔw, coolness, wa exposed himse pr. 3312. - 'you have four please, join u reply: me nsa
v. [red. tɔtɔ] wrest, pervert,

1. to meet (with), fall in with; to come or light on (upon), to find; me too no ɔkwaŋ mu, I fell in with him on the way. pr. 14, 3307-10. - 2. to reach, arrive at, come up with, overtake, catch; woato nea Onyankɔpɔŋ bɔ too wɔŋ hɔ, they have attained to their divine destination; - eto fam', it reaches to the ground; s. kuw, v. - pr. 3313. 3338; to come upon. Am. 9,10; to attack, cf. pèe. - ehĩa wato wɔŋ, F. poverty has overtaken them, Mf. Gr. p. 107. - ɔwɛŋ ato wo, it is your turn to keep watch; asɔre ato wo, it is your turn to preach; n'ano ato me, lit. his mouth has reached me, i.e. he has spoken ill of me, s. ano; n'ano to O-nyame, he blasphemes God. - 3. to come up to, perf. to equal, match: wato no, now he equals him (in riches, knowledge &c.) - 4. to join, attach one's self (to). pr. (1810). 2811. - 5. to expose one's self (to the heat of a fire or of the sun, to the cold &c.): to gya, to warm one's self at the fire; to awia, to warm one's self in the sun; to awɔw, to expose one's self to the cold; mekoto awɔw, I am going to seek coolness; - wato ne hɔ séré, he has exposed himself to laughter; cf. serew. pr. 3312. - Phr. woato yeŋ, (prop. 'you have found us', sc. at our meal), please, join us (sc. in our meal)! - reply: me nsa wom', no, thank you!

1. red. tɔtɔ 1. to turn, twist, wrest, pervert, distort; - to transgress, violate, break, infringe, act contrary to: a) tɔ mmăra, to transgress the law. pr. 1412. 3317. - b) tɔ, nsu: watɔ no nsu; he has violated his sworn covenant; watɔtɔ wɔŋ hɔ nsu, they have mutually broken their covenanted obligations. - tɔ ntam, to disregard or violate (the obligations of) an oath. pr. 3316. 3663. - 2. to entangle, involve, complicate, confound, make intricate, embroil (cf. tɔa): a) ɔhene mmăra atɔ wo = woatɔ ɔhene mmăra (s. 1); wo mmăra a wohyɛe me no atɔ wo, you are yourself at variance with the law you gave me, have transgressed your own law given to me; - b) ɔtɔ me sɔ, he involves me in guilt, he charges me falsely (s. ɛsɔ) = ode asem a menyee (or enni me so) de ato me so, asem a ɔde to me so, ebiara nni me so; - c) ɔtɔtɔ m'ano, he accuses me falsely; - d) ɔtɔtɔ wɔŋ ntam', he sets them at variance with each other, throws them into contention; wɔkā yi, ntɔtɔ wɔŋ ntam', as they agree or are good friends now, do not disunite them! - e) watɔtɔ asɛm no = wadánnáŋ asem no ani na ensi n'asɛm trènee so bio, na wayɛ no basa-basa, he has confounded the matter, has made it intricate. - 3. intr. to be entangled, confused, confounded, disconcerted, discordant, disturbed, embroiled, endangered. pr. 2. 3345. - Phrases: a) ne ti atɔ, his head is entangled, his life is in danger = he has been declared guilty of death. - b) n'ani atɔ, n'anyiwa tɔ, F. his face is confounded, i.e. he is ashamed, bashful. Mk. 8,38. - c) kete no atɔtɔ, the mat has been woven wrongly, improperly, faultily; - d) ɔkā asɛm no a, n'ano tɔtɔ = ontumi ŋkā mmă entɛe, when he represents the matter or relates the story, his mouth is confused (he confounds himself), i.e. he cannot relate it aright; cf. ano 12 A. - e) ɔnè no ntam' atɔtɔ (kaŋ no wɔye nnamfo, nnansá-yi woaye sakasaka, wɔŋkā bio), they have disunited, have fallen

out with one another; Onyankɔpɔŋ nè nnipa ntam’ atɔtɔ, there is disruption (a state of discord) between God and man. — 4. tɔ kwaŋ, to miss or lose the way, to go astray; cf. fɔm kwaŋ, yera ɔkwaŋ. pr. 479. — 5. to injure, spoil, destroy, kill: nsu ntɔ wo, abosom ntɔ wo, the fetish-water, the guardian spirits shall kill thee! — 6. tɔ..aduru, to attack, injure, or kill by poison, to poison. pr. 3315. — 7. tɔ..ano, to curse, imprecate, execrate one's self: watɔ n'ano, he has cursed (falsely accused, cf. 2) himself. (se ebia I were dead!), cf. anotɔ. pr. 435 f. — 8. tɔtɔ ano, s. 2c.

to turn or change by heat: 1. to bake; to roast, to dress by applying to the fire without using any pot or pan, cf. kisã, kyew; tɔ abɔdoo, to bake bread; tɔ ɔde, to roast yam; tɔtɔ brɔde, to roast plantains; tɔtɔ nãm, to roast meat. pr. 111. 216. 364. 825. 3407. — 2. tɔtɔ, to cause to fade, wither or shrivel by exposing to fire for a few moments = de kã ogya, e.g. leaves that are to be used as a medicine. — 3. tɔ dua, to make a fire round about a tree in order to kill it. pr. 3314. — 4. tɔtɔ kuru, to dress or foment a hurt, wound or sore with warm water or medicaments. pr. 365. 1423 f.
mashed yam (first boiled, then crushed by pressure or pounded) with or without palm-oil. pr. 560. 2701. 3215.

breech, buttocks, posteriors, anus, the hinder part or parts of an animal body; cf. sisia, trũmu. pr. 35. 424. 1749. 3318. — bɔ..tɔ, to punish; obɔɔ nè mɔŋ tɔ, he punished his people. — ɔŋwɔrãm ne to ntama, he pulls off the cloth from his body. — pa..to ase, to retract; cf. pa 9. — ɔde ne to da ase, he is ungrateful. — wantrã ne to sɔ baabiara, he did not stay at any place; he did not take a rest. — né tɔ atim (okɔ baabi na wakɔtrã hɔ koraa na n'ani agye hɔ na ɔmpɛ se ɔba bio), he has settled permanently; mintú mé tɔ wɔ há, I will not leave this place; wabɔ or wayi wó tɔ ato hɔ (ato guam'), he has revealed all your secrets; né tɔ ádã or áyi adi (wo nneyee [bone] ada adi na nnipa nyinaa ahũ wo guásò, na enni wo ŋko-koamudé biara a ennaa adi ɛ), his secrets have been revealed; gener. of bad conduct = n'ani awu, he has been put to shame; wóayì né tɔ akɔŋŋua na hwee nni né tɔ bio a otrã so. — 2. hind part, hind end, of any other object: páane no tɔ kwaŋ (= paane no aniwa, asɔ, hwene) sũa, — tɛrew, the eye of the needle is small, — is wide. pr. 2590. — ɛhyɛŋ tɔ, the stern, after or hinder part of a ship. Mk. 4,38; — of a vessel: the part which it rests on the ground: aɔ̃owa tɔ, the bottom of a brass basin, s. ɔsrãmãŋ. — 3. the end of immaterial things: twa..to, to cut the hind part, i.e. to cut off, finish; wátwà asém no tɔ, he has brought the palaver to end; ɛtɔ ntwae, the end has not yet come; eda a eto rentwa da, the day or time whose end will never come, i.e. eternity. — taa..to, to finish; cf. taa.

1. to join, conjoin, bring or put together; t. guaha, s. this. — 2. to connect, file, string; to tie in weaving; to talk: t. nsententeŋ or, as., to make or multiply words, talk a long string of words; ɔtoá nsentɛŋ a hwee nnim', he talks a great deal,

but there is nothing in it; otoá nténtéŋ, he spins a long yarn, talks at random, tells a long story; nea ɔretoa ne ŋkramɔsɔm hɔ asɛm bi, he is talking about Mohammedanism; - to be coupled together. Ex. 26,11. - 3. to trace, track, follow the trace or track of, pursue: aboa na wɔtoa no, e.s. woakɔtow aboa tuo na waŋwu n'anaŋmu hɔ na ɔkɔ, na wutiw no. - 4. to take up, renew, resume something that had been interrupted. - 5. to fall upon, be hard upon, press hard or close, to urge, trouble, to attack (with abuse or blows), to assault, assail (Eccl. 4,12), challenge (cf. tua, twa mpoa). pr. 215. - bɔ toa.., to rush against (somebody); cf. bɔ 11. - 6. to apply to, assail with petitions, urge, solicit; waguan atoa no, he has taken refuge with him. Ps. 2,12. 31,2; wo bone ahye wo so ara se deŋ, na woreye apa abaw, na wode kotoa no a, ɔrempam wo da. - 7. to design beforehand in dice-play or in the game called ntɛwsi (not in ghɔmatow). - 8. Phr. n'asɛm ntoa, he is inconsistent with himself, he is an unprincipled man, unstable, unsteady, fickle in his manners and doings; n'asɛm antoa, his dealings had no consistency, through improper conduct he could not hold his position. - 9. toá so: a) caus. to join, put to, sew to, adjust together; ntama ye tiaa a, wode bi toá so; - b) to adjoin, lie or be next to, be contiguous; Begörɔfó tòà Kämánäfo so; wɛbɔ nsra toá no sɔ, they encamp next to him. Nu. 2,5. - c) to fit, agree, suit, be adjusted or adapted: ne ti tòà nó sɔ, his head stands on him. 2 Kg. 6,31; eyi de, entoa so koraa, this composition (of two words) will not do at all. - d) to continue, to proceed in (a speech or narration &c.): wokɔ asɛm a, toa so na ɛŋkosi prekɔ ansä-na woagyae; mekɔe no, na ɔkasa, na ɔtoaa ne kasa so ara kosii; - metoa so makɔ Anyinam, I shall proceed to A. - e) to follow: asɛm a ɛtoa so yi, the following story; afé tòà afé sɔ, year after year. 2 Sam. 21,1. - f) toa..so, to edify. 1 Thess. 5,11. - 10. toatoa so, a) to be put or arranged in a row; - b) to follow after one another in a row: mɔŋkɔ no ntoatoa so, go one after the other! - c) to be full, fat (closely set with grains, of ears of maize). Gen. 41,5. ɔ-toá, inf. joining, rejoining, renewal, restoration of a disruption; cf. toa 4. K. § 1.8.

tãŋá, tẽŋá, v. [red. trãtrã], F. tsẽŋã, 1. to sit down, to place one's self on a seat; it expresses the action, whilst the state of sitting, the posture of being on a seat, is expressed by te, Gr. § 102, 3; trã ase! móntrã ase! or, móntrã asé è! sit down! take a seat or seats, be seated! trã fam' sit down on the ground! watrã abrogua so, he has placed himself on a chair (pr. 371); yɛtrã baabi a, yeatrã = nea yɛtrã de, eŋhiá, it does not matter where we sit; metrã ase a, entrã (prop. when I try to sit down, it is impossible), I cannot keep quiet, it is unbearable or intolerable to me; kotrã or bɛtrã, to go or come to sit down, to settle, take up habitation; de.. trã, caus. to seat, place on a seat, cause to sit down or to occupy a post, site, situation; to station, locate, settle, establish; --otu kotrãa Akyem, he emigrated to Akem; otuu woŋ kotrãa Babel, he carried them away to Babel (and settled them there). — 2. to sit, dwell, live at a place (in the pret. and fut. tenses, when the contin. te cannot be used): ɔtrãa Aburi, he lived at Ab. (but is no more there); ɔpɛ se obetrã Ab. daa, he wishes that he may be able to live at Ab. always; cf. ɔte Ab., he lives at Ab. at present; ne yere wui no, na ɔte Ab., when his wife died, he lived at Ab. — 3. to stay, remain, continue: trã ha kakra, stay here a little! wobsɔ, na me de, metrã ha, you are going to depart, but I shall stay here; metrã ha adapɛŋ anaŋ, I shall stay here four weeks; asase betrã hɔ daa, the earth will continue for ever; mã entrã hɔ, leave it there, let it remain where it is, let it be as it is, let the matter alone = mã eŋka; - akutu no mmerɛe ɛ, mã entrã dua no tree! 4. trã ɔhene hɔ, to sit by the side of a king, to be a counsellor of the king's; trã asɛm hɔ, to attend a palaver or public transaction. pr. 370. - 5. Phr. ɔntrã ase ŋhwɛ, he does not sit and look at, i.e. he is not indifferent (to), not listless, apathetic, careless; regardless (of). K. § 189. - 6. trã hɔ, trã ase (cf. te hɔ, te ase) to live; ɔbetrã-ase daa = obenyã daa ŋkwã, he will live for ever. - trã ase, to live on; to subsist: enyɛ obosu so na afurum nam trã ase, the ass does not live on dew (like the cricket in the fable).

v. [red. tutú] to pull or draw, move or remove with a short and quick motion: 1. to draw out any thing that is fixed, to root out, get out; to pull out (ŋhwi, a hair, pr. 2333, sē, a tooth, agyaŋ, an arrow, pr. 372); to take out (nsɔe, a thorn, pr. 313). - to pluck (ŋwura, weeds, pr. 592; young plants, pr. 3367); to tear out, to pick out (ani, one's eye, pr. 1880); to pluck (mmere, mushrooms, pr. 373); to cut (sare, grass for thatching); - tu dẽ, to take out the ripe yam, pr. 3362; tutu mfuw mu ade or nnuan, to reap the fields. Ja. 5,4. - 1a. otuu m'asem mu, he made my statement invalid; mituu m'asem mu, I retracted my statement. - 2. intr. to be pulled (plucked or torn) out; n'ani biakɔ atu, he has lost one of his eyes; - to fall out; né sē nyinaa atu (atutu), pr. 401; - okra-maŋ no koŋ hō atu, the neck of that dog is bare; - to be torn or taken out, to be worn off; utama no ani atu; - n'ani atu atɔ ne nsam', s. ani; - tutu, to be uprooted, of a tree, pr. 1047. - 3. tutu, to pluck, i.e. strip by plucking (akokɔ, a fowl, anomaa, a bird, pr. 382). - 4. tu hō, to remove by brushing, to brush; - tu m'atade ani or so, brush my clothes! - 5. Phr. tu ase, a) to get out the root, fig. to begin from the very outset: tu ase (kā) kyere me, tell me all from the beginning, relate me the whole fully, at full length, at large, in detail, minutely! - b) watu tumpaŋ yi ase, he has drunk off this whole bottle. - 5a. tu bisa, to question, put a question to; wotu bisa no sē..; - ótù asɛm mã me, a) he puts a question to me, asks me something; - b) he gives me an answer; otutu nsɛm mã me, he puts questions to me. - 6. tu, to take out, dig, make (amɔa, a hole in the ground, abura, a well, pr. 3361). - 7. tu kuru, to cause an open sore, pr. 1425; to ulcerate, suppurate; watútu akúru, ne hōnam nyinaa atutu akuru, he (his whole body) is full of sores. - 8. to draw, scoop (water with the hand or with a calabash): otu nsu de hyira n'ano, s. hyira 6b, pr. 3366; tu nsā kora mã bɛre me! - 8a. intr. to flow out;

the strength of his arms has been taken out, i.e. he is discouraged, dismayed, he despairs of: n'ab. atu ade no hɔ = enyé no fɛw bio, ontumi nye bio.
a) to provoke to anger, cf. fuw or horaŋ or huru bo; b) to excite; b) to frighten, discourage, dishearten; cf. tu abasam'; F. tu.. akoma;

twi: ne bo or ne kōma atu
eng: he is frightened, in consternation, perplexed, disheartened, discouraged, dismayed; he despairs. Eccl. 2,20.
to send or dispatch a messenger; wotuu no bofo kɔɔ Aburi; tu adwumayɛfo, to send forth labourers. Mt. 9,38.
to admonish, exhort; s. fo. pr. 912.

to take out the eyes and look or direct to, i.e. to cast a piercing look at: wɔatu wɔŋ ani de rehwe no, otutu n'ani (re)kyere me, s. ani & poo; (tu)tu ani hwe, also: to stare at; otu n'ani hyɛ me, he casts an angry look at me, sets his face against me; otu n'ani kyere no, he eyes him (1 Sam. 18,9) = otu n'ani kyere no; wo(tu)tu wɔŋ ani sii kũrow no so, they turned their attention to the town.

a) to take or cut off parts of the end, to point, give a point to, sharpen (the sticks to be fixed in the ground in building a house); b) otutu m'asɛm ano sisi (mekã asɛm a, na wadaŋ ani), he distorts my words or cause, lit. he pulls out the borders of my matter and puts them in other places. c) otu m'ano wɔ fam', he refuses to hear me, to hearken to me.
(to pull out one's ear,) to persuade, win over; F. tu asõ asõmã, to persuade, pacify, conciliate. Mt. 28,14.
to whisper; to plot secretly, to devise mischief. Ps. 41,7(8); perh. taken from the sound of splashing, cf. 8.42.
to call forth, bring about, arrange: agoru, ɔprenteŋkoro, a game or play, asaw, a dance. tu agoru, to take part in a play.
(Ak.) to pain, smart, ache (diff. 7): ekuru no tutu me. pr. 1859; cf. tutuw.
to drive back, to force one to give up his position; tutu ŋkraŋ. pr. 313.
to put one off concerning a debt, to defer, put off payment. pr. 155. 722. 1368. 3217. 3398; cf. ŋkadeŋ, akatutu.
to pace, go on slowly; t. wo anaŋ duom'! s. ɛnaŋ.
otu ne tia me, he lifts up his foot (heel) against me, he kicks me. (John 13,18); fig. he opposes me.
to fly (from the jerking motion of the wings): anomaa tu ɔsoro (wim).
to rise: ohuruhúrów tu
to fly up, jump up; otu fãm me, he jumps up and embraces or hugs me.

to be thrown or spattered on, so as to be fastened, to stick, cling or cleave to; to follow hard after. 1 Chron. 10, 2; ɔkõ no tu tare woŋ, the battle overtook them; wotu tare woŋ dii woŋ akyi, they pursued hard after them. Judg. 20, 42. 45.

intr. & tr., to remove from, to change one's (dwelling-)place; matutu mafi Akũropoŋ makotřa Aburi; I have removed from Akr. to Ab.; matu no mafi ofi no mu, I have caused him to leave that dwelling; cf. 10.

to go (away or off). pr. 1036; to go, remove, depart, or journey from (Numb. 33), to set out, set forth, set forward. Nu. 2, 17; to break up, de-camp; to emigrate; Agyeman nẽ ne maŋ atu akɔye dom, Agy. and his people have emigrated and become enemies (to their former master or compatriots, s. dəm); woatu afi guam' ho, they have left the assembly; - to break up (a session or meeting): gua no atu, the session or assembly has been broken up or dissolved, has dispersed; əmãa gua no tui, he dismissed the assembly. Acts 19, 41.
to lead or carry away, to cause or force to emigrate. Job 12, 23. 2 Kg. 24, 14ff.; otuu woŋ kɔe, he carried them away captive. Jer. 52, 28. 30.
to desert, elope, run away, escape privately.
to consult (leaving a greater circle and standing apart, s. agyina).
da, to adjourn, postpone, defer; woatú ahyè dá, lit. they have parted (or, woatu asɛm no, they have put aside the matter) and fixed a day; cf. wəabə asɛm no ato hə.
to leave for, set out or forth on a journey, to journey, travel; cf. 14a. pr. 3338. 3363.
to travel with great speed, in forced marches.
to walk slowly, stealthily or secretly after; otu me nnee = ənam m'akyi brɛoo, ohintaw di m'akyi; cf. odi (or ənam) me ntɛntɛso; odi me nsəŋŋə odi m'akyi komm.
to walk along in water or a brook.
he has been delivered or freed from his pressing circumstances.

twi: aduaŋ no atu (or atə) me hō
eng: (e.s. aduaŋ a midii no asã me yafunum'), I feel no further strength from that food (being digested long ago; Germ. die Speise hält nicht mehr vor); aduaŋ no ntú me hō ntɛm, that food (is heavy for or clogs my stomach?) does not let me feel hunger soon.
to grow or be pale, emaciated, tabid, worn out; watu k. fitaa.
(or display) a tuft of blossoms, to bloom, said of maize.
F. to move = twiw. (Mt. 23, 4).
to put aside, apart, to remove; - (prep.) without. 1 Pet. 3, 1.
inf. flying; anõmaa kyerɛ ne ba otu, pr. 2883.
Ak. s. ntuw.
F. end, bottom = eto.
pl. a-, hole, den, lair of a beast in the earth. pr. 1838.
adv. completely (dark); ade sãã so tuu, whilst this was going on, night fell; it grew quite dark (it continued or was deferred into the darkness of night); oda fam' tuu, he lies flat on the ground.
the sound produced by something falling to the ground.
clasp, embrace; yɛ atuu, to embrace; to give a hearty reception; woyɛ at., they embrace each other; meyɛ no at., I embrace him; cf. bam, fãm.

v. [red. tuatua] 1. followed by locative complements (ano, hō, mu, so): a) intr. to stick (at), to be stuck, fixed, fastened, applied to: boneywone tùa otuo ano, the bayonet is fixed on the end of the musket; ntuaano tua tumpaŋ ano, the cork is in the mouth of the bottle; aben tua onipa ano, mouth. pr. is a woun. hō, I have ntakara tu. - tua dəm army, to troops. - t. over, be cl. b) caus., to where: əde dua) túa t. into the m. tua dade s. kɛse bi an. large fami the extrem: tùa tətɛ, eb. have hoofs, - 3. tua. ed in: m'at. in my head or obstruct to r. , 1 aba .urn baŋ .nom', de .. tua ana Gen. 2, 21. mana a etu nothing at at! onipa ano, the horn is applied to the mouth. pr. 79; ekuru t. me nsa hɔ, there is a wound on my hand; kuru tua me hɔ, I have a wound, a sore. pr. 3368; ntakara tuàtua ne hōnam mu. pr. 1659; - tua dɔm ano, to be at the head of an army, to head an army, to command troops. - t. (ŋhyiam ' &c.) ano, to preside over, be chairman of (a meeting &c.). - b) caus., to stick, fix, fasten, put somewhere: ɔde ntuaano (ahabaŋ, būrodna, dua) tuá tumpaŋ ano, he puts a cork into the mouth of the bottle; ɔde dua tua dade so, s. 8. - wode no tuaa abusua kɛse bi ano, he was made head of a large family (tribe). - 2. to have at the extremities of the body: mmoa bi tùa tɔte, ebinom tùa awɛrew, some beasts have hoofs, others have paws with claws. - 3. tua.. mu, a) intr. to lie, be situated in: m'ani tua me tirim, my eyes are in my head. pr. 2294. - b) tr. to close or obstruct a hole, fill up a void or gap, to mend, repair; ahina a.s. biribi hɔ aba tokuru a, wotuá = wosiw; kotua baŋ nom', go and repair that fence! de .. tua anaŋmu, to close or stop an aperture, gap or opening; s. 1. - b) to stop one's mouth, lit. & fig.: wode biribi a.s. asɛm tua onipa ano na ontumi ŋkasa bio; - c) to reply, espec. in refutation: obi akā wo betuatua nsɛm a wubisa no ano, now I will answer your questions; - d) tuatua ano, to contradict. Tit. 2,9. - 5. etuátua m'asɔ, the report, talk or noise stops or fills my ears, it is always ringing in my ears. - 6. to apply (pepper, soap) to the anus: wotua no mako = wɔde mako hye ne to. - 7. tua kaw, to fill up or replace what is wanting: a) to (re)pay a debt; to make amends. pr. 132. 374. 3111. 3369; cf. hye or si anaŋmu; b) also simply tua, to suffer for, pay for, pay damages, expiate. pr. 728. - c) to punish: ɔbétúa wɔŋ (asɛm no so) ka-bone, he will punish them (for it); - d) to reward: ɔde akatua-pa betua wɔŋ, he will reward them well. - 8. t., to join well, sit close, fit; caus. to fit on: ɔde dua tua dade so, he fastens a piece of wood on the iron; s. 1. - 9. tua, to be compatible or consistent with, to agree with: mfɛntom yi nɛ mmāra antua, the interest taken is not compatible with the law, = wɔmmārae sɛ wónnye saa mf. yi; cf. 14. - 10. to fall or hit on: m'ani tua wo mprempreŋ sɛ woakofa ŋhoma no; m'ani tua ɔwifo sɛ wakɔ akɔwia ade, my eye fell on, i.e. I saw with my own eyes... - 11. to fall upon (Ex. 5,3), to attack, assault, assail (unexpectedly and with force, cf. toa), espec. to surprise early in the morning: wotua wɔŋ, s. ɛdɔm 2 akohyia na dɔm no mu biakɔ asɛre anadwo na woakɔ wɔŋ a wonɛ wɔŋ hyia no nsram' na wonɛ wɔŋ akɔ anɔpa; s. ntua, inf. - wotua na wɔ-hyew kūrow, they assault and burn a town; - bɔ tua .., to rush against, to attack unexpectedly. - 12. to besiege, block up, invest; to enclose, encompass, surround: wotua kūrow no (pratū); wotua no pratū ne sɛ: onipa wɔ daŋmu na wɔakotoa no na onnyɛ ɔkwaŋ mfa baabiara; s. pratū; tua .. (hɔ) hyia, to besiege &c., lay siege to. Deut. 20,12. 19. Mic. 4,14. - 13. to anticipate, to be before in doing: t. ahema, to be early in doing, to begin a work or any thing early in the morning before the usual time: mituaa ahemadakyɛ or anɔpa mekoɔ hɔ, I went there early in the morning, I rose early and went there; - osu tuaa anɔpatutu, very early in the morning it began to rain. - 14. .. hɔ tua: asɛm yi hɔ tua (= as. yi hɔ nni kwaŋ, a.s. woakā na woanni no saa a, ɛnyé yiye), this word is a) incontestable, incontrovertible, indisputable, irrefragable, irrefutable, b) indispensable, imperative. - 15. ne hɔ tua, a) ɔmfɔŋe ɛ, he is well fed, corpulent, stout; - b) he is at ease, quite comfortable. - 15a. tua dúá, to become or be fat (only of animals); oguáŋ à ótúà dúá, a fat sheep. - 16. t., to abstain from: otua (ne hɔ) aduaŋ, nsā, he (shuts

himself up against, i.e.) abstains from food, liquor, he prohibits himself to take food, palm-wine &c., in the way of a religious observance; watua ne hō ade amä Iehowa, he has separated himself unto Jehovah as a Nazarite. Num. 6. - 16b. (tr.) tua ōhome, to hold one's breath. - 17. to prohibit or forbid a person anything to eat or drink: ōhene de bi ye akrakwaa a, otua no n'akyide nyinaa; ne mpanyimfo atua no nsä = abra no mmorösä-nom. - 18. t. nsu, to drink water (copiously); ode nsu (aduru) tuá ne ti, he drinks water (medicine).
inf. [s. tua 11] 1. a sudden attack, a taking by surprise: Asenfo de nt. na ekum dom. - 2. siege. Nah. 3, 14.

habit, custom; nea woye no dabiara; ode .. aye t., he is doing it habitually.

v. 1. intr. to open, break or burst forth, begin (to take its flow or course): a) asusow atue, the rainy season has begun or set in; asusow rebetue, the r. s. is approaching. pr. 3138; - b) asu tue, the (water of the) river, lagoon or lake bursts forth, breaks out [G. fãa fɛ, tíki]. - 2. tr. to open in order to give a free passage or course: a) woretue asu, they are letting out the water, pent up in the lagoon into the sea in order to catch the fishes which had remained unmolested for some months, [G. ametiki faa]; - b) tue nsã, to draw (off) the liquor (wine, beer, rum) from a large cask into a small one (aguadifo hwie nsã fi hãse mu gu paŋkraŋ mu); to pour out. Jer. 48, 12; - c) tue nsã ano, to let out, tap, broach, uncork the liquor (wotu ne nsã wode tuaa nsã no ano fi ano); - d) tue kwaŋ, to open a road that had been shut up (okwaŋ asiw na afei woadi asɛm no na woamã akwaŋ bio); watue emu-kɔ, he has opened (i. e. initiated or consecrated) the going (i. e. the way). Mk. 2, 4. - f) tue sũ, to commence wailing. - g) tue ayi, to repeat a funeral custom after a certain time (a fortnight to 6 months); Guanfo nè Dkraŋ fo tue ayi, ɛ.s. wosaŋ ye ayi koro no ara a woyɛɛ kaŋ no bio. - h) tue mmära, to revoke an edict, to repeal a law.

Ak. timi, F. tum, v. 1. to be able, (can); it denotes an ability depending on natural gifts, on physical conditions, or on power and influence; diff. nim; it is followed by se or by a v. in the consec. or, when neg., by a neg. v., s. Gr. § 256 Rem. Wóbetúmi ayè déŋ? or Edeŋ na wobetumi aye? what would you be able to do? (said in abuse or scorn; otherwise: wunim deŋ ye?) -- misusuw se métúmi maye ade bebree, I think I can do many things; metumi maye kyeŋ (se)nea ŋkürofo bebree susuw, I can do more than many people think; ontumi nye me hwee, he can do me nothing (no harm); mintumi mensoa adesoa no, I cannot carry this load; otumi papaye, he can do good. pr. 3375-84. -- 2. to be able to withstand, to match, master, overcome; to be a match for, to be equal to (followed by a passive object): mantumi nò, I could not withstand or overcome him; n'ahaŋkafo ntumi no, his hammock-men are not able to carry him; ntama (or otäm) a nsu nt. no, waterproof (sheeting); s. Gr. § 203 Rem. pr. 2264. -- 3. (foll. by an inf.) to be accustomed or know well (to do), to be well versed (in doing): otumi saa yo, Gr. ib. - to dare: küromhofo tumi ahòho hwe.

pl. a-, musket, gun. pr. 282. 456. 798 f. 3386-95; atuo = atu(o)-tow, pr. 376. - parts of a gun: otubaa, otuduá, tuboná, sábon, asó, tantiá, kantama, katae, agyeŋkwá, akita-twerebo, twerebo, akókɔsẽrẽ, twenewa, dade, ani, nsa; - bɔ or di tuo, to shoot one's self. pr. 2495; tow tuo, to fire a gun; woatow no wim' tuɔ se ne to ŋŋkã agua yi so da-biara-da, he has been publicly declared unfit for the throne for ever; ɔtow n'anom tuo, he apologizes publicly; he withdraws a word or opinion, he recants; - n'anim bɔɔ or tow tuo, s. anim A. - cf. otufo, ntutá.
different kinds of guns: bɔmtii, ɔdantá, kaŋkaŋ-tuo, akãrawa, akuapém, akwadamma.
inf. 1. taking up arms (lit. guns). — 2. = mãnsõ.
Okw. the state-room in a house.
i-, pl. a-, e-, F. = otúo.
v. to search thoroughly among, rummage; yeat. ne ŋhoma no mu, yeaŋhũ nea wohwehwe no, we have gone through his book without finding what you wanted.
pl. n-, F. garden; túrom, in the garden.
túróm, túròm', pl. a-, n-, garden; ŋkũrõfo ayeyɛ nturo pii wɔ hɔ. - túróm-hwefo, túró-yɛfó, gardener. Lk. 13,7. Isa. 61,5.
straight, right &c., s. tõrodoo.

adv. ever; in neg. sentences: never; syn. da; mérem'má bió t., I shall never (no more) come. - Sometimes it merely gives emphasis to the negation or affirmation: enním óo t., it is not at all true! ɛwom' óo t., it is quite true!
adv. denoting the sound of the dawuru; ɔkãe pɛ, na obi amã ɔdawuru so t. t. t. akyini ŋkũro no nyinaa mu, no sooner did he speak, than some one began to strike the ɔd. all through the towns.

v. [red. tu(ru)turu] to carry on the arm, back or shoulders. pr. 376f. 3103. Nu. 11,12. Isa. 40, 11. 49,22; ɔturu ne ba wo n'abasa so, she carries her child in her arms; (ɔtùru.., she takes up..; ɔturu... she carries..); cf. kura; t. mma, to bring up (and keep alive) children; mawo mma du mituruu wɔŋ mu anum, I have given birth to ten children, of whom five are still alive.
-bó: ɔbɔ nt. (n. s. onipa fi kũrow mu kɔ kũrow mu di asakasákasɛm nè apempensi), he does mischief, extorting money &c.
hole, fissure, crack; syn. tokũru, mpaee.

= trũmu.

(ogya nt.), sparks (of fire); small particles flying out with a crackling noise.

[red. turúturuw] to throw out small particles, spatter, to sputter out: ogya no t., the fire sparkles, emits sparks; wɔkyew abũrow a, eturúturuw, when corn is roasted, single grains or small particles fly out with a crackling noise; tumpaŋ (ahina, toa n. a.) aturuw, a bottle (pot, flagon) has burst spattering and spilling its contents; nsɔe turuturuw, thorns crackle. inf. eruption, explosion.
inf. [tu so] the act of dethroning or deposing, dethronement, deposition.

men grown so far as to be able to fire guns, i.e. fit to bear arms.
inf. journey. Ex. 17,1; di at., to journey (with herds &c.). Gen. 2,19.
pl. a., nomad.
pl. t., settler, colonist; pl. at., strangers, foreigners. Isa. 5,17; s. otubrafo.
adv. densely, thickly; abontɛŋ so afuw t., the road (street) is thickly overgrown.
Okw. a humming beetle.
tútututu, a. early, is used only in connection with anɔpa: anɔpa tútututu, very early in the morning; ɔkyéna anɔpatútu, to-morrow morning.
adv. imitative of the sound of boiling water; ehuru t., it boils and bubbles.
pr. n. of an Akuapem town.
pr. n. m.
= túãfuru.
a certain tree; dua kese bi a wotwitwa n'abãã bi de seŋ bofunnua.
tútuhúnu, a species of stinging fly = ɔbenem, ɔbɛnom.
scab, scald, scall, scurf. Lev. 13,30f.

pl. a., a quarrlesome person.
red. v. turu.

Phil. 1,16; di at., to quarrel; cf. di 92; ɔkɔpe no at., he insults or provokes him. - 2. a certain disease, violent pain in the limbs, aching in the bones with swelling of the limbs; ɔyare bi a daa nyinaa ɛmã wó nnòmpé mú yɛ wo yáw na ɛhoŋhoŋ' wo; periostitis.

1. dust (flying in the air; mfutama, dust of the ground). - 2. bɔ.. tutuw, to expose to shame, to hold up to shame, to disgrace publicly by shouting after a person (hû, wô, yê, hô!); wòbo no t. = wohuro no; mómmo no t.!
inf. = atuo-twẽ.
v. F. to boast, brag, vaunt; ótùw, or ótùw ne hô, or óyè n'tùw', he boasts; Akr. ɔhoahoa ne hô. - n'tùw', inf. boasting.
a. (used only in cpds.) desolate, uninhabited, decayed; aftúw, odantúw = ofi, ɔdaŋ a ada ntuw; cf. kwaeberentuw.
F. = etũ, den. Mt. 21,13.

1. mould, a substance like down (consisting of microscopic plants) on plants, clothes &c.; mildew. - gye ntuw, to mould, grow mouldy, fusty, musty. pr. 1417. - 2. da ntuw, to lie or sleep without fire; ɔda nt. = ɔnná ogya. pr. 3365. - of a way: to be destitute of travellers. pr. 3372.
the sound produced by something falling into the water; t. na ɔtow hwee nsu mu.
atúùyé inf. embrace. Eccl. 3,5.
toẽa, v. F. = toa; toẽa do, to follow, succeed.
tõea, F. = tõa, to accuse (Mk. 3,2).
tuĩa, F. = tua.

Many of the different meanings of this word may, in a generalizing way, be reduced to this: to pass (move, or cause to move) in a line, espec. in an effective movement through (on, over, across, along, by the side of &c.) any thing. - 1. to cut, gash, wound (with an edged tool): ɔsekaŋ nnamnam twa wo a, ɛkom'; cf. pira, bɔ akãm or ŋkãmãã; - red. to wound the feelings. Acts 7,54; me yam' twitwa hyehye me, it is heart-rending to me; cf. yam' B .2. - 2. red. to cut up, cut to pieces, ch. 1, 6. 12. 8,20. - 3. to cut, (bullets) from hew or form of a certain pr. 1352. 339. a palm-tree. pr. 991 for a bridge. reap: awi, gra tu sare); - to (cf. tew, tet twa ..mene, t 387. - 7. to off, sever; du 3401; fufua, pr. 583; nsa, 5,30; ti, one's otwitwa ne ŋpua hô yi 4); to c cut short, sho 1892; to travel a) to cut off a ) to pare (the = twa tiaa, cutting, make to bring to a make to cease Gen. 11,6. Pr. twa..to, to cu put an end to, tò or dùã or tail of an end, has d etó twà, the e an end; n'ama misery will s rentwa da, hi endless. - 14. stay: mogya n Tshi-English

to cut, make by cutting: abo, slugs (bullets) from lead- or iron-bars, (also to hew or form stones), kora, a calabash of a certain size; poma, a walking-stick. pr. 388; sämā, figures on a person's head. pr. 2002.
to cut down, fell: abe, a palm-tree. pr. 3460; brødee, brøfere. pr. 1352. 3399 f.; to hew: dua, wood (cf. tow). pr. 991. 1244; twene, a tree serving for a bridge. pr. 3406.
to cut, mow, reap: aẅi, grain, emō, rice (cf. bu abürow, tu sare);
to gather: obobe-aba, grapes (cf. tew, tetew).
to cut through: twa..mene, to cut some one's throat. pr. 387.
to kill for an offering. pr. 1661; cf. 40.41: twa oguaŋ.

to cut off, sever: dubāa, a branch; gyentia. pr. 3401; fufuu, a pinch or bit of foofoo. pr. 583; nsa, naŋ, one's hand, foot. Mat. 5,30; ti, one's head, to behead. pr. 2651f.; otwitwa ne ŋhwi, he cuts his hair, ..ne ŋguaŋ hō ŋhwi, he shears his sheep (cf. yi 4); to be cut off. Josh. 3,13.
to cut short, shorten, ɔkwaŋ, a way. pr. 1892; to travel. pr. 2265.

a) to cut off a piece of. pr. 142. 577. 3407. - to pare (the nails, cf. bu); to clip; - b) = twa tiaa, to cut short, shorten by cutting, make shorter; to abridge; - c) to bring to a sudden termination, to make to cease; ɔtwá so = ɔmā egyae. Gen. 11,6. Job 42,2.

to cut off, bring to an end; come to an end: asɛm no ŋh. atwa; asu no atwa (wɔ) m'afuw ano, the river is dried up near my plantation; cf. twitwa, - twa..kyene, to cut off (& cast away). Prov. 24,14. pr. 9. 10.
to cut off the hindmost end, to put an end to, to finish: wátwà asém no tò or dùa, he has cut off the hind part or tail of the matter, has brought it to an end, has done away with it.
to cut off, the end is cut off, it comes to an end; n'amanne no betwa ntɛm, his misery will soon be ended; n'anigye to rentwa da, his joy will never cease, is endless.

to cease to flow, to stay: mogya no atwa, the blood has been stanched; ŋŋo no twae, the oil stayed. 2 Kg. 4,6; tr. to stop from flowing, to stanch: aduru no atwa mogya no, that medicine has stanched the blood; ennyā atwayɛ, it is not easily stanched or stopped. Lam. 3,19.

to cross (over), to pass over. pr. 389.3405. - ɔde korow twaa asu no, he crossed the river in a canoe; - sɛ asu yi yiri a, otwa ŋkürɔfo a etwam' ha no, if the river rises, he ferries over the people who pass here; wontumi mfa you ntwa asu no, they cannot take you over the river. - twa in connection with another v. serves for the prep. or adv. over, across; oguare twaa asu no, he swam across the river; ɛtwene nni asu-bɔnteŋ no so nti, oguare twae, there was no bridge across the river, therefore he swam over. - to intersect. F. ɔde wɔŋ twa' sar n, he led them through the wilderness.
to pass by, overtake, outstrip. pr. 383; watwa me hō kɔ, he (has) passed by me; mitwaa no hō ɔkwaŋ mu, I passed him on the road.
to omit, syn. kwati, gyaw; - watwa ne nyiŋ hō or mu, he or she has passed the proper age (for a certain purpose) = wabu ne mmerem', ne mmere atwam'.
a) to cut asunder (twa..mu abien). Mt. 24,51. - to cut off, F. Ps. 90, 10.
to interrupt: watwa n'assm mu [G. efɔlɛ ẅiemɔŋ]; mintwá wò mú, I will not interrupt you.

b) to insert, put between, put in (a new beam &c); - to go or pass through. Ex. 26,28; to extend throughout. - afáhyɛ no nnuu so a, ɔde foforo ntwá abosonsomfo maŋ mu, no new yam is brought into a heathen town before the celebration of the yam-festival.
c) to correct, cancel, strike out (e.g. in writing). - twa or twitwa..mu mfomso, to correct the mistakes in an exercise.
d) to impregnate, penetrate (of salt) beyond what is proper: ŋkwaŋ yi, ŋkyene atwam' (ŋkyene atwa ŋkwaŋ yim'), the soup is over-salted, salted too much [G. ŋo efomli tsö].
e) to pass over: ɔsram twa maŋ
to pass by, of persons. to go to and fro. to pass, go by; of time. to pass away, vanish, perish.
to pass by. to pass the edge or front of, i. e. to be beforehand, to anticipate, do sooner than another.
to pass before my eyes (with a transitory flash), i. e. I caught a glimpse of him.
to pass, elapse (of time).
to draw a line, to make a streak with, to touch.
to spread or lay on.
to be drawn (of a line), to be cut across; to cut off a measured part from the rest, to measure.
to part, separate, divide (intr., drawing, as it were, a line between themselves), to disunite.
to turn, wheel or whirl round; to turn to look back, i.e. he is constant.
to be constant.
he (she) is handsome.
to look about, turn back, turn round.
to be home-sick.
to faint: to faint from weariness &c.
to have an epileptic fit or fits; to be lunatic; to have a fit of hysterics.
to surround, encircle.
to go round something; a circle.
to denounce, denunciate, to inform against.
to be urging, pressing; it is necessary that ...; must.

(me) sε mekɔ, I must go; it is mostly used in the contin. form: abofra yε merew, na etwa sε obi (bε)hwe nɔ (so); but may also occur in the pret.; ɔkɔm bae, na etwaa (wɔŋ) sε wɔkɔɔ asase bi so kɔtɔɔ abürow, there came a famine, and they were obliged to go to another country to buy food, = ɔkɔm bae, na etwa (wɔŋ) sε wɔkɔ asase bi so kɔtɔ ab. Cf. hia 2 & sε, v. 3.

to appease, assuage, soothe, pacify, satisfy, to speak kindly to (Gen. 34,3): ne bo fuwi na ose: ɔmpene; na mitwaa ne bo metɔɔ ne yam' ma ɔpenee; osuro sε ɔbεba me ŋkyεŋ, na enti mitwaa ne bo metɔɔ ne yam' na ɔbae; s. εbo.
to desert, run away; cf. abɔrɔdɔo.
to disclose, reveal, discover, make known what has been kept secret.
to celebrate the yearly yam-custom (prob. from the killing of sheep for expiatory or propitiatory sacrifice, s. odwira).

to kill a sheep by cutting its throat, hence: to atone for, make atonement, to appease: ohyiraa ɔhene ara pε na wotwaa oguaŋ, or wɔkofaa oguaŋ betwae, when he had cursed the king, a sheep was immediately brought and killed for an expiation; wɔkotwaa no guaŋ, they killed a sheep for him from respect or good will or in order to appease him; the same may be done to appease one's husband or wife. pr. 384.
to wail.
= kyini.
prop. to cut asunder the pad, i.e. to break off connection or relationship; ɔnε n'abusüafo atwa k.
to deceive, delude, decoy, take in; to calumniate. pr. 2294. 3402f.
to start a dispute, contend in words, dispute with anger, altercate, wrangle.
to wean (a child); to be weaned; watwa ne ba nufu, she has weaned her child; ne ba atwa nufu, her child has been weaned.

to 'cut out' the lines for the advancing warriors, to form the lines, to place in regular lines or ranks, to range, arrange, or array an army. for encampment or battle, to set the battle in array; woatwa yεŋ so mp., they are encamped or are in battle-array against us.
so, to pick; take up, catch or invent some matter for (false) accusation; cf. bɔ 97 .. osusukã.
to circumcise.
to cease breeding or child-bearing; wátwà àwó, he or she begets no more children.
F. to tear, rend. Mk. 9, 20. 26. = twεtwε.
F. = bɔ afɔre (Comm. p. 15).
anyim, F. to fall down before. Mk. 3, 11.
F. = pɔ ahuru, to foam. Mk. 9, 20.
F. = boa, di atoro, to lie, tell a lie.
to speak Akan.
(ewɔ), F. to lament. Mt. 11, 17. Cf. 42.
inf. 1. cutting &c. - wóbɔ twá, they are in the van. 2. harvest. 3. epilepsy, cf. twa 31, abiribiriw.
(Ntwea?), one of the orig. families of the Tshi people; cf. App. D.

pl. a-, scar, cicatrice, cicatrix. pr. 2030; kuru a awu na n'amɔa a εka nɔ, εn'na wɔfre nɔ twá; wɔ hɔ baabi a εnyε wo yaw no na biribi yε hɔ (hurts the place) a, wuse: εhɔ de, mede hɔ mabu atwã = mibu no sε εnyε me yaw; - ɔde ne hɔ abu atwã, he is insensible, indifferent, unfeeling, cold, callous to it; εyε twã, a) it is a scar; b) it is so, it is true = εte sa, εwom'.
a certain prickly plant; wura bi .. a εyε yaw sε; εkyere mmoa a wɔŋ hɔ wɔ ghwi na wɔkofam' a, na asuso wɔŋ ghwi mu. pr. 800.
s. atwëaa.
a. tough; tenacious; elastic; fufuu, ëwere a wɔwe no, ntini nso yε twãã; syn. hũãã, hũãñï, twãñï, twãpãã, sãã; cf. mãã, mãtãmãtã.
harvest. Mt. 9, 38.
harvest(-time). 1 Sam. 12, 17.
touch-stone; obo a wode twa sika hwe se eye sika pa anase sika bone.
pl. n-, hedgehog? Guinea-pig, similar to wea; jerboa? an animal as large as a small pig or goat, going in herds, living in rocks. pr. 537. Lev. 11,5. - rabbit.
harvest-day.
a day's march or journey.
F. measure, bushel. Mt. 23,32. Mk. 4,21; cf. twa 25.
pl. id. [twa 15] ford; passage. Josh. 2,7. Isa. 16,2. Jer. 51,32.
adwúma, a job = ɔbɔnnɔ-dwúma.

lit. the cutters, those who are to cut into the enemy, the company that begins the battle, the van, van-guard, front or first line; wodi tw., they are in the van. - tw. hene, leader of the advance guard.
pl. tw., 1. pioneer. - 2. reaper. Mt. 13,30. - 3. processionary caterpillar. - 4. The falling sickness, epilepsy; cf. twa 31.
Akp. whirlwind.
n-, inf. [twa, to pass, gu, to fall in plentifully]: di a-, to pass numerously; ŋkatawiá di a-; nnɔmaa no di dua no so atw. (= wotwa wɛe); mmoa di deŋkyɛdeŋkyɛ no ani atwagu. Cf. di 36.
pl. a-, (F. n-) [ahina, twa 25] measuring pot, holding 12 -15 gallons.
inf. [twa 26] turning or wheeling round. pr. 169. 620.
inf. [twa 22] circumference.
wheel, 1 Kg. 7,30.
[twa 22] inf. probation or trying of gold on a touch-stone. - o-twá-hwɛfó, assayer, trier. Jer. 6,27.
inf. cutting something asunder with one stroke; ŋkrante (a ano seŋ) atw., a (very) sharp cutlass; aduru atw., a quick-working medicine.
ye .. tw., to scare or frighten away; obiara ba ne ŋkyeŋ a, ɔreŋye no tw.
inf. [twa 8, kã, to dip] the dipping into or eating from the same dish; fellowship. 2 Cor. 6,14; di tw., to have friendly intercourse, to be in close communion together; di 82, twawe, akãpimahwe &c.
inf. the keeping up of friendly intercourse.
v. n. [twa, to cut, ka, to remain] what remained after repeated cutting, i. e. remnant of a bale of cloth, ntama a wóatɔ atɔ na akã asé; awi ntw., stubble. Ex. 5,12.
measuring calabash = susukora; cf. twa 3. 25.
breeches, a garment worn by men, covering the hips and thighs. Ntafo atade ne no; ntwòntwó, wònó.
a certain insect.
twa. mu, s. twa 17. 18.
[twa mu] passover, pasch, a feast of the Jews; the sacrifice offered. at the feast; F. apahõ. Mt. 26,2. 17 ff.
v. [s. red. twintwam] to become dry, lean, to languish, to pine away, of one who has consumption; of plants: to wither, fade; syn. botow, kagyaw, kisã, nyãm; cf. twaŋ.
hemorrhage = ɔdweaa.
the imperfect tense, past tense. Gram.
F. veil, curtain. Mt. 27,51.
ntwamú-mmõhõs, id. Ex. 27,21. twaŋ, v. (better: twàm) s. red. twintwaŋ.
adv. languidly: mekɔtoo no no, na aniwu (or awershow) nti ne ti si fam' (or, si ase) tw., his head drooped or hung down heavily; misii me ti ase tw., I bowed down in sadness. Ps. 35,14. Jer. 14,2.
a. clammy, glutinous; dua yi mu nsu ye tw., cf. twãã.
-nsãmã, a bird with white and black spots on the head, building its nest in hollows of rocks.
name of a month, about April(?); s. osram.
a. tough, tenacious, pliable; hama ye tw., cf. twãã, sãã.
twẽapẽa, a certain tree, little sticks of which are chewed to cleanse the teeth; dua a wówe de twiw wɔŋ sê so. pr. 1905; cf. sēfufudua.
atwàpó, atwàpó, syn. abontwene. twapotí, a. apotibaa.
stroke; cf. ye seŋ ɔya better than kasa yi ye c your short of the previa of the pr. s.
1. = twa. 2. = twa = etwa se holy. 3. = twa.

[red. twatware] to cut, i.e. 3078. 2. to intersect; to start of, to 11 to catch; cf. asɛm ano, 12 end; s. a 12 in the 19 day's journey ling in the st wuse: fa h yi guan no, wek no. 3. s dizzy, e.g. wit to cause to fai no, he is faint no, he faints, blood by his w tware no, the me has made him pirakuru atw. to piti. 4. about or conce = ɔkɔmfo ŋky = wokɛ a wokobisa nu. ntwareé [cf. twa ling; dross; sik twabo no atwit atwaréé, ford; Judg. 3,28. ntware-mú, inf. cross, to pass
atwopo, pl. n-, axe, hatchet; syn. abonua, akümä, poopoo.
a short thick stick &c., cf. apotibaa.

a little bit cut off at one stroke; cf. bu-prekõ, te-prekõ; otw. ye seŋ oyare a eye hü yi, death is better than this dreadful disease; wo kasa yi ye otw. seŋ wo anim-difo no de, your short speech is better than that of the previous speaker (or than those of the pr. speakers); - final decision.
1. = twa, twëtwë (Mk. 9,20). 2. = twa: etwa se me hö tew, I must be holy. 3. = tware.

[red. twitware] 1. = twa 15, to cut, i.e. cross a way. pr. 3076. 2. to cut off, stop, intercept, intersect; to cut (one) out, to get the start of, to outrun, to meet in order to catch; cf. buw 6. pr. 210. - tw. asem ano, to bring a matter to an end; s. twa 12. - tware wi, to travel in the evening to shorten the next day's journey and thus avoid travelling in the sun. - aboa bi guaŋ a, wuse: fa hayi tware nol aboa no reguaŋ no, mekotwaree no na mikum no. 3. to stun, make senseless or dizzy, e.g. with a blow on the head; to cause to faint: a) (impers.) etwàre no, he is fainting; wapira na àtwàre no, he faints, swoons, from loss of blood by his wound; - b) aduru no a-tware no, the medicine (being too strong) has made him faint; nsä, okom, a-pirakuru atw. no; cf. twa, to beraw, to piti. 4. tware so, to inquire about or concerning: ótwàre yàré sò = okobisa nea efi so na oyare no bae (wö okomfo ŋkyeŋ); wökotwàré sò hwè = wökobisa ade okomfo ŋkyeŋ a. s. wokobisa funu.
[cf. twa 22] bad gold, not sterling; dross; sika-bone, sika mu fi; nea twabo no atwitwa; cf. biŋ, tia.
ford; cf. asutwaree, atwae. Judg. 3,28.
inf. [s. twa 17]: di nt., to cross, to pass through.
[twe ase] obsc. scoundrel, rascal; a most impudent abuse.
[atɛm]: ŋkodidii atw., he began to use most insolent and impudent language.

inf. [twa 27, si, to stop]: di a-, to describe a circle, to go or turn round; to compass round about. Job 16,13; wodi a. n. s. nnipa pii ,bö kontonkroŋ, a. s. onipa biakö twa ne hö si n'anaŋmu; wodi no hö a., they walk or dance round him; cf. di kyinhyia; - n'aniwa di a., his eyes are rolling, from pride, haughtiness, anger. - atwásí-tútúw, rolling or whirling dust. Isa. 17, 13.
[G. otšwa-ši-ogbo, thou strikest, i.e. fallst to the ground, thou diest] the cholera; chicken cholera, contagious disease of fowls.
[twa, to separate, taa, to stand]
n-, sack-cloth.
inf. end; enni ntwato (= ase), better: eto rentwa da, cf. etó 3.
inf. [twa, to so] false accusation; syn. asötö, anotötö; mmoto-so, osusukä. pr. 3409.
(nest or) swarm of ants, bees, wasps; oḍaŋ a ahohow, kotokürödü, mpennaa n.a. ye wö nnua so; nnowatwáw. pr. 1753.
inf. [twa 8, we, to eat] cutting and eating together (of the same piece): di tw., to have communion together; cf. twákä.
adv. imitative of the noise produced by a stone or piece of wood cast into the bush.
inf. [twa, yère] false accusation, unfounded imputation; aspersion; cf. osusukä.

v. [red. twëtwë] 1. to draw, pull, drag, lug: aponkö twë teaseenam, the horses draw the carriage; ótwë dua di n'akyi, he is dragging a piece of wood after him; otwëë adaka fii mpa ase, he drew forth a box from the under the bed; - twë mfëtewee so, to harrow. Job 39, 10; twë nnosoa, to carry loads; - to draw out (a sword). pr. 1486;

tuo, he takes up his gun to fight; cf. kā 33, atutwẽ. - twẽ.. ba, to attract. - la. to be handsome, beautiful, fine; odaŋ a otwẽ, a fine house; ŋhwireŋ a otwẽ, a beaut. flower; pl. adaŋ a otwẽtwẽ &c.; aberante or ababaa a ne hō twẽ, a hands. young man or woman; ŋhwireŋ yi twẽ, this flower is beaut.
2. to drive: mframa twẽ amunuŋkum, the wind drives the clouds; yemã mframa twẽẽ yeŋ, we let our ship drive. Acts 27, 15.

3. to withdraw, retire, return, decrease, sink (of water). Gen. 8, 3. Am. 8, 8: ɛpo retwẽ, the sea ebbs; watwẽ ne hō kɔ, he has withdrawn; twẽ wo hō, As. (Akp.) be off! cf. guaa. - (obsc.) otwẽ ne hō = ɔtã, he farts.
4. to remove (e.g. one's leg). pr. 719. 962.
5. twẽ naŋ, to tread in weaving.
6. to withdraw mutually: wotwẽẽ woŋ hō kɔe, they fell out with each other and fought.
7. twẽ ne hō ase, to creep, to move slowly by drawing the body along the ground as a worm or reptile does; cf. otwẽasee; otwẽ ne hō ase, he crawls off, with-draws secretly.
8. twẽtwẽ, intr. to be stretched.

9. twẽ mu, a) to draw out in length, to lengthen (out). pr. 3419; Ex. 19, 13: long (adv.); twẽ kotoku mu, to open a bag or purse, opp. dwōm ano; - otwẽ ne naŋ mu, s. ɛnaŋ. - b) to stretch, extend: otwẽ ne mũ, he stretches himself or his limbs, cf. ɔtẽe ne mũ; metwẽ me mũ merepe anim de, Phil. 3, 13. pr. 507; - c) otwẽ ne ta mu, he draws his bow. 1 Kg. 22, 34.

10. .. mu twẽ, to be drawn out; be to interrupted (the interval between the two armies were interrupted for a while): dɔm abieŋ no ŋhyiam' no mu twẽẽ kakra, the hostilities between the two armies were interrupted for a while; n'awo mu twẽẽ, the time between her bearing of children grew long, she ceased to bear children. Gen. 29, 35.
11. .. ntam' twẽ, it is far from .. F. Mk. 12, 34.
12. .. so twẽ, to be diminished, to decline, abate (the upper part withdrawing or flowing off): n'ahɔɔdeŋ so antwẽ, his natural force was not abated.

13. twẽ, to protract, prolong, prorogue, postpone, put off, defer, delay, adjourn: woatwẽ asɛm no ahye da, the matter has been deferred to a certain (fixed) day; woatwẽ asɛm no ato hɔ, the matter has been put off indefinitely. - twẽ.. to mu, to prolong the time or postpone the term for (paying a debt, carrying out a work &c.); wɔntwẽ da biara ntom', not one day more is allowed (e.g. to complete some work). - twẽtwẽ asɛm, to continue or keep on contending.
14. twẽ hama, F. twẽ tonto = bɔ ntonto, to draw lots. Mt. 27, 35; cf. ahamatwẽ.
15. twẽ kanea, to trim a lamp.
16. twẽ .. kãra, to recall a person's soul; s. ɔkra.
17. twẽ akurodo, to carol, play, sport, frolic, wanton.
18. twẽ mãnsɔ, to be at variance.
19. twẽ ŋwōrãm: ntam' a etwẽ ŋwãname no yɛɛ ŋdeŋ, the discord, tension increased (Ger. die Spannung wuchs immer mehr); s. ŋwōrãm.
20. twẽ mpẽnã, to form a connection or cohabit with a man or woman not legally married; to live in a state of concubinage.
21. twẽ sika, to draw, demand money which is due.
21a. to draw in (air), to pant (for), catch at with open mouth. Ps. 119, 131.
22. twẽ .. asɔ, to pinch or pull some one's ear, i. e. to punish (for disobedience), to chastise, castigate, discipline; woatwẽ n'asɔ, he has been punished.
23. twẽ ataa (wɔ .. hɔ), to struggle, contend (for).
24. twẽ .. toa so, to reconcile, reunite; Brɔfo atwẽ Akuapem nè Ŋkraŋ atoa so.

25. red. otwẽtwẽ ne hō, he loiters, lingers, hesitates; wosoma no a, ɔmmɔ paŋkraŋ ŋkɔ; biribiara a orekɔye no, ɔnyé no mprempreŋ, na ogyina hɔ kakra; wantwẽtwẽ ne hō sɛ ɔbɛye sa, he did not defer to do so. Gen. 34, 19.
26. red. watwẽtwẽ ne hō, he has dressed himself as a beau, dandy, fop or coxcomb, having pulled in his trousers or other dress so as to make
to contract: ntwetwẽ nsɛm no biara mp.; kyerɛw ne nyinaa mã mã; s. pũa, v. 1.
ne tirim atwetwẽ no = ne t. akyere no.
ne yam' hyehye no, twitwa no, he is moved with compassion. Mt. 18,27.
to provoke; yɛde atwɛtwɛ wo abufuhyew no asɛnsɛŋ hɛn do, we have thereby provoked thy wrath and indignation against us.
to draw near; cf. twiw 1.
to draw out the breast (in order to give suck to the young. Lam. 4,3).
completely, entirely; woakã ne nyinaa atom' twɛ, they have told everything in entirety; ɛbɔ sɔ twɛ = pɛ.
female genitals; vagina. pr. 3279. 3579 a.

a species of antelope, the duyker, cf. ɔdabɔ. pr. 1427. 1437. 1570. 1791. 3410-18. - ɔnɛ me te twɛ-ŋhoma (or adowa-ŋhoma) so, he is sitting with me on the skin of an ɔtwɛ (or adowa), i.e. we are not on good terms with each other. Otwɛ yɛ aboa a osũa, enti ne ŋhoma no nso sũa a nnipa baanu trã so a, ɛnye 'ye. - s. ɔtwɛawo. - atwɛ-bɛŋ, a horn of the ɔtwɛ.
a species of grasshopper.
dinosoa hɔ atwɛ, to carry loads; cf. twɛ 1.
a species of bean, growing in the earth like the ground-nut; cf. atádwé; when cooked they are called abobɔe.
a certain game; di or sisi or tow atwɛ, to play with small sticks (made of palm branches) on a level piece of ground with a number of holes (18-20) in it. pr. 2968; s. agoru.

to look, seek or search for or after, to search out: wotweɛ no, they search him out; ɔtweɛ n'afum' ade; ɔkɔtweetwe abe, he goes in search of palm-nuts; ɔtweetwee ne mme so sɛ ɔbenyã bi ana; mekɔtweetwee (= mekɔhwehwe) me hɔ sɛ menyã ntrama bi mamã wo ana? (Jer. 50,20).

to pick out what is laughable about a person, to censure, criticise, satirise, to mock, deride: wotwee no they are mocking him = wodi no hɔ fɛw, woserew no. - 3. tweɛ .. so, to go over (the boughs) again. Deut. 24,20.
bɔ or kɔ a-, to arrange or hold a battue; nnipa bebree bom' kɔ wuram' na wɔmã mmofra kasa pam mmoa bɛre wɔŋ na wokum wɔŋ; cf. (boa)boafo, homofo, tabaŋfo.
interj. s. pãtwɛ; serew tw., to laugh heartily.
the sound of a chirping bird; sũ twɛ.., to chirp. Isa. 10, 14.
dog, bitch; cf. ɔkramaŋ, ɔtwea-taŋ. pr. 474. 1345. 3632.
abusively: a mean worthless fellow, good-for-nothing fellow, wretch.
s. Ntwa.
a small dog. pr. 913.
slave (only his own master may call him so). pr. 1788.
a sack; wode kente na ɛye; cf. awotwaa; - osu yɛe yeŋ sɛ atw., we were drenched (by rain).
interj. expressing utmost disregard or contempt; tush!
corner, extremity of something angular, e.g. of a table, a house &c., external angle; cf. hiŋ, kokoam', batwɛw, Ak. batwɛs.
the head corner-stone.
a species of climber, hama bi a ɛye deŋ.
wire.
chain worn as an ornament, about the neck, wrist or loins, made of silver or gold.
a certain bead; s. ahene.
a byname of God, s. Onyankɔpɔŋ; it is said to mean the Almighty; nea ɔbɔ ade nyinaa. [fr. twɛ adi ampɔŋ or twɛ adua & pɔŋ or tweri dua a, wompɔŋ?]
one who drags the beheaded corpses away] 1. nickname of pataku.
the corpse-dragger (to the king), i.e. of victims who had been killed or sacrificed.
a species of pot-herb.
Akw. woato no atw. = woato no sraha.
s. twãpɛa.
pl. a- [aboa a ɔtwẽ ne hɔ ase] serpent, snake; cf. ɔwo; reptile; dragon.
s. twáase, (obsc.) scoundrel, rogue, rascal.
n., = atwaatãm.
bitch.
s. atweaa.
s. twẽaa., wire.
the cry of fowls when alarmed.
woaŋwo yeŋ otw., we are not foundlings (like the young of antelopes, which are said to be left by their mothers after birth).
inf.: di a-, to remove from one place to another.
pl. n., F. = otwẽwa, ramrod.
twébéw’, twéem’, twô, interj. certainly, of course, to be sure!
adv. completely, entirely; waye tw., he is silent; wamũa n’ano tw. = koraa, he keeps perfectly silent.
inf. [bɔ atwee] arranging or holding a battue.
magnet, loadstone.
= ŋkábom’.
Ak. = tweré.
inf. a play; s. átwẽ.
certainly; ɔrewu ara tw.
pl. n., Ky. [that which is drawn] drawer of a table, chest of drawers &c.; kɔtwẽ twẽẽ no na yi ades no bẽra!
[that which is drawn] wire; kɔbere or aɔwa ntwẽẽ, wire of copper or brass; s. twẽa. - ntwẽẽwá [dim.] thin wire.
better: twaitwai, q. v.
persons engaged in a battue; woŋ a wokɔ atwee no; s. atwee.
pl. a-, a fawn. Cant. 4, 5.
the sound produced by squirting liquor from the mouth; ohinam tw.
inf. withdrawal, retirement.
monastery.
pl. -fo, monk; cf. ɔkokorani.
a piece of elastic.
inf. seduction; banishment. Lam. 2, 14.
a hat made of the skin of an otwẽ (an antelope). pr. 1112. 2894.
adv. 1. completely, entirely, thoroughly; s. twɔ̃m. - 2. nimbly, strongly; otiá fam’ twẽm twẽm twẽm = pìm pìm pìm.
one kind of the itch; wadɔ ntwẽm = ɔyare asẽ.
adv. s. twebeem.
F. = ntwɔ̃ma.
ntwómma, a bead; s. ahene.

[lit. draw, let me draw, or that I also may draw, i.e. do what you please and let me also do what I please] discord; tw. mpá woŋ nsem mu; contention for mastery. pr. 3501. - di tw., to be disunited, to be at variance with each other; cf. di 92; omaŋ no nè woŋ hene di tw.; Iehowa na mo nè no nnni tw., do not rebel the Lord! 6, 15.
etwene, bridge, & bone. pr. 3406.
Ky. length; ɔdaŋ no atw. si anammɔŋ 20. 1 Kg. 6, 2. 20; Akr. n-, Gen. 6, 15.

v. [red. twentwɛŋ] to wait; twɛŋ kakrá, wait a little; tr. to wait for, expect: mã yentrã ha ntwɛŋ no, let us sit down (or remain) here and wait for him. pr. 390. 3421. - twɛŋ .. ase, to loiter, linger, tarry, delay: wótwɛŋ woŋ náŋ ase kàkrá (e.s. wo-nam bɛrɛɛoo, wɔnnam se kaŋ no bio), they slacken their pace or gait a little, make little halts while walking; twentwɛŋ wo naŋ ase, slacken your pace! cf. tutu wo anaŋ duom, go on slowly! ɔtwentwɛŋ ne hɔ (or ne naŋ) ase, he loiters, lingers, hesitates; sika a ɔde betua ka no yaw a eye no nti, ɔtwen twɛŋ (ka no tua) ase, because he grudges the money required for paying his debt, he is slow in paying it; - to defer. Prov. 19, 11. - ɔtwɛŋ ne nsa, he is greedy, voracious.
adv. nimbly, cleverly: ohu-rúw’ twɛŋ twɛŋ = ífɛŋ feŋ, he jumps about nimbly.
v. Aky. = kyene.
bridge; ɛtwéne da asubɔnteŋ no so, there is a bridge across the river; cf. mpata 3.
pl. a- or n-, Ak. = akyene, drum; kā tw., to drum. - n-twentá, hooked drum-sticks.
twer ..., a large tree similar to kyeneduru, with smaller leaves, used both for house-building and drums.
pl. n-, Aky. rammer, ramrod, gun-stick; wode tw. na ɛpoma tuo; - ɔretwē n-, he takes (notes) down the number of the men (warriors, soldiers) belonging to a company.
a plant; its fruit is nyaŋkont'rama (= kwakunt'rama).
pl. a-, a healthy, vigorous, energetic, strong person; onipa a ɔwɔ ahõɔdeŋ, oyare biara ŋhaw no; ɔye ɔtw. = ɔhõedeŋfo; ɔnyé otw. = ɔye ɔyarefo. Isa. 59, 10.
red. v., s. tweŋ.
ɔyè tw. tw., he loiters, lingers = ɔtwentweŋ ne naŋ ase.
mebaa ha no mefa ha a, tw. tw. miŋhũ no, when I came here, it was difficult (impossible?) for me to find him.
a broad deep wooden vessel used in digging gold.
v. F. = tweri, to lean on; to confide on. Mt. 27,43.
F. = ntweri; si -, to dig a winepress, wine-vat. Mk. 12, 1.
pl. id. F., leg, shank; knee; bu -, to bow the knee. Mt. 27,29; to kneel.

v. 1. to gnash, grate, grind; abufuw nti ótwère ne "ase", he grinds his teeth (ebinom de "ase" kā hõ, na ebinom nso kā "twere" ŋkutoo); ebinom wu a, wɔŋ hõ ye wɔŋ yaw nti wotwere wɔŋ sẽ ansã-na wɔawu. 2. to peel with the teeth: tw. abɛ. pr. 68. 75. 1590. 1739; tw. abuŋ, to eat unripe fruit (sour grapes. Jer. 31, 29). - 3. = tweŋ, to wait for.
v. Ak. = 1. twerɛw. - 2. = kyerɛw; red. tweretwere.

Ak. twèrɛe, twedee, pl. a-, the hand half-clenched on purpose to strike with it; also the blow thus inflicted. pr. 3251; (a knock with the knuckles). - tow or bɔ tw., to inflict such a blow. pr. 1629. 2824. 3252. 3422. - mmea bɔ tw. - oyii twedee na ɔde abɔ me hwene so; - kɔ atwereɛ, to fight with the fists. pr. 518. - cf. kutruku, kotɔromũa, nsàkɔtɔ.
F. pl. n- 1. a species of frog; cf. apɔtoro. pr. 1548. - 2. = aketekré, cricket.
a beetle similar to tɛferew.
dwɛrɛbɛe.
pl. a-, flint(-stone); cf. otuo. pr. 490. 1629. 2824. 3252. 3422. - twèrebo-túo, a musket fitted with a flintlock, flint-stone gun.
a large tree; s. tweneboa.
pl. n-, a species of rodent animal.
pl. a-, a person fighting with his fists [knuckles]; Aky. Ɔkw. atwerebɔfo.
atwerorɔ, a species of grasshopper. pr. 1548.
Aky. = antweri.
atweri-, [tweri, gyedua]: ye atw., to be idle, lazy.
v. to scratch as a hen; to scrape, grate; s. wɛre, wɛrew & the foll.
red. v., to scratch, paw: ɔpɔŋkɔ de ne naŋ tw. fam', the horse paws the ground with his foot; - to scrape with a knife; cf. hũã.
pl. n-, pistol, revolver; syn. kodiawuo.

v. [red. twitweri] 1. to incline, lean against: ótwèri duá, he is leaning against a tree; ètweri hó, it is leaning there; - de .. tweri, caus., to put or place so as to lean against: fa tuo no tweri kokoam', put the musket into the corner. - 2. to trust or confide, have or place confidence in; to rely on: mã yɛmfa yɛŋ akyi ntweri wo, let us place our confidence in thee. - 3. n'anim tweri hɔ daguaa se ahwehwe, his face is shining brightly like a looking-glass; m'anim twerii = minyãã anuonyam, s. anim.
1. a place for squashing the
F. atweri, pl. n-, ladder, scale, stairs; F. steps, stairs made of wood, stone, bricks; s. at'rápòè, atweres. pr. 341. 3002; - odi ant. no so aforosĩaŋ, he goes up and down the ladder.
a palm-tree to be ascended by a ladder.
the back of a chair.
s. atwere ...
a fluid of any kind.
Ak. = atwerede, grasshopper.
F. = sètwere, gnashing of teeth. (Mt. 13, 42).
[ade a wotwẽ wo ase] thumb-bolt, sliding catch-bolt.
the 'ham' of an ɔtwẽ (antelope). pr. 1570.
-dade [ade a wode twẽ biribi so]† rake.
a shrub (with blossoms like those of the coffee-tree), whose root is eaten.
ɔ-, pl. n-,† locomotive. Chr. twétia: twa.. tw., to circumcise. [G. fo ketia].
twetiafó, -ní, pl. twetiafo, a circumcised man; cf. momɔnotɔ, oduafoɔ.
a species of small ant, ntétéa bi.
inf. circumcision, practised by some of the surrounding tribes, as the Ŋkranfo, Hũafo, but held in great disdain by the Twi-tribes. - twetia-twá-mù-fó, the circumcised. Phil. 3, 3.

red. v., s. twẽ, espec. 8. 13. 25-28. 30. 32; otw. ne naŋ mu, s. ɛnãŋ; - tw.. to fam', to let down. Acts 9, 25; - .. wuhũ a, ɛmã wo tirim tw. wo, it is a touching sight; - mede nsuohyew twétwẽẽ me mfẽ, I fomented my side with hot water.
si .. a-, to deride, mock; syn. sereserew; Onyaŋkɔpɔŋ, wonsí no atw. Gal. 6, 7. - F. = goru hɔ. Mt. 27, 29. 41.
adv. : ɔserew tw., he laughs heartily, roars with laughter.
pl. a-, mocker, scorner; F. ɔ-twetwesini, pl. a- -fo.
wɔ-, to go astray, be erring, wander, roam about : ówò ntw., ɛ.s. obi nam kwaŋ na wayera rekyini wuram' hwehwe ɔkwaŋ; ɔde no wo ntw., he leads him wrongly, astray, out of the way.
Ak. = ápànέ, s. ampaŋ.
the sound heard when the key is turned in a lock; ɔtoo poŋ no mu tw., he locked the door.
syn. kyéŋkyereŋŋ; osu antɔ nti fam' aye tw., as it has not rained, the ground is hard and dry; opp. dɔfoo.
the rushing sound of chariots; ye tw., to rush. Jer. 47, 3.
a species of bat.
twõ, twow.
pl. n-, ramrod = twenewa.
pl. a- [otwẽ, dim.] a young ɔtwẽ (antelope). pr. 1099. 1437; gazelle. Cant. 2, 7.
[red. twitwi] 1. to thrust, push or knock about; wotwi no = wosunsũm no. 2. Ak. = twiw, twuw.
F. to draw near. Mt. 15, 8.

n. 1. twi or twitwi, retreat. Agyemaŋ de (twi, or) twitwi bɛbɔ Yaw Duodu so, Agy. fell back upon Y. D. - 2. bɔ.. twi, to thrust, push or drive back, to repel, repulse: yɛabɔ dɔm no twi, we have driven back the enemy (perhaps only for a while, not yet defeated). - 3. bɔ twi, intr. to be alarmed by sad or joyful news; to be in a stir, agitation, tumultuous commotion; to get up in confusion, to run together hastily and confusedly, but with determined steps: woate sε asemmne a emu ayɛ hũhũ reba ɔmaŋ mu, sε ebia dɔm reba n. a. a, na ɔmaŋ no abɔ twi = abɔ wi. - 4. nneema a skɔɔ twi kɔɔ bὲrɛmáŋ nyinaa, all things together; ode nneema a skɔɔ
nyinaa kɔe, he went away with all his property.
Aky. -e, pl. a-, 1. leopard. pr. 851; cf. ɔsebɔ, kŭrotwiamansã, asabontwi (odontwi). - 2. a drum; s. akyene.
(= Twii), Twì, the Tshi Language, comprising Akan, Brɔŋ or Kãmãnã, and Fante. - Cf. Gr. Introd. Notes.
Ak. = ntwiw-anim.
inf. [bɔ twi] public alarm; confusion connected with it.

a large edible root, similar to the tubers of yam, with large leaves like the plants of the Arum family (Taro? Indian turnip?); one kind has been brought to Akem and Akuapem from Wasa, another, called kɔɔkɔ, from the West-Indies; a similar kind, known in Akr., Akuap., Fante for a long time, is amaŋkani.
one of the original families of the Tshi people; cf. App. D.
a tree bearing red flowers (tulip tree).
1. a species of (pot-)herb. - 2. a cutaneous eruption on the legs; cf. dwofãã.
[F. Kwiforo] a district of the Gold Coast to the north of Wasa, and the Tshi tribe inhabiting it, written by Europ.: Juffer, Tufel &c. Gr. p. X.
Twì-kásá, the Tshi language.
o-Twíni, pl. (a) -fo, Twifo, a man of the Tshi nation; cf. Ɔkanni.
ahɔɔdɛŋ,† electro-magnetic power.
better: ntwene-ntá; s. atwené.

red. v. twãm, to become dry, hard (duaba bi, aduam-momono biara a wonoae, kuru aním nsu a ekata anim sɛ nea awu); lean, thin, wrinkled (onipa yi atw.; n'anim atw.); - to fade away. Ps. 18,(46). 45. - watw. sɛ mmabaa, he is lean.
v.n. scurf, scab; ade a atwintwam kuru anim.
red. v. twaŋ, to become lean, wrinkled; F. to wither.
waye -, he reels, staggers, tumbles; cf. ntintaŋ; gyabagyaba.
noise as of something falling to the ground; ɔhwee fam' tw.
better: ntwene-ntá, s. atwené.
v. to slander, calumniate. pr. 371.
inf. slander, calumny. pr. 3270; railings. 1 Tim. 6,4.
a small species of ant; aboaa a esɔ kakra kyeŋ ntetea na ɔka wo a eye yaw sɛ, nsɔ ɔka wo a, na ŋkūrɔfo se: obi retwiri wo.
