v. [red. wòwɔ, wòwɔ̀e] 1. (orig. to stick to a place), to be or exist in a place: ɔwɔ hé? where is he? mewɔ hó, I am here, present; ɔwɔ daŋ mu, he is in the house; shɔ na afi akese bi wowɔe, there are (or were) some large houses. In this sense wɔ is used almost exclusively in the contin. form (but: ɛnó wɔ hɔ ànsã [lit. that may remain aside &c.] let us leave that aside for the meantime - ɛno ntrã hɔ ansã); besides trã the vv. ba or kɔ are used to supply the wanting forms, and the neg. is taken from the v. di: onni hɔ, he is not there, not present. pr. 97. 1300. 2268. 2347. 3439f. - ɛwɔ obi.., there is some one.., pr. 3437. - ɛwɔ nea óyé na onyá, somehow he gets (at) it .pr. 3438. - wɔ hó tè dɛ́n? how do you do? mewɔ hó sáára, I am still unwell. - ɛwɔ wo hɔ, Aky. = ɛwɔ wo nsam', it rests with you, it is in your power (to do or give something). Prov. 3,28. - ɔwɔ hó wɔ hó ara, he is (or was) in the same condition. - ɛwɔ hɔ wɔ hɔ à, we sometimes go there, we go there now and then. - ɛwɔ hɔ na oyaree, in course of time he was taken ill. - sε ɛwɔ hɔ wɔ hɔ à.., if it once gets so far; if it lasts for some time. - 2. wɔ often serves merely to introduce an adjunct of place, stating the place in which the action expressed by a preceding verb is going on; it is then not translated at all: oye adwuma wɔ afuw so, he does (some) work (and in doing this work) is on the plantation; i.e. he is working in the plantation; magyaw me poma wɔ ne dag mu, I have left my stick in his house; mihũu no wɔ Mamfε, I saw him at Mamfe; mekɔ-hwεε no wɔ afiase, I went to visit him in the prison; mihũu no [wɔ] hɔ mprempreŋ, I saw him there just now; odi gua wɔ baabi, he is trading somewhere. The aux. v. wɔ is, however, better omitted wherever it can be done without injuring the intelligibility of the sentence, espec. in Ak.; s. Gr. § 102,3. 117. 223,1. 224. 225. pr. 353. 883. 1319. 1457. 3025. - wɔ is used of an indefinite, casual or transitory stay at a place, te of a stay of some duration. - 3. Phrases: a) wom' = wɔ mu (to be in,) to be real, actual, to be truly so: asεm yi wòm' àmpá, the matter is really so; neg. enním', it is not so; - ɛbewom' sε..., = ebia, sesεe, gyàma (gyàbea), perhaps. - ɛwom' wom' no, (e.g. in narrating) 'so it went on for some time'. - b) m'aní wɔ só, my eye dwells on (it), i.e. I have it in my mind, have not forgotten it. - c) ɔwɔ só, he is renowned, held in esteem; ɔbosom a ɔwɔ so baakɔ neŋ. - 4. (orig. to stick to a person) to be in the possession of, to belong to, to be some one's property: ɛwɔ me, Ak. = ɛye me dea, it is not mine; ɛnní wɔ me = ɛnye me dea, it is mine; ɔdáŋ yi wɔ me, this house belongs to me. pr. 2942; Gr. § 102, 2. Rem. - 5. to have, possess, hold, to be possessor or master of: ɔwɔ sika pii, he has much money; aberekyi wɔ mmeŋ, the goat has horns; ɔwɔ mmosea (wɔ) ne kotoku', he has pebbles in his bag; mewo abusũafo wɔ and in Akem; mewo nnamfo bebree (wɔ) kũrow yim', I have many friends in this town. pr. 3439-45. - In this sense also v. contin. form get, obtain, is taken from the has nothing. ɛhɔ wɔ asεm, what he has task, business. wowɔ yε wo you here?

corn; cf. awio; ne yam' resi no awuo, 1. he is illiberal, stingy. — 2. he is in great anxiety.

v. 1. to scrape or peel (off), in smaller particles than by wae, cf. wẽrew, twere, twerew; wopo abrɔbe a, wowere n'ahabaŋ so na wuyi mu abrɔbemfuturu. pr. 459. - 2. to pull the feet in order to trip, overthrow, throw down: ɔwẽre nó ahwè fám' = okuw no ahwe hɔ = waso ne naŋ na watwẽ no amã wahwe ase; wantumi aŋwẽré me, s. kuw, v. - 3. atamfo rewere gum', the enemies are fighting boldly.

seems to have orig. signified the part of the body enclosed by the ribs and breastbone, the chest, thorax, and its contents, and is no more used in a bodily sense, except in some peculiar phrases. [G. mii]. 1. the heart or breast as the seat of the affections and capacities of the soul: a) né wẽre áhòw, his heart is dried up, i.e. he is in (deep) grief, dejected, sad, sorrowful, looks downcast; also: ne ẅ. ahow ne hɔ; me ẅ. ahow no, I am angry with him = mempe no, wayi me abufuw, mafa no abufuw. Ex. 16,20; - b) ɔhow me ẅ., he grieves me, makes me sorrowful, causes me grief or pain, makes me angry &c. - c) ɔkyekye me wẽre, lit. hẽ binds up my (wounded) heart (cf. mũhãmã), i.e. he comforts, consoles, he cheers me up again; - d) ne wẽre akyekye, he is comforted, consoled, has found composure, his heart has been set at rest. - 2. the heart as the seat of courage, trust and confidence: a) ne wẽre aba, F. his peace of mind, courage or confidence has come (again); cf. 1d & awẽrsba. - b) wabɔ ne wẽre, F. he has provided for his confidence, i.e. has secured his success or welfare = wasũa nea ehĩa na dabi ode bɛye biribiara a, obɛnyã biribi adi. - óhũ né wẽre bó, he learns to comfort or console himself. pr. 582. - c) me wẽre hye wo mu, F. my confidence is in thee; ɔde ne wẽre ahyɛ Onyaŋkp. mu, he has put his trust or confidence in God. - d) nyã wẽre, to trust; - e) hɛn wẽre twer (tweri) wo ahũmobor kɛse no, F. we trust in Thy great mercy; ne dziŋ mu ɔde ne were betwer. - 3. the mind, memory: a) ne wẽre afi, his mind has come off it, i.e. he has forgotten it = n'ani apa so; wɔŋ ẅ. remfi wɔŋ mu biakõ, none of them will be forgotten; kae m'asɛm yiye, mmã wo ẅ. mmfi! remember my words well; remember well what I said, do not forget it! pr. 259. 3510. - b) né wẽre áfi, he has forgiven (an offence, injury or wrong). pr. 492.

the skin of the living human body; the thick skin of the sole of the foot and of thick-skinned quadrupeds; ne hõnam ani nyinaa yɛ dennennenney sɛ ẅ.; àyisãã, pere ẅ., na mpere merebo! pr. 2289. 3511. 3667; ababawa a ne wẽrem' yɛ fɛ, a girl with a beautiful skin. - Phrases: 1. ɔnsẽŋ ne wẽrem', he has not (sufficient) room in his skin, he hõnam yɛ no sɛ ensõ mmã no, i.e. he is ready to leap out of his skin. - ohũ ne wẽrem' ade, he is suffering; syn. ohũ amanne. - 2. di ..wẽré, to take satisfaction for a killed person from..: woredi no ẅ. = woredye onipa a wakum wɔŋ busũani no ho sika; wukum wo yɔŋkõ nipa a, na wogye wo so akatua: nnipa baasoŋ (ɛne wogye

akoa nè afãnaa?) na woagye asiede (wo-abu dehwerede na woatua); cf. di 57. — 3. to..wéré, a) to avenge, to take satisfaction for, by punishing the injuring party, to vindicate by inflicting pain or evil on the wrongdoer, to inflict just punishment upon evildoers on behalf of ourselves or of others for whom we act; to revenge, to inflict pain or injury for, in a spiteful, wrong or malignant spirit, to wreak vengeance for, maliciously: métɔ mé wéré wo m'atamfo nsam' or ho or so, I avenge myself on my enemies (perh. orig. I vindicate my skin from or against my opponents); metɔ no w̃. mama me nua, I execute vengeance on him in behalf of my brother; - b) to pay what is demanded or due as satisfaction for killing a person: meretɔ or mekótɔ no w̃. = meretua onipa a mikum no no abusãfo ka, merekotua no anyãsoŋ ka.
to be in open enmity; me nè no kyi aw̃.; awéré a onè me kyi no, emu ye deŋ.

thick (& hard); mpuran aw̃., heavy timber, a strong beam; dua yi ye aw̃., this tree is high and thick (and its wood hard).
the act of taking satisfaction or compensation for a man's life; revenge; revengefulness; vengeance; me na aw̃. wo me, vengeance is mine. Rom. 12,19; cf. awéretɔ. ɔ-wéredífó, revenger. Ps. 99,8.

any sickness in the stomach or abdomen; indigestion; "me yam' ye pupu-pupu; ade sã a, na m'afuru ahye (or hye); mikesiw a, kaŋkaŋ; mididi a, enyé me de".
[ɔyafunu] great hunger.

[con. ne yáfunu] that part of the body which is between the breast and the thighs: belly, abdomen; wokyeŋ wəŋ y. ye ayi, pɛ sika = wonnidi bebree a. s. wonnidi koraa, they abstain from food on account of a funeral custom or from avarice. pr. 250. 874. 3526f. - ne yáf. ntumi nnyina, she does not conceive. - yàfúnu-ba, pl. yafumma, offspring &c., s. yafumma.
belly, espec. its inner part, abdomen, stomach: aduru ŋweneŋwene sa yafunum' yare; wòmb; syn. yam'. pr. 412.
better than : ɔyafumyare.
əyáká, a species of -sea-fish = esiré. [treatment.
F. persecution, cruel
s. óyàá.
v. to grind (abũrow, corn) on a large stone by means of a smaller one (s. o̦wiyammo, -ba), - a work always performed by women; cf. dwow.

a disease of the skin; salt-rheum; also ringworm; oyare bi; ɛrebebi ase a, asẽ biakõ pɛ na étòw hó, na afei ŋkete-ŋkete totow hó na eyerew aa kosi sɛ ekata ohõnam nyinaa so; ebi-nom de, sε woaŋhwe no yiye a, edaŋ wəŋ kwata. pr. 1547. - kinds: yam-pá nè téferè-yám.

yá mù [con. ne yám'] the inner cavity of the human or animal body, the chest as well as the abdomen, belly, womb, and its contents, viz, the heart, lungs and other intestines (bowels, guts); cf. ayam'de; hence also the heart, bosom; - any cavity; hãmã-yam', the (inner) part of a climbing plant which touches the tree; cf. ŋkrante-yam', nsayam'; - pr. 41: the interior of a house. A. the word used in a physical sense: berebo da onipa yam' nifã, the liver is in the right (side of the) abdomen; ne yam' ka no, he has belly-ache; ne yám' ábò, he has lax or loose bowels, having too frequent discharges. pr. 1529; ne yam' (ntumi nnyina, a) he (or she) has loose bowels; b) she does not conceive, cf. ɔyafunu; ne yam' atim, his bowels are no more loose; s. tim 3; - me yam' asã me nnɛ, e.s. me yam' a eyɛɛ me kũsun no agyae, to-day I feel relief from my stomach-complaint; me yam' ato me, I am now free from stomach-complaints; me yam' atew me, I have recovered my appetite; - okã ne yam', he eats something, takes some refreshment; ɔde hãmã abə ne yam', s. tabə mühãmã; - ɔrewu ne yam', he is suffering (bodily or mentally).

B. The following phrases express, not physical or bodily, but psychological functions, or phenomena of the mind (Gr. § 216-19), or contain the word (yam') in a figurative sense. 1. me yam' te sε me nsam', what-is-in-my-heart-is (as plain or as clearly visible) as what is in my hands, i.e. I am telling you the plain truth. - 2. ne yam' hyehye no or (twi)twa no, a) he feels compassion, is compassionate; cf. ehóhøre; F. ne yam' twẽ no. Mt. 18,27. - b) he is in great anxiety, in painful uneasiness
inf. looseness of the bowels; diarrhoea.
[yam' ade] a decent expression for stomach (ofuru, nsonokese, nsonopoŋ), intestines, entrails; watwa ne yam' mã n'ayam'de nyinaa ayi agu; the inwards. Ex. 29, 13.
stomachic(s); medicine for disorder in the bowels.
[yam, v.] place where corn is ground; mill; cf. awiyameé.
pl. a- [yaŋ, v.] drummer; s. okyeremã.
otwa ne y. mã no, he meets him half-way by showing (him) how he can be pacified.

[yam' ogya] exasperation; grief; ohye no y., he incenses him, enkindles or inflames him to violent anger, irritates, provokes, exasperates, enrages him; ode awɛrho ba no so. 1 Sam. 1, 7; ohyehye ne hō y., he worries himself. Isa. 8, 21.

[s. yam'] bowels yearning from compassion or anguish; anxiety, anguish or trouble of conscience, remorse, compunction, compassion (also for one's own body); nnyã ne hō ay., do not worry yourself about him! Prov. 24, 19.
inf. [s. yam'] compassion, commiseration; anxiety.
-keka, belly-ache, stomach-ache, colic. pr. 394. 1546.
a species of yam; s. ɔdé.

[s. yam'] niggardliness, stinginess; bɔ..ay., to act stingily or illiberally (towards). pr. 486. 1981; s. bɔ..kãne; wòbɔ Nyaŋkp. ay. = wonni nea Onykp. sērɛ sɛ wónye mmã no so; ye ay., to be (habitually) unkind, stingy &c.; oyi me ay., he says I am illiberal, stingy, niggardly.
pl. a-, niggardly, stingy, illiberal person, who does not give any thing to others; miser. pr 3530-34.
s. ɛyám. — yampaeaw? pr. 1248.
ayam'tué, inf. looseness of the bowels = ayam'bɔ.
a-, pl. a- [ɔdé a ehye or ɛwɔ odé yam?] the first crop, the produce of the second crop; ammo mpow, mpow pá nea wotù wò mpow.
inf. [s. yam'] good-nature, kindness, liberality, bounty. pr. 3535; n'ayam'yé or compassion.
de, a good-hearted, kind person. pr. 3535.
pl. a- [s. yam'] charitable, merciful person. pr. 3535.
inf. [s. yam'] kindness, readiness to help. ayamí-adé, 22, 18. — aya, Judg. 5, 9. — will, willingly.
yam not taken out with the first crop, but remaining to the time of the second crop; ɔdɛ à wɔántú ammã ammɔ mpɔw, na etrã ho kosi se wotu mpɔw pã mù; ɔdɛ à wómpàgè dá, ná wotù wɔ mpówbére mu.
inf. [s. yam'] good-heartedness, good-nature, benevolence, benignity, liberality, bountifulness, charitableness. pr. 3535; n'ay. dôsô, he is very kind or compassionate. Ja. 5,11.
deeds or acts of benignity; good-heartedness &c.
pl. a-, a benevolent, liberal, charitable, merciful (Prov. 11,17. 19,6) person. pr. 3536 f.

inf. [s. yam'] free-will, willingness, readiness, alacrity of mind. — ayam'yí-adé, freewill-offering(s). Lev. 22,18. — ayam'yifo, pl. id. volunteer. Judg. 5,9. — ayam'yí-sò, of a free will, willingly. Lev. 22,21.
the breast of an animal, as far as the ribs go. pr. 502.
v. to drum; yan akyene, to beat a drum with sticks (formed as hooks); cf. kã aky. — ayáŋ, inf..s. akyenekã.

v. [red. yenyaŋ] 1. to lie in, to lean, rest or repose on ("yaŋ" ase dôsõ kyeŋ "tweri", yaŋ has a wider sense than tweri): òyaŋ (pl. wòyenyaŋ) apakaŋ mu or boŋkrã mu; dua no abu yaŋ dua no ŋkoŋmu; cf. babayeŋteŋ; — òyaŋ hó = òwɔ ho, he is here, present. — 2. caus. to put, set, or lay down or on, to lean or rest upon, to lay over, so as to support a thing at some place of support or rest; maběre nti mede m'áděsoa mayáŋ hó; òde áyàŋ só, he has put down his load at a resting-place (ayagee); mede brukuu mayaŋ brukun yi-so; — (Ɔkw.) to hang round the neck; óyàŋ ahené, she hangs beads round her neck; óyàŋ ahené, she wears &c.
the scaffold of poles outside the town used as a privy, necessary (ɛyaŋ hɔ ntia); W.C.; cf. dúá-sò, duasee, kãasee, maŋkyiri, tea.
place where loads are put down, that the carriers may take some rest, resting-place (nea wodé adésoa yaŋ daa nè nea wòsɔe daa); cf. asose.
v. Gy. to wear round the neck (sika, ahene). pr. 1378.
necklace.
pl. s. ɔyaa.
v. F. = yantam.
[yam', agya] the back (opp. to yam', the front) of the human body; da ay., to lie on the back. pr. 2023.
reply to salutations, addressed to one born on a Thursday; s. Yaw, yàa. Gr. § 147,9.
v. to wallow; òyantám' fàm'; měkɔè no, òde ne hó yàntám' fam' na mekɔmãa no so.
F. banteŋ, long, lengthwise.
[ɛyam, dua] a plant used as a medicine for "yam".
v. F. = yare, to be sick, to have pain.
s. ɔyare.

v. 1. to be sick, be ill: ne hō yɛ deŋ, ǝnyaree peŋ, he has a strong constitution, he is never sick. pr. 26. — 2. to be ill of, suffer from, be afflicted with: oyare mpete, atiridii, he has the small-pox, he has fever; y. gyapim; anom'dew, ntoto, twow, ayamka &c. pr. 392-4. 3548; ǝnyaré yare biara, s. tew 10; ǝyaré yàre-pá, he suffers from a real sickness; ebia ǝyare bi bɛyare wò bá, perhaps your child will fall ill. - Cf. dodow & duru, vv. - red. yarèyàre.

pl. a-, n--wá, ayareyàré, sickness, illness, disease. pr. 356. 3540-47; ne y. agyae, his disease is over; - oy. ye ne naŋ, he is diseased in his feet; he suffers in his legs. - fa wo hō nyarewa ase nnansã yi, the frequent cases of sickness have become less of late; - di yare, to recover from a sickness; medi yare yi ana? s. di 40. - sa..yare, to heal or cure from sickness: aduru yi asa no yare; wasa ne y. amã no.
pl. n., F. = ɔyare, ɔyarewa; cf. ɔyere.
1. a multitude of diseases. 2. an epidemic disease, pestilence, plague; oy. asi kürow mu, aba ɔmaŋ mu = owu aba ɔmaŋ mu na ekum nnipa pii; cf. owuyare.
pl. a-, F. yarfo, sick person, patient; invalid, sickly person; one afflicted with some bodily defect; cripple. pr. 286. 1045. 3549f. — ayaré-fó-dáŋ, infirmary, hospital.
pl. id., = ɔyarefo.
a cutaneous eruption on the lips; herpes labialis.
a tender of sick persons; nurse. K. § 262 ŋk.
sick-bead; cf. hũ 3 & yare 2.
inf. [sa yare] the act, art or power of healing, of curing a disease.
reward for curing a disease, physician's fee. pr. 3545.
pl. a-, one that heals or cures a disease, doctor, physician; cf. oduyefo.
di y., to be an invalid; odi y. = ne hō nye no deŋ.
pl. n., 1. s. oyare. 2. cf. asonokā.
owuyare, deadly sickness, fatal disease; pest, pestilence, plague.
F, yaryar, red. v. yare, Mk. 1,32.
s. oyare.
the lower part of the belly; abdomen; pubic region; - ayáase-máŋ (jocosely) one feels hungry.
aduaŋ. pr. 782.
v. [red. yeyaw], Ak. ye, to abuse, chide, scold, upbraid, revile, insult, affront. pr. 409. 442. 3552f.; śyàw no, syn. óhòro no, ɔbɔ no ahohora, ɔbɔ no adapaa, ɔsopa no &c.
inf., F. ɛ-, abuse, scolding, upbraiding, reviling, railing, insult, invective, abusive speech. pr. 411. 3551; cf. oye, oyes. — yaw, a. wild, fierce.

ɛyáw [cf. oyare] pain, ache, bodily distress; mental distress, grief; òpe no yáw, he wants to cause him pain; ne yaw kāā wɔŋ, they were sore. Gen. 34,25. — yedi yaw, it grieves us; we are sorry for it. - ye yáw', to pain, give pain; cf. dokow, v. pr. 59. 464. 588; éyè yáw' sê, it is very painful; ɔbaakɔ ye yaw, to be alone is hard, pr. 452; eye no yaw pa ara dodo sê, it grieves him exceedingly; me ti yè me yáw' = beŋ me, I have a headache; ɔkwaŋ no mu ye yaw, the way is rough, difficult; fig. ne sika ye no yaw, his money pains him, i.e. it is painful to him to spend it, though circumstances make it necessary. pr. 2951f. - ne hō ye no yaw, a) he is effeminate, too sensitive to (bodily) pain: ne hō ye no yaw dodo nti, ommá wòn-súáŋ' no; - b) he is envious, jealous, spiteful (ɔmpé se ne yɔŋkɔ n'nyā papa a wanyā no bi).
di..yaw, to attend on a hunter = di abɔfó. pr. 549. — ókò ayàw, he carries venison for hunters; said only of men; mmea nni ayaw.
F. Kwaw, pr. n. of a male born on a Thursday. Gr. § 41,4; cf. yaa-ó & App. B III.
Yaá, F. A'bá [= Ayábá] pr. n. of a female ditto. - asase Yaa, (As.) the earth which was created on a Thursday, and whose day of service (is or) was a Thursday? Cf. Afuwa & asase 1.
Ak. = aẅowa, brass.
bowl. Zech. 12,2.
Ak. earthen vessel, dish; s. kuku, asaŋka.
Thursday. - ayaw-dáé = awukudae; s. adae.
pl. a-, the attendant of a hunter; cf. bofoya.
a. painful; owúù wù y., he died a very painful death.
ayeyáde [ade a ɛyɛ yaw] torments, torture; wóyè no ay., they torment him. - F. ye..ayaayaadze, to persecute = taa.
grievous matter, injury, wrong, insult; wadi me ay.
yayáàya, syn. basabasa; ye..y., a) to confound; to prevent a person by noise from making his statements

v. (red. yeyɛ; cf. yɔ, ɔye, ɔyɔ, nyee) 1. a) to come or enter into existence, be created or produced: ɛnye hãŋŋ! let there be light! eyee hãŋŋ, there was light. Gen. 1,3. - b) to come to pass, come about, happen, occur, chance, befall, take place: eyee dɛŋ na ahina no bɔe? how did it happen that the pot was broken? minnim senea eyee, I do not know how it came to pass. - c) to be done, performed, executed: eyee saa, it was so. Gen. 1,7.9; dabɛn na eyinom beye? when will these things be? Lk. 21,7; aye senea wohyee no, it is done as thou hast commanded. Lk. 14,22; nea entumi nye nnipa fäm' no, Onyankɔpɔn fäm' de, sbetumi aye, the things which are impossible with men are possible with God. Lk. 18,27. - d) se ɔbeye a, F., if it be possible. Mt. 26,39. - e) Sometimes the v. ye serves instead of adverbs or conjunctions expressing time, manner or intention: eyɛ saa no, Swissifo asɔm' dwoo woŋ, when it had come thus, i.e. in this way, by or after this, the Swiss had at length peace; nea ebeye na wɔanyɛ sika nti wosii ɔmaŋ no apempem n.a. Gr. § 264,2. Rem. § 279 Rem. 2. - ɛyɛ a..., when opportunity offers, occasionally, now and then, sometimes; cf. pawá; woye a, bɛra me fi, come to my house occasionally, come to see me sometimes; anye saa a..., else, otherwise; - anye anye a, nnipa ɔha kɔɔ hɔ, at least 100 people went there. - f) ye hɔ, F. = ba mu, to be done, be fulfilled; ɔnye hɔ, so be it; wo apedze nye hwɔ, thy will be done. Mt. 24,3. (26,42). - g) ɛnye änsä, let it be for the present! - 2. a) to become, grow, turn, come to be (to assume or receive the character or quality expressed by the noun or adj. forming the complement): ohia na ɛmä ɔdehye ye akoa, poverty causes a freeman to become a slave. pr. 1344. - in the perf. and fut. also: to be; ne sika nyinaa asä, wayɛ ohiani, all his gold is gone, he is (or has become) a poor man; wayɛ akwakoraa, he is an old man; ɔdaŋ no ayɛ gow, that house is ruinous; m'atade ayɛ fi, my coat is dirty. pr. 1292. 1344. 3556. 3579. 3580. John 1,14; woye no saa a, ɛbeye yiye (contracted: ɛbeye' ye), if you make it (or do) so, it will be right. - b) to behave, conduct one's self: otuu no fo se ɔnye papa or ɔnye abofra pa, he admonished him to behave well, to conduct himself like a good boy; ɔnyɛ papa, he behaves badly; - ye kyikyiri-kyikyiri, to be unruly &c.

3. in the contin. form (Gr. § 91,2. 102, 1. 167. 168. 199, 2. 3) to be, = to have or posses the character or quality expressed by the noun or adj. forming the complement: ɔye abofra, he is a boy; ɔye ɔbayifo, he is a sorcerer; sika ye fe, gold is pretty; abrobɛ buŋ nye fremfrem, an unripe pine-apple is not sweet. pr. 60. 2154. 2950. 3555. 3563 f. 3574; asem no ye asɛmpá, the report is good news, or, proves to be true; ɔye ɔhene, he is a king. - 4. impers. a) with a succeeding noun or a sentence: to be. = to turn out to be: eye ɔhene, it is the king; ɛnyé ɔhéne (ne no), it (or, that) is not the king; ɛyɛ no anihaw, it is laziness on his part; ɛnyé me anisɔ, s. anisɔ; ɛnyé me awɛrefiri, it is not forgetfulness on my part. - b) The neg. ɛnyé must be employed when the v. ne, marking identical existence, is to be made negative: ɛnyé me núa ne no, or, ɔnyé me núa, he is not my brother; cf. Gr. § 199,1. 247, 1. 3a. pr. 3593. 3601-5. - c) In a sent. connected with a preceding sent. by way of co-ordination, the neg. ɛnyé is sometimes put instead of a repetition of the predicate in the neg., the same predicate having occurred in the preceding sent. in the affirmative; in Eng. in this case merely the adv. not is used, = it is not true of: ɔbarima bi wu a, ne mma na edi n'ade; ɛha yi de, ne wofase na odi, ɛnyé nè mmá, when a man dies, his children (generally) inherit his goods; but here his nephew inherits, not his children. pr. 1892. Gr. § 253, 3. - d) eye and ɛnyé serve also to make any member
of a sentence prominent, s. Gr. § 247; enyé mè bá nà wóhweé nò? was it not my child that you flogged? pr. 3064. 3371.

to be in number, to amount, rise or reach to a certain number or quantity: wòye or wóyè (= wósi) nnipa dú, they are ten in number; wòaye aduonu, they have increased to twenty; the fut. does not state the exact number, but merely the amount probable in the opinion of the person speaking: mmofra beye se aduonu na ewɔ hɔ (or, mmofra wò hɔ beye se 50), there are about fifty boys there; mato ŋkokɔ beye se aduonu; wobe- beye se oha, they will amount to a hundred. Gr. § 175, 2.

to appear, seem, look: éyé me or óyé me sè wàdà, he seems to me to sleep; eye me se osu betɔ nne, I think we shall have rain to-day; ebeye yeŋ se yeasɔ dae, we shall be like them that dream; asase no ye se eba aduaŋ na nsu pii wò so, the country appears to be fertile and well watered.
to be in some state: ye bra, to be in the state or period of menstruation; ye kuna, to be in the state of widowhood (pr. 3567); ỳe k., s. kuna; cf. 10e.

to show, exhibit, manifest or display (some inclination, temper, quality): ye nnam. pr. 3572; ye anẽm, nsi; ye ntem; ye timobɔ &c.; ye hũ, to be in fear, be afraid, be a coward. pr. 3568. 3638; - ye akaw; - to be addicted to: ye anihaw, werehunu; - ye ahantaŋ, to indulge in pride, to pride oneself on, to be proud; ye ahõpe, abosompe, bŭrofope, anuonyampe, apse- madi &c.; ye potwaa; ye berebere. pr. 3558; ye nyãã; - ye aniyiyi, to be ca- reless; - ye ŋkommomĩm. pr. 3569; ye meŋkɔ-medi. pr. 3571; ye atiwase. pr. 3575. - ye fakye, ye nteŋ, F. (see these and other words, of which the meaning is not given here, in their proper places).
8a. éyè fe dè, nansó ènyé dè, it is pretty, but it is not sweet or agreeable; éyè nã, ehó yè nã (pr. 991. 2950), s. onã.

9. to make (to cause to exist, be or become) in various senses: a) to produce, create: Onyankɔpoŋ yee ẅiase nè nea ewɔ mu nyinaa. Acts 17, 24; óyee asase nè soro. Gen. 2, 4; cf. bɔ (ade); - ye ahuru, to make foam, i.e. to foam; ye ŋkãnare = gye ŋk.; ye hoo, to make a tumultuous noise, a roar. pr. 3582. - ye hɔ ŋko, F. to make unclean. - b) to form, frame, fashion, fabricate, manufacture, construct: wòde abéŋ (nà é)yè afé, combs are made of horn; ye afiri, to make an engine &c. - ode owɔ yee kesua mãã no, he gave him a snake instead of an egg. - c) to institute, constitute, compose, organize, arrange, set on foot, set in operation: ye (..) ha, to go hunting (to give chase to, to hunt after). pr. 3578. - ye ayi, to perform a funeral ceremony. - d) to make or convert into: óye ne hɔ apanyimmaa, he makes himself, i.e. behaves as a pert, impudent person, plays the malapert. - e) to put into a state or condition (expressed by a qualifying noun or adj.), to constitute, to appoint or elect to an office or employment (often with the aux. v. de for the passive object): woyéè no safohéne, or, wòde nó ysè os. Gr. § 205, 1. 5; ye wo hɔ hare! s. hare; óyee no kroŋkroŋ. Gr. § 205, 2. John 17, 17; - ye.. yiye, to make good, i.e. to mend, repair; ye ne hɔ yiye, to ease oneself; s. 10c & yiye. - 10. to do; a) in general: pr. 439. 2283. 3557. 3581; woye deŋ (ni)? what are you doing? what shall this be? adé no, wódè beyé dèŋ? what will you do with that? mã yeŋ biribi yenye, give us something to do! pr. 3561f. - ye nea wósè yé, do what you have been told to do! - ye.. hɔ biara, to one's utmost or one's best; óyee hɔ biara se obekyekye me ẅere, he did his best to comfort me; - miduu hɔ no na ode aye hɔ dedaw, when I arrived there, he had already gone. - b) to effect, produce an effect or result, bring about, work out, carry through; to ac- complish, fulfill, achieve, effectuate: woáyè adé! you have done a (great) thing, accomplished a noble object, achieved an important undertaking, performed a praiseworthy work; well done! - anye no hwee, it makes no impression upon him. - c) to .. for, to .. cute, transact; i.e. to com- adwuma, to do work, a wanye n'adwuma, he having done his work, your business; - yi yi bone, to do evil, to keep: ye sukuu, to keep, observe; y mm ye kuna, to observe the hood; cf. 7. - 11. call forth (from), exci- anibere, to excite lust 3573; ye yaw, to cause pain. pr. 440; ye m cause or excite wathi to be loathsome, odic mmobɔ, to excite pity erable); ye.. h.ne, - abufuw, - ania di, - asõm' yaa, - ahòhow, wõa) &c., see these.

12. to happen or occur to, be done to, befall (cf. 1): edeŋ na aye no na osũ, what is the matter with him that he weeps? kobisa no dekõde a aye no, go and ask him what is the matter with him; wofa ho a, ade bɛye wo! if you go that way (take that road), something will befall you, i.e. that way is dangerous. pr. 473. — 13. to something to a person, espec. to do harm to somebody: mentee se osãmãŋ aye onipa biribi da-biarada or peŋ, I never heard that a ghost ever did a man any harm. pr. 440. 3455. — oyɛfo aye me, a mischievous enemy has done me harm; wáyè no = waye no bone bi a ɛkã no baabi a ɛmma, he has done something extremely and unconceivably bad to him. pr. 35; hwe nea woaye me asɛm yi hɔ (= nea wonè nò yɛ or yó (inf.), he has done all he troubled me about this matter! wãwie nò, has made away with him. — 14. to affect with (produce an effect or change upon), to cause to, do to, bring upon, inflict on, commit upon, show or offer to: oye me bone, yiye, ahohora, ŋkɔmponade, aninyanne, aniwude, anuonyanne, ayayade, ayisãde &c. — 15. to apply to, rub with: oye m'anim ŋkyene, m'atiko yisa, s. ŋkyene; kũrobow ne hũãm a mmea yam ys; wode ye woŋ hɔ, s. mmõwa; - ye .. a-duru. pr. 2819. — 16. To affect as (or according to the manner of): oyɛ me sesã, he acts upon me as a departed spirit. — 17. to treat as: oyɛ me hɔho, he receives, i.e. lodges and entertains me as a guest. — 18. to bestow care upon: ye (ɔ)ba, to bring up, nourish, maintain, care well for a child. pr. 1177. — 19. to apply, use, make use of: ye asõ, to listen, hearken; mónye (nò) asõ, give or lend an ear (to him)!

Heb. 11,35. 40. [The forms eyee,

as heard in quick speaking, may be mistaken for a pret. or fut. tense, but are only contractions of eye yiye, ebéye yiyé; cf. ayɛ yiye, anye yiye, erenye yiyé; wo hō ade nyé; ne hō ade a eye nti.., s. shō B.

(with an obj.) to be good for, useful to: oyé mè or òye me (wo) m'adwuma nom', he is a good help to me in my work; ō, onipa yi, oyé mè. or òye me (= oyé mà me), ah, this man is of good service to me; eyé nò (or èye no), it is good for him, useful to him.

inf. the act of making, doing, performing &c. - Ak. = oyáw, animkã. òyé! (ɔkw.) an exclamation (inserted in the discourse) expressing embarrassment.

yê, interj. a) a reply to a call, showing that it has been heard; wofre wo a, wugye so se: yê! - b) a shout indicating determination, joy, scorn &c. Gr. § 145, 1: well (then)! hurrah! huzza! yê, óni-óo! ah, there he is! mmofra di no yê yê = wohuro no.
adv. amain (with sudden force, strength or violence), violently and suddenly; cf. yersdede; wode mirika yèe rehyiá nò, they came running amain to meet him.
= wèe.

F. = nyee, nneyɛe.

a. broad, wide, large; ɔwɔ ano y., he has a broad mouth; n'ano yɛ y., his m. is broad; akuru y., a large wound.
F. n., manner of doing or making; performance; fashion, style; minnim ne y., I do not know how to make it. - ye-béw, place of doing &c.
a person who has lost his former fame; daŋ or yɛ ay.
ye .. ay., to do (something) negligently, carelessly.
[oyere bone] a bad wife. pr. 3641.

[ade a woyɛ, ade a yɛwɔ yɛ] 1. a thing made, work. Isa. 29, 16. - 2. a thing to be done, custom, duty. Deut. 25, 5; ɔde obea no ko ne kürom' akoye no n'áyéde, he has taken her into his town to treat her as is customary in the family; - cf. ahyeyede, ahyede, asede. K. § 19.
one who has been a wife for a long time. pr. 3642.

Akr.; a-yéfa-dee, Ak.; ayé-fere, Aky. [oyere-fa ade] fine for adultery, indemnification claimed by, or paid to, the offended husband. pr. 3643. - tɔ ay., to pay for adultery with another man's wife. - ayéfare-sãŋ, ayéfa-san, inf. denying the charge of adultery. pr. 1667. - ayéfa-sɛm = ayérefasɛm.
[con. ne yéfo] 1. maker, doer, author. - 2. mischief-maker, a mischievous enemy (nea wakum wo ba bi pɛŋ a. s. wamã woanyã amane bi pɛŋ); ɔyéfo aye me, s. yɛ 13.
F. = apapa, good, just, pious persons (Mt. 5, 45).
[ayeforo ade] presents given by the bridegroom to the bride - ayɛfo-hyía = ayeforohyía.

pron. 1. we (prefixed to the v.: ye-, ye-), poss. our, obj. us; Ak. yɛne, yere, yɛŋ, F. ɛhyen(nom), nye, nyere, hyen. Gr. § 53-59. - 2. Ak. = wɔŋ, wɛŋ, Ab. bɛŋ. Gr. § 58. Rem. 2.

a making once for all. K. § 229.
pl. yermo, yernom, F. = oyere, yerenom. Mt. 19,3.8.
v. F. = yare.

Ak. hāra, F. yew, 1. to go astray, to lose one's way; wàyéra ɔkwáŋ, he has lost the way, cf. watɔ kwaŋ; way. wuram', he has lost himself in the bush. - tr. ɔde y. ne naŋ so kwaŋ, he seeks thereby to obliterate his tracks so as to mislead or frustrate investigation. - tew ani yera, to frustrate. Ezra 4,5. - 2. to be lost: adé no ayéra, minhú, the thing is lost, I cannot find it. pr. 565. 817-19. 1077. 1319; me sekaŋ ayera (me), or (tr.), may. me sekaŋ, I have lost my knife; syn. me sek. afi me nsa; hwe n' iye, mmã ɛnyera, take care of it, do not lose it (prop. do not let it be lost); eso ayera, every trace or vestige of it is lost; - ne ŋkwã ayera no. - 3. to pass away, vanish (away. Ja. 4,14), disappear: osram ayera, miŋhũ bio, the moon has disappeared, I see it no longer; mprempreŋ na miŋhũ no, na sesee way., I saw him only this moment, but now he is gone; oyerae wɔŋ anim. Lk. 24,31. asem no ayera m'ani so = afi or apa m'ani so, me wɛre afi, the matter has vanished from my memory. - 4. to be killed: kaŋ no, sɛ wɔrebedi asɛm anadwo na wɔmpe sɛ obi te a, na wo-abo dawuru sɛ: ɔhene sɛ: obiara a ofi anadwo yi beyera = wɔbekum no; a. s. ɔhene wu na wɔreye n'ayi a, na nnipa nyinaa nim sɛ, wosi kwaŋ so a, wɔ-béyéra = wɔbekum wɔŋ; wayéra nɛ náŋ sɔ (kwáŋ), vulg. his tracks are lost = wɔakum no a. s. woatɔŋ no, wɔayi no hɔ. - 5. wayera me sɔ (or, me naŋ so), lit. 'he has made me lost', wiped away my existence; wayéra ŋo, he has caused it to be lost.
inf. perdition, destruction, ruin; abolition. Ob. 12. Heb. 8,13. - ɔ-yerábá, pl. oyerá-mma, son of perdition. John 17,12: a prodigal.

Ak. hãram [red. yerámyéram] 1. to yawn, gape. — 2. to shout (at), hoot (at), threaten severely; obuee n'ano pɛ na woyeramyeram no mã ogyaee, as soon as he opened his mouth, they shouted at him so loudly that he left off speaking. — 3. y. (wokum guaŋ na wode ŋhoma no akɔhata aŵia so, na wode nnua abobom' na awo; cf. pa 5 c.); yere ŋhoma no mu, stretch or smoothe that crumpled paper! wáyère háma no mù pintiŋŋ, he has strained the cord very tensely (tightly); óyère ne honam ahɔ-odeŋ mu, he exerts the strength of his body; — wágye asem no áyère mú, he has taken up the case and (stretched it, i.e.) pushed it farther than the others of his party would have done. — yère hó = si hɔ or tim hɔ pintiŋŋ, to stand fast or immovable; n'akwaŋ yere hɔ pintiŋŋ, his ways are rigid, i.e. firm, unwavering. Ps. 10,5. — ɔdaŋ - yère..bo, to enlarge the chest; cf. fuw or horaŋ bo. pr. 1157. — y. wo hɔ = bɔ mmoḍeŋ! wóyèrée woŋ hɔ dii saa dwuma no, in doing such work they exerted themselves to the utmost. — yere.. koko de yɛ.., to risk, hazard. — ɔyeree ntamaḍaŋ no kataa trãbea no so, he spread the tent over the tabernacle. Ex. 40,19. — 2. y. akyene, to stretch a skin upon a drum, to cover a drum by stretching a skin upon it. — 3. to rest upon one's head, e.g. a heavy load requiring the straining of one's nerves or muscles: èyere wo (= èsɔ wo), it is heavy (or, presses) on your head; mihyiaa no na adesoa yere no (= sɔ no) when I met him, he was carrying a heavy load on his head. — 4. áyère só, prop. it has been stretched or strained (upon), i.e. it has been put to the utmost strain so that it cannot bear any more; asem no ay. so, the case or matter is hard, difficult, trying; — the words: sɛ ayere so a, (= sɛ emu ayɛ deŋ a,) serve to express the adv. absolutely, positively, utterly, by all means, at any rate, at most, at the utmost, or, with negation, by no means &c.: áyère só koraa (e. s. woyɛ no biribiara na ɛnye yiye, or, wokã no baabi na ɛmma) na wuntumi ŋkɔ a, mã obi ŋkɔ, if you cannot by any means go, let another go; sɛ éyère só à.., in case of necessity; sɛ enyéré so à, ŋkɔ sá, except in case of necessity he does not go to war. — 5. s. yeyere 2. 3. — 6. n'ani yere so, nso eŋhũ hwee, he does all he can to be able to see, but in vain. — Cf. katere.
v. = yerɛw.
pl. nom, Ak. ɔye [con. ne yére] 1. wife, spouse or lawful consort of a

man; pr. 410. 430. 3645-54. — 2. a woman destined to become one's wife, cf. siyere. — 3. the wife's sister. — hyia or ware y., to take a wife, to marry; fa ɔy., to commit adultery with another man's wife. — Cf. ɔyekoro. — (ɔ)yerenom baanu aware, bigamy. — (ɔ)yerenom dodow aware, polygamy. — 4. the father's sister's daughter, the mother's brother's daughter, the mother's sister's son's wife. [cf. oyare.

F. sickness, disease; yèredede, 1. a. acid, sharp, biting to the taste, acrid, pungent, hot: wókàw yisá à, éyè y. — 2. adv. 'at one go', at full speed, speedily, with rapid strides &c.: ade kyĕe no, na ode hwee (kwaŋ) so y. kodnu Osu, the next morning he set out and without interruption proceeded or hastened on to Osu; cf. yĕe; ɔbɔɔ y. kotow hyee wɔŋ so, he rushed impetuously or furiously upon them; cf. bɔ 11; bɔ y. = tu mirika, to hasten, to hurry. — 3. okwàŋ yérè-dɛé, a straight road.
many wives; polygamy. pr. 3655; — ay. aware, polygamy.
a medicine [aduru] to enlarge or fester [yere] a wound, to make it ulcerate.

ne hɔ ate ay., efí biara nni ne hɔ biem, he has become quite clean, there is no longer any uncleanness about him.

twi: àyerɛm: tew yeŋ àyerɛm, mfa wo nsa ŋkā! clear the space for us, grant us a clear, free, open space, give us free hand or scope (and let us fight out our scuffle), do not meddle in it! àyerɛm òo! obi oo obi ŋŋkā oo! nobody shall interfere to pacify them, let them fight (and we shall see who is the strongest)! Kwasi atew Kwaku nè Kofi àyerɛm, Kws. has urged on (or instigated) Kwk. and Kf. to fight (instead of pacifying them), he has set them to a fair trial of strength.

eng: duel, single combat.
a bird with red eyes. pr. 2317.
s. yereba.

[red. yereyerew] 1. to spread, e.g. a fluid, a drop of oil on a garment, a drop of ink on blotting-paper; cf. baa, bae, terɛw &c.; ŋŋó yèrɛw ɔpóŋ no sò, oil spreads on the table. - nsú y. ntama mu, water penetrates cloth; nsú ayèrɛ-yerɛw ɔsapów no mu, the sponge is soaked with water; fa kafe no yère-yerɛw adiwo; yɛreyerew kafe no mu! spread out the coffee! - ɔyerɛw' dɔm no mu, he set the battle in array, arranged his army. 1 Chron. 19,17. — 2. né bò yerɛw' no, he feels disgust or nausea; cf. fono. — 3. F. to blaze, to be vivid.
inf. spread, expansion, enlargement.
red. v., s. before.
glittering, sparkling; ogya dew y.; anyinam pae y. pr. 3656.

wɛrɔdɔɔ &c.
[asɛm a woaye] 'a word made for an occasion'; invention, fiction, unfounded tale; eyi de, eye ayésém kwa = asɛm bi a ennim' koraa na woboapa afa rekã se nea ɛwom', opp. nokwásém).
Ak. ɔyesuo [ye, esu] method; ɔkwaŋ a wɔnam so ye biribi.
[oyere|substituted [cf. tɛw, v.] in the place of one who died; wosi wo ayetɛw n.s. woware obi ba na wo yere no awu na wɔmã wo yere foforɔ si anaŋmu.
yãw; ye y., dzi y. (Mk. 3,5).
yera, to lose; to be lost. Mt. 5,13.
aye. Mt. 9,8.
a root.
yiw. Mt. 5,37.
aɔwɔwá.
[ware yere] marriage, matrimony; di ay., to intermarry; cf. di 85. — ayeware-dí, inf. intermarriage.
F. brazen vessel.
múmɔ, name of a month; about June, s. ɔsram.
ɔyéá.
an evil disease. Eccl. 6,2; cf. ayàyáde.
red. v. yaw. — ayeyayáw, inf. (repeated) abusing, scolding &c.; cf. ɔyáw.
red. v. ye. — ayɛ-yé, s. -yé.
red. v. yɛ; ɔyɛɛyɛe n'ano, he smiles.
inf. [ye ayɛ] the act of making presents. pr. 3658.

ayeyéde [ade biara a wode ye obi aye a.s. wode kye obi; enyé akatua, nanso enyé sɛ ese se wode mã no] a present, gift, donation, offering, oblation; wode ŋŋuan, ŋkokɔ, ŋkesua, nsã, ntama, ntrama, sika, kɔye abosom aye (to obtain his protection). — ayɛyéde-mã, inf. oblation. Dan. 9,27.
favourite wife, the most beloved among a plurality of wives. pr. 3433.

v. red. 1. s. yere. — 2. y. ne hɔ, to puff one's self up, to be inflated, swell: krakum y. ne hɔ (e.s. ɔyɛ ne hɔ kuroo or kusuu no), the turkey-cock puffs himself up. — 3. ɔyeyéré n'anim (ɔyɛ n'anim sɛ ɔbarima de), he looks big, struts, swells, assumes a pompous, ostentatious, or arrogant air or manner.

[asɛm à éyeyeré so] extravagance, eccentricity, rash or inconsiderate (mode of) proceeding, precipitation; stubborness, wilfulness, obstinacy &c.; asɛm a sye dey, nanso nyansã nni mu pii; di ay., to be stubborn, wilful, capricious, &c.
inf. [yi aye] praise, laud, commendation. pr. 1505. 3657.
praises, Isa. 63,7. — yeyífó, pl. id. praiser, extoller. pr. 3533.

v. [red. yiyi] 1. to take away, remove, take off, take out: yi nneɛma no fi poŋ so, remove the things from the table! óyi hoŋ fi dompem' na odi, he takes the marrow out of the bones and eats it; adaka no si poŋ ase, yi fì adi, the box is under the table, take it out! koyi aduaŋ wɔ mukaase, go and fetch the food from the kitchen! yi ne ŋkataso, take off the lid or covering! yɛde tow yi de yi yeŋ ku mu afɔa or yeŋ hɔ mmusu, by this poll-tax we ward off the sword from our neck, turn off our danger. — 2. yi aguade, to take out goods or wares: a) woyi hyɛn mu ag., they unload, unlade, discharge, disembark or land goods; b) woyi aguade, they buy or purchase goods from a shop or store. — 3. yi atade, to take, pull, put or cast off a coat or other European clothes; cf. pa. — 4. yi, to shave, take off the hair; óyi ne tí, ne bogyess, he shaves (the whole of) his head, his beard; cf. bu 10, anim B. — woyi wɔŋ hene ti, they dethrone their king; cf. yi 14. Formerly the head of the king was shaved at his deposition as a sign of his being divested of royal power and dignity. — nnera oyii ne ti, yesterday he (the medicine-man) dismissed him from treatment as cured. (On recovery, the heathen natives cut their hair short or shave it off). — oyi ne ti so, he cuts his hair. — 4a. oyi ne ti, he cuts off his head; ogyina n'atiko reyi (ne ti) afi so, he stood behind him preparing [prop. commencing] to cut off his head. — 5. yi..hɔ, to remove: wóayl no hɔ, euphem. expr. = wɔakum no, they have killed or executed him, cf. wayera ne naŋ so.

6. yi..hɔ, a) to rinse, wash away: wuguare samina wie a, wode nsu foforo yi wo hɔ; — b) yiyi hɔ, to clean, cleanse, purge. Joh. 15,2. — 7. yi mu, a) to rinse, wash out: fa nsu foforo koyi asaŋka yi mu! — b) yi or yiyi mu, to pick out, choose, select from or among: mamã-wo ade yi a, nyiyi mu! pr. 399; yiyi mu, to purify. Ps. 12, (6). 7. — c) to except; to exclude from. pr. 1093.

8. yi, to pick out, choose, elect, select; yi bofo = tu bofo; yi.. si hɔ, to elect and present. pr. 543. — 9. to set apart, appoint, take for some purpose. pr. 3659; — yi.. to hɔ, to select for a special purpose, set apart.
10. yi..ani, a) to turn away the eye (from): ɔye adwuma a, onyiyi ani = ohwɛ so yiye. — b) wayi m'ani ahye me ŋkyeŋ-

mu (wamã m'anidaso ayɛ ɔkwa), he has disappointed me. - c) ntama yi, éyi n'ani (= ani tew pɛ), this cloth gives or has its proper colour; the colour appears as it ought to be without dulness or admixture. - 10a. oyi n'ani so (kakra), he takes a (short) nap. - 11. yi anim, prop. to produce, i.e. show a frank, candid, open face; to set one's face to, have the decided intention, be bent upon: s. anim; wokã asɛm a, yi wo anim kã, na nnipa nyinaa nte, speak with a bare, open face, without fear, that all may understand! John 7,13; - oyii n'anim siesiee ogye no de bae, He directly prepared and procured salvation; wanyi n'anim na osiesiee wɔŋ mãã ogye no, he indirectly prepared them for salvation. K. § 207.

a) (to remove the obstacle,) to make a beginning with eating (new yam); - b) to give an account, to answer or account for; - c) to interpret, to explain the white man. - d) to answer; to gainsay; to refute, confute, disprove (a statement); to defend; to plead for; to clear (one's self) from an accusation; oyi n'ano, he vindicates or justifies himself; obi kɔkã asɛm bi to wo so na wokoyi ano a, ɛnna wose: wayi n'ano; - oyiyi ano, he answers; he gainsays; - e) to make excuse, to apologize; oyi ano sɛ ontumi ŋkɔ; - wokãã asɛnkoro yiyii wɔŋ hɔ ano. - yi saŋkũ ano, s. saŋkũ. - yi anom, lit. to clear one's mouth: wayi n'anom, he has relished his food.

to draw away the hand; euphem. for to eat: mekoyi mè nsá mabà mprémprɛŋ ara; moáyì mo nsá àná? have you eaten already? - 14. yi.. so: a) to lift off, take off or away from upon, to detract, diminish; to uncover &c. - b) to dethrone: wóyi no só = wótù no só. - 15. yi.. tirim' to speak out or uncover one's thoughts, opinion or sentiments; to disclose one's self; to make a declaration; oyii ne t. kyerɛɛ me, he 'broke' his mind to me; wayi ne tirim akã, he has confessed (it) plainly.

to take or give out one's heart, i.e. to do something heartily, cordially, with purpose: miyii me yam' mekyerɛɛ no, I frankly and sincerely told him what I had against him; miyi me yam' (fitaa) meda wo ase, I thank you (very) heartily; woyii wɔŋ yam' pefee or kroŋkroŋ gyee asɛm no, they received the word willingly and sincerely, with all readiness. Acts 17,11; oyi ne yam' redi (or, sɛ obedi) asɛmmone, he purposely commits wickedness.
to be evacuated: aduru no amã ne yam' (nneɛma) ayi or ayiyi, this medicine has evacuated his bowels.
to cause to loathe, become loathsome to: aduan no ayi me = afono me.

to catch in a snare or net, to entangle, apprehend: yi anɔmaa, apataa. pr. 2491. 3113; .. sɛ wommeyi no asɛm mu, .. to catch, trip him in his words. Mk. 12,13; to catch, seize, s. adwow. - 20. to take to one's self, appropriate: yi adwow, to kidnap, panyar, s. adwow.
to release, liberate, deliver: oyii me (fi or wo) afiase; cf. gye 25.

a handsome, fine-looking person; paragon, élite, the best, finest; ao, woye oy.! mé yímã ne wo! (used of a person of the other sex); minni oy. bi wɔ baabi; afofanto yi ye oy., this butterfly is an (unusually) fine one. Cf. feŋ.
a private person; opposite: odehye; cf. ayemfo.
[dim.] an unimportant, unpresuming, simple, modest person.
a certain charm; kuru wɔ hɔ na wode wo sumaŋ kɔ hɔ a, na kuru ketewa no aye koküroo.
a young person, male or female, not yet full-grown. pr. 3665.

(As.): to 1. stretch out one's feet towards a corpse; opanyin bi wu a, ne yerenom te ne funu anim tẽetẽe woŋ naŋ a ekyere awershow, when a man of rank dies, his wives sit before the corpse stretching out their feet (in its direction) as a sign of grief. 2. also, to lament during a funeral; ayi ase nantew nè sù. ayinaŋtó, inf. 1. stretching out one's feet &c. 2. lamentation. Cf. ayi.
the second funeral of a deceased person; ye ay., to perform such a f.
s. nasireni.
osüi ara adekyẽe y., he (a lion) roared all night till day-break; syn. wée.

bɔ or tu y., to rush, dash: woŋ nyinaa bɔɔ y. kɔɔ ɔkɔ no ano. Jer. 46,9; Ba yiridi(yiridi), to rush, dash, to come in crowds; tu mirika y. (y.), to run very fast.
F. = yinom, pl. of yi, pron. (Mt. 1, 20. 10, 2.5).
inf. an overflowing, flood, inundation. Dan. 9,26.

sãwisá, Guinea-pepper, Cayenne pepper, grains of paradise; a species of Amomum and its seeds. pr. 2306. 3542. [G. gbowyei]; memãa no sika bi se ɔmfa nto yisa bi nye ne hɔ, I gave him some money to defray part of his expenses for medical treatment.
a certain European cloth; s. ntama.
àyísãã, ayisãwa, pl. nyisãã, orphan.
things [ade] done to an orphan; óyè no ay., he uses him spitefully, illtreats him [G. efele niiseniianii].
"father of orphans", an honourable appellation.

[asé a, se obi yi a, égù ne tiri ase no; cf. awosɛ, mmaninwɔw] shudder, horror, dread; ay. pini me, agu me so, apirim me, my blood runs cold at a shocking or painful sight; awow apatuw agu me so na me hɔ aye se nsẽwã-nsẽwã, I am seized with a cold shudder.
pl. a- [osekaŋ a wode yi] razor; kinds: anséèyi, oyiwá, atéwa, kümtõã, kyiriafasé, ŋhwéã. [G. yišekakla].
pl. id. Ab. a week = dapɛŋ, nnaawotwe. — Ayisí, pr. n. m.; s. App. E.

pr. n. of the genius of the day called Kwasida (Sunday); the name is also used in addressing a male person born on a Sunday (Kwasí = akoa-Ayisi): yaa ayisi, s. yaa & Gr. § 41, 4. 147,9. Cf. kurutiayisi.
a part separated for an oblation,
for a specific purpose. Ezek. 48,9. [G. adu-du-duction].
wóyi-tótó, pl. a-.
privy member, the part which is exposed. Lev. 56,3. 4. Mt. 5,29.
aids, helps; cf. ayi.
yíw, Ak. yie, yiw, yie, cf. wie; - yiw, come? yes; woyiw, the negative question; negation and affirmation considered with a verb: he not yet come? o-yiwá, o-yiwá, a kind of razor.

yiyei, red. yiyé [red. of ye] v. to be good, y., remember me; adwum' y., a good work weu; - a-dè yiyé, it is agreeable. - 2. benefit; welfare; - ye yiye: 2282; àyè yiyé, it is good; ni aye yiye, it is prosperous; ye yiye (contr. e-ye so that it might be tekrekyi; .. enyé - to thrive, be well, to make well, pr. 785. - c) to make well, 3560. 3576f.
to ease (one's mind), to prosper. 1.
fair, handsome.
inf. (ye ayi) funeral rites; o-yiye-búru, a handsome person; opp. omu-yiyé, a bad person; opp. omu-yiyé, a bad person; - yiyedifó, II. Ps. 69,(22). 23.
for a specific purpose or possessor. Ezek. 48,9-12. 20f. - diminution, reduction.
pl. -fo, eunuch; one whose privy member is cut off; cf. ɔsae, which is only used of beasts. Isa. 56,3. 4. Mt. 19, 12.
aids, to pay for expenses of a chief's funeral (Ra.).

Ak. yie, interj. yes; yea; well; - cf. wie; - waba (ana)? yiw, is he come? yes; - when said in reply to a negative question, it corroborates the negation and must, in Eng., be rendered with no: so ɔmmae ɛ? yiw, is he not yet come? no.
o-yiwáŋ [mpanyin kasa] a smaller kind of razor; s. oyisekaŋ.
yiyei, red. v. ye.

[red. of ye] 1. adv. well: kae m'asem y., remember my words well! hwe wo adwuma y., attend well to your work! maye m'adwuma y., I have done my work well; - after an adj. very; ɛnyé dè yíyé, it is not very sweet or agreeable. - 2. n. good; good quality; benefit; welfare; syn. pápa. pr. 2282; - yɛ yiye: a) to turn out well. pr. 2282; àyè yíyé, it is well now; n'ahenni aye yiye, his reign has been prosperous; ye no sɛnea woye a ɛbɛye yiye (contr. ɛbe 'ye), make (or do) it so that it may turn out well; - (cf. hene, anisɔde). tekrekyi; .. ɛnyé yiye, cf. hène, anisɔde). - b) to make well, i.e. to mend, repair. pr. 785. - c) to do good (to). pr. 396. 3560. 3576f. - d) euphem. pr. 396. yiye, to ease oneself; cf. nɛ. - di yiye, to prosper. 1 Kg. 2,3.
pl. a-, a person goodly of form; fair, handsome. 1 Kg. 1,6. Job 42,15.
inf. [ye ayi] performance of the funeral rites; mourning.
a handsome, yet dirty, person; opp. ɔnumɔwésɛwa.
inf. [di yiye], F. eyiedzi, welfare, prosperity; security. Prv. 1,32. - yiyedifó, those who are at ease. Ps. 69,(22). 23.
pl. a-, mourner. 2 Sam. 14,2.
pl. a-, a good, pious person.
inf. certain knowledge, certainty, assurance.
-yɔ́, inf. well-doing; doing good. Heb. 13,16; performance of duties; prosperity. - yiyeyέfó, pl. id. benefactor.
